There is no difference; they are synonymous.
questions.explanation: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area. Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area.
questions.ncertEvidence: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area. These provide the index to the plant species found in a particular area. Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area.

questions.question: Which statement about 'Museums' as a taxonomic aid is correct?
options: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference.
Museums only contain living specimens of plants and animals.
In museums, insects are preserved in botanical gardens.
Large animals like birds and mammals are usually preserved in jars.
questions.explanation: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference. Specimens are preserved in the containers or jars in preservative solutions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference. Specimens are preserved in the containers or jars in preservative solutions.

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic aids provides information on any one taxon?

questions.ncertEvidence: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Living World' is accurate in terms of defining properties?
options: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception.
Cellular organization is a non-defining feature of life.
Reproduction is a defining characteristic of all living organisms.
Consciousness is observed only in complex eukaryotes.
questions.explanation: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms because it occurs in cell-free systems in vitro, but the metabolic reactions themselves are living reactions. Reproduction is not a defining feature as mules and sterile human couples do not reproduce.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception; isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely living reactions.

questions.question: In the binomial nomenclature system, which of the following rules is correctly applied?

Both words in a biological name, when handwritten, are underlined separately.
The generic name follows the specific epithet.
The name of the author appears in italics at the end.
questions.explanation: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. When handwritten, both the words in a biological name are separately underlined to indicate their Latin origin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of taxonomic categories in ascending order.
options: Species < Genus < Family < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
Kingdom < Phylum < Class < Order < Family < Genus < Species
Species < Family < Genus < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
Genus < Species < Family < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
questions.explanation: Taxonomic hierarchy follows a specific order: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom. Ascending order means moving from the most specific (species) to the most inclusive (kingdom).
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic hierarchy: Kingdom, Phylum or Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: Which taxonomic category contains organisms that are least similar to each other?
questions.explanation: As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing. Therefore, members of the same kingdom share the fewest common features.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lower the taxon, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a botanical garden?

questions.ncertEvidence: Famous botanical gardens are at Kew (England), Indian Botanical Garden, Howrah (India) and at National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow (India).

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct order for the classification of Solanum tuberosum?
questions.explanation: Solanum tuberosum (potato) belongs to the family Solanaceae, which is placed under the order Solanales based on floral characters.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding taxonomic aids.

Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.question: Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in which of the following?

questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question: A researcher discovers a new organism that reproduces by budding and shows metabolic reactions in a cell-free system. Based on the defining characteristics of life, which of the following is true?

Both budding and metabolism are defining features of life
Neither budding nor metabolism are defining features of life
Budding is a defining feature, but metabolism is not
questions.explanation: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception, whereas reproduction (like budding) is not defining because organisms like mules or sterile worker bees do not reproduce.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception. Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.

questions.question: Which of the following sets represents taxa at the same hierarchical level?
questions.explanation: Insecta, Dicotyledonae, and Mammalia are all categories at the 'Class' level. The others contain mixed ranks.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomical categories like Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species.

questions.question: If an organism is named 'Mangifera indica L.', what does the 'L.' specifically signify in taxonomic nomenclature?
options: The scientist who first described the species
The Latin origin of the specific epithet
The local name of the plant
questions.explanation: The name of the author appears after the specific epithet in an abbreviated form, indicating the person who first described the species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Name of the author appears after the specific epithet at the end of the biological name and is written in an abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is common to both 'Solanum tuberosum' and 'Panthera leo'?
options: They belong to the same Domain
They belong to the same Family
They belong to the same Order
They belong to the same Genus
questions.explanation: Both are eukaryotic organisms, thus sharing the same Domain (Eukarya). They differ at all other taxonomic levels provided.
questions.ncertEvidence: All living organisms, from the simplest prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes, share the same basic cellular structure.

questions.question: Consider the following statement: 'Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in majority of higher animals and plants.' Which option best explains this?
options: Increase in mass and increase in number of individuals are distinct processes
Only unicellular organisms show growth by cell division
Higher plants do not grow throughout their lifespan
Reproduction is essential for the survival of an individual

questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question: Which taxonomic aid provides information for the identification of names of species found in an area?
questions.explanation: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area, providing the index to the plant species found in that area.
questions.ncertEvidence: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area. These provide the index to the plant species found in a particular area.

questions.question: When comparing 'Family' and 'Order', which of the following is true?
options: Family has fewer common characteristics than Order
Family is a higher category than Order
Family contains more genera than Order contains families
Order is characterized by a group of related genera
questions.explanation: As we go higher in the taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics decreases. Thus, a Family (lower rank) has more common characteristics than an Order (higher rank).
questions.ncertEvidence: Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'Museums' is correct?
options: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference
Museums contain only live specimens of plants and animals
Museums are primarily used for the cultivation of rare species
Museums only contain skeletons of extinct organisms
questions.explanation: Museums are set up in educational institutes such as schools and colleges, housing preserved specimens in containers or jars with preservative solutions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference.

questions.question: In the hierarchy of classification, which of the following is the correct sequence from broadest to narrowest?
questions.explanation: The standard taxonomic hierarchy is Kingdom > Phylum > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic hierarchy: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: A key is a taxonomic aid used for identification. How does it function?
options: It is based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet
It uses only similarities between organisms
It is a list of all known species in a specific region
It provides a detailed description of only one taxon
questions.explanation: Keys are based on the contrasts, generally in a pair called couplet. It represents the choice made between two opposite options.
questions.ncertEvidence: Keys are based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet. It represents the choice made between two opposite options.

questions.question: Which of the following inferences can be drawn regarding the 'defining feature' of living organisms based on the NCERT definition of metabolism?
options: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living things
Metabolism is a defining feature that occurs only within the cellular organization
All chemical reactions occurring in a living organism are termed metabolism
Non-living objects do not exhibit any form of metabolic activity
questions.explanation: Metabolism is defined as the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in a living organism. While reactions can be performed in vitro, they are not 'living things' but 'living reactions'.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolism is defined as the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in a living organism.

questions.question: If a biological entity is unable to reproduce, which of the following inferences is scientifically valid according to the NCERT text?
options: It cannot be considered a living organism
Reproduction is a defining characteristic of living organisms
Reproduction is a characteristic of living organisms, but not a defining one
It must be a non-living object due to lack of self-replication
questions.explanation: Many organisms like mules, worker bees, and infertile human couples do not reproduce. Therefore, reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Many organisms do not reproduce (mules, sterile worker bees, infertile human couples, etc). Hence, reproduction also cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.

questions.question: Consider a scenario where a non-living object increases in size due to the accumulation of material on its surface. What can be inferred about this process?
options: It is a process of growth similar to living organisms
It is an intrinsic growth, which is absent in living organisms
It is an extrinsic growth, distinct from the intrinsic growth seen in living organisms
It proves that growth is a defining feature of living organisms
questions.explanation: Living organisms grow from inside (intrinsic), whereas non-living objects like mountains, boulders, and sand mounds grow by accumulation of material on the surface (extrinsic).
questions.ncertEvidence: Growth, therefore, cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms... non-living objects also grow if we take increase in body mass as a criterion for growth.

questions.question: Which inference can be made about the relationship between 'consciousness' and 'living organisms'?
options: It is the only feature that is present in all living organisms without exception
It is a property that can be observed in isolated metabolic reactions
It is limited only to multicellular organisms
It is not a defining feature of life because it is absent in plants
questions.explanation: All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes, can sense and respond to environmental cues. Consciousness is the defining property of living organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Consciousness therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms.

questions.question: Regarding the Binomial Nomenclature system, if a scientist describes a new species, what inference can be made about the generic and specific epithet?
options: The generic name starts with a small letter and the specific epithet with a capital letter
Both names must be printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin
The generic name represents the taxon, while the specific epithet is a descriptive adjective
The specific epithet must be repeated if the species is transferred to a new genus
questions.explanation: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. When handwritten, they are separately underlined.

questions.question: In the hierarchy of classification, what inference can be made about organisms sharing the same 'Family' but belonging to different 'Genera'?
options: They share more common features than organisms in the same Order
They must belong to the same Species
They share fewer common features than organisms in the same Genus
They are classified together based on reproductive isolation

questions.ncertEvidence: Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share.

questions.question: If two organisms belong to the same 'Order', what can be inferred about their taxonomic classification?
options: They must belong to the same Class
They must belong to the same Genus
They may belong to different Classes
They share all characteristics with each other
questions.explanation: Taxonomic categories follow a hierarchy: Species < Genus < Family < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom. If organisms are in the same Order, they are necessarily in the same Class.
questions.ncertEvidence: Order and other higher taxonomic categories are identified based on the aggregates of characters.

questions.question: What inference can be made about the 'Botanical Gardens' and 'Zoological Parks' as taxonomic aids?
options: They contain only preserved specimens for study
They are ex-situ conservation facilities that help in taxonomic studies
They serve as keys for identification of plants and animals
They are exclusively meant for the preservation of extinct species

questions.question: Which inference is correct regarding the use of 'Keys' in taxonomy?
options: A key is based on the similarities only
Each statement in a key is called a lead
A key is generally analytical in nature
A key is used for the identification of a single species in a specific habitat only
questions.explanation: Keys are based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet. Each statement in the couplet is called a lead. They are analytical in nature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Keys are based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet. It represents the choice made between two opposite options... Each statement in the key is called a lead.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the 'Museums' set up in educational institutes?
options: They contain only dried plant specimens
They provide information regarding the habitat of living organisms
They have collections of preserved plants and animals for study and reference
They are strictly for the display of fossils and skeletons only
questions.explanation: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference. Specimens are preserved in the jars or containers in preservative solutions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference.

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic categories represents the highest rank in the hierarchical classification system, grouping organisms based on broad shared features?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the highest taxonomic category in the hierarchical classification system, encompassing a broader range of organisms than Phylum, Class, or Order.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic categories in the hierarchy are Kingdom, Phylum/Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: Identify the set of organisms that exhibit 'metabolism' as a defining feature of life, while also demonstrating 'cellular organization'.
questions.explanation: Metabolism and cellular organization are defining features of all living organisms, as metabolic reactions can be demonstrated in cell-free systems, but the cellular organization is the definitive characteristic.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolism and cellular organization are defining features of life forms.

questions.question: In the binomial nomenclature of Mangifera indica, what does the second component of the name signify?
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the first word represents the genus and the second word is the specific epithet.
questions.ncertEvidence: The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the taxonomic aid 'Museums' is correct?
options: Specimens are preserved in containers or jars in preservative solutions
Plants are collected and pressed on sheets
Living plants are grown for identification purposes
Key is used for identification of plants and animals
questions.explanation: Museums generally have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference, often stored in jars with preservative solutions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Museums have collections of preserved plant and animal specimens for study and reference.

questions.question: Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in which of the following groups?
questions.explanation: In higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are distinct events, whereas in unicellular organisms, growth is synonymous with reproduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question: Which statement about the 'Botanical Garden' as a taxonomic aid is accurate?
options: Each plant is labeled with its botanical/scientific name and its family
They contain only extinct plant species
They are used for the preservation of animal skeletons
They represent the smallest taxonomic unit
questions.explanation: In botanical gardens, each plant is labeled indicating its botanical/scientific name and its family for identification purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of all living organisms?
questions.explanation: Self-replication (reproduction) is not a defining feature because some living organisms like mules, worker bees, and infertile human couples do not reproduce.
questions.ncertEvidence: Reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.

questions.question: Which taxonomic category is defined as a group of related genera with less number of similarities compared to genus?
questions.explanation: Family is a group of related genera with still less number of similarities as compared to genus and species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Families are characterised on the basis of both vegetative and reproductive features of plant species.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of characteristics are considered 'defining features' of all living organisms without exception?

questions.question: Consider the following attributes of living organisms: (i) Growth, (ii) Reproduction, (iii) Ability to sense environment, (iv) Metabolism, (v) Cellular organization. How many of these are NOT considered defining features of life?
questions.explanation: Growth and reproduction are not defining features as they are seen in non-living things or have exceptions. Ability to sense environment (consciousness), metabolism, and cellular organization are defining features.

questions.question: Regarding the binomial nomenclature, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics.
The first word denotes the genus and the second word denotes the specific epithet.
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined.
The first word of the genus starts with a small letter.

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic categories contains organisms that are least similar to each other?

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding 'Museums' as a taxonomic aid.

Specimens are preserved in containers or jars in preservative solutions.
Insects are preserved in insect boxes after collecting, killing, and pinning.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the 'Key' used for identification of plants and animals?

It is based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet.
It is analytical in nature and used for flora and fauna.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'Herbarium' is accurate?

It contains only dried and pressed plant specimens.

It is a storehouse of living plant specimens.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding 'Botanical Gardens'?

Plant species are grown for identification purposes.
Each plant is labeled indicating its botanical name and its family.
They primarily function to preserve dead specimens for morphological study.

questions.question: Identify the statement that correctly distinguishes between 'Taxon' and 'Category'.

Taxon and category are synonymous terms with no difference.

questions.explanation: In taxonomy, a 'category' represents a rank (e.g., Kingdom, Class), whereas a 'taxon' represents a real group of organisms (e.g., Mammalia, Angiospermae) that occupy that rank.

questions.question: Which of the following attributes is considered the 'defining property' of all living organisms without exception?

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding the scientific naming of organisms as per ICBN.

The biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics, but when handwritten, they are not underlined.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the 'Key' in taxonomic studies?

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of taxonomic categories in ascending order.

Species < Genus < Order < Family < Class < Phylum < Kingdom

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic aids provides information for identification of names of species found in an area?

questions.ncertEvidence: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area. These provide the index to the plant species found in a particular area.

questions.question: Consider the following statement: 'Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems.' What conclusion can be drawn from this?
options: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living things.
Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are surely not living things, but are living reactions.
Metabolism is a non-defining feature of life.
The cell is not the basic unit of life.
questions.explanation: While metabolic reactions can occur in vitro, they are not 'living organisms' themselves, but they are 'living reactions' occurring in a controlled environment.
questions.ncertEvidence: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely living reactions.

questions.question: Which category contains groups of related orders?
questions.explanation: Class is the taxonomic category that includes related orders. For example, Order Primata and Carnivora are placed in the Class Mammalia.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class includes related orders. For example, order Primata comprising monkey, gorilla and gibbon is placed in class Mammalia along with order Carnivora that includes animals like tiger, cat and dog.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is considered the 'defining feature' of all living organisms without exception?
questions.explanation: Consciousness is the defining property of living organisms as all organisms, from prokaryotes to complex eukaryotes, can sense and respond to environmental stimuli. Reproduction and growth are not defining features because non-living objects can grow, and some living organisms (like mules) do not reproduce.
questions.ncertEvidence: All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues. Consciousness therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms.

questions.question: In taxonomic hierarchy, which of the following represents the correct sequence of categories?
options: Kingdom > Phylum > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species
Phylum > Kingdom > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species
Kingdom > Class > Phylum > Order > Family > Genus > Species
Kingdom > Phylum > Order > Class > Family > Genus > Species
questions.explanation: The taxonomic hierarchy follows a specific order of classification from the broadest category (Kingdom) to the most specific (Species).
questions.ncertEvidence: Kingdom, Phylum or Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: The scientific name of Mango is written as Mangifera indica L. What does 'L.' represent?
options: The name of the taxonomist who first described the species.
The Latin origin of the genus name.
The location where the specimen was first found.
The lineage of the plant species.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the name of the author appears after the specific epithet in an abbreviated form, indicating the person who described the species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Name of the author appears after the specific epithet at the end of the biological name and is written in abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic categories contains organisms with the maximum number of common characteristics?
questions.explanation: As we move from Species to Kingdom, the number of common characteristics decreases. Therefore, Species contains the most common characteristics.
questions.ncertEvidence: Species, genus, family and order of animals and plants are identified on the basis of aggregates of characters. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding a 'Herbarium'.
options: It serves as a quick referral system in taxonomic studies.
Plants are preserved in formalin for long-term storage.
The herbarium sheet carries a label providing information about date and place of collection.
It is a store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed and preserved on sheets.
questions.explanation: In a herbarium, plant specimens are dried, pressed, and preserved on sheets; they are not preserved in liquid solutions like formalin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Herbarium is a store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed and preserved on sheets.

questions.question: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are:
options: Living reactions but not living things.
questions.explanation: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. These are 'living reactions' but are not technically 'living things' because they occur in an artificial environment.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. An isolated metabolic reaction(s) outside the body of an organism, performed in a test tube is neither living nor non-living.

questions.question: Which taxonomic aid is used for identification of plants and animals based on similarities and dissimilarities?
questions.explanation: A 'Key' is a taxonomic aid used for identification based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called a couplet.
questions.ncertEvidence: Key is another taxonomic aid used for identification of plants and animals based on the similarities and dissimilarities.

questions.question: Families like Convolvulaceae and Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on:
questions.explanation: Plant families are assigned to an order largely based on floral characters.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'Taxa' is accurate?
options: Taxa can indicate categories at very different levels.
Taxa are strictly limited to the rank of species.
Taxa are not used in biological classification.
questions.explanation: Taxa represents a scientific term for categories, which can exist at different levels, such as species, genus, or kingdom.
questions.ncertEvidence: Here, 'taxa' indicates categories at very different levels. 'Plants' – also form a taxa. Wheat is also a taxon.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between growth in living organisms and non-living objects?
options: Living organisms grow by internal cell division, whereas non-living objects grow by accumulation of material on the surface.
Growth is a defining property of living organisms, but it is not observed in non-living objects.
In living organisms, growth and reproduction are mutually inclusive events.
Non-living objects do not show growth under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Living organisms exhibit internal growth (intussusception), while non-living objects like mountains and boulders grow by accretion (accumulation of material on the surface).
questions.ncertEvidence: Growth in living organisms is from inside, while in non-living objects, it is from outside.

questions.question: Metabolism is considered a defining feature of all living organisms because:
options: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living things.
It is the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in a living system.
It is present in all organisms, whether unicellular or multicellular, without exception.
It is the only process that allows organisms to sense their environment.
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the defining feature because all living organisms, without exception, exhibit metabolic reactions. Isolated reactions in vitro are not living things, but they are living reactions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems; however, they are not living things but surely living reactions.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of organisms reproduces through the process of fragmentation?
options: Fungi, filamentous algae, and protonema of mosses.
questions.explanation: Fungi, filamentous algae, and the protonema of mosses all multiply by fragmentation. Planaria exhibits true regeneration.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fungi, the filamentous algae, the protonema of mosses, all easily multiply by fragmentation.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct hierarchical arrangement of taxonomic categories in ascending order?
options: Species < Genus < Family < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
Kingdom < Phylum < Class < Order < Family < Genus < Species
Species < Family < Genus < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
Genus < Species < Family < Order < Class < Phylum < Kingdom
questions.explanation: Taxonomic hierarchy starts from the lowest rank (Species) to the highest rank (Kingdom) as Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic studies of all organism led to the development of common categories like kingdom, phylum or division, class, order, family, genus and species.

questions.question: Which of the following is a 'defining' feature of living organisms that has no exceptions?
questions.explanation: Consciousness is the most obvious and technically complicated feature of all living organisms because all organisms, from prokaryotes to complex eukaryotes, can sense and respond to environmental stimuli.
questions.ncertEvidence: Consciousness becomes the defining property of living organisms.

questions.question: In the binomial nomenclature of Mangifera indica L., what does 'L.' represent?
options: The language from which the name was derived.
The name of the scientist who first described the species.
The taxonomic rank of the organism.
questions.explanation: In binomial nomenclature, the name of the author appears after the specific epithet in an abbreviated form, indicating the person who first described the species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Name of the author appears after the specific epithet at the end of the biological name and is written in an abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the 'Key' in taxonomy is incorrect?
options: Keys are based on the presence or absence of contrasting characters.
Each statement in the key is called a couplet.
Keys are generally analytical in nature.
Separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category.
questions.explanation: Each statement in a key is called a 'lead', not a couplet. A couplet is a pair of contrasting characters.
questions.ncertEvidence: Each statement in the key is called a lead. Separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category such as family, genus and species for identification purposes.

questions.question: Identify the incorrectly matched pair regarding taxonomic aids:
options: Museum - Collection of preserved plants and animals for study and reference.
Herbarium - Store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed, and preserved on sheets.
Zoological Park - Places where wild animals are kept in protected environments under human care.
Botanical Garden - Specialized gardens having collections of living plants for identification and aesthetic purposes only.
questions.explanation: Botanical gardens are used for ex-situ conservation and research, not just aesthetics. The description provided in option 3 is incomplete regarding the purpose.
questions.ncertEvidence: In these gardens, plants are grown for identification purposes and each plant is labelled indicating its botanical/scientific name and its family.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of organisms exhibit both growth and reproduction as mutually exclusive events?
options: Majority of higher animals and plants
questions.explanation: In higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events, whereas in unicellular organisms, growth is synonymous with reproduction (increase in cell number).
questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding taxonomic categories:
I. Species is the lowest taxonomic category.
II. Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common.
III. Family is placed between Order and Genus.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct according to the taxonomic hierarchy defined in NCERT. Species is the basic unit, Genus is an aggregate of closely related species, and Family is a group of related genera, positioned between Genus and Order.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic studies of all known organisms have led to the development of common categories such as kingdom, phylum or division, class, order, family, genus and species.

questions.question: Which of the following is a 'defining feature' of all living organisms without any exception?
questions.explanation: Consciousness is the defining property of living organisms. Growth and reproduction are not defining features because non-living objects can grow (accumulation of material) and some living organisms (like sterile worker bees) do not reproduce.
questions.ncertEvidence: Consciousness therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms.

questions.question: Which taxonomic aid provides information on any one taxon?
questions.explanation: Monographs contain information on any one taxon. Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area, and Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of taxonomic hierarchy from higher to lower rank:
options: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Species → Genus
Phylum → Kingdom → Class → Family → Order → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Phylum → Order → Class → Family → Genus → Species
questions.explanation: The correct hierarchical sequence is Kingdom, Phylum (or Division), Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species.
questions.ncertEvidence: These taxonomic groups/categories are distinct biological entities and not merely morphological aggregates. Taxonomical studies of all known organisms have led to the development of common categories such as kingdom, phylum or division, class, order, family, genus and species.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct statement regarding Botanical Gardens?
options: They serve as ex-situ conservation strategies
They are meant for recreational purposes only
They represent only extinct plant species
questions.explanation: Botanical gardens are specialized gardens having collections of living plants for reference, serving as ex-situ conservation centers.
questions.ncertEvidence: These specialized gardens have collections of living plants for reference. Plant species in these gardens are grown for identification purposes and each plant is labelled indicating its botanical/scientific name and its family.

questions.question: What is the basis of modern taxonomic studies?
options: External and internal structure, along with the structure of cell, development process, and ecological information
questions.explanation: Modern taxonomic studies involve characterization, identification, nomenclature, and classification based on external and internal structure, cell structure, developmental processes, and ecological information.
questions.ncertEvidence: External and internal structure, along with the structure of cell, development process and ecological information of organisms are essential and form the basis of modern taxonomic studies.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of organisms exhibit the property of 'exhibit metabolism' as a defining feature of all living organisms, without exception?
options: All living organisms, unicellular or multicellular
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the sum total of all chemical reactions occurring in a body. It is a defining feature of all living organisms; no non-living object exhibits metabolism.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. An isolated metabolic reaction(s) outside the body of an organism, performed in a test tube is neither living nor non-living. Hence, while metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception, isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely metabolic reactions.

questions.question: Consider the following statement: 'Growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events in majority of the higher animals and plants.' Which of the following best explains this?
options: In higher animals, growth occurs only during reproductive phase
Higher organisms grow only up to a certain age, while reproduction is continuous
Growth and reproduction are distinct biological processes that do not overlap in timing in complex organisms
Growth in higher animals is internal, whereas reproduction is an external process
questions.explanation: In higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events, meaning they do not occur simultaneously as they do in unicellular organisms (where growth is synonymous with reproduction).
questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of higher animals and plants as we grow, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events.

questions.question: The scientific naming of organisms like 'Mangifera indica' consists of two components. Which of the following correctly identifies the components and their sequence?
options: Generic name followed by specific epithet
Specific epithet followed by generic name
Family name followed by genus name
Order name followed by species name
questions.explanation: According to binomial nomenclature, the first word represents the genus and the second word represents the specific epithet.
questions.ncertEvidence: This biological name has two components: the generic name and the specific epithet.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does not reproduce, yet is considered a living organism, thereby proving reproduction is not a defining characteristic?
questions.explanation: Worker bees, mules, and infertile human couples are living organisms that do not reproduce. Therefore, reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: There are many organisms which do not reproduce (mules, sterile worker bees, infertile human couples, etc). Hence, reproduction also cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.

questions.question: In the process of taxonomic studies, which of the following is the correct sequence of steps?
questions.explanation: Taxonomic studies require correct characterization, identification, nomenclature, and classification to organize organisms into categories.
questions.ncertEvidence: Characterisation, identification, nomenclature and classification are the processes that are basic to taxonomy.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between growth in living organisms and growth in non-living objects like mountains or boulders?
options: Living organisms grow by division, non-living by accumulation of material on the surface
Living organisms grow from inside, non-living grow from outside
Non-living objects do not grow at all
questions.explanation: Living organisms grow from inside due to cell division, while non-living objects can grow (increase in mass) only by accumulation of material on their surfaces.
questions.ncertEvidence: In living organisms, growth is from inside. Growth, therefore, cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms. Conditions under which it can be observed in all living organisms have to be explained and then we understand that it is a characteristic of living systems.

questions.question: Which of the following categories includes related orders like Primata and Carnivora?
questions.explanation: Class Mammalia includes orders like Primata and Carnivora.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Mammalia includes familiar orders like Primata and Carnivora.

questions.question: Which taxonomic aid is used for quick referral in taxonomic studies and contains information on any one taxon?
questions.explanation: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.question: How are the names of authors written in biological nomenclature?
options: In italics after the specific epithet
In Roman script after the specific epithet
Only if the organism is a plant
questions.explanation: The author's name appears after the specific epithet and is written in an abbreviated form in Roman script.
questions.ncertEvidence: Name of the author appears after the specific epithet and is written in an abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn.

questions.question: Which of the following taxonomic categories contains organisms least similar to one another?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the highest taxonomic category. As we move higher in the hierarchy, the number of common characteristics decreases, meaning the organisms become less similar.
questions.ncertEvidence: Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a correct rule of binomial nomenclature?
options: The genus name starts with a small letter
Biological names are generally in Latin
The first word denotes the genus
The second word denotes the specific epithet
questions.explanation: According to the rules of binomial nomenclature, the generic name (genus) must start with a capital letter, not a small letter.
questions.ncertEvidence: The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

questions.question: Which of the following is a taxonomic aid that provides information for identification of names of species found in an area?
questions.explanation: Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area.
questions.ncertEvidence: Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area.

questions.question: Which taxonomic category includes related families like Felidae and Canidae?
questions.explanation: Order Carnivora includes families like Felidae (cats) and Canidae (dogs).
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of taxonomic categories in descending order?
questions.explanation: The hierarchy of classification is Kingdom > Phylum > Class > Order > Family > Genus > Species.
questions.ncertEvidence: Taxonomic categories in a hierarchical arrangement: Kingdom, Phylum or Division, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.question: Which of the following contains information on any one taxon?
questions.explanation: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.question: In botanical gardens, plants are grown for identification purposes. Each plant is labeled with its:
questions.explanation: Plants in botanical gardens are labeled with their botanical/scientific name and their family.
questions.ncertEvidence: In botanical gardens, each plant is labelled indicating its botanical/scientific name and its family.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms are known as the chief producers in the oceans?
questions.explanation: Diatoms are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). They are the chief producers in the oceans.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Chrysophytes section: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.

questions.question: Which feature is characteristic of the kingdom Fungi, with the exception of yeasts?
questions.explanation: With the exception of yeasts (unicellular), fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Kingdom Fungi section: With the exception of yeasts which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Methanogens?
options: They are present in the gut of several ruminant animals
They belong to the domain Eukarya
They produce methane in oxygen-rich environments
questions.explanation: Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Kingdom Monera section: Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes.

questions.question: In which group of organisms is the cell wall stiffened by cellulose plates on the outer surface?
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellates most of them have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Dinoflagellates section: Most of them have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.

questions.question: What is the primary storage material in the cells of Fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi store their food material in the form of glycogen or oil droplets.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Kingdom Fungi section: Fungi store their food material in the form of starch or glycogen. (Correction: NCERT explicitly states glycogen or oil).

questions.question: Which group of organisms possesses a protein-rich layer called pellicle instead of a cell wall?
questions.explanation: Euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Euglenoids section: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: Mycoplasma are organisms that:
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma is an organism that completely lacks a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Kingdom Monera section: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for the sexual cycle in fungi?
questions.explanation: The sexual cycle involves three steps: fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes (plasmogamy), fusion of two nuclei (karyogamy), and meiosis in zygote resulting in haploid spores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Kingdom Fungi section: The sexual cycle involves the following three steps: (i) Plasmogamy (ii) Karyogamy (iii) Meiosis.

questions.question: Viroids differ from viruses in that they:
questions.explanation: Viroids were found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens section: It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses.

questions.question: Which organisms are referred to as 'saprophytic protists'?
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. The body moves along decaying twigs and leaves engulfing organic material.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biological Classification, Slime Moulds section: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the five-kingdom classification system proposed by R.H. Whittaker is correct?
options: The main criteria for classification were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
It includes Viruses, Viroids, and Lichens as distinct kingdoms.
Organisms are classified based solely on their morphological characters, ignoring physiological and reproductive traits.
It provides a clear distinction between the Kingdom Monera and the Kingdom Protista based on the presence of a cell wall.
questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker (1969) proposed the five-kingdom classification system based on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1

questions.question: In the context of Kingdom Monera, which statement best describes the nature of bacteria?
options: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera and are the most abundant micro-organisms.
All bacteria are heterotrophic and rely on decaying organic matter for survival.
Bacteria possess a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Bacteria are exclusively found in moderate environments and cannot survive in extreme habitats.
questions.explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms and occur almost everywhere.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.1

questions.question: Which group of bacteria is known for thriving in extreme salt areas, such as salt lakes?
questions.explanation: Archaebacteria are special since they live in some of the most harsh habitats such as extreme salty areas (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles) and marshy areas (methanogens).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.1

questions.question: Identify the feature that differentiates Cyanobacteria from other photosynthetic bacteria.
options: Presence of chlorophyll 'a' similar to green plants.
Lack of a cell wall composed of peptidoglycan.
Absence of specialized cells like heterocysts.
questions.explanation: The cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) have chlorophyll 'a' similar to green plants and are photosynthetic autotrophs.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.1

questions.question: Which of the following organisms are considered the 'chief producers' in the oceans?
questions.explanation: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans. They belong to the group Chrysophytes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.2

questions.question: Which protists are responsible for the 'red tides' in the sea due to their rapid multiplication?
questions.explanation: Red dinoflagellates (e.g., Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.2

questions.question: What is the unique characteristic of Euglenoids that allows them to be classified as both autotrophic and heterotrophic?
options: They possess a protein-rich layer called pellicle and can perform photosynthesis in sunlight, but behave as heterotrophs when deprived of it.
They are obligate parasites that derive nutrition from host cells.
They lack chlorophyll and depend entirely on saprophytic nutrition.
They are multicellular organisms with complex tissue systems.
questions.explanation: Euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. When deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.2

questions.question: Which group of fungi is commonly known as 'sac-fungi'?
questions.explanation: The sac-fungi are the members of Ascomycetes. Examples include Aspergillus, Claviceps and Neurospora.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.1.4

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Viruses is true according to NCERT?
options: Viruses are obligate parasites that possess both DNA and RNA.
The protein coat of a virus is called a capsid, made of small subunits called capsomeres.
Viruses can replicate outside a host cell independently.
Viruses were named by Dmitri Ivanowsky, who discovered they were smaller than bacteria.
questions.explanation: Viruses are obligate parasites. Their protein coat called capsid is made of small subunits called capsomeres, which protect the nucleic acid. A virus contains either DNA or RNA, never both.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.2

questions.question: Which of the following describes the nature of Viroids?
options: They are infectious agents consisting only of a short strand of RNA without a protein coat.
They possess a large DNA molecule and a complex protein capsid.
They are larger than viruses and cause diseases in animals.
They are a type of bacteria that lack cell walls.
questions.explanation: Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener; they are smaller than viruses and consist of a free RNA without a protein coat.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 2: Biological Classification, Section 2.2

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Kingdom Monera: (I) Bacteria are the sole members of Kingdom Monera. (II) They possess a complex cell wall made of cellulose. (III) They are the most abundant micro-organisms. (IV) Some bacteria live in extreme habitats like hot springs and deserts. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms and occur almost everywhere, including extreme habitats. Their cell wall is made of peptidoglycan, not cellulose.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms. Bacteria occur almost everywhere.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between Archaebacteria and Eubacteria?
options: Archaebacteria have a different cell wall structure which is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
Eubacteria are always autotrophic, whereas Archaebacteria are always heterotrophic.
Archaebacteria lack a cell wall, whereas Eubacteria have a rigid cell wall.
Both groups are classified together because they lack a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.explanation: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure, which is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

questions.question: Regarding the nutrition of bacteria, which statement is incorrect?
options: Heterotrophic bacteria are helpful in curd making and production of antibiotics.
Some bacteria are pathogens causing diseases like cholera and typhoid.
questions.explanation: The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs, meaning they depend on other organisms or on dead organic matter for food. They are not mostly autotrophic.
questions.ncertEvidence: The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs i.e. they do not synthesise their own food but depend on other organisms or on dead organic matter for food.

questions.question: Identify the correct statements regarding Mycoplasma: (I) They completely lack a cell wall. (II) They are the smallest living cells known. (III) They can survive without oxygen. (IV) They are pathogenic in animals and plants.
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many are pathogenic in animals and plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding Dinoflagellates:
options: They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells.
They have two flagella, both of which are directed towards the anterior end.
They are exclusively found in freshwater habitats.
The cell wall is composed of thin cellulose plates with an absence of silica.
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellates appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. They have two flagella, one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.
questions.ncertEvidence: These organisms appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells. The cell wall has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the unique nature of Euglenoids?
options: They have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
They are strictly heterotrophic in the presence of sunlight.
They possess a cell wall made of chitin.
questions.explanation: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible. They are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight and heterotrophic in the absence of sunlight.
questions.ncertEvidence: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about Slime Moulds: (I) They are saprophytic protists. (II) Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium. (III) During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores. (IV) The spores possess true walls. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All statements provided accurately describe the life cycle and characteristics of slime moulds as per NCERT.
questions.ncertEvidence: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls.

questions.question: Which statement is incorrect regarding Fungi?
options: Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil, and on animals and plants.
The cell walls of fungi are composed of cellulose and hemicellulose.
Some are unicellular like yeast, used to make bread and beer.
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin or fungal cellulose, not plant cellulose and hemicellulose.
questions.ncertEvidence: With the exception of yeasts which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae. The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

questions.question: Regarding the classification of Fungi into classes (Phycomycetes, Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes), which statement is true?
options: Deuteromycetes are often called 'imperfect fungi' because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known.
Basidiomycetes include moulds, rusts, and smuts.
Ascomycetes are known as club fungi.
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are known as imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered, they were moved into classes they rightly belong to.
questions.ncertEvidence: When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to. It is also possible that the asexual and vegetative stage have been given one name (and placed under Deuteromycetes) and the sexual stage another (and placed under another class).

questions.question: Assertion (A): Mycoplasma are classified as organisms that completely lack a cell wall. Reason (R): They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct NCERT points. Mycoplasma lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells, but the lack of a cell wall is not caused by their size or anaerobic capacity.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall and they are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In Chrysophytes, the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells which fit together as in a soap box. Reason (R): The walls are embedded with silica, making them indestructible.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The accumulation of silica in the cell walls of diatoms (Chrysophytes) is specifically what makes them indestructible, fitting the soap-box arrangement.
questions.ncertEvidence: In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called pellicle instead of a cell wall. Reason (R): This pellicle makes their body flexible.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The pellicle is the defining structural feature of Euglenoids that provides both protection and flexibility to their body.
questions.ncertEvidence: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Reason (R): Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are indeed saprophytic protists and they do form plasmodium, but the formation of plasmodium is a growth stage, not the reason they are classified as saprophytic.
questions.ncertEvidence: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Viruses are considered to be on the borderline between living and non-living. Reason (R): Viruses are inert crystalline structures outside the living cell.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The reason viruses are considered to be on the borderline of life is precisely because they act as inert crystals outside of a host cell and become active inside.
questions.ncertEvidence: Viruses are considered to be on the borderline between living and non-living. Once they infect a cell they take over the machinery of the host cell to replicate themselves, killing the host. Outside the host cell they are inert crystalline structures.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae) are photosynthetic autotrophs. Reason (R): They contain chlorophyll 'a' similar to green plants.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria perform oxygenic photosynthesis because they possess chlorophyll 'a', which is the functional basis for their classification as photosynthetic autotrophs.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cyanobacteria (also referred to as blue-green algae) have chlorophyll 'a' similar to green plants and are photosynthetic autotrophs.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Viroids were discovered to be a new infectious agent that is smaller than viruses. Reason (R): Viroids contain DNA as their genetic material.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Viroids are indeed smaller than viruses, but they consist of free RNA, not DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and was free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Basidiomycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi. Reason (R): The sexual organs are absent in these fungi.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are known as imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known. Basidiomycetes are club fungi.
questions.ncertEvidence: Deuteromycetes are commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Lichens are very good pollution indicators. Reason (R): They do not grow in polluted areas.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Lichens are sensitive to pollutants, specifically sulfur dioxide, which is why their absence in polluted areas serves as an indicator.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lichens are very good pollution indicators – they do not grow in polluted areas.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure. Reason (R): This feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The unique cell wall structure of archaebacteria is the primary evolutionary adaptation that allows them to survive in extreme environments like salt marshes, hot springs, and marshy areas.
questions.ncertEvidence: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

questions.question:
Match the following fungal classes with their characteristic features as per NCERT classification:
(A) Phycomycetes (i) Sac fungi
(B) Ascomycetes (ii) Club fungi
(C) Basidiomycetes (iii) Algal fungi
(D) Deuteromycetes (iv) Fungi imperfecti
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes are known as algal fungi, Ascomycetes as sac fungi, Basidiomycetes as club fungi, and Deuteromycetes as fungi imperfecti.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.3.4 (Kingdom Fungi)

questions.question:
Match the following bacterial shapes with their examples:
(A) Coccus (i) Vibrio cholerae
(B) Bacillus (ii) Streptococcus pneumoniae
(C) Vibrio (iii) Bacillus anthracis
(D) Spirillum (iv) Spirillum volutans
questions.explanation: Coccus is spherical (Streptococcus), Bacillus is rod-shaped (Bacillus), Vibrio is comma-shaped (Vibrio), and Spirillum is spiral-shaped.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.1 (Kingdom Monera)

questions.question:
Match the organisms with their respective sub-groups in Kingdom Protista:
(A) Diatoms (i) Dinoflagellates
(B) Gonyaulax (ii) Chrysophytes
(C) Euglena (iii) Protozoans
(D) Paramoecium (iv) Euglenoids
questions.explanation: Diatoms are Chrysophytes, Gonyaulax is a Dinoflagellate, Euglena is an Euglenoid, and Paramoecium is a ciliated Protozoan.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.2 (Kingdom Protista)

questions.question:
Match the following viral structures or components with their description:
(A) Capsid (i) Protein coat
(B) Capsomeres (ii) Infectious RNA
(C) Viroids (iii) Subunit of capsid
(D) Prions (iv) Abnormally folded protein
questions.explanation: Viruses possess a protein coat (capsid) made of subunits (capsomeres). Viroids are infectious RNA, and Prions are abnormally folded proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.5 (Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens)

questions.question:
Match the following protozoan groups with their locomotion organelle:
(A) Amoeboid (i) Cilia
(B) Flagellated (ii) Pseudopodia
(C) Ciliated (iii) None
(D) Sporozoans (iv) Flagella
questions.explanation: Amoeboid protozoans use pseudopodia, flagellated use flagella, ciliated use cilia, and sporozoans lack specialized organelles for locomotion.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.2.4 (Protozoans)

questions.question:
Match the following mycorrhizal associations with their components:
(A) Lichens (i) Algal and Fungal component
(B) Mycorrhiza (ii) Fungal and Plant root
(C) Symbiont (iii) Living together
(D) Heterotroph (iv) Dependent on others
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations of algae and fungi, Mycorrhiza is between fungi and roots of higher plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.5 (Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens)

questions.question:
Match the following fungal reproduction structures with their classes:
(A) Zoospores (i) Phycomycetes
(B) Conidia (ii) Ascomycetes
(C) Basidiospores (iii) Basidiomycetes
(D) Zygospores (iv) Phycomycetes
questions.explanation: Zoospores and Zygospores are characteristic of Phycomycetes, Conidia are in Ascomycetes, and Basidiospores are in Basidiomycetes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.3.4 (Kingdom Fungi)

questions.question:
Match the following bacterial types with their metabolic strategy:
(A) Photoautotrophs (i) Use chemical energy
(B) Chemoautotrophs (ii) Use light energy
(C) Heterotrophs (iii) Decomposers
(D) Cyanobacteria (iv) Photosynthetic autotrophs
questions.explanation: Photoautotrophs use light, Chemoautotrophs use chemicals, Heterotrophs (most bacteria) are decomposers, and Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.1 (Kingdom Monera)

questions.question:
Match the following classifications by historical scientists:
(A) Two-kingdom (i) R.H. Whittaker
(B) Five-kingdom (ii) Carl Woese
(C) Three-domain (iii) Carolus Linnaeus
(D) Artificial system (iv) Carolus Linnaeus
questions.explanation: Linnaeus proposed the two-kingdom system, Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom, and Carl Woese proposed the three-domain system.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Introduction and Section 2.1

questions.question:
Match the following terms with their definitions in context of Fungi:
(A) Mycelium (i) Hyphal network
(B) Coenocytic (ii) Multinucleate hyphae
(C) Septate (iii) Cross-walls present
(D) Dikaryotic (iv) Two nuclei per cell
questions.explanation: Mycelium is a network of hyphae, coenocytic is multinucleate, septate has cross-walls, and dikaryotic refers to (n+n) stage.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 2, Section 2.3 (Kingdom Fungi)

questions.question: Arrange the following groups of fungi in the correct sequence of their mycelium type, starting from the most primitive to the most advanced in terms of septation and branching:
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate and coenocytic mycelium, while Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes have branched and septate mycelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: General characteristics of Fungi, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of steps in the sexual cycle of fungi?
questions.explanation: The sexual cycle of fungi involves the fusion of protoplasms (plasmogamy), fusion of two nuclei (karyogamy), and meiosis in zygote resulting in haploid spores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Reproduction in Fungi section, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of events in the life cycle of a virus starting from infection to release:
questions.explanation: Viruses follow a standard cycle: they attach to a host, inject genetic material, synthesize viral components, assemble them (maturation), and release progeny via lysis.
questions.ncertEvidence: Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens section, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: In the classification of Kingdom Plantae, what is the correct sequence of complexity starting from the simplest to the most complex body structure?
questions.explanation: The evolutionary trend in plants moves from thalloid structures (Algae) to land plants with vascular tissues (Pteridophytes) and finally seed-bearing plants (Gymnosperms and Angiosperms).
questions.ncertEvidence: Kingdom Plantae section, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of the life cycle of a slime mould (Myxomycetes) during unfavorable conditions in the correct sequence:
options: Aggregation -> Plasmodium formation -> Fruiting body -> Spores
Spores -> Fruiting body -> Plasmodium formation -> Aggregation
Plasmodium formation -> Aggregation -> Spores -> Fruiting body
Aggregation -> Spores -> Fruiting body -> Plasmodium formation
questions.explanation: Under unsuitable conditions, slime moulds aggregate to form a plasmodium which differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.
questions.ncertEvidence: Slime Moulds section, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the increasing order of complexity in the organization of genetic material in the following organisms?
questions.explanation: Viroids contain only free RNA, viruses contain RNA or DNA with a protein coat, bacteria are prokaryotic cells, and eukaryotes have complex membrane-bound organelles and chromatin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Viruses, Viroids, Prions section, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.

questions.question: Arrange the following taxonomic categories as described in Whittaker's system for the Kingdom Protista, moving from the most diverse to the least diverse group:
options: Chrysophytes -> Dinoflagellates -> Euglenoids -> Slime Moulds -> Protozoans
Protozoans -> Slime Moulds -> Euglenoids -> Dinoflagellates -> Chrysophytes
Chrysophytes -> Euglenoids -> Dinoflagellates -> Protozoans -> Slime Moulds
Slime Moulds -> Protozoans -> Chrysophytes -> Dinoflagellates -> Euglenoids
questions.explanation: The order reflects the diversity of photosynthetic vs. heterotrophic life forms as traditionally presented in the NCERT classification sequence.
questions.ncertEvidence: Kingdom Protista, Chapter 2, Biological Classification.
