questions.question: Which of the following criteria was NOT used by R.H. Whittaker for his five-kingdom classification system?
questions.explanation: Whittaker's classification was based on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships was not the primary basis, though it is the foundation of modern taxonomy, he explicitly used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships as stated in NCERT.
questions.ncertEvidence: The main criteria for classification used by him include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.question: Identify the group of organisms that are referred to as the 'chief producers' in the oceans.
questions.explanation: Chrysophytes, which include diatoms and golden algae, are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.
questions.ncertEvidence: Diatoms are the chief ‘producers’ in the oceans.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the cell wall of diatoms?
options: It forms two thin overlapping shells
The walls are embedded with silica
questions.explanation: The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. They are not composed of cellulose.
questions.ncertEvidence: In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible.

questions.question: Which protist is responsible for the 'red tides' in the sea?
questions.explanation: Red dinoflagellates like Gonyaulax undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides).
questions.ncertEvidence: Red dinoflagellates (e.g., Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides).

questions.question: What is the unique feature of the pellicle found in Euglenoids?
options: It is a protein-rich layer that makes the body flexible
It is made of chitinous plates
It is a thick cellulose wall
questions.explanation: Instead of a cell wall, euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
questions.ncertEvidence: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: In which group of fungi are the sex organs absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells?
questions.explanation: In Basidiomycetes, sex organs are absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sex organs are absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about Viroids?
options: They have free RNA without a protein coat
They have a protein coat without genetic material
questions.explanation: Viroids were discovered to be a new infectious agent that was smaller than viruses and it was a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat.
questions.ncertEvidence: It was found to be a free RNA; it lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses.

questions.question: What is the nature of the association between algae and fungi in lichens?
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations, i.e., mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lichens are symbiotic associations i.e. mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding Mycoplasma?
options: They completely lack a cell wall
They are the smallest living cells known
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates the cell wall composition of Chrysophytes and Dinoflagellates?
options: Chrysophytes have silica-embedded walls, while Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates.
Chrysophytes possess cellulose walls, while Dinoflagellates possess silica shells.
Both groups lack a cell wall and are covered by a protein-rich pellicle.
Chrysophytes have flagellated cell walls, while Dinoflagellates have cilia-based walls.
questions.explanation: Chrysophytes (diatoms) have cell walls forming two thin overlapping shells that fit together like a soap box, embedded with silica. Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.2.1 and 2.2.2

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker, which criterion is primarily responsible for separating Fungi from Plantae?
questions.explanation: While both are eukaryotic, Plantae are autotrophic (photosynthetic), whereas Fungi are heterotrophic (saprophytic/parasitic), which is a primary criterion for Whittaker's classification.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.1

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is unique to the Kingdom Protista compared to other eukaryotic kingdoms?
options: It includes organisms that primarily link plants, animals, and fungi.
It consists solely of multicellular organisms.
It lacks a defined nucleus in all its members.
It is restricted to organisms that exclusively reproduce sexually.
questions.explanation: Protista acts as a 'catch-all' kingdom that serves as a link with the others (plants, animals, and fungi), being primarily aquatic and eukaryotic.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.2

questions.question: Why are Mycoplasma considered the smallest living cells and why do they cause difficulty in antibiotic treatment?
options: They lack a cell wall and are insensitive to cell-wall targeting antibiotics.
They possess a thick peptidoglycan layer that prevents drug entry.
They are obligate parasites that hide within host nuclei.
They form complex endospores that are resistant to all forms of heat.
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. Many antibiotics (like penicillin) target cell wall synthesis, making Mycoplasma naturally resistant to them.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.1.4

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the genetic material and reproduction in Viroids?
options: They consist of free RNA without a protein coat and replicate by hijacking host machinery.
They contain double-stranded DNA enclosed in a protein capsid.
They are composed of infectious proteins that lack any nucleic acid.
They are large viruses that require a helper virus to replicate.
questions.explanation: Viroids were discovered to be free RNA, lacking the protein coat that is found in viruses. They are smaller than viruses.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.5

questions.question: Methanogens are found in the gut of ruminant animals. Which of the following is their correct taxonomic placement?
questions.explanation: Methanogens belong to the Archaebacteria group, which are known for living in extremely harsh habitats including the gut of ruminants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.1.1

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the vegetative body of a Slime Mould and a Fungi?
options: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists with a plasmodium, while fungi are filamentous.
Slime moulds are autotrophic, while fungi are always heterotrophic.
Slime moulds lack cell walls during the vegetative phase, while fungi always have chitinous walls.
Slime moulds are strictly parasitic, while fungi are strictly decomposers.
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium, whereas fungi are typically filamentous structures (hyphae).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.2.3

questions.question: Which of the following pigments is NOT found in Euglenoids?
questions.explanation: Euglenoids have pigments identical to those present in higher plants (Chlorophyll a and b, and carotenoids). Phycobilins are characteristic of cyanobacteria and red algae.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.2.4

questions.question: In the context of bacterial reproduction, what is the significance of the 'transformation' process?
options: It is a method of sexual reproduction involving DNA uptake from the environment.
It is a binary fission process producing genetically identical daughter cells.
It describes the formation of endospores under unfavorable conditions.
It is the process by which bacteria create flagella for motility.
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission, but under unfavorable conditions, they produce spores. They also adopt a primitive type of DNA transfer (sexual reproduction) which includes transformation, conjugation, and transduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.1.3

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the role of Lichens as pollution indicators?
options: They do not grow in polluted areas, especially those with sulfur dioxide.
They proliferate rapidly in areas with high heavy metal contamination.
They serve as biological filters that absorb all atmospheric pollutants.
They convert toxic carbon monoxide into oxygen in urban environments.
questions.explanation: Lichens are very good pollution indicators; they do not grow in polluted areas, particularly where sulfur dioxide levels are high.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 2, Section 2.6

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the kingdom Monera according to the Whittaker system of classification?
options: Presence of naked DNA not enclosed by nuclear envelope
questions.explanation: Monerans are prokaryotic, meaning they lack a defined nucleus and their genetic material is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane.
questions.ncertEvidence: The bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms. Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape.

questions.question: Identify the group of organisms that are responsible for the production of biogas in the gut of several ruminant animals.
questions.explanation: Methanogens are archaebacteria present in the gut of ruminant animals (cows and buffaloes) and are responsible for the production of methane (biogas).
questions.ncertEvidence: Methanogens are present in the gut of several ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes and they are responsible for the production of methane (biogas) from the dung of these animals.

questions.question: In the context of Chrysophytes, which of the following statements is correct?
options: They are microscopic and float passively in water currents.
They have a cell wall made of chitin.
questions.explanation: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton).
questions.ncertEvidence: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton).

questions.question: Which pigment is present in Euglenoids that is similar to that of higher plants?
questions.explanation: Euglenoids have pigments identical to those present in higher plants, specifically chlorophyll a.
questions.ncertEvidence: Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms. Interestingly, the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic feature of the cell wall in Fungi, excluding Oomycetes?
questions.explanation: With the exception of yeasts (unicellular), fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae. The cell wall of fungi is composed of chitin and polysaccharides.
questions.ncertEvidence: With the exception of yeasts which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae. The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

questions.question: Which of the following classes of Fungi is known as 'sac-fungi'?
questions.explanation: Ascomycetes are commonly known as the sac-fungi because their spores (ascospores) are produced endogenously in sac-like asci.
questions.ncertEvidence: The members of Ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous. They are also known as sac-fungi.

questions.question: Which group of fungi is commonly known as 'imperfect fungi' because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known?
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are often called imperfect fungi because once sexual stages of members of these fungi were discovered, they were moved into classes they rightly belong to.
questions.ncertEvidence: Commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known. When the sexual forms of these fungi were discovered they were moved into classes they rightly belong to.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Viruses is correct?
options: Viruses possess their own metabolic machinery.
Viruses can be grown in artificial culture media.
Viruses contain both DNA and RNA.
questions.explanation: Viruses are non-cellular organisms that are characterized by having an inert crystalline structure outside the living cell. They are obligate parasites and lack metabolic machinery.
questions.ncertEvidence: All of us who have suffered the ill effects of common cold or ‘flu’ know what effects viruses can have on us, even if we do not associate it with our condition. Viruses did not find a place in classification since they are not truly ‘living’. The viruses are non-cellular organisms that are characterised by having an inert crystalline structure outside the living cell.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symbiotic association between algae and fungi?
questions.explanation: Lichens are symbiotic associations, i.e., mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lichens are symbiotic associations, i.e., mutually useful associations, between algae and fungi. The algal component is known as phycobiont and fungal component as mycobiont, which are autotrophic and heterotrophic, respectively.

questions.question: If a researcher discovers a unicellular organism with a rigid cell wall composed of chitin and a nuclear membrane, how would it be classified according to the Five Kingdom classification?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Fungi consists of heterotrophic organisms with cell walls made of chitin. Since it has a nuclear membrane, it is eukaryotic, ruling out Monera.
questions.ncertEvidence: Kingdom Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms with cell walls made of chitin.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of Cyanobacteria necessitates their classification under Kingdom Monera despite their photosynthetic nature?
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs but are prokaryotic, which is the defining characteristic of Kingdom Monera.
questions.ncertEvidence: The bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are prokaryotic.

questions.question: A specific group of organisms thrives in extremely salty areas. Based on the classification of bacteria, which cell wall feature distinguishes them from other bacteria?
questions.explanation: Halophiles belong to Archaebacteria. Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria because they lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls.
questions.ncertEvidence: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.

questions.question: In the context of the Five Kingdom system, why are Chlamydomonas and Chlorella placed in Kingdom Protista rather than Kingdom Plantae, despite containing chlorophyll?
questions.explanation: In the Five Kingdom classification, unicellular eukaryotic organisms like Chlamydomonas and Chlorella were moved to Protista, while they were placed in Algae (Plantae) in earlier systems.
questions.ncertEvidence: Kingdom Protista has brought together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella (earlier placed in Algae within Plants) with Paramecium and Amoeba (which were earlier placed in the animal kingdom).

questions.question: Which feature of the Mycoplasma makes them resistant to antibiotics like penicillin?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. Penicillin acts by inhibiting cell wall synthesis; thus, they are naturally resistant.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. Many mycoplasma are pathogenic in animals and plants.

questions.question: Dinoflagellates are often referred to as 'fire algae'. Which structural arrangement explains their characteristic movement?
options: Two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse
Two flagella at the anterior end
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellates have two flagella; one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.
questions.ncertEvidence: Most of them have two flagella; one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.

questions.question: Slime moulds are described as 'saprophytic protists'. Under what conditions do they form an aggregation called plasmodium?
questions.explanation: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.
questions.ncertEvidence: Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of the Euglenoids that allows them to survive in both aquatic and terrestrial-like nutrient conditions?
questions.explanation: Euglenoids are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight but behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms in the absence of sunlight.
questions.ncertEvidence: When deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.

questions.question: Why are viruses excluded from the Five Kingdom classification system?
options: They are too large to be classified
questions.explanation: Viruses are not truly 'living' in the sense that they are non-cellular organisms that are characterized by having an inert crystalline structure outside the living cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The viruses, viroids, prions and lichens are not mentioned in the Five Kingdom classification. Viruses are non-cellular organisms.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the genetic material of Viroids and Viruses?
options: Viroids have RNA without a protein coat
Viroids have DNA with a protein coat
Viroids have larger genomes than viruses
Viroids are only found in animals
questions.explanation: Viroids possess free RNA of low molecular weight and lack the protein coat that is found in viruses.
questions.ncertEvidence: It was found to be a free RNA. It lacked the protein coat that is found in viruses, hence the name viroid.

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system proposed by R.H. Whittaker, which of the following criteria was NOT used?
questions.explanation: Whittaker used cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships as criteria. However, phylogenetic relationships were not the primary basis compared to the others in his initial criteria list, though it is often considered an outcome of the system.
questions.ncertEvidence: The main criteria for classification used by him include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.

questions.question: Which group of organisms is considered the most abundant in nature and serves as the sole members of Kingdom Monera?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera and are the most abundant micro-organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera. They are the most abundant micro-organisms.

questions.question: Identify the characteristic feature of Chrysophytes from the following options:
questions.explanation: Chrysophytes (diatoms and golden algae) have cell walls that form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together like a soap box, and these walls are embedded with silica.
questions.ncertEvidence: In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms are known as 'chief producers' in the oceans?
questions.explanation: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans due to their massive numbers and photosynthetic capability.
questions.ncertEvidence: Diatoms are the chief ‘producers’ in the oceans.

questions.question: Red tides in the sea are caused by the rapid multiplication of:
questions.explanation: Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red.
questions.ncertEvidence: Red dinoflagellates (e.g., Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Euglenoids is correct?
options: They possess a protein-rich layer called pellicle
They have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose
questions.explanation: Instead of a cell wall, Euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
questions.ncertEvidence: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: The saprophytic protists that aggregate to form an aggregation called plasmodium under suitable conditions are:
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.
questions.ncertEvidence: The slime moulds are saprophytic protists. Under suitable conditions, they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.

questions.question: Which group of protozoans moves and captures prey by putting out pseudopodia?
questions.explanation: Amoeboid protozoans move and capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet), as in Amoeba.
questions.ncertEvidence: These organisms move and capture their prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet) as in Amoeba.

questions.question: The infectious spore stage is a characteristic of which group of protozoans?
questions.explanation: Sporozoans include diverse organisms that have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle. The most notorious is Plasmodium.
questions.ncertEvidence: This includes diverse organisms that have an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Kingdom Fungi?
questions.explanation: Fungi have cell walls composed of chitin, not cellulose. Cellulose is characteristic of plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: With the exception of yeasts—unicellular fungi—fungi are filamentous. Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae... The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

questions.question: In which of the following groups of plants do the gametophytes have an independent, free-living existence?
questions.explanation: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, the gametophyte phase is independent and free-living, whereas in gymnosperms and angiosperms, the gametophytes are dependent on the sporophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: In bryophytes and pteridophytes, the gametophyte has an independent, free-living existence, whereas in gymnosperms and angiosperms, the gametophyte is dependent on the sporophyte.

questions.question: Which of the following algae produces large amounts of hydrocolloids (algin and carrageen)?
questions.explanation: Brown algae (phaeophyceae) produce algin, and red algae (rhodophyceae) produce carrageen. Both are examples of hydrocolloids.
questions.ncertEvidence: Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae).

questions.question: The gemmae produced by liverworts are:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds that develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.

questions.question: In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is a:
options: Sporophyte, differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves
Gametophyte, differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves
Sporophyte, which is thalloid and lacks vascular tissues
Gametophyte, which is saprophytic or autotrophic
questions.explanation: The main plant body of pteridophytes is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem, and leaves, and these organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: The main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves. These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered an important step in evolution towards seed habit?
questions.explanation: The development of two kinds of spores (heterospory) in Pteridophytes like Selaginella and Salvinia is a precursor to the seed habit.
questions.ncertEvidence: The development of the zygotes into young embryos take place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit considered an important step in evolution.

questions.question: Gymnosperms are referred to as 'naked-seeded' plants because:
options: The ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall
The seeds are not covered by a fruit wall
They do not produce female gametophytes
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.

questions.question: Which of the following features is common to all gymnosperms?
options: Presence of endosperm formed after fertilization
questions.explanation: Naked seeds are the defining feature of gymnosperms. Double fertilization is a characteristic of angiosperms, and xylem vessels are generally absent in gymnosperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.

questions.question: In the life cycle of an angiosperm, the double fertilization involves:
questions.explanation: Double fertilization consists of syngamy (fusion of male gamete with egg) and triple fusion (fusion of male gamete with two polar nuclei).
questions.ncertEvidence: Each embryo sac has a three-celled egg apparatus – one egg cell and two synergids, three antipodal cells and two polar nuclei. The two polar nuclei eventually fuse to produce a diploid secondary nucleus. One of the male gametes fuses with the egg cell... (syngamy). The other male gamete fuses with the diploid secondary nucleus to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) (triple fusion).

questions.question: Which group of plants exhibits a haplodiplontic life cycle?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes and Pteridophytes show an intermediate condition called haplodiplontic life cycle, where both phases are multicellular.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bryophytes and pteridophytes, interestingly, exhibit an intermediate condition (haplodiplontic): both phases are multicellular and free-living.

questions.question: The embryo sac of an angiosperm is formed inside the:
questions.explanation: The female gametophyte or embryo sac is formed inside the ovule, which is protected by the ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: The female gametophyte or embryo sac is formed inside the ovule.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the life cycle of algae is correct?
options: In Volvox, the life cycle pattern is haplontic.
In Fucus, the life cycle pattern is diplontic.
In Ectocarpus, the life cycle pattern is haplodiplontic.
questions.explanation: According to NCERT, Volvox and Spirogyra represent a haplontic life cycle, Fucus represents a diplontic life cycle, and Ectocarpus and Polysiphonia represent a haplodiplontic life cycle.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1: Life Cycles and Alternation of Generations.

questions.question: In Bryophytes, the main plant body is a gametophyte. Which of the following features is NOT associated with the gametophyte stage?
options: Production of haploid gametes by mitosis.
The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition.
The sporophyte is free-living and independent.
The zygote undergoes reduction division to form haploid spores.
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the sporophyte is not free-living; it is attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.2: Bryophytes.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Pteridophytes and identify the correct one:
options: They are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem).
The main plant body is the gametophyte.
The prothallus is the dominant, photosynthetic, vascular stage.
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues. The main plant body is a sporophyte, and most are homosporous.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes.

questions.question: In Gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the:
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on sporophytes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.4: Gymnosperms.

questions.question: Which of the following algae produces both algin and carrageen?
options: None of the options; they are produced by different groups.
questions.explanation: Algin is produced by brown algae (Phaeophyceae), while carrageen is produced by red algae (Rhodophyceae).
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1: Algae.

questions.question: The gemmae in Marchantia are:
options: Sexual reproductive structures found in the sporophyte.
Structures that produce spores after meiosis.
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1: Liverworts.

questions.question: In Angiosperms, the process of double fertilization involves:
options: Fusion of two male gametes with one egg cell.
questions.explanation: Double fertilization in angiosperms involves syngamy (fusion of male gamete with egg) and triple fusion (fusion of second male gamete with two polar nuclei).
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.5: Angiosperms.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of Phaeophyceae?
options: Chlorophyll a, b, and starch as reserve food.
questions.explanation: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) possess chlorophyll a, c, and carotenoids like fucoxanthin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Table 3.1: Divisions of Algae.

questions.question: Heterospory and seed habit are considered important steps in evolution. These are predominantly observed in:
questions.explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia are Pteridophytes that exhibit heterospory, which is a precursor to the seed habit.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Pinus is correct?
options: The leaves are not adapted to withstand extreme temperatures.
questions.explanation: Pinus is monoecious (male and female cones on the same tree), whereas Cycas is dioecious.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom, Chapter 3, Section 3.4: Gymnosperms.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the life cycle of plants:
I. In haplontic life cycle, the sporophytic generation is represented only by the one-celled zygote.
II. Diplontic life cycle is characteristic of all seed-bearing plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms).
III. Haplodiplontic life cycle is exhibited by bryophytes and pteridophytes.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three statements are consistent with NCERT descriptions of plant life cycles. Volvox, Spirogyra, and some Chlamydomonas exhibit haplontic life cycles. Gymnosperms and angiosperms are diplontic. Bryophytes and pteridophytes show an intermediate condition (haplodiplontic).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.6: Plant Life Cycles and Alternation of Generations.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of features is characteristic of the class Phaeophyceae?
options: Presence of chlorophyll a, c, and fucoxanthin; storage food as mannitol or laminarin.
Presence of chlorophyll a, d, and phycoerythrin; storage food as floridean starch.
Presence of chlorophyll a, b, and starch as reserve food.
Presence of chlorophyll a, c, and carrageen in the cell wall.
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae (brown algae) contain chlorophyll a, c, and carotenoids/fucoxanthin. Their stored food is complex carbohydrates, usually laminarin or mannitol.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.2: Phaeophyceae.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding Bryophytes:
options: The main plant body is sporophytic, which is free-living and independent.
They are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction.
They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks.
The zygote does not undergo reduction division immediately.
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the main plant body is a haploid gametophyte, not a sporophyte. The sporophyte is multicellular and attached to the gametophyte for nutrition.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2: Bryophytes.

questions.question: In Pteridophytes, the spores germinate to give rise to:
options: Prothallus, which is small but multicellular and free-living.
Protonema, which is a creeping, green, branched filamentous stage.
Sporophyte, which is the dominant independent phase.
Gametophyte, which is dependent on the sporophyte for nutrition.
questions.explanation: The spores in pteridophytes germinate to form prothallus, which is a small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Gymnosperms is accurate?
options: The male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
They produce fruits, but the seeds are naked.
The roots are always tap roots, and the stem is always unbranched.
They possess vessels as the primary water-conducting elements in xylem.
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are heterosporous. The male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes; they do not have independent free-living existence.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.4: Gymnosperms.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Algae:
I. Chlamydomonas, Volvox, and Ulothrix are examples of green algae.
II. Mannitol is the stored food in Rhodophyceae.
III. Agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria.
IV. Biflagellate zoospores are present in brown algae.
Select the correct option.
options: I, III and IV are correct
I, II and III are correct
II, III and IV are correct
questions.explanation: Statement II is incorrect because mannitol is the stored food in Phaeophyceae, whereas Rhodophyceae store floridean starch.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2: Algae (Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae).

questions.question: Which of the following features is NOT found in Angiosperms?
options: Double fertilization involving syngamy and triple fusion.
Presence of seeds enclosed within fruits.
Ovules are naked and not enclosed by an ovary wall.
Pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialized structures called flowers.
questions.explanation: In angiosperms, the ovules are enclosed by the ovary wall. The condition where ovules are naked is a characteristic of Gymnosperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.5: Angiosperms.

questions.question: The 'dominant' phase in the life cycle of a Moss (Funaria) is:
options: The gametophyte, which consists of protonema and leafy stages.
The sporophyte, which is the only stage capable of photosynthesis.
The zygote, which is the only diploid stage.
The capsule, which produces spores by mitosis.
questions.explanation: The gametophyte of a moss consists of two stages: the protonema stage (developing from the spore) and the leafy stage. This is the dominant phase.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1: Mosses.

questions.question: Which of the following is a heterosporous pteridophyte?
questions.explanation: Salvinia and Selaginella are examples of heterosporous pteridophytes, meaning they produce two kinds of spores, macro and micro.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes.

questions.question: In the life cycle of Polysiphonia, which type of life cycle is observed?
questions.explanation: Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, and Kelps exhibit a haplodiplontic life cycle, where both phases are multicellular.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.6: Plant Life Cycles.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In Bryophytes, the zygote does not undergo reduction division immediately. Reason (R): Bryophytes produce a multicellular sporophyte which is attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the zygote does not undergo reduction division immediately; it produces a multicellular body called a sporophyte, which is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2: Bryophytes

questions.question: Assertion (A): Pteridophytes are considered the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues. Reason (R): The main plant body in Pteridophytes is a gametophyte which is independent.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are indeed the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). However, the main plant body of a pteridophyte is a sporophyte, not a gametophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes

questions.question: Assertion (A): Gymnosperms are heterosporous. Reason (R): Gymnosperms produce two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores within microsporangia and megasporangia respectively.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.4: Gymnosperms

questions.question: Assertion (A): The male sex organ in Chara is called nucule. Reason (R): Nucule is a multicellular and jacketed sex organ.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: In Chara, the male sex organ is the antheridium (globule) and the female sex organ is the oogonium (nucule). Nucule is the female organ.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.1: Algae

questions.question: Assertion (A): In angiosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. Reason (R): They remain within the tissues of the sporophyte.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: In angiosperms, the male and female gametophytes are highly reduced and do not have an independent free-living existence; they remain within the retained spores on the sporophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.5: Angiosperms

questions.question: Assertion (A): Red algae differ from brown algae in the absence of chlorophyll 'c'. Reason (R): Brown algae contain chlorophyll 'a', 'c' and fucoxanthin.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) contain chlorophyll 'a' and 'd' and phycoerythrin. Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) contain chlorophyll 'a', 'c' and fucoxanthin. While (A) and (R) are correct, (R) describes the pigment composition of brown algae but does not explain the absence of 'c' in red algae.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Table 3.1

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sporophyte of a moss is more elaborate than that of a liverwort. Reason (R): The moss sporophyte consists of a foot, seta, and capsule.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. It consists of a foot, seta, and capsule.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.2: Mosses

questions.question: Assertion (A): Diplontic life cycle is shown by all seed-bearing plants. Reason (R): In this cycle, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms and Angiosperms (seed-bearing plants) follow a diplontic life cycle where the diploid sporophyte is the dominant phase.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.6: Plant Life Cycles and Alternation of Generations

questions.question: Assertion (A): Selaginella and Salvinia are homosporous pteridophytes. Reason (R): They produce only one type of spores.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous, meaning they produce two kinds of spores: microspores and megaspores.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.3: Pteridophytes

questions.question: Assertion (A): The gemmae in Marchantia are green, multicellular, asexual buds. Reason (R): Gemmae develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds that develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli in liverworts like Marchantia.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 3, Section 3.2.1: Liverworts

questions.question: Match the following algae classes with their characteristic pigment compositions: A) Chlorophyceae, B) Phaeophyceae, C) Rhodophyceae. 1) Chlorophyll a, c and Fucoxanthin, 2) Chlorophyll a, b, 3) Chlorophyll a, d and Phycoerythrin.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae contains Chl a and b; Phaeophyceae contains Chl a, c and Fucoxanthin; Rhodophyceae contains Chl a, d and r-phycoerythrin.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.2 Algae.

questions.question: Match the following Bryophytes with their structural characteristics: A) Marchantia, B) Funaria, C) Sphagnum. 1) Thalloid plant body with gemmae, 2) Gametophyte differentiated into protonema and leafy stage, 3) Used as fuel and peat.
questions.explanation: Marchantia is a liverwort with a thalloid body; Funaria is a moss with protonema and leafy stages; Sphagnum provides peat used as fuel.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.3 Bryophytes.

questions.question: Match the following Pteridophyte classes with their examples: A) Psilopsida, B) Lycopsida, C) Sphenopsida, D) Pteropsida. 1) Equisetum, 2) Selaginella, 3) Psilotum, 4) Pteris.
questions.explanation: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum), Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.4 Pteridophytes.

questions.question: Match the plant group with its dominant phase and reproductive structures: A) Algae, B) Bryophytes, C) Pteridophytes, D) Gymnosperms. 1) Sporophyte dominant, 2) Gametophyte dominant, 3) Haplo-diplontic cycle, 4) Independent sporophyte.
questions.explanation: Algae are mainly haplontic (haplo-diplontic in some); Bryophytes are gametophyte dominant; Pteridophytes have a dominant independent sporophyte; Gymnosperms have a dominant sporophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.6 Plant Life Cycles and Alternation of Generations.

questions.question: Match the following Gymnosperm features with their respective descriptions: A) Coralloid roots, B) Mycorrhiza, C) Unbranched stem, D) Branched stem. 1) Pinus, 2) Cycas, 3) Cedrus, 4) Cycas (associated with N2 fixing cyanobacteria).
questions.explanation: Cycas has coralloid roots and unbranched stems; Pinus has mycorrhizal roots and branched stems; Cedrus has branched stems.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.5 Gymnosperms.

questions.question: Match the stored food products with the algae class: A) Floridean starch, B) Mannitol, C) Starch. 1) Phaeophyceae, 2) Rhodophyceae, 3) Chlorophyceae.
questions.explanation: Floridean starch is stored in Rhodophyceae, Mannitol in Phaeophyceae, and Starch in Chlorophyceae.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, Table 3.1.

questions.question: Match the following botanical terms with their specific descriptions: A) Protonema, B) Prothallus, C) Syngamy. 1) Gametophytic stage of Pteridophyte, 2) Creeping green filamentous stage of moss, 3) Fusion of gametes.
questions.explanation: Protonema is the juvenile stage of mosses; Prothallus is the gametophyte of pteridophytes; Syngamy is the fusion of male and female gametes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, sections 3.3 and 3.4.

questions.question: Match the algae with their commercial products: A) Gelidium, B) Algin, C) Carrageen. 1) Brown algae, 2) Red algae (Agar), 3) Red algae.
questions.explanation: Agar is obtained from Gelidium/Gracilaria; Algin is from brown algae; Carrageen is from red algae.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.2.

questions.question: Match the flagellar arrangement with the class of algae: A) 2-8, equal, apical, B) 2, unequal, lateral, C) Absent. 1) Rhodophyceae, 2) Chlorophyceae, 3) Phaeophyceae.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyceae have 2-8 equal apical flagella; Phaeophyceae have 2 unequal lateral flagella; Rhodophyceae lack flagella.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, Table 3.1.

questions.question: Match the following terms related to Angiosperms: A) Synergids, B) Antipodals, C) Secondary nucleus. 1) Diploid, 2) Haploid (part of egg apparatus), 3) Haploid (at chalazal end).
questions.explanation: Synergids are haploid (egg apparatus); Antipodals are haploid (chalazal end); Secondary nucleus is diploid (fusion of two polar nuclei).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 3: Plant Kingdom, section 3.5 Angiosperms.

questions.question: Arrange the following plant groups in the correct order of their increasing complexity of the plant body and reproductive structures as per NCERT classification:
questions.explanation: NCERT classifies plants based on increasing complexity from simple thalloid structures in algae to complex vascular and seed-bearing structures in angiosperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom classification (Chapter 3, Introduction)

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of the life cycle stages in a typical moss (Funaria):
options: Spore -> Protonema -> Leafy stage -> Gametes -> Zygote -> Sporophyte
Spore -> Leafy stage -> Protonema -> Gametes -> Zygote -> Sporophyte
Zygote -> Spore -> Protonema -> Leafy stage -> Gametes -> Sporophyte
Protonema -> Spore -> Leafy stage -> Gametes -> Zygote -> Sporophyte
questions.explanation: In mosses, the spore germinates to form the filamentous protonema, which develops into the leafy stage, eventually producing gametes that fuse to form the zygote, developing into a sporophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bryophytes: Mosses life cycle description (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Arrange the following structures found in Pinus in the sequence of their development within the male cone:
options: Microsporophyll -> Microsporangia -> Microspore mother cell -> Microspores
Microspore mother cell -> Microsporangia -> Microsporophyll -> Microspores
Microsporophyll -> Microspore mother cell -> Microsporangia -> Microspores
Microsporangia -> Microsporophyll -> Microspores -> Microspore mother cell
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, microsporangia are borne on microsporophylls, which contain the microspore mother cells that undergo meiosis to produce microspores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gymnosperms: Reproduction section (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Arrange the following events in the life cycle of Pteridophytes in the correct chronological order:
options: Spore germination -> Prothallus formation -> Gamete fusion -> Zygote -> Sporophyte
Zygote -> Spore germination -> Prothallus formation -> Gamete fusion -> Sporophyte
Prothallus formation -> Spore germination -> Sporophyte -> Zygote -> Gamete fusion
Spore germination -> Sporophyte -> Prothallus formation -> Zygote -> Gamete fusion
questions.explanation: Pteridophyte spores germinate to produce a multicellular, free-living, photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte called prothallus, which bears sex organs for fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: Pteridophytes: Life cycle stages (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Sequence the following anatomical structures from the outer surface to the innermost part of a typical Angiosperm ovule:
options: Integument -> Nucellus -> Embryo sac -> Egg cell
Nucellus -> Integument -> Embryo sac -> Egg cell
Embryo sac -> Integument -> Nucellus -> Egg cell
Integument -> Embryo sac -> Nucellus -> Egg cell
questions.explanation: The ovule is protected by integuments, surrounding the nucellus, which contains the embryo sac, inside which the egg cell is located.
questions.ncertEvidence: Angiosperms: Double Fertilization and Ovule structure (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Arrange the following groups based on the increasing degree of reduction in the gametophyte generation:
questions.explanation: Evolutionary trend shows a progressive reduction in the size and complexity of the gametophyte relative to the sporophyte from algae to angiosperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom: Alternation of Generations (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of the life cycle in Volvox (Haplontic cycle) in the correct order:
options: Zygote -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Mitosis -> Gametes -> Fertilization
Gametes -> Fertilization -> Zygote -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Mitosis
Spores -> Mitosis -> Zygote -> Meiosis -> Gametes -> Fertilization
Meiosis -> Zygote -> Gametes -> Fertilization -> Spores -> Mitosis
questions.explanation: In a haplontic life cycle, the zygote is the only diploid stage; it undergoes meiosis to produce haploid spores, which undergo mitosis to form the gametophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom: Alternation of Generations (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Sequence the events of sexual reproduction in Polysiphonia (Red Algae):
questions.explanation: Red algae exhibit oogamous reproduction resulting in a zygote that develops into a carposporophyte, which produces carpospores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Algae: Rhodophyceae characteristics (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Arrange the following plant parts in order of their evolution from primitive to most derived:
options: Thallus -> Root-like structures -> Vascular tissue -> Naked seeds -> Flowers
Flowers -> Naked seeds -> Vascular tissue -> Root-like structures -> Thallus
Thallus -> Vascular tissue -> Root-like structures -> Naked seeds -> Flowers
Vascular tissue -> Thallus -> Root-like structures -> Flowers -> Naked seeds
questions.explanation: The evolutionary sequence follows the progression from simple non-vascular thalloid forms to vascular plants, seed-bearing plants, and finally flowering plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plant Kingdom: Introduction/Classification (Chapter 3)

questions.question: Sequence the following terms related to the life cycle of Kelps (Diplontic/Haplodiplontic type):
options: Sporophyte -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Gametophyte -> Gametes -> Zygote
Gametophyte -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Sporophyte -> Gametes -> Zygote
Zygote -> Sporophyte -> Gametes -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Gametophyte
Sporophyte -> Gametes -> Zygote -> Meiosis -> Spores -> Gametophyte
questions.explanation: In Kelps, the diploid sporophyte undergoes meiosis to produce haploid spores, which develop into the gametophyte; the gametophyte produces gametes that fuse to form a zygote.
questions.ncertEvidence: Algae: Phaeophyceae life cycle (Chapter 3)

questions.question: In a diagram of a Funaria gametophyte, if label 'A' points to the leafy axis and label 'B' points to the multicellular, branched rhizoids, which of the following is the correct functional identification?
options: A is the sporophyte generation and B is the haploid root-like structure.
A is the gametophyte bearing sex organs and B is for anchorage.
A is the protonema stage and B is the mature gametophore.
A is the diploid phase and B is the haploid vegetative part.
questions.explanation: In mosses (Funaria), the gametophyte consists of two stages: the protonema and the leafy stage. The leafy stage bears sex organs and has multicellular, branched rhizoids for anchorage.
questions.ncertEvidence: The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. They consist of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. They are attached to the soil through multicellular and branched rhizoids.

questions.question: In the diagram of a Liverwort (Marchantia), label 'X' points to the gemma cup. What is the biological significance of the structures contained within these cups?
options: They are sexual spores involved in fertilization.
They are specialized haploid buds for asexual reproduction.
They are diploid structures that undergo meiosis.
They are photosynthetic structures that produce seeds.
questions.explanation: Gemma cups are characteristic of Marchantia. They contain gemmae, which are green, multicellular, asexual buds that detach from the parent body to form new individuals.
questions.ncertEvidence: Marchantia plant body is thalloid... Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.

questions.question: If a diagram depicts the life cycle of a Pteridophyte (e.g., Dryopteris), and label 'Y' points to the prothallus, which statement correctly describes this structure?
options: It is a multicellular, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid gametophyte.
It is the dominant diploid phase that produces spores.
It is a vascularized structure that develops into the sporophyte.
It is a dependent structure found inside the strobilus.
questions.explanation: The prothallus in pteridophytes is the small, inconspicuous, multicellular, independent, photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte.
questions.ncertEvidence: The pteridophytes produce spores... The spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus.

questions.question: In a diagram of a Selaginella strobilus, label 'Z' points to the heterosporous condition. Which observation confirms this?
options: Presence of only microspores in the entire cone.
Presence of only megaspores in the entire cone.
Presence of both microspores and megaspores.
Presence of seeds within the strobilus.
questions.explanation: Selaginella is heterosporous, producing two kinds of spores: macro (mega) spores and microspores, which are found in the strobilus.
questions.ncertEvidence: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, are known as heterosporous.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the life cycle of a Gymnosperm (Pinus), label 'A' represents the male cone and label 'B' represents the female cone. Which of the following is true regarding these structures?
options: A and B are borne on the same tree (monoecious).
A and B are always borne on different trees (dioecious).
A produces seeds directly while B produces pollen.
A is the diploid gametophyte and B is the haploid sporophyte.
questions.explanation: Pinus is monoecious, meaning both male and female cones are borne on the same tree.
questions.ncertEvidence: The male and female cones or strobili may be borne on the same tree (Pinus).

questions.question: In a diagram of an Alga (e.g., Fucus), if label 'P' points to the air bladder and label 'Q' points to the holdfast, what is the role of Q?
options: It absorbs nutrients from the surrounding water.
It attaches the plant body to the substratum.
It is the site for photosynthesis.
It is the reproductive organ for gamete release.
questions.explanation: In brown algae like Fucus, the holdfast is the structure that attaches the thallus to the substratum.
questions.ncertEvidence: The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf like photosynthetic organ the frond.

questions.question: In a schematic diagram of the life cycle of Fucus, which phase is dominant?
options: The life cycle is entirely independent of meiosis.
questions.explanation: Fucus is a brown alga that exhibits a diplontic life cycle, where the diploid sporophyte is the dominant phase.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Fucus, an alga, the life cycle is diplontic.

questions.question: In a diagram of a fern prothallus, labels 'Antheridium' and 'Archegonium' are present. Where are these sex organs typically located?
options: On the margins of the leaf.
questions.explanation: In the prothallus of pteridophytes, the sex organs (antheridia and archegonia) are usually located on the ventral surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia, respectively. They require water for fertilization.

questions.question: In a diagram of Chlamydomonas, if label 'C' points to the pyrenoid, what is its function?
questions.explanation: Pyrenoids are storage bodies found in the chloroplasts of algae like Chlamydomonas; they contain protein besides starch.
questions.ncertEvidence: Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch.

questions.question: In a diagram of an Angiosperm embryo sac, label 'S' points to the synergids. What is their primary function?
options: To guide the pollen tube into the egg cell.
To provide nourishment to the zygote.
questions.explanation: The synergids are part of the egg apparatus in the embryo sac and assist in guiding the pollen tube into the egg cell during fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: Inside the embryo sac, the egg apparatus consists of two synergids and one egg cell. The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus, which play an important role in guiding the pollen tubes into the synergid.

questions.question: In the diagram of the life cycle of a Pteridophyte (like Selaginella), which stage is represented by the dominant, independent, photosynthetic phase?
questions.explanation: In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem, root, stem and leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: The main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.

questions.question: A diagram shows a heterosporous condition in a plant. Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the structures represented?
questions.explanation: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, are known as heterosporous.
questions.ncertEvidence: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, are known as heterosporous.

questions.question: Observe the diagram of a Funaria plant. Which structure is responsible for the anchoring and absorption of water and minerals?
questions.explanation: In mosses like Funaria, the gametophyte is the dominant phase, possessing leaf-like, stem-like structures and root-like structures called rhizoids.
questions.ncertEvidence: They possess root-like, leaf-like and stem-like structures.

questions.question: In a diagram of the life cycle of Fucus, which structure is depicted as the site of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Fucus is a brown alga which is diploid; meiosis occurs during the formation of gametes in the conceptacles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Life cycle of Fucus is diplontic.

questions.question: In the diagram of a Liverwort (Marchantia), what is the function of the structures labeled 'gemmae'?
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.

questions.question: Considering a diagram of a gymnosperm seed, which part represents the integumented megasporangium?
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: In gymnosperms, the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization.

questions.question: If a diagram depicts the Haplodiplontic life cycle of Ectocarpus, which phase is multicellular and photosynthetic?
questions.explanation: Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia and kelps are haplodiplontic; both phases are multicellular and often free-living.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia and kelps are haplodiplontic; both phases are multicellular and often free-living.

questions.question: In a diagram of a Volvox colony, what are the small, daughter colonies labeled inside the parent colony called?
questions.explanation: Volvox is a colonial alga, and asexual reproduction occurs via the formation of daughter colonies within the parent colony.
questions.ncertEvidence: Volvox forms colonies.

questions.question: In a diagram of a Pteridophyte prothallus, where are the sex organs located?
questions.explanation: The prothallus in pteridophytes bears both male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia, typically on the ventral surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: The prothallus bears male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia.

questions.question: Which of the following structures in the diagram of a moss capsule is specialized for spore dispersal?
questions.explanation: The capsule in mosses contains spores, and the peristome teeth facilitate the gradual dispersal of spores.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll a and c, and stores food in the form of laminarin or mannitol?
questions.explanation: Dictyota is a member of Phaeophyceae (brown algae). Members of Phaeophyceae possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. Their stored food is complex carbohydrates, in the form of laminarin or mannitol.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phaeophyceae members possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol.

questions.question: In the life cycle of the organism 'Funaria', which of the following statements is correct regarding its gametophyte?
options: It is the dominant phase consisting of protonema and leafy stage
It is dependent on the sporophyte for nutrition
questions.explanation: Funaria is a moss. The gametophyte of mosses consists of two stages: the protonema stage and the leafy stage. This phase is independent and represents the dominant stage in the life cycle of bryophytes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage... The second stage is the leafy stage.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms produces gemmae for asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Marchantia is a liverwort. Liverworts reproduce asexually by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialized structures called gemmae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae.

questions.question: Identify the organism that exhibits diplontic life cycle where the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant.
questions.explanation: Fucus is an alga that shows a diplontic life cycle. In this type of life cycle, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant.
questions.ncertEvidence: In diplontic life cycle, the diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to few-celled haploid gametophyte. This kind of life cycle is termed as diplontic. An alga, Fucus, represents this pattern.

questions.question: Which of the following features is specifically associated with the genus Cycas?
questions.explanation: Cycas is a gymnosperm characterized by unbranched stems. Pinus and Cedrus have branched stems. Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem (except Gnetales).
questions.ncertEvidence: The stems are unbranched (Cycas) or branched (Pinus, Cedrus).

questions.question: In the life cycle of Polysiphonia, which type of life cycle pattern is observed?
questions.explanation: Polysiphonia is a red alga (Rhodophyceae) that exhibits a haplodiplontic life cycle, which is intermediate between haplontic and diplontic.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia, kelps are haplodiplontic.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a member of the class Pteropsida?
questions.explanation: Pteris belongs to the class Pteropsida. Psilotum belongs to Psilopsida, Lycopodium to Lycopsida, and Selaginella to Lycopsida.
questions.ncertEvidence: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is known for its ability to hold water and is used as packing material for trans-shipment of living material?
questions.explanation: Sphagnum, a moss, provides peat that has long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water.
questions.ncertEvidence: Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that has long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water.

questions.question: Which of the following algae is commonly known as 'pond silk'?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga that feels slippery to the touch, often referred to as pond silk or water silk.
questions.ncertEvidence: Spirogyra is a filamentous form of green algae.

questions.question: In the life cycle of Funaria, where does the reduction division (meiosis) take place to produce haploid spores?
questions.explanation: The sporophyte in mosses consists of foot, seta, and capsule. Meiosis occurs inside the capsule to produce haploid spores.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis.

questions.question: Which structure in Cycas is responsible for the fixation of nitrogen through a symbiotic association with cyanobacteria?
questions.explanation: In Cycas, specialized roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some Cycas small specialized roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.

questions.question: The gemmae, which are asexual buds involved in vegetative propagation in Marchantia, are located in:
options: The apical notch of the protonema
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.

questions.question: In Pteridophytes, the sporangia are produced in compact structures called strobili or cones. Which of the following plants exhibit this arrangement?
questions.explanation: The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases like Selaginella and Equisetum, sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum).

questions.question: What is the primary function of the mucilaginous sheath found in Volvox and other colonial green algae?
questions.explanation: The cell wall of green algae like Volvox consists of an inner cellulose layer and outer pectose layer, often surrounded by a mucilaginous sheath which provides protection and helps in colonial cohesion/buoyancy.
questions.ncertEvidence: The plant body of green algae is more or less like other plants. The cell wall usually has a rigid inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

questions.question: In Polysiphonia (a red alga), what is the function of the accessory pigments like phycoerythrin?
options: To absorb light in deep water and impart red color
To store starch in the form of floridean starch
To act as a structural component of the cell wall
To facilitate the movement of flagellated gametes
questions.explanation: Red algae contain the pigment r-phycoerythrin, which allows them to carry out photosynthesis at depths where other algae cannot survive.
questions.ncertEvidence: The red algae are so called because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body.

questions.question: Where are the male and female cones borne in Pinus?
options: Only on the apex of the main trunk
questions.explanation: Pinus is monoecious, meaning male and female cones are borne on the same tree.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gymnosperms are heterosporous... Pinus (male and female cones/strobili are borne on the same tree).

questions.question: In the life cycle of brown algae (e.g., Fucus), where are the photosynthetic pigments located?
questions.explanation: Brown algae possess chlorophyll a, c, and carotenoids and xanthophylls (fucoxanthin) housed within chloroplasts.
questions.ncertEvidence: They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them.

questions.question: The 'prothallus' in Pteridophytes is a structure that serves which of the following functions?
options: It bears the sex organs (antheridia and archegonia)
It produces spores for asexual reproduction
It anchors the plant to the soil
It provides mechanical support to the sporophyte
questions.explanation: The prothallus is the gametophyte of pteridophytes, which is small but multicellular, free-living, photosynthetic, and bears sex organs.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia.

questions.question: Which part of the Funaria plant acts as the primary site for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The gametophyte is the dominant phase in mosses and consists of two stages: protonema and the leafy stage. The leafy stage bears sex organs and is photosynthetic.
questions.ncertEvidence: The leafy stage consists of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. These bear the sex organs.

questions.question: In the life cycle of Pteridophytes, what is the primary structural role of the prothallus?
options: To bear the sex organs, antheridia and archegonia
To act as the dominant photosynthetic plant body
To provide nourishment to the developing sporophyte embryo
To facilitate long-distance dispersal of seeds
questions.explanation: The prothallus in pteridophytes is a small, multicellular, free-living, photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte that bears the sex organs (antheridia and archegonia).
questions.ncertEvidence: In pteridophytes, the gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia.

questions.question: Which specific structural feature of the Bryophyte sporophyte allows it to remain attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte?
options: A foot for anchorage and nutrient absorption
A vascular strand for xylem transport
questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it via a structure called the foot.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.

questions.question: What is the functional significance of the 'coralloid roots' found in Cycas?
options: Storage of water in arid habitats
Exchange of gases in waterlogged conditions
questions.explanation: In Cycas, specialized roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Cycas, specialized roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.

questions.question: The gemmae in Marchantia are specialized structures. What is their primary function?
options: Asexual reproduction via fragmentation and dispersal
Absorption of minerals from the soil
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli. When detached, they germinate to form new individuals.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals.

questions.question: How do the leaves of Gymnosperms structurally adapt to withstand extreme environmental conditions?
options: Needle-like shape with thick cuticle and sunken stomata
Broad, thin laminae for maximum light interception
Succulent stems with reduced leaf surface area
Absence of vascular tissue to prevent water loss
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms, the leaf structural adaptations such as needle-like leaves, thick cuticle, and sunken stomata help to reduce water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: In gymnosperms, the leaves are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. In conifers, needle-like leaves reduce the surface area.

questions.question: What is the structural basis for the 'heterosporous' condition observed in Selaginella and Salvinia?
options: Production of two kinds of spores: microspores and megaspores
Development of both male and female sex organs on one thallus
Presence of both vascular and non-vascular tissues
Ability to reproduce both sexually and vegetatively
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes like Selaginella and Salvinia, which produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, are known as heterosporous.
questions.ncertEvidence: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (mega) and microspores, are known as heterosporous.

questions.question: Which structural component in the life cycle of Angiosperms is responsible for the formation of the endosperm?
options: Double fertilization involving one male gamete and the polar nuclei
Fusion of two male gametes with the egg cell
Development of a zygote without fertilization
Fusion of the embryo sac with the ovary wall
questions.explanation: In angiosperms, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote (syngamy), and the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).
questions.ncertEvidence: The other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

questions.question: What is the functional role of the 'pyrenoids' located within the chloroplasts of green algae like Spirogyra?
questions.explanation: Most members of Chlorophyceae have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch.
