questions.ncertEvidence: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The majority of the pteridophytes are homosporous.

questions.question: Coralloid roots are associated with which of the following gymnosperms?
questions.explanation: In Cycas, small specialized roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Cycas, small specialised roots called coralloid roots are associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as the 'amphibian of the plant kingdom'?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction.

questions.question: Which of the following phyla is characterized by the presence of a water vascular system and radial symmetry in the adult stage?
questions.explanation: Echinoderms possess an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and a unique water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Echinodermata section.

questions.question: Which specific cells are responsible for the water transport system in Porifera?
questions.explanation: Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum. This pathway is maintained by flagellated cells called choanocytes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Porifera section.

questions.question: Flame cells are the specialized excretory structures found in which of the following phyla?
questions.explanation: In Platyhelminthes, specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Platyhelminthes section.

questions.question: True coelom is defined as a body cavity which is lined by:
questions.explanation: Coelom is the body cavity which is lined by mesoderm. Animals possessing this are called coelomates.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Basis of Classification section.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms exhibits the phenomenon of bioluminescence?
questions.explanation: Bioluminescence (the property of a living organism to emit light) is well-marked in Ctenophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Ctenophora section.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the class Chondrichthyes?
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes are cartilaginous fishes that possess placoid scales, ventral mouth, and lack an operculum.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Class Chondrichthyes section.

questions.question: Metamerism is a characteristic feature observed in:
questions.explanation: In Annelida, the body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres and, hence, the name Annelida.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Annelida section.

questions.question: Which of the following respiratory structures is found in Arachnids?
questions.explanation: In Phylum Arthropoda, respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs, or the tracheal system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Arthropoda section.

questions.question: The mantle cavity is a characteristic feature of which phylum?
questions.explanation: In Molluscs, the space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which gills are present.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Phylum Mollusca section.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of Class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk-producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom, Class Mammalia section.

questions.question: Which of the following phyla is characterized by the presence of a water vascular system, which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration?
questions.explanation: The water vascular system is a unique feature of the phylum Echinodermata, assisting in locomotion and physiological processes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Echinodermata: The most distinctive feature is the presence of water vascular system which helps in the locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.

questions.question: In which of the following organisms is the notochord present only in the larval tail?
questions.explanation: Ascidia belongs to Urochordata (Tunicata), where the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Urochordata, notochord is present only in larval tail.

questions.question: Consider the following features: (i) Organ-system level of organization, (ii) Bilateral symmetry, (iii) True coelomates with metamerism. Which phylum exhibits these characteristics?
questions.explanation: Annelids exhibit organ-system level of organization, bilateral symmetry, and are true coelomate animals with metameric segmentation.
questions.ncertEvidence: They exhibit organ-system level of body organisation... They are bilaterally symmetrical... They are true coelomate animals and metamerically segmented.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Cnidarians is incorrect?
options: They exhibit only the medusa form.
They are aquatic, mostly marine, sessile or free-swimming.
They exhibit tissue level of organization.
Cnidoblasts are used for anchorage, defense, and capture of prey.
questions.explanation: Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms: polyp and medusa. Some exhibit metagenesis (alternation of generation).
questions.ncertEvidence: Cnidaria exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the phylum Ctenophora?
options: Presence of eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
questions.explanation: Ctenophores, commonly known as sea walnuts or comb jellies, bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.

questions.question: Which of the following animals possesses a rasping organ for feeding called radula?
questions.explanation: Molluscs have a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula, except in some bivalves.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Mollusca, the mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Identify the phylum that is exclusively marine, triploblastic, and exhibits radial symmetry in the adult stage.
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are exclusively marine, triploblastic, and coelomate. Adults exhibit radial symmetry, while larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.
questions.ncertEvidence: All echinoderms are marine... Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: Which class of Chordata is characterized by the presence of a pneumatic bone and a crop and gizzard in the digestive tract?
questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) have long bones which are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic) and possess a digestive tract with additional chambers, the crop and gizzard.
questions.ncertEvidence: The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers, the crop and gizzard... long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Aschelminthes is correct?
options: They are often referred to as roundworms due to their circular cross-section.
They possess a well-developed muscular system.
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes are called roundworms because their body appears circular in cross-section. They are pseudocoelomates, not acoelomates.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section, hence, the name roundworms.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is responsible for excretion in Platyhelminthes?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells in Platyhelminthes that help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Specialised cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Porifera:

III. They are hermaphrodites.

questions.explanation: Sponges exhibit intracellular digestion, have a skeleton of spicules or spongin fibres, and are hermaphrodites (eggs and sperm produced by the same individual).
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Porifera: Digestion is intracellular. Skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres. Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite).

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is common to both Cnidaria and Ctenophora?
questions.explanation: Both phyla exhibit tissue level of organization. Cnidoblasts are unique to Cnidaria, comb plates are unique to Ctenophora, and while Cnidaria are mostly marine, they include freshwater forms like Hydra.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Cnidaria and Phylum Ctenophora: Both exhibit tissue level of organization.

questions.question: In Platyhelminthes, identify the correct match for the specialized cells and their function:
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells in Platyhelminthes that help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Platyhelminthes: Specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Aschelminthes is incorrect?
options: Alimentary canal is incomplete with a well-developed muscular pharynx.
Often females are longer than males.
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes have a complete alimentary canal with a well-developed muscular pharynx, not an incomplete one.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Aschelminthes: Alimentary canal is complete with a well-developed muscular pharynx.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of animals are correctly characterized by their respiratory organs?
options: Prawns: Gills, Scorpion: Book lungs, Insects: Tracheal system
Prawns: Book lungs, Scorpion: Gills, Insects: Tracheal system
Prawns: Tracheal system, Scorpion: Gills, Insects: Book lungs
Prawns: Gills, Scorpion: Tracheal system, Insects: Book lungs
questions.explanation: In Arthropoda, respiratory organs vary: gills in aquatic forms (prawns), book lungs in arachnids (scorpion), and tracheal system in insects.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Arthropoda: Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: The presence of a mantle cavity and a rasping organ called radula is a characteristic feature of:
questions.explanation: Molluscs have a mantle cavity and a file-like rasping organ for feeding called radula.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Mollusca: The space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which gills are present... The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique diagnostic feature of the phylum Echinodermata in its adult stage?
questions.explanation: While they have a water vascular system and calcareous ossicles, their adult stage is uniquely characterized by radial symmetry despite being deuterostomes (bilateral larvae).
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Echinodermata: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question:
Consider the following features of Hemichordata: 
I. Body is cylindrical and composed of anterior proboscis, collar and trunk. 
II. Circulatory system is open type. 
III. Respiration takes place through gills. 
Which of the above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hemichordates possess a body divided into proboscis, collar, and trunk, have an open circulatory system, and respire through gills.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Hemichordata: Body is cylindrical and is composed of an anterior proboscis, a collar and a long trunk... Circulatory system is of open type... Respiration takes place through gills.

questions.question: Which of the following classes is correctly matched with its respective respiratory structure?
options: Amphibia: Lungs and gills, but not skin
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish) have gills that are separate and without operculum (gill cover).
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Chondrichthyes: Gills are separate and without operculum (gill cover).

questions.question: Identify the feature that is common to both Aves and Mammalia:
questions.explanation: Both Aves and Mammals are homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals that maintain a constant body temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Aves and Class Mammalia: Both are homeothermous (warm-blooded) animals.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Sponges exhibit a cellular level of organization. Reason (R): In sponges, cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates and do not form true tissues.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Ctenophores are known as sea walnuts or comb jellies. Reason (R): The body of ctenophores bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.explanation: Ctenophores possess eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion, hence the name comb jellies.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ctenophora: The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.

questions.question: Assertion (A): All chordates possess a post-anal tail at some stage of their life. Reason (R): The presence of a post-anal tail is one of the fundamental chordate characteristics.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Chordates are characterized by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits, along with a post-anal tail.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chordata: Fundamental characteristics include a post-anal tail.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Members of Platyhelminthes are often called flatworms. Reason (R): They exhibit dorso-ventrally flattened bodies and are mostly endoparasites found in animals including human beings.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes are called flatworms due to their dorso-ventrally flattened body. Most of them are endoparasites.
questions.ncertEvidence: Platyhelminthes: dorso-ventrally flattened body, hence are called flatworms; mostly endoparasites.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry in the adult stage. Reason (R): The larvae of echinoderms are bilaterally symmetrical.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.question: Assertion (A): Birds are homeothermic animals. Reason (R): Birds are able to maintain a constant body temperature regardless of the external environment.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals, like birds and mammals, possess the ability to maintain a constant body temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Aves: They are homeothermous (warm-blooded) animals, i.e., they are able to maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.question: Assertion (A): In Mollusca, the space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity. Reason (R): Feather-like gills are present in the mantle cavity which have respiratory and excretory functions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.ncertEvidence: Mollusca: The space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which feather-like gills are present.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Annelids are the first group of animals to exhibit true segmentation or metamerism. Reason (R): The body surface of annelids is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.ncertEvidence: Annelida: Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cyclostomes are parasites on some fishes. Reason (R): They have a circular and sucking mouth without jaws.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes have a circular and sucking mouth, which facilitates their parasitic mode of life on other fishes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cyclostomata: All living members are ectoparasites on some fishes; they have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Reptiles are poikilothermic animals. Reason (R): Reptiles do not have the ability to regulate their internal body temperature.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Reptiles are cold-blooded (poikilothermic) animals, meaning they cannot maintain a constant internal body temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Reptilia: They are poikilotherms.

questions.question:

questions.question:

B. Book lungs - 2. Prawn

questions.explanation: Prawns respire via gills, scorpions via book lungs, cockroaches via a tracheal system, and flatworms via body surface diffusion.

questions.question:

D. Liver fluke - 4. Miracidium

questions.question:

questions.question:
Match the following chordate classes with their characteristic heart structure:

B. Amphibia - 2. Two-chambered

questions.question:
Match the following animals with their symmetry type:

C. Annelids - 3. Radial symmetry
D. Adult Echinoderms - 4. Radial symmetry
questions.explanation: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical. Ctenophores are radially symmetrical. Annelids are bilaterally symmetrical. Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Animal Kingdom: Basis of classification - Symmetry.

questions.question:
Match the following organisms with their unique diagnostic feature:
A. Taenia - 1. Metamerism
B. Pheretima - 2. Hook and suckers
C. Periplaneta - 3. Chitinous exoskeleton
D. Pila - 4. Calcareous shell
questions.explanation: Taenia (tapeworm) has hooks and suckers, Pheretima (earthworm) shows metamerism, Periplaneta (cockroach) has a chitinous exoskeleton, and Pila (snail) has a calcareous shell.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Animal Kingdom: Diagnostic features of Platyhelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, and Mollusca.

questions.question:

questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes have placoid scales, Osteichthyes have an operculum, Mammals possess mammary glands, and Reptiles have dry, cornified skin.

questions.question:

B. Earthworm - 2. Open circulatory system

questions.question:

questions.question: Arrange the following phyla in the increasing order of their evolutionary complexity based on body organization and symmetry as per NCERT:

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of water transport in the water vascular system of Echinodermata:

Madreporite → Ring canal → Stone canal → Radial canal → Tube feet

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of structures through which air passes during respiration in insects (Cockroach):

questions.question: Arrange the following classes of Chordata in the sequence of their appearance in the geological time scale (earliest to latest):

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of taxonomic hierarchy for the class Mammalia:

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence of excretion in birds:

questions.explanation: Birds are uricotelic. They lack a urinary bladder, and waste travels from kidneys via ureters to the cloaca for excretion.

questions.question: Arrange the following structures of the human eye (analogous to other animal sensory organs) in the sequence light passes through them:

questions.question: Sequence the following events in the life cycle of a liver fluke (Fasciola hepatica):

questions.question: In the diagram of Sycon (a sponge), if 'A' represents the osculum and 'B' represents the spongocoel, what is the primary function of the current generated through these structures?

questions.question: Given the diagram of Aurelia (jellyfish), which label represents the characteristic stinging structures used for defense and prey capture?

questions.question: Identify the structure in the diagram of Nereis (Annelida) that aids in swimming and locomotion.

questions.question: In the diagram of a typical Arthropod, which tagma is associated with the sensory functions and bears the compound eyes?

questions.question: In the diagrammatic representation of Pila (Mollusca), the 'file-like rasping organ' used for feeding is labeled as:

questions.ncertEvidence: The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion.

questions.question: In a diagram of the life cycle of a Fasciola (Liver fluke), the structure 'Y' depicts the presence of a suckers. Which class of Platyhelminthes does this organism belong to and what is the function of the suckers?
questions.explanation: Fasciola (Liver fluke) belongs to class Trematoda. Parasitic flatworms like Fasciola use hooks and suckers to attach themselves to the host.
questions.ncertEvidence: Some of them absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface. Some members like liver fluke possess hooks and suckers.

questions.question: In a diagram comparing the circulatory systems of Phylum Arthropoda and Phylum Mollusca, which structural feature is common to both?
options: Presence of a dorsal heart with lateral ostia
Presence of hemoglobin in blood cells
questions.explanation: Both Arthropoda and Mollusca (with the exception of Cephalopods) exhibit an open type of circulatory system where blood flows in body cavities called sinuses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Circulatory system is of open type in Arthropoda and Mollusca.

questions.question: In a diagram of the respiratory system of a Prawn (Arthropod), the structure labeled 'Z' represents the gills. Which of the following is true regarding respiratory organs in this phylum?
options: Respiration occurs via gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system
Respiration occurs exclusively through the skin
Respiration occurs via lungs located in the mantle cavity
questions.explanation: Arthropods exhibit diverse respiratory organs including gills, book gills, book lungs, or the tracheal system depending on their habitat.
questions.ncertEvidence: Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: In a diagram representing the cross-section of an Aschelminthes (roundworm), why is the body cavity referred to as a 'pseudocoelom'?
options: The body cavity is not lined by mesoderm
The body cavity is completely lined by ectoderm
The body cavity is filled with fluid-filled cells
questions.explanation: In Aschelminthes, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm, hence it is called pseudocoelom.
questions.ncertEvidence: In animals, in which the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom.

questions.question: In the diagram of a Chordate body plan, which of the four fundamental characteristics is correctly identified as a dorsal, hollow, and fluid-filled structure?
questions.explanation: Chordates are characterized by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chordates are animals having a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the excretory organs of a Platyhelminth, the structure labeled 'Flame cell' is highlighted. What is its primary function?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells in Platyhelminthes that help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Specialised cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.question: In a diagram depicting the segmentation in an Annelid, which term correctly describes the repetitive arrangement of body parts?
questions.explanation: Annelids exhibit metameric segmentation, where the body is externally and internally divided into segments or metameres.
questions.ncertEvidence: Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres and, hence, the phylum is named Annelida.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms exhibits a closed circulatory system and possesses parapodia for swimming?
questions.explanation: Nereis is an aquatic annelid that possesses lateral appendages called parapodia which help in swimming and has a closed circulatory system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Annelids like Nereis, an aquatic form, possesses lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming.

questions.question: Which organism is characterized by the presence of a radula for feeding and a calcareous shell, yet belongs to the phylum Mollusca?
questions.explanation: Pila (apple snail) is a mollusc that features a rasping organ for feeding called radula and a calcareous shell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula in molluscs like Pila.

questions.question: Identify the organism that shows radial symmetry in the adult stage but bilateral symmetry in the larval stage, and possesses a water vascular system.
questions.explanation: Asterias (starfish) is an echinoderm showing radial symmetry in adults and bilateral in larvae, with a characteristic water vascular system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical; the most distinctive feature is the presence of water vascular system.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a vertebrate that lacks jaws and belongs to the class Cyclostomata?
questions.explanation: Petromyzon (lamprey) is a jawless vertebrate belonging to the class Cyclostomata.
questions.ncertEvidence: All members of the class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.

questions.question: Which organism is known for having a body supported by a notochord throughout its entire life, extending from head to tail region?
questions.explanation: In Cephalochordates like Branchiostoma, the notochord extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Cephalochordata, notochord extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is a member of Phylum Porifera and possesses a canal system for water transport?
questions.explanation: Spongilla is a freshwater sponge (Porifera) that utilizes a water transport or canal system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Spongilla is a freshwater sponge.

questions.question: Which organism is a Cnidarian that exhibits the 'metagenesis' phenomenon, involving alternation of generations between polyp and medusa forms?
questions.explanation: Obelia exhibits metagenesis where polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae produce polyps sexually.
questions.ncertEvidence: Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

questions.question: Which organism is a flightless bird and is a member of the class Aves?
questions.explanation: Struthio (Ostrich) is a well-known flightless bird belonging to class Aves.
questions.ncertEvidence: Some birds are flightless (e.g., Struthio).

questions.question: Identify the organism that belongs to the phylum Ctenophora and uses eight rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion.
questions.explanation: Ctenoplana is a ctenophore characterized by eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion (e.g., Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana).

questions.question: Which organism is a viviparous mammal that belongs to the order of egg-laying mammals?
questions.explanation: Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) is an oviparous (egg-laying) mammal, not viviparous. The question tests identification of the outlier in the context of mammalian reproduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: Most mammals are viviparous and produce young ones. However, Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) is oviparous.

questions.question: In the phylum Porifera, what is the primary function of the choanocytes and where are they located?
options: Lining the spongocoel and canals; water transport and filtration
Distributed in the mesohyal; digestion of complex proteins
Found in the osculum; regulation of water exit flow
Attached to spicules; structural support for the body wall
questions.explanation: Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals in sponges. They are flagellated cells that create water currents to bring in food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Canal system in Porifera: water enters through ostia into spongocoel and goes out through osculum. This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste. Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals.

questions.question: Cnidoblasts are characteristic of Cnidaria and are primarily utilized for which of the following?
options: Anchorage, defense, and capture of prey
Excretion of nitrogenous wastes and osmoregulation
Digestion of food within the gastrovascular cavity
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) contain nematocysts and are present on the tentacles and the body, used for anchorage, defense, and capture of prey.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic. They have central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Cnidoblasts are used for anchorage, defense and for the capture of prey.

questions.question: Flame cells are specialized excretory structures found in Platyhelminthes. What is their specific role?
options: Circulation of nutrients in the body
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes possess specialized cells called flame cells which help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Platyhelminthes have organ level of organisation. Specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.question: The radula is a file-like rasping organ used for feeding. In which phylum is it found and what is its location?
questions.explanation: Molluscs have a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula, located in the mouth (buccal cavity).
questions.ncertEvidence: The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula in Molluscs.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the water vascular system in Echinoderms and where is the madreporite located?
options: Locomotion, capture/transport of food and respiration; aboral surface
questions.explanation: The water vascular system in Echinoderms is distinctive for locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration. The madreporite is on the aboral surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: An important feature of Echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.

questions.question: Malpighian tubules in Arthropods serve which specific physiological function and where are they situated?
options: Excretion; at the junction of midgut and hindgut
Sensory reception; on the head region
questions.explanation: In insects (a class of Arthropoda), Malpighian tubules are excretory organs located at the junction of the midgut and hindgut.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretion in Arthropods takes place through Malpighian tubules.

questions.question: In which animal group is the proboscis gland located, and what is its function?
questions.explanation: Hemichordates have a rudimentary structure in the collar region called proboscis gland, which acts as an excretory organ.
questions.ncertEvidence: Hemichordates have a rudimentary structure in the collar region called proboscis gland.

questions.question: Parapodia are lateral appendages found in Annelids. What is their primary function?
questions.explanation: Nereis, an aquatic annelid, possesses lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming.
questions.ncertEvidence: Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming.

questions.question: What is the function of the air bladder in Osteichthyes, and where is it located?
options: Regulation of buoyancy; in the body cavity
questions.explanation: In bony fishes (Osteichthyes), an air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Osteichthyes, air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy.

questions.question: The statocyst in invertebrates is an organ of equilibrium. Where is it commonly found?
questions.explanation: Statocysts are sensory organs for balance (equilibrium) found in many invertebrates, such as the antennules of crustaceans.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sensory organs like tentacles, eyes, statocysts (balance organs) are present in Arthropods.

questions.question: Which of the following structures in Phylum Porifera is primarily responsible for creating and maintaining the water current essential for food gathering, respiratory exchange, and removal of waste?
questions.explanation: Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals. The beating of their flagella creates the water current required for all physiological functions in sponges.
questions.ncertEvidence: Water transport or canal system in Porifera.

questions.question: Cnidoblasts are diagnostic features of Phylum Cnidaria. Which of the following is NOT a primary function of these specialized cells?
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts contain nematocysts used for anchorage, defense, and capture of prey. They are not involved in the excretion of nitrogenous waste.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cnidarians exhibit cnidoblasts on the tentacles and the body.

questions.question: Consider the following statement regarding Ctenophora: 'Comb plates are ciliated structures that facilitate locomotion.' How many of these plates are present in a typical ctenophore?
questions.explanation: Ctenophores, commonly known as sea walnuts or comb jellies, possess eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ctenophora body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates.

questions.question: In Platyhelminthes, specialized cells called flame cells are primarily responsible for which physiological process?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells in flatworms that help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Specialised cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes.

questions.question: The presence of a muscular foot is a characteristic feature of Phylum Mollusca. What is the specific function of the 'radula' found in the buccal cavity of these organisms?
questions.explanation: The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula, in molluscs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Which structure in Annelida acts as a hydrostatic skeleton and facilitates locomotion by aiding in muscle contraction?
questions.explanation: In annelids, the fluid-filled coelom acts as a hydrostatic skeleton, which works in conjunction with longitudinal and circular muscles to facilitate locomotion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Annelids possess longitudinal and circular muscles which help in locomotion; aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages, parapodia.

questions.question: Echinoderms possess a unique water vascular system. Which of the following is the primary function of this system?
options: Locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration
Structural support for the body wall
questions.explanation: The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of the water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.

questions.question: In the phylum Arthropoda, the respiratory organs vary significantly based on habitat. Which of the following is NOT a respiratory organ found in this phylum?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are the excretory organs of Platyhelminthes. Arthropods respire through gills, book gills, book lungs, or the tracheal system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Respiratory organs in Arthropoda are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: Which specific structure in Hemichordata is responsible for excretion?
questions.explanation: Hemichordates have a circulatory system of open type and excretion takes place through the proboscis gland.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretory organ is proboscis gland in Hemichordata.

questions.question: In Class Chondrichthyes, the placoid scales are directed backward. What is the primary functional significance of this arrangement?
questions.explanation: Placoid scales are characteristic of cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes). Their backward orientation helps in streamlining the body to reduce drag in water.
questions.ncertEvidence: Skin is tough, containing minute placoid scales in Chondrichthyes.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of water flow in the canal system of Sycon?
questions.explanation: In sponges, water enters through minute pores called ostia into the central cavity spongocoel and goes out through the osculum.
questions.ncertEvidence: Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum.

questions.question: Arrange the following developmental stages of Fasciola hepatica (Liver fluke) in the correct chronological order of their life cycle:
questions.explanation: The life cycle of Fasciola involves multiple larval stages starting from Miracidium which enters the intermediate host, developing into Sporocyst, Redia, Cercaria, and finally the infective Metacercaria.
questions.ncertEvidence: Some members like Liver fluke (Fasciola) live in the host, including human beings. They have life cycles involving many larval stages.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of the passage of food through the digestive tract of a typical Earthworm?
options: Mouth -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Stomach -> Intestine -> Anus
Mouth -> Gizzard -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Intestine -> Anus
Mouth -> Pharynx -> Gizzard -> Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Intestine -> Anus
Mouth -> Oesophagus -> Pharynx -> Gizzard -> Stomach -> Intestine -> Anus
questions.explanation: In Pheretima, the alimentary canal consists of mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, gizzard (for grinding), stomach, intestine, and anus.
questions.ncertEvidence: The alimentary canal is a straight tube and runs from first to last segment of the body. A terminal mouth opens into the buccal cavity (1-3 segments) which leads into muscular pharynx.

questions.question: In the respiratory system of insects like cockroaches, what is the correct sequence of air movement?
questions.explanation: Air enters the body of an insect through spiracles, travels through a network of tracheal tubes, reaches the fine tracheoles, and finally diffuses into the tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cockroach respiratory system consists of a network of trachea, that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles present on the lateral side of the body.

questions.question: Identify the correct order of the life cycle stages in Ascaris lumbricoides within the human host environment:
options: Ingestion of embryonated egg -> Larva in intestine -> Circulation -> Lungs -> Pharynx -> Intestine -> Adult
Ingestion of larva -> Intestine -> Lungs -> Circulation -> Adult
Ingestion of adult -> Intestine -> Pharynx -> Lungs -> Adult
Ingestion of egg -> Pharynx -> Lungs -> Intestine -> Circulation -> Adult
questions.explanation: Ascaris eggs are ingested, hatch in the intestine, larvae migrate through blood circulation to lungs, then move to the pharynx, are swallowed, and mature in the intestine.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ascaris, which is endoparasite found in the intestine of human beings, allows for internal fertilisation and direct or indirect development.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly represents the flow of blood in the circulatory system of a cockroach?
questions.explanation: In cockroach open circulatory system, blood from sinuses enters the heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly through the aorta.
questions.ncertEvidence: The blood from sinuses enter heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to sinuses again.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of anatomical structures encountered by the water vascular system in Echinoderms starting from the intake?
options: Madreporite -> Stone canal -> Ring canal -> Radial canal -> Tube feet
Stone canal -> Madreporite -> Ring canal -> Radial canal -> Tube feet
Madreporite -> Ring canal -> Stone canal -> Radial canal -> Tube feet
Tube feet -> Radial canal -> Ring canal -> Stone canal -> Madreporite
questions.explanation: The water vascular system starts with the madreporite, water flows through the stone canal into the ring canal, then radial canals, and finally the tube feet.
questions.ncertEvidence: An important feature of echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which helps in capture and transport of food, respiration and locomotion.

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of the metamorphosis in a butterfly in the correct order:
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis in insects typically involves the developmental sequence of egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
questions.ncertEvidence: Development may be indirect (larval stages present) or direct. Many insects undergo metamorphosis.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct chronological sequence of the excretory process in a cockroach involving Malpighian tubules?
options: Haemolymph -> Malpighian tubules -> Uric acid formation -> Hindgut -> Rectum -> Excretion
Haemolymph -> Hindgut -> Malpighian tubules -> Uric acid formation -> Rectum -> Excretion
Uric acid formation -> Malpighian tubules -> Haemolymph -> Hindgut -> Excretion
Malpighian tubules -> Haemolymph -> Rectum -> Hindgut -> Excretion
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules absorb nitrogenous waste from haemolymph, convert it to uric acid, pass it into the hindgut, where water is reabsorbed in the rectum before excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut.

questions.question: In the process of alternation of generation in Obelia, choose the correct sequence of life cycle phases:
questions.explanation: Obelia exhibits metagenesis where the sessile polyp form reproduces asexually to produce medusae, and the free-swimming medusa form reproduces sexually to form zygotes that develop into polyps.
questions.ncertEvidence: Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually.

questions.question: In the phylum Porifera, which of the following is an exception to the general rule of body symmetry?
questions.explanation: Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, which is an exception to the general trend of radial or bilateral symmetry seen in other animal phyla.
questions.ncertEvidence: Poriferans are mostly asymmetrical animals.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms represents an exception to the characteristic radial symmetry found in most adult Echinoderms?
questions.explanation: Pinctada belongs to the phylum Mollusca, which exhibits bilateral symmetry, unlike the adult Echinoderms which exhibit radial symmetry.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: Which of the following molluscs is an exception to the general feature of having a shell?
questions.explanation: While most molluscs have a calcareous shell, the class Cephalopoda, specifically the octopus, lacks an external shell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump.

questions.question: Which of the following chordates is an exception to the rule that the notochord is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult stage?
questions.explanation: Petromyzon is a cyclostome where the notochord persists throughout life, unlike other vertebrates where it is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column.
questions.ncertEvidence: In cyclostomes, the notochord is present throughout the life of the animal.

questions.question: Which of the following groups of animals is an exception to the rule of having a closed circulatory system among highly evolved invertebrates?
questions.explanation: Arthropods possess an open circulatory system, whereas most other complex phyla like Annelids and Chordates possess a closed circulatory system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Circulatory system is of open type in Arthropoda.

questions.question: Which of the following birds is an exception to the general characteristic of flight adaptation in the class Aves?
questions.explanation: Struthio (Ostrich) is a flightless bird, serving as an exception to the general avian characteristic of flying.
questions.ncertEvidence: Some birds like ostrich are flightless.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is an exception to the general rule that members of the phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria) exist in two body forms?
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia belongs to Phylum Ctenophora, which lacks the metagenesis/polymorphism characteristic of many Cnidarians.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa.

questions.question: Which of the following mammals is an exception to the defining characteristic of giving birth to young ones (viviparity)?
questions.explanation: Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) is an oviparous (egg-laying) mammal, which is an exception to the general viviparous nature of mammals.
questions.ncertEvidence: Most mammals are viviparous and produce young ones, but some like Ornithorhynchus are oviparous.

questions.question: Which of the following fish is an exception to the general rule that all fish have a bony endoskeleton?
questions.explanation: Trygon (sting ray) belongs to Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes), whereas the others belong to Osteichthyes (bony fishes).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chondrichthyes are cartilaginous fishes, while Osteichthyes are bony fishes.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is an exception to the rule of being triploblastic?
questions.explanation: Hydra belongs to Phylum Coelenterata, which is diploblastic, whereas the other options are triploblastic.
questions.ncertEvidence: Animals in which the developing embryo has a third germinal layer, mesoderm, in between the ectoderm and endoderm are called triploblastic; Coelenterates are diploblastic.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes between the body symmetry of Ctenophora and Cnidaria?
options: Ctenophora exhibits radial symmetry, whereas Cnidaria exhibits biradial symmetry.
Both Ctenophora and Cnidaria exhibit radial symmetry.
Ctenophora exhibits biradial symmetry, whereas Cnidaria exhibits radial symmetry.
Ctenophora exhibits bilateral symmetry, whereas Cnidaria exhibits radial symmetry.
questions.explanation: NCERT classifies both Ctenophora and Cnidaria (Coelenterata) under the radial symmetry category, though ctenophores are often described as biradial in advanced texts, NCERT explicitly states radial symmetry for both.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.3 and 4.2.4.

questions.question: Identify the key difference in the excretory structures of Platyhelminthes and Aschelminthes.
options: Platyhelminthes use flame cells, whereas Aschelminthes use a renette cell or excretory pore.
Platyhelminthes use nephridia, whereas Aschelminthes use flame cells.
Platyhelminthes use malpighian tubules, whereas Aschelminthes use protonephridia.
Platyhelminthes use flame cells, whereas Aschelminthes use nephridia.
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes possess flame cells for osmoregulation and excretion. Aschelminthes possess an excretory tube to remove waste through an excretory pore.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.5 and 4.2.6.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement regarding the respiratory organs of Arthropoda and Mollusca.
options: Arthropods use gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system, while Molluscs use feather-like gills.
Arthropods use lungs, while Molluscs use tracheal systems.
Arthropods use skin, while Molluscs use lungs.
Arthropods use only tracheal systems, while Molluscs use book lungs.
questions.explanation: Arthropods show a diverse respiratory system (gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system), whereas Molluscs typically use feather-like gills for respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.7 and 4.2.8.

questions.question: How do the body cavities of Aschelminthes and Annelida differ?
options: Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, whereas Annelida are true coelomates.
Aschelminthes are acoelomates, whereas Annelida are pseudocoelomates.
Aschelminthes are true coelomates, whereas Annelida are pseudocoelomates.
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates because the mesoderm is present in scattered pouches, whereas Annelids are the first group to possess a true coelom.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.1.3.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the circulatory system status of Arthropoda and Echinodermata?
questions.explanation: Both Arthropoda and Echinodermata (in the adult stage) possess an open type of circulatory system as per the standard NCERT table.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Table 4.1.

questions.question: Distinguish between the skeletal support of Porifera and Cnidaria.
options: Porifera have spicules or spongin fibers, whereas Cnidaria generally lack a formal internal skeleton but may have calcium carbonate in corals.
Porifera have calcium carbonate shells, whereas Cnidaria have spicules.
Porifera have chitinous exoskeletons, whereas Cnidaria have calcareous endoskeletons.
Both rely solely on hydrostatic skeletons.
questions.explanation: Sponges (Porifera) are supported by spicules or spongin fibers. Cnidarians do not have a standard internal skeleton, though corals secrete calcium carbonate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.1 and 4.2.3.

questions.question: Identify the correct distinction between the circulatory systems of Annelida and Arthropoda.
options: Annelida possess a closed circulatory system, while Arthropoda possess an open circulatory system.
Annelida possess an open circulatory system, while Arthropoda possess a closed circulatory system.
questions.explanation: Annelids (like earthworms) are the first to have a closed circulatory system, while Arthropods possess an open circulatory system.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.7 and Table 4.1.

questions.question: Which feature differentiates the nervous system of Ctenophora from Platyhelminthes?
options: Both exhibit a primitive nervous system, but Ctenophora is generally considered to have a more diffuse nerve net compared to the ladder-like system of Platyhelminthes.
Ctenophora have a complex brain, whereas Platyhelminthes lack nervous tissue.
Platyhelminthes have a nerve net, whereas Ctenophora have a ventral nerve cord.
There is no difference between the two.
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes exhibit the first sign of cephalization with a ladder-like nervous system, whereas lower phyla like Ctenophora/Cnidaria possess a diffuse nerve net.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.5.

questions.question: Select the correct difference regarding the habitat of Hemichordata and Chordata.
options: Hemichordata are exclusively marine, whereas Chordata are found in diverse habitats.
Hemichordata are exclusively freshwater, whereas Chordata are marine.
Hemichordata are terrestrial, whereas Chordata are exclusively marine.
questions.explanation: Hemichordates are a small group of worm-like marine animals, whereas Chordates are found in all types of environments.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.2.10.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the segmentation status of Annelida and Arthropoda?
options: Annelida: Metameric segmentation, Arthropoda: Metameric segmentation.
questions.explanation: Both Annelida and Arthropoda exhibit metameric segmentation (metamerism).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 4, Section 4.1.5.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms exhibits radial symmetry in its adult form but bilateral symmetry in its larval stage?
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms like Asterias exhibit radial symmetry, whereas their larvae exhibit bilateral symmetry.
questions.ncertEvidence: Echinoderms: Adults are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: In which phylum is the presence of a 'radula' for feeding a defining characteristic?
questions.explanation: Molluscs possess a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mollusca: They have a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Which of the following classes of Phylum Chordata is characterized by the presence of a pneumatic bone structure?
questions.explanation: Birds (Aves) have endoskeleton fully ossified and long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic).
questions.ncertEvidence: Aves: Endoskeleton is fully ossified (bony) and the long bones are hollow with air cavities are called pneumatic.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is correctly matched with its respective respiratory organ?
questions.explanation: Prawns respire via gills, scorpions via book lungs, and earthworms via moist skin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Various respiratory organs like gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system are used in Arthropods; Earthworms use moist cuticle.

questions.question: The presence of 'Choanocytes' or 'collar cells' is a unique feature of:
questions.explanation: Choanocytes line the spongocoel and the canals in sponges (Porifera).
questions.ncertEvidence: Porifera: The spongocoel and the canals are lined with collar cells or choanocytes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common trait between Annelids and Arthropods?
questions.explanation: Both Annelids and Arthropods exhibit metameric segmentation (body divided into segments).
questions.ncertEvidence: Annelida: Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres; Arthropoda: Body is covered by chitinous exoskeleton.

questions.question: Select the organism that belongs to the subphylum Urochordata.
questions.explanation: Ascidia (also known as Sea squirt) is a member of Urochordata.
questions.ncertEvidence: Urochordata: Notochord is present only in larval tail, e.g., Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum.

questions.question: Which class of vertebrates is noted for having a heart with two chambers, one auricle and one ventricle?
questions.explanation: Fishes, including cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes), possess a two-chambered heart.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chondrichthyes: Heart is two-chambered (one auricle and one ventricle).

questions.question: Cnidoblasts are used by Cnidarians for:
options: Anchorage, defense, and capture of prey
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts contain nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and capture of prey.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cnidaria: Cnidoblasts or cnidocytes are used for anchorage, defense and for the capture of prey.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the phylum Platyhelminthes is correct?
options: They are mostly endoparasites found in animals including human beings
They possess a complete digestive system
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes are acoelomate, bilaterally symmetrical, and are mostly endoparasites.
questions.ncertEvidence: Platyhelminthes: Mostly endoparasites found in animals including human beings.

questions.question: An organism is found to possess a true coelom, metameric segmentation, and a closed circulatory system. Which of the following sets of characteristics would further confirm its placement in Phylum Annelida?
options: Presence of parapodia and chitinous setae for locomotion
Presence of a radula and a muscular foot
Presence of a water vascular system for prey capture
Presence of flame cells for osmoregulation
questions.explanation: Parapodia and setae are diagnostic locomotive structures in Annelids like Nereis. Radula is for Mollusca, water vascular system for Echinodermata, and flame cells for Platyhelminthes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Annelida: Aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic. They possess longitudinal and circular muscles which help in locomotion. Nereis, an aquatic form, possesses lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming.

questions.question: A biologist discovers a marine animal with radial symmetry in the adult stage and bilateral symmetry in the larval stage. Which additional feature would this organism most likely exhibit?
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry, while larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. The water vascular system is a unique diagnostic feature of the phylum Echinodermata.
options: Presence of a water vascular system
Presence of a notochord throughout life
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Echinodermata: All are exclusively marine with organ-system level of organisation. Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. An excretory system is absent. Water vascular system is distinctive feature.

questions.question: If an organism is identified as having a pseudocoelom and is dioecious with internal fertilization, which of the following is most characteristic of its digestive system?
options: Complete alimentary canal with a well-developed muscular pharynx
Incomplete digestive tract with a single opening
Absence of digestive system due to parasitic lifestyle
questions.explanation: Pseudocoelomates (Aschelminthes) possess a complete alimentary canal with a muscular pharynx, distinguishing them from the incomplete digestive systems of Platyhelminthes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Aschelminthes: The alimentary canal is complete with a well-developed muscular pharynx.

questions.question: A student observes an animal under a microscope that lacks a circulatory system, respiratory system, and excretory system. It is multicellular, and its body wall is composed of two layers of cells. To which phylum does this animal most likely belong?
questions.explanation: Cnidarians are diploblastic (two cell layers) and lack specialized systems for circulation, respiration, and excretion, relying on diffusion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Cnidaria: They are aquatic, mostly marine, sessile or free-swimming, radially symmetrical animals. They are diploblastic. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular.

questions.question: Which of the following traits in a chordate specimen indicates that it belongs to the subphylum Vertebrata rather than Urochordata or Cephalochordata?
options: Replacement of notochord by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult
Presence of a dorsal hollow nerve cord
questions.explanation: While all chordates share the four basic features, vertebrates are distinguished by the presence of a vertebral column that replaces the notochord.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Chordata: Vertebrates have a ventral muscular heart with two, three or four chambers. Kidneys for excretion and osmoregulation. Paired appendages which may be fins or limbs. Notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.

questions.question: An animal possesses a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages, and breathes through book lungs. This organism belongs to which class?
questions.explanation: Book lungs are specific respiratory organs found in members of the class Arachnida, such as scorpions and spiders, within the phylum Arthropoda.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Arthropoda: Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: Which feature of the Class Chondrichthyes is a significant adaptation for their predatory lifestyle in marine environments?
options: Placoid scales and ventrally located mouth
Presence of an air bladder for buoyancy
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) have placoid scales and a ventral mouth. Air bladders (which regulate buoyancy) are absent, requiring them to swim constantly.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Chondrichthyes: Mouth is located ventrally. Notochord is persistent throughout life. Skin is tough, containing minute placoid scales. Due to the absence of air bladder, they have to swim constantly to avoid sinking.

questions.question: An organism is described as having a mantle cavity, a file-like rasping organ for feeding, and an unsegmented soft body. What is the primary function of the 'radula' in this organism?
questions.explanation: The radula is a file-like rasping organ found in molluscs used specifically for feeding.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Mollusca: The anterior head region has sensory tentacles. The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Which of the following features distinguishes Class Amphibia from Class Reptilia?
options: Amphibians have moist skin without scales, while reptiles have dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales
Amphibians are warm-blooded, while reptiles are cold-blooded
Amphibians undergo internal fertilization, while reptiles undergo external fertilization
Amphibians have a four-chambered heart, while reptiles have a three-chambered heart
questions.explanation: Amphibians lack scales and have moist skin for cutaneous respiration, whereas reptiles possess dry, cornified skin with scales or scutes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Amphibia: Skin is moist (without scales). Class Reptilia: The skin is dry and cornified, having epidermal scales or scutes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic that unites all members of the phylum Platyhelminthes?
options: Presence of a complete digestive tract
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes are commonly known as flatworms because their bodies are dorso-ventrally flattened. They are acoelomate and have an incomplete digestive system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Platyhelminthes: They have dorso-ventrally flattened body, hence are called flatworms. These are mostly endoparasites found in animals including human beings.

questions.question: An organism is found to possess a closed circulatory system, true coelom, and metamerism. Which of the following features would you also expect to find in this organism?
questions.explanation: The description matches Phylum Annelida (e.g., Nereis). Parapodia are lateral appendages found in aquatic annelids like Nereis which help in swimming.
questions.ncertEvidence: Annelids exhibit metamerism, closed circulatory system, and true coelom; Nereis, an aquatic form, possesses lateral appendages, parapodia.

questions.question: If an animal exhibits radial symmetry in its adult form but bilateral symmetry in its larval stage, it must belong to which phylum?
questions.explanation: Echinoderms are unique because they show radial symmetry in adults but bilateral symmetry in larvae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Echinoderms: Adults are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: A student observes an animal with a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages, and an open circulatory system. Which respiratory structure is most likely present in this organism?
questions.explanation: The features describe Phylum Arthropoda. Respiratory organs in arthropods include gills, book gills, book lungs, or tracheal system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Arthropods: Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations of characteristics is exclusively found in Phylum Ctenophora?
questions.explanation: Ctenophores are characterized by eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion and the property of bioluminescence.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ctenophores bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in locomotion. Bioluminescence is well-marked in ctenophores.

questions.question: In the context of chordate evolution, which feature first appeared in the group that also exhibits a post-anal tail and pharyngeal gill slits?
questions.explanation: The fundamental characteristics of Chordata include the presence of a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Chordata animals are fundamentally characterised by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits.

questions.question: An animal possesses a muscular foot, a mantle cavity, and a rasping organ for feeding. Which of the following best describes its circulatory system?
questions.explanation: The features describe a Mollusc (e.g., Pila). Most molluscs have an open circulatory system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Molluscs have a mantle cavity with gills, a file-like rasping organ for feeding called radula, and an open circulatory system.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is characterized by the presence of flame cells used for osmoregulation and excretion?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells for osmoregulation and excretion in Phylum Platyhelminthes. Taenia is a platyhelminth.
questions.ncertEvidence: Platyhelminthes: Specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.question: A vertebrate is identified by its skin which is dry, lacks glands, and possesses scales. This animal belongs to which class?
questions.explanation: Class Reptilia is characterized by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes, and lack of skin glands.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class Reptilia: The skin is dry and cornified, lacking glands (except salt glands in some).

questions.question: Which of the following is a common trait between Aves and Mammals?
questions.explanation: Both Aves and Mammals are homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals capable of maintaining a constant body temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Birds (Aves) and Mammals are homeotherms (warm-blooded) animals, i.e., they are able to maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.question: Which specific trait in the phylum Ctenophora distinguishes it from Cnidarians despite both being diploblastic?
options: Presence of eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
Presence of tissue level of organization
questions.explanation: Ctenophores are characterized by eight external rows of ciliated comb plates which help in locomotion, a feature absent in Cnidarians.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Ctenophora, commonly known as sea walnuts or comb jellies, bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates.

questions.question: In the phylum Platyhelminthes, 'flame cells' are primarily associated with which physiological process?
questions.explanation: Flame cells are specialized cells in Platyhelminthes that function in osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Specialized cells called flame cells help in osmoregulation and excretion in Platyhelminthes.

questions.question: Which of the following organismal features is a defining characteristic of the Phylum Mollusca, distinct from Annelids?
options: Body covered by a calcareous shell and unsegmented
Presence of a mantle cavity for respiration
Complete digestive system with mouth and anus
questions.explanation: Molluscs are unsegmented with a soft body covered by a calcareous shell, whereas Annelids are metamerically segmented.
questions.ncertEvidence: Body is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump; usually covered by a calcareous shell.

questions.question: Which feature of the water vascular system in Echinoderms is fundamentally linked to the capture and transport of food?
questions.explanation: The water vascular system in Echinoderms plays an important role in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: An important feature of echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of animals exhibit radial symmetry in their adult stage?
questions.explanation: Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry, while Coelenterates and Ctenophores exhibit radial symmetry throughout their life cycles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: Which feature is unique to the class Mammalia among all chordates?
options: Presence of hair on the body
questions.explanation: The presence of milk-producing glands (mammary glands) and a muscular diaphragm are unique characteristics of mammals.
questions.ncertEvidence: The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished. They also have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running, climbing, burrowing, swimming or flying.

questions.question: In Hemichordates, the proboscis gland is functionally analogous to which structure in other invertebrates?
questions.explanation: The proboscis gland is the excretory organ found in Hemichordates.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretory organ is proboscis gland.

questions.question: Which of the following respiratory structures is correctly matched with its respective organism group?
questions.explanation: Arthropods like scorpions and spiders use book lungs for respiration, whereas Annelids use moist skin or parapodia, and Molluscs use gills (ctenidia).
questions.ncertEvidence: Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system.

questions.question: The phenomenon of 'metagenesis' is observed in which group of animals?
questions.explanation: Metagenesis refers to the alternation of generation between polyp and medusa forms, seen in Obelia.
questions.ncertEvidence: Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

questions.question: Which characteristic of Class Chondrichthyes is responsible for the protection of the gills?
questions.explanation: In Chondrichthyes, the gill slits are separate and without an operculum (gill cover), making them vulnerable compared to Osteichthyes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gill slits are separate and without operculum (gill cover).

questions.question: Which of the following sets of animals is correctly matched with their respective phylum and level of organization?
questions.explanation: Spongilla (freshwater sponge) belongs to Porifera which exhibits cellular level of organization. Pleurobrachia exhibits tissue level, and Platyhelminthes exhibit organ level, not organ-system level.
questions.ncertEvidence: Porifera exhibit cellular level of organization; Ctenophora exhibit tissue level; Platyhelminthes exhibit organ level.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the phylum Echinodermata.
options: They possess a water vascular system.
Excretory system is well-developed with flame cells.
questions.explanation: Echinoderms lack an excretory system; flame cells are characteristic of Platyhelminthes for osmoregulation and excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Echinoderms have an organ-system level of organization; digestive system is complete; excretory system is absent.

questions.question: Which of the following features is NOT common to both Chordata and Hemichordata?
questions.explanation: Post-anal tail is a diagnostic feature of Chordata but is absent in Hemichordata.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chordates are characterized by presence of notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and paired pharyngeal gill slits, and a post-anal tail.

questions.question: Select the organism that exhibits metamerism and possesses a closed circulatory system.
questions.explanation: Pheretima (earthworm) belongs to Annelida, which is characterized by true metameric segmentation and a closed circulatory system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Annelids exhibit organ-system level of body organization and bilateral symmetry. They are coelomate animals and have a closed circulatory system.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is characterized by the presence of a radula for feeding?
questions.explanation: Radula is a file-like rasping organ for feeding found in most Molluscs including Pila, Dentalium, and Chaetopleura.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mollusca: The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.question: Which of the following is a distinguishing feature of the class Chondrichthyes?
options: Presence of air bladder for buoyancy
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes have placoid scales, ventral mouths, and lack an operculum and air bladder, which are features of Osteichthyes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chondrichthyes: Mouth is located ventrally. Notochord is persistent throughout life. Placoid scales are present.

questions.question: Identify the phylum that is exclusively marine, exhibits bioluminescence, and lacks cnidoblasts.
questions.explanation: Ctenophores (comb jellies) are exclusively marine, bioluminescent, and lack cnidoblasts (which are found in Cnidaria).
questions.ncertEvidence: Phylum Ctenophora: Exclusively marine, radially symmetrical, diploblastic organisms with tissue level of organization. Bioluminescence is well-marked.

questions.question: Which of the following classes of Vertebrata is correctly matched with its respiratory organ?
questions.explanation: Amphibians can respire through lungs, skin, and gills. Cyclostomes use gills for respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: Amphibians: Respiration is by gills, lungs and through skin. The skin is moist (without scales).

questions.question: In which phylum are the animals 'pseudocoelomate'?
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (roundworms) possess a pseudocoelom, whereas Platyhelminthes are acoelomate and Annelida/Arthropoda are eucoelomate.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Aschelminthes, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: Exoskeleton of feathers is a characteristic feature of Aves, not Mammalia.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mammalia: Unique feature is the presence of mammary glands. Skin is unique in possessing hair. External ears or pinnae are present.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of animals correctly represents organisms that exhibit radial symmetry in their adult form but belong to a phylum characterized by bilateral symmetry in larval stages?
questions.explanation: Echinoderms (Asterias, Echinus) exhibit radial symmetry in the adult stage but are bilaterally symmetrical as larvae. Hydra and Aurelia are Cnidarians which are radially symmetrical throughout their life cycle.
questions.ncertEvidence: Echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry in the adult stage, but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the phylum Ctenophora: A) They possess bioluminescence. B) Digestion is both extracellular and intracellular. C) They exhibit indirect development. D) Sexes are separate. Select the option with the correct combination of statements.
questions.explanation: Ctenophores are hermaphrodites (sexes are not separate). Therefore, statement D is incorrect.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ctenophores are hermaphrodite, and reproduction takes place only by sexual means.

questions.question: Which of the following features is shared by both Platyhelminthes and Nemathelminthes (Aschelminthes)?
questions.explanation: Both phyla are triploblastic. Platyhelminthes are acoelomate and have an incomplete digestive system, while Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate and have a complete digestive system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Platyhelminthes and Aschelminthes are triploblastic animals.

questions.question: In which of the following organisms is the notochord replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult?
questions.explanation: All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates. The notochord is replaced by the vertebral column only in subphylum Vertebrata.
questions.ncertEvidence: In vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.

questions.question: Identify the animal that exhibits a closed circulatory system despite lacking a true coelom.
