Root cap, Elongation, Meristematic activity, Maturation
Meristematic activity, Root cap, Elongation, Maturation
questions.explanation: The root apex is covered by the root cap, followed by the region of meristematic activity, then the region of elongation, and finally the region of maturation.
questions.ncertEvidence: The root is covered at the apex by a thimble-like structure called the root cap. A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length. The region of maturation is proximal to the region of elongation.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of development in the formation of a flower from the floral meristem?
options: Shoot apical meristem transforms into floral meristem, floral primordia develop, floral appendages form
Floral appendages form, floral primordia develop, shoot apical meristem transforms
Floral primordia develop, shoot apical meristem transforms, floral appendages form
Shoot apical meristem transforms, floral appendages form, floral primordia develop
questions.explanation: The shoot apical meristem changes to a floral meristem, which then produces floral primordia that eventually develop into floral appendages.
questions.ncertEvidence: During floral development, the shoot apical meristem changes to a floral meristem. Internodes do not elongate and the axis gets condensed. The apex produces different kinds of floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves.

questions.question: In the process of seed germination, identify the correct sequence of events following the absorption of water:
options: Radicle emerges, hypocotyl elongates, plumule emerges
Plumule emerges, hypocotyl elongates, radicle emerges
Hypocotyl elongates, radicle emerges, plumule emerges
Radicle emerges, plumule emerges, hypocotyl elongates
questions.explanation: Upon water absorption, the radicle emerges first to anchor the plant, followed by the elongation of the hypocotyl, and subsequently the plumule.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot seeds, the radicle emerges first, followed by the plumule. Hypocotyl elongation in epigeal germination raises the cotyledons above ground.

questions.question: Arrange the following whorls of a flower in a sequence from the outermost to the innermost part:
questions.explanation: A flower typically has four whorls arranged successively on the thalamus: Calyx (outermost), Corolla, Androecium, and Gynoecium (innermost).
questions.ncertEvidence: A flower has four kinds of whorls arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called thalamus or receptacle. These are calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium.

questions.question: Identify the correct order of developmental stages in the formation of a lateral root starting from the primary root:
options: Pericycle cells divide, primordium forms, pierces cortex, emerges
Cortex cells divide, primordium forms, pierces pericycle, emerges
Endodermis cells divide, primordium forms, pierces pericycle, emerges
Pericycle cells divide, pierces endodermis, primordium forms, emerges
questions.explanation: Lateral roots originate from the pericycle. Cells of the pericycle divide to form the primordium, which then pushes through the cortex and epidermis to emerge.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lateral roots originate from the pericycle. The cells of the pericycle divide and form the root primordium, which pushes through the cortex and epidermis.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of tissue layers in a dicot stem from the periphery towards the center?
options: Epidermis, Hypodermis, Cortex, Endodermis, Pericycle, Vascular bundles
Epidermis, Cortex, Hypodermis, Endodermis, Vascular bundles, Pericycle
Epidermis, Endodermis, Cortex, Hypodermis, Pericycle, Vascular bundles
Epidermis, Hypodermis, Endodermis, Cortex, Vascular bundles, Pericycle
questions.explanation: In a dicot stem, the sequence from outside to inside is Epidermis -> Hypodermis -> Cortex -> Endodermis -> Pericycle -> Vascular bundles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The transverse section of a typical young dicotyledonous stem shows that the epidermis is the outermost protective layer... Cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells... The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis... Next to the endodermis is the pericycle... Vascular bundles are arranged in a ring.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of events in the formation of a typical leaf primordium:
options: Shoot apical meristem initiated, leaf primordia develop, leaf expansion, maturation
Leaf primordia develop, shoot apical meristem initiated, leaf expansion, maturation
Shoot apical meristem initiated, leaf expansion, leaf primordia develop, maturation
Maturation, leaf expansion, leaf primordia develop, shoot apical meristem initiated
questions.explanation: Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order.
questions.ncertEvidence: Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order. They are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Arrange the following developmental steps of a microsporangium in an anther:
options: Archesporial cells, Primary parietal cells, Sporogenous tissue, Microspores
Sporogenous tissue, Primary parietal cells, Archesporial cells, Microspores
Primary parietal cells, Archesporial cells, Sporogenous tissue, Microspores
Microspores, Sporogenous tissue, Primary parietal cells, Archesporial cells
questions.explanation: The archesporial cells divide to form primary parietal cells (outer) and primary sporogenous cells (inner), which eventually lead to microspores.
questions.ncertEvidence: The archesporial cells divide to form primary parietal cells towards the outside and primary sporogenous cells towards the inside. The sporogenous tissue gives rise to microspores.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of fruit development post-fertilization?
options: Ovary enlarges, wall becomes pericarp, ovule becomes seed
Ovule becomes seed, ovary enlarges, wall becomes pericarp
Wall becomes pericarp, ovary enlarges, ovule becomes seed
Ovary enlarges, ovule becomes seed, wall becomes pericarp
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovary matures into the fruit. The ovary wall becomes the pericarp, and the ovules develop into seeds.
questions.ncertEvidence: After fertilisation the ovary develops into fruit. The ovary wall develops into pericarp and the ovules develop into seeds.

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of endosperm development in a typical dicot embryo sequence:
options: Zygote, Proembryo, Globular embryo, Heart-shaped embryo, Mature embryo
Zygote, Heart-shaped embryo, Globular embryo, Proembryo, Mature embryo
Proembryo, Zygote, Globular embryo, Heart-shaped embryo, Mature embryo
Zygote, Globular embryo, Proembryo, Heart-shaped embryo, Mature embryo
questions.explanation: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo, which develops into the globular, heart-shaped, and finally the mature embryo.
questions.ncertEvidence: The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo.

questions.question: In the majority of dicotyledonous plants, the primary root is a taproot. Which of the following plants is an exception where the primary root is short-lived and replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem?
questions.explanation: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system, as seen in wheat.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. Such root systems are observed in the wheat plant.

questions.question: Most leaves in angiosperms are green and perform photosynthesis. In which of the following plants are leaves modified into small, green, spine-like structures to reduce water loss?
questions.explanation: In Australian Acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived. The petioles expand, become green, and synthesize food, while leaves may be modified into spines in some xerophytic conditions, or reduced to prevent transpiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Australian Acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived. The petioles in these plants expand, become green and synthesise food.

questions.question: Stems generally bear buds, which may be terminal or axillary. Which of the following is an exception where the stem is modified into a flattened, fleshy structure containing chlorophyll for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Opuntia has flattened stems (phylloclades) that contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, an adaptation to arid environments.
questions.ncertEvidence: Opuntia, have flattened stem and Euphorbia, have fleshy cylindrical stem. They contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.question: Generally, roots are positively geotropic. Which of the following plants exhibits roots that grow vertically upwards (pneumatophores) to get oxygen for respiration?
questions.explanation: In plants such as Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards to get oxygen for respiration. Such roots are called pneumatophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards to get oxygen for respiration. Such roots are called pneumatophores.

questions.question: In most plants, the flower is actinomorphic (radial symmetry). Which of the following plants is an exception showing zygomorphic (bilateral) symmetry?
questions.explanation: In zygomorphic flowers, the flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane. Examples include pea, Gulmohur, bean, and Cassia.
questions.ncertEvidence: When a flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, the aestivation of the corolla is vexillary. Which of the following describes the arrangement of the petals in this specific exception?
options: One posterior standard, two lateral wings, two anterior keel petals
Five petals overlapping in a circular pattern
All petals fused into a tube
questions.explanation: In vexillary aestivation, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral wings, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Underground stems are usually meant for storage. Which of the following is an exception where the underground stem is modified for perennation and vegetative propagation but is not a rhizome?
questions.explanation: Colocasia is an example of a corm, which is an underground stem modification, whereas ginger and turmeric are rhizomes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, Colocasia are modified to store food in them.

questions.question: Typically, the ovary is superior in hypogynous flowers. Which of the following plants is an exception where the ovary is inferior (epigynous)?
questions.explanation: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, making the ovary inferior, as seen in guava and cucumber.
questions.ncertEvidence: In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary. Hence, the ovary is said to be inferior, e.g., guava and cucumber.

questions.question: Leaves usually arise from the nodes and bear a bud in their axil. Which structure is an exception to the rule that leaves do not bear buds, but the structure itself (a modified leaf) may bear buds?
questions.explanation: In Bryophyllum, adventitious buds arise from the notches present at margins of leaves, which is a method of vegetative propagation.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants such as Bryophyllum, the leaves also help in vegetative reproduction by the formation of adventitious buds at the leaf notches.

questions.question: Most flowers have four whorls. Which of the following is an exception where the floral appendages are not distinguished into distinct calyx and corolla, but are referred to as perianth?
questions.explanation: In the family Liliaceae (e.g., Lily), the calyx and corolla are not distinct, and the whorl is called the perianth.
questions.ncertEvidence: When calyx and corolla are not distinct in a flower, it is termed as perianth, e.g., in lily.

questions.question: In the context of placentation types, what is the primary distinction between 'Free Central' and 'Axile' placentation?
options: Axile has septa, whereas Free Central lacks septa.
Free Central has septa, whereas Axile lacks septa.
Axile is found in unilocular ovaries, whereas Free Central is in multilocular ovaries.
Both have ovules attached to the ovary wall.
questions.explanation: In Axile placentation, the placenta is axial and the ovary is multilocular (e.g., China rose). In Free Central, the ovules are borne on a central axis without septa (e.g., Primrose).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.4 Placentation.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct distinction between 'Epigynous' and 'Hypogynous' flowers regarding the position of the ovary?
options: In epigynous, the ovary is inferior, while in hypogynous, it is superior.
In epigynous, the ovary is superior, while in hypogynous, it is inferior.
Both represent flowers with a half-inferior ovary.
Epigynous flowers have petals inserted below the ovary.
questions.explanation: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position (superior ovary). In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary (inferior ovary).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Parts of a Flower.

questions.question: What is the structural difference between a 'Cyme' and a 'Raceme' type of inflorescence?
options: In a raceme, the main axis continues to grow, whereas in a cyme, the main axis terminates in a flower.
In a cyme, the main axis continues to grow, whereas in a raceme, the main axis terminates in a flower.
Both are types of indefinite inflorescence where the main axis grows indefinitely.
Raceme is a type of definite inflorescence while cyme is indefinite.
questions.explanation: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow. In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower, making it limited in growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.1 Inflorescence.

questions.question: Identify the key difference between 'Staminode' and 'Stamen'.
options: A staminode is a sterile stamen, whereas a stamen is the fertile male reproductive organ.
A stamen is a sterile structure, whereas a staminode is the fertile part of the androecium.
Both terms refer to the same fertile reproductive structure.
Staminodes are found only in gynoecium.
questions.explanation: A stamen consists of a filament and an anther. If a stamen is sterile, it is referred to as a staminode.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Androecium.

questions.question: How do 'Syncarpous' and 'Apocarpous' conditions differ in terms of carpel arrangement?
options: Syncarpous ovaries have fused carpels, while apocarpous ovaries have free carpels.
Apocarpous ovaries have fused carpels, while syncarpous ovaries have free carpels.
Both terms describe the number of ovules present in a locule.
Syncarpous refers to a single carpel, whereas apocarpous refers to multiple ovaries.
questions.explanation: When carpels are fused, it is syncarpous (e.g., mustard and tomato). When carpels are free, it is apocarpous (e.g., lotus and rose).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Gynoecium.

questions.question: Compare 'Epiphyllous' and 'Epipetalous' conditions in flowers.
options: Epiphyllous stamens are attached to the perianth, while epipetalous stamens are attached to petals.
Epipetalous stamens are attached to the perianth, while epiphyllous stamens are attached to petals.
Both terms refer to stamens attached to the gynoecium.
Epiphyllous refers to stamens attached to the sepals.
questions.explanation: When stamens are attached to petals, they are epipetalous. When they are attached to the perianth (tepals), they are epiphyllous.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Androecium.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between 'Pinnately compound' and 'Palmately compound' leaves?
options: In pinnately compound leaves, leaflets are on a common axis (rachis), while in palmately compound leaves, leaflets are attached at a common point (tip of petiole).
In palmately compound leaves, leaflets are on a common axis (rachis), while in pinnately compound leaves, leaflets are attached at a common point (tip of petiole).
Pinnately compound leaves have a single blade, while palmately compound have multiple blades.
Both are terms for simple leaves with deep incisions.
questions.explanation: In a pinnately compound leaf, a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis. In palmately compound leaves, the leaflets are attached at a common point, i.e., at the tip of the petiole.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.3.2 The Leaf.

questions.question: Distinguish between 'Actinomorphic' and 'Zygomorphic' symmetry in flowers.
options: Actinomorphic is radial symmetry, while zygomorphic is bilateral symmetry.
Zygomorphic is radial symmetry, while actinomorphic is bilateral symmetry.
Actinomorphic flowers cannot be divided into two equal halves, while zygomorphic can.
Both describe flowers that lack symmetry (asymmetric).
questions.explanation: When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane, it is actinomorphic (radial). If it can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic (bilateral).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Symmetry.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Epigyny' and 'Perigyny' regarding thalamus involvement?
options: In perigyny, the ovary is half-inferior and the thalamus forms a cup-shaped structure, whereas in epigyny, the ovary is inferior and the thalamus encloses the ovary completely.
In epigyny, the ovary is half-inferior, whereas in perigyny, the ovary is superior.
Both have the ovary at the base of the flower with no thalamus modification.
Perigyny results in a superior ovary.
questions.explanation: In perigyny, the ovary is half-inferior (e.g., plum, rose). In epigyny, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, resulting in an inferior ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.4.3 Parts of a Flower.

questions.question: Differentiate between 'Fibrous root system' and 'Adventitious root system'.
options: Fibrous roots originate from the base of the stem in monocots, whereas adventitious roots originate from parts of the plant other than the radicle.
Adventitious roots originate from the radicle, while fibrous roots originate from the stem.
Both systems originate exclusively from the radicle of the embryo.
Fibrous roots are characteristic of dicot plants.
questions.explanation: In monocots, the primary root is replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem (fibrous). Roots that arise from parts other than the radicle are called adventitious roots.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants, Section 5.1 The Root.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, the aestivation of the standard petal (vexillum) is described as:
questions.explanation: In Fabaceae (papilionaceous flowers), the posterior standard petal overlaps the two lateral wings, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior keel petals. This arrangement is termed imbricate aestivation, specifically a subset known as vexillary.
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, the posterior standard overlaps the two lateral wings which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior keels; this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the root system in mustard plants?
options: Primary root is replaced by a cluster of roots
The primary root persists and continues to grow
Roots arise from the base of the stem
questions.explanation: Mustard plants are dicotyledonous, which characteristically possess a tap root system where the primary root (radicle) persists and elongates to form the primary root.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicotyledonous plants, the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of primary root which grows inside the soil.

questions.question: Identify the correct pairing of the plant and its specific root modification:
questions.explanation: Banyan trees possess prop roots that grow downwards from branches to provide support, which are a type of adventitious root modification.
questions.ncertEvidence: In banyan, the hanging structures that support the tree are called prop roots.

questions.question: The edible part of the banana plant is technically a:
questions.explanation: Banana is classified as a berry because it is a fleshy fruit developed from a superior ovary, lacking a hard endocarp.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fruit is a berry if it develops from a superior or inferior ovary, is fleshy, and has no hard endocarp.

questions.question: In monocotyledonous seeds, the outer covering of the endosperm which separates the embryo is called:
questions.explanation: The outer covering of the endosperm in maize (a monocot) is the proteinaceous aleurone layer.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the seeds of cereals such as maize the seed coat is membranous and generally fused with the fruit wall. The outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a proteinous layer called aleurone layer.

questions.question: Which of the following floral characteristics is typical of the family Solanaceae?
questions.explanation: Solanaceae members generally exhibit actinomorphic symmetry, superior ovaries, and epipetalous stamens.
questions.ncertEvidence: Solanaceae: Flowers actinomorphic, Ovary superior, Stamens epipetalous.

questions.question: Phylloclades are specialized stems found in:
questions.explanation: Phylloclades are flattened or cylindrical green stems modified for photosynthesis in xerophytic plants like Opuntia.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Opuntia, the stem is modified into a flattened green structure called phylloclade.

questions.question: In the floral formula of the family Liliaceae, the perianth is represented as:
questions.explanation: Liliaceae is characterized by a perianth (P) consisting of 3+3 tepals, often united at the base.
questions.ncertEvidence: Liliaceae: Perianth 3+3, often united into tube; valvate aestivation.

questions.question: The placenta is attached to the developing seed near the:
questions.explanation: The hilum is the scar on the seed coat through which the developing seeds were attached to the fruit.
questions.ncertEvidence: The hilum is a scar on the seed coat through which the developing seeds were attached to the fruit.

questions.question: In racemose inflorescence, the floral axis:
questions.explanation: In racemose inflorescence, the main axis continues to grow and flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession.
questions.ncertEvidence: In racemose type of inflorescences the main axis continues to grow, the flowers are borne laterally in an acropetal succession.

questions.question: A student observes a plant where the primary root is replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the base of the stem. Which type of root system is this, and in which plant would you expect to see it?
questions.explanation: In monocotyledonous plants like wheat, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem, forming a fibrous root system.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system, as seen in the wheat plant.

questions.question: If a plant exhibits 'epiphyllous' stamens, where are they attached, and what is the typical floral formula representation for this condition?
options: Attached to the perianth; A attached to P
Attached to the petals; A attached to C
Attached to the ovary; A attached to G
Attached to the sepals; A attached to K
questions.explanation: When stamens are attached to the perianth (tepals), the condition is called epiphyllous, as seen in the lily family (Liliaceae).
questions.ncertEvidence: When stamens are attached to the perianth as in the flowers of lily, they are called epiphyllous.

questions.question: Consider a flower with the following floral formula: Br ⊕ ♂ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2). Which of the following statements regarding this flower is correct?
options: It is a bracteate, actinomorphic, bisexual, gamosepalous, gamopetalous flower with a superior ovary.
It is an ebracteate, zygomorphic, unisexual, polysepalous, polypetalous flower with an inferior ovary.
It is a bracteate, actinomorphic, pistillate, gamosepalous, polypetalous flower with a half-inferior ovary.
It is a bracteate, zygomorphic, staminate, polysepalous, gamopetalous flower with a superior ovary.
questions.explanation: Br stands for bracteate, ⊕ for actinomorphic, ♂ for staminate (male), K(5) for gamosepalous calyx, C(5) for gamopetalous corolla, and G(2) for superior ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the floral formula, Br stands for bracteate, ⊕ for actinomorphic, ♂ for staminate, K for calyx, C for corolla, and G for gynoecium.

questions.question: A plant specimen shows leaves that are modified into tendrils for climbing and stipules modified into spines for defense. Which plant is this?
questions.explanation: In Pea, leaves are modified into tendrils for climbing, while in some species like Acacia, stipules are modified into spines for protection.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants such as peas, leaves are modified into tendrils for climbing, and in some plants such as in Australian Acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived. The petioles in these plants expand, become green, and synthesise food.

questions.question: In a flower, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other floral parts are situated below it. What is this condition, and what is the ovary called?
questions.explanation: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior, e.g., mustard, china rose and brinjal.

questions.question: If you observe a stem that is subterranean and spreads to new niches, forming new plants when older parts die, which type of modification is this?
questions.explanation: Underground stems of some plants like ginger and turmeric spread to new niches and when older parts die, new plants are formed. This is a characteristic feature of a rhizome.
questions.ncertEvidence: Underground stems of some plants such as grass and strawberry, etc., spread to new niches and when older parts die new plants are formed. In plants like ginger and turmeric, rhizome also acts as an organ of perennation.

questions.question: Identify the type of aestivation where margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction.
questions.explanation: In imbricate aestivation, the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction, as seen in Cassia and Gulmohur.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and gulmohur, the aestivation is called imbricate.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of plants represents the correct pairing of the type of placentation found in them?
questions.explanation: Marginal placentation occurs in pea, axile in lemon/china rose, and parietal in mustard/argemone.
questions.ncertEvidence: The placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary (Marginal - Pea). When the placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary, the placenta is said to be axile (Lemon). In parietal placentation, the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary (Mustard).

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, what is the specific arrangement of petals in the corolla known as?
questions.explanation: In Fabaceae, the corolla consists of five petals: a posterior standard, two lateral wings, and two anterior ones forming a keel. This is called vexillary or papilionaceous aestivation.
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: A plant has a tap root that stores food and becomes fleshy. Which of the following is a classic example of this modification?
questions.explanation: Carrot, turnip, and adventitious roots of sweet potato store food. However, carrot is a modification of the tap root system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food.

questions.question: If a plant exhibits a taproot system and its leaves show reticulate venation, what can be inferred about the arrangement of its floral parts?
options: The floral parts are likely in multiples of four or five (pentamerous/tetramerous).
The floral parts are strictly in multiples of three (trimerous).
The plant must have parallel venation in its cotyledons.
The plant will possess fibrous root modifications.
questions.explanation: Plants with taproot systems and reticulate venation are typically dicotyledons. Dicot flowers are usually pentamerous or tetramerous, whereas monocots are trimerous.
questions.ncertEvidence: Dicotyledonous plants are characterized by taproot systems, reticulate venation, and flowers that are usually pentamerous or tetramerous.

questions.question: A researcher observes a plant where the stem is underground, fleshy, and stores food, but it lacks nodes and internodes. What can be inferred about this structure?
options: It is not a stem, as stems must possess nodes and internodes.
questions.explanation: The fundamental definition of a stem in NCERT is that it bears nodes and internodes; if a structure lacks these, it cannot be classified as a stem regardless of its underground position.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers and fruits. It develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed. The stem bears nodes and internodes.

questions.question: In a flower where the ovary is situated below the calyx, corolla, and androecium, which of the following floral formulas would be incorrect for this condition?
questions.explanation: If the ovary is inferior, it is represented by a bar above the G (Ḡ). A bar below the G (G) denotes a superior ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary. The ovary is said to be inferior. In floral formula, it is denoted as Ḡ.

questions.question: Consider a plant with leaf-like flattened structures performing photosynthesis, and these structures bear buds at their margins. What can be inferred about the nature of these 'leaves'?
options: They are phylloclades, which are modified stems.
They are true leaves showing vegetative propagation.
questions.explanation: Leaves of Bryophyllum possess buds at their margins that develop into new plantlets, a form of vegetative propagation.
questions.ncertEvidence: Leaves of Bryophyllum possess buds at their margins that develop into new plantlets.

questions.question: If a flower has its floral whorls arranged such that the ovary is half-inferior, what is the correct representation for the gynoecium in the floral formula?
options: G with a bar above it
G with a bar below it
G with a bar in the middle
questions.explanation: Perigynous flowers have a half-inferior ovary, which is represented in a floral formula by a bar placed in the middle of the G (Ḡ).
questions.ncertEvidence: If ovary is half inferior, it is represented as Ḡ.

questions.question: A student identifies a flower as Actinomorphic. Which of the following conditions must be true for this inference to hold?
options: The flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the center.
The flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane.
questions.explanation: Actinomorphic flowers exhibit radial symmetry, meaning they can be divided into two equal halves by any plane passing through the center.
questions.ncertEvidence: When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre, it is said to be actinomorphic.

questions.question: If a plant's stem is modified into a green, flattened structure for photosynthesis and possesses nodes and internodes, what is the correct classification?
questions.explanation: A phylloclade is a stem modification where the stem becomes green and flattened to perform photosynthesis, maintaining its characteristic nodes and internodes.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Opuntia, the stem is modified into a flattened, green, fleshy structure (phylloclade) and contains chlorophyll and carries out photosynthesis.

questions.question: In a pea plant, the leaf is pinnately compound. What can be inferred about the axillary bud in this plant?
options: The axillary bud is present in the axil of the leaflets.
The axillary bud is absent in the axil of the leaflets.
The axillary bud is modified into a tendril.
The entire leaf is a modified axillary bud.
questions.explanation: A key distinction between a simple leaf and a leaflet of a compound leaf is that the axillary bud is present in the axil of the petiole in simple leaves, but not in the axil of leaflets in compound leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: The leaf is simple or compound. A bud is present in the axil of petiole in both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axil of leaflets of the compound leaf.

questions.question: If a plant exhibits valvate aestivation, what can be inferred about the petal arrangement?
options: The margins of petals overlap one another without any particular direction.
The margins of petals touch one another at the margin, without overlapping.
One margin of the petal overlaps the next one.
The largest petal overlaps the two lateral petals.
questions.explanation: Valvate aestivation is characterized by petals in a whorl just touching one another at the margin, without overlapping.
questions.ncertEvidence: When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate.

questions.question: A researcher finds a plant where the fruit develops from a monocarpellary superior ovary. What can be inferred about the nature of this fruit?
questions.explanation: A simple fruit develops from the ovary of a single flower, which may be monocarpellary or multicarpellary syncarpous.
questions.ncertEvidence: A fruit developed from the ovary of a single flower is called a simple fruit.

questions.question: Which of the following modifications best describes the root system in Rhizophora growing in swampy areas?
questions.explanation: In Rhizophora, roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards to obtain oxygen for respiration; these are called pneumatophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards to get oxygen for respiration.

questions.question: Identify the structure that develops from the axillary bud in plants like Bougainvillea and Citrus to provide protection.
questions.explanation: Axillary buds of stem may get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns in plants like Citrus and Bougainvillea to protect from browsing animals.
questions.ncertEvidence: Axillary buds of stem may get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns.

questions.question: In which plant family is the placentation described as 'free central'?
questions.explanation: When the ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose, the placentation is called free central.
questions.ncertEvidence: When the ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose, the placentation is called free central.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the aestivation in Calotropis is correct?
questions.explanation: When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate.
questions.ncertEvidence: When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate.

questions.question: The presence of a 'pulvinus' leaf base is a characteristic feature of which family?
questions.explanation: In leguminous plants (Fabaceae), the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus.
questions.ncertEvidence: In leguminous plants the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus.

questions.question: In a flower, the 'epipetalous' condition is observed in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Stamens attached to the petals are epipetalous, as seen in the brinjal flower (Solanaceae family).
questions.ncertEvidence: Stamens may be attached to the petals as in brinjal.

questions.question: Which type of fruit is developed from a monocarpellary superior ovary and is one-seeded?
questions.explanation: In mango and coconut, fruit is known as a drupe. They develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded.
questions.ncertEvidence: In mango and coconut, fruit is known as a drupe. They develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one-seeded.

questions.question: The 'scutellum' in a monocot seed is actually a modified:
questions.explanation: In the seeds of cereals such as maize, the embryo is small and situated in a groove at one end of the endosperm. It consists of one large and shield-shaped cotyledon known as scutellum.
questions.ncertEvidence: It consists of one large and shield-shaped cotyledon known as scutellum.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an underground stem modification for perennation?
questions.explanation: Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, colocasia are modified to store food in them. Ginger is Zingiber.
questions.ncertEvidence: Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, colocasia are modified to store food in them.

questions.question: The floral formula '⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2)' represents which family?
questions.explanation: The given floral formula describes the Solanaceae family, characterized by gamosepalous calyx, gamopetalous corolla, epipetalous stamens, and bicarpellary ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: Floral formula of Solanaceae: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2).

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the root system in flowering plants.
options: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the base of the stem.
In wheat, the root system is of the adventitious type.
In monstera, roots arise from parts other than the radicle.
The primary root and its branches constitute the fibrous root system in dicotyledonous plants.
questions.explanation: The primary root and its branches constitute the tap root system in dicotyledonous plants, not the fibrous root system.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicotyledonous plants, the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of primary root which grows inside the soil. It bears lateral roots of several orders that are referred to as secondary, tertiary, etc. roots. The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system.

questions.question: Which of the following plant parts is NOT correctly matched with its specific modification for storage?
questions.explanation: Carrot is a modification of the tap root, not an adventitious root.
questions.ncertEvidence: Roots in some plants change their shape and become fleshy and modified for storage of food. Examples: tap roots of carrot, turnip, and adventitious roots of sweet potato.

questions.question: Select the plant that does NOT exhibit stem modification for vegetative propagation.
questions.explanation: Citrus plants have axillary buds modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns for protection, not for vegetative propagation.
questions.ncertEvidence: In plants like mint and jasmine a slender lateral branch arises from the base of the main axis and after growing aerially for some time arch downwards to touch the ground. A lateral branch with short internodes and each node bearing a rosette of leaves and a tuft of roots is found in aquatic plants like Pistia and Eichhornia.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about phyllotaxy is incorrect?
options: In alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner.
In opposite phyllotaxy, a pair of leaves arise at each node and lie opposite to each other.
In whorled phyllotaxy, more than two leaves arise at a node and form a whorl.
Mustard and China rose show opposite phyllotaxy.
questions.explanation: Mustard and China rose exhibit alternate phyllotaxy, not opposite.
questions.ncertEvidence: In alternate type of phyllotaxy a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sun flower plants.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect match between the plant and its leaf modification.
options: Onion: Fleshy leaves for food storage
Australian Acacia: Fleshy leaf for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: In Australian Acacia, the leaves are small and short-lived; the petioles expand, become green and synthesize food, not the leaf itself.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants, the leaves of the petiole expand, become green and synthesise food. These are called phyllodes, e.g., in Australian Acacia.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of the family Fabaceae?
questions.explanation: Fabaceae is characterized by a monocarpellary, unilocular ovary, not polycarpellary/apocarpous.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ovary superior, mono carpellary, unilocular with many ovules, style single.

questions.question: Find the incorrect statement regarding aestivation.
options: Valvate: Sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping.
Twisted: One margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on.
Imbricate: The margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction.
Vexillary: The largest petal overlaps the two lateral petals which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals, seen in Solanaceae.
questions.explanation: Vexillary (or papilionaceous) aestivation is characteristic of the Fabaceae family, not Solanaceae.
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Which of the following floral formulas represents a plant with actinomorphic, bisexual flowers, hypogynous ovary, and epipetalous stamens?
questions.explanation: The formula ⊕, ⚥, K(5), C(5), A(5), G(2) correctly represents the Solanaceae family features (Actinomorphic, bisexual, gamosepalous, gamopetalous, epipetalous stamens, bicarpellary ovary).
questions.ncertEvidence: Solanaceae: Floral formula: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A(5) G(2). The 'A' and 'C' connection represents epipetalous condition.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a drupe?
questions.explanation: Tomato is a berry, whereas Mango and Coconut are drupes.
questions.ncertEvidence: In mango and coconut, fruit is known as a drupe. They develop from monocarpellary superior ovaries and are one seeded.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement about the placentation types.
options: Marginal: The placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary.
Axile: The placenta is axial and the ovules are attached to it in a multilocular ovary.
Parietal: The ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral part.
Free central: Ovules are borne on central axis and septa are present.
questions.explanation: In free central placentation, the ovules are borne on the central axis and septa are absent.
questions.ncertEvidence: When the ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose the placentation is called free central.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, which of the following statements regarding the aestivation and petal arrangement is correct?
options: The standard petal overlaps the two lateral wings, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals.
The two smallest anterior petals overlap the lateral wings, which overlap the posterior standard petal.
The standard petal is overlapped by the two lateral wings, which are overlapped by the keel.
All five petals are arranged in a whorl with twisted aestivation.
questions.explanation: In vexillary aestivation (Fabaceae), the posterior standard (vexillum) overlaps the two lateral wings, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Which of the following plant parts is morphologically equivalent to a modified leaf?
questions.explanation: In Nepenthes (pitcher plant), the leaf lamina is modified into a pitcher to trap insects. Thorns of Citrus are modified axillary buds, and the spines of Opuntia are modified leaves, but the question specifically targets the leaf lamina modification.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants such as Australian acacias, the leaves are small and short-lived. The petioles in these plants expand, become green and synthesise food. Leaves of certain insectivorous plants such as pitcher plant, venus-fly trap are also modified leaves.

questions.question: Consider the following statement regarding root systems: 'The primary root and its branches constitute the fibrous root system.' Identify the flaw.
options: The primary root and its branches constitute the tap root system.
The fibrous root system originates from the radicle.
The tap root system is commonly observed in monocotyledonous plants.
Adventitious roots are the primary roots in dicotyledonous plants.
questions.explanation: The primary root and its branches constitute the tap root system, characteristic of dicotyledons. Fibrous root systems originate from the base of the stem, not the radicle.
questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of the dicotyledonous plants, the direct elongation of the radicle leads to the formation of primary root which grows inside the soil. It bears lateral roots of several orders that are referred to as secondary, tertiary, etc. roots. The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a correct match between the plant modification and the function performed?
options: Storage roots of Sweet potato: Photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores are specialized roots in Rhizophora that grow vertically upwards to obtain oxygen for respiration in swampy areas.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants such as Rhizophora growing in swampy areas, many roots come out of the ground and grow vertically upwards. Such roots, called pneumatophores, help to get oxygen for respiration.

questions.question: In a flower, if the gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located at the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, the flower is described as:
questions.explanation: In perigynous flowers, the gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located at the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level.
questions.ncertEvidence: If gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located at the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, it is called perigynous.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the stem is incorrect?
options: The stem bears nodes and internodes, but only nodes produce leaves.
The stem develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed.
The stem is generally positively phototropic and negatively geotropic.
The stem provides support to branches, flowers, and fruits.
questions.explanation: The stem bears nodes and internodes; leaves are borne at the nodes, but the statement implies 'only' nodes produce leaves which is true, however, the structure of the stem itself is defined by the presence of nodes and internodes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers and fruits. It develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed. The stem bears nodes and internodes.

questions.question: Identify the correct pairing of the placentation type and its representative plant example.
questions.explanation: In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached to it, as seen in sunflower and marigold.
questions.ncertEvidence: In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached to it as in sunflower, marigold.

questions.question: Which structure in a flower is responsible for the protection of floral parts in the bud stage?
questions.explanation: The calyx is the outermost whorl of the flower and the sepals are leaf like and protect the flower in the bud stage.
questions.ncertEvidence: The calyx is the outermost whorl of the flower and the members are called sepals. Generally, sepals are green, leaf like and protect the flower in the bud stage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between a bulb and a corm?
options: A bulb is a condensed stem with fleshy scale leaves, while a corm is a swollen underground stem base.
Both are modifications of the root system.
A bulb lacks nodes, whereas a corm has prominent nodes and internodes.
A corm is always found in aquatic plants.
questions.explanation: Bulbs (like onion) consist of a short stem covered by fleshy leaves, while corms (like Colocasia) are condensed underground stems.
questions.ncertEvidence: Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, colocasia are modified to store food in them. They also act as organs of perennation to tide over conditions unfavourable for growth.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement regarding the symmetry of flowers.
options: Zygomorphic flowers can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane.
Actinomorphic flowers can be divided into two similar halves only in a lateral plane.
All flowers are either actinomorphic or zygomorphic.
questions.explanation: Zygomorphic flowers (e.g., pea) exhibit bilateral symmetry, meaning they can be divided into two identical halves by only one vertical plane.
questions.ncertEvidence: When a flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia.

questions.question: Which of the following plants exhibits a tap root system where the roots are modified for storing food?
questions.explanation: In tap root systems, roots like those of carrot and turnip are modified for food storage. Sweet potato is an adventitious root modification.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food.

questions.question: In which plant are the stem tendrils developed from axillary buds, helping the plant to climb?
questions.explanation: Stem tendrils are slender and spirally coiled structures which develop from axillary buds in plants like gourds (cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon) and grapevines.
questions.ncertEvidence: Stem tendrils which develop from axillary buds are slender and spirally coiled and help plants to climb such as in gourds (cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon) and grapevines.

questions.question: Identify the type of leaf arrangement where a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as seen in China rose.
questions.explanation: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sunflower.
questions.ncertEvidence: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sunflower.

questions.question: When the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction, the aestivation is called:
questions.explanation: If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and Gulmohar, the aestivation is called imbricate.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and Gulmohar, the aestivation is called imbricate.

questions.question: In a flower, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. This condition is termed as:
questions.explanation: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.
questions.ncertEvidence: In hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the family Fabaceae regarding its androecium?
questions.explanation: The family Fabaceae is characterized by diadelphous stamens (usually 9+1 arrangement).
questions.ncertEvidence: Androecium: stamen ten, diadelphous, anther dithecous.

questions.question: In Solanaceae, the fruit is usually:
questions.explanation: Members of the family Solanaceae typically have berry or capsule type fruits.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fruit: berry or capsule.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the embryo is responsible for the development of the shoot system?
questions.explanation: The plumule is the portion of the embryo axis that develops into the shoot system, while the radicle develops into the root system.
questions.ncertEvidence: The plumule and radicle are the two parts of the embryo axis, with the plumule developing into the shoot and the radicle into the root.

questions.question: The lateral branches originate from the basal and underground portion of the main stem, grow horizontally beneath the soil and then come out obliquely upwards giving rise to leafy shoots in:
questions.explanation: In banana, pineapple and Chrysanthemum, the lateral branches originate from the basal and underground portion of the main stem, grow horizontally beneath the soil and then come out obliquely upwards giving rise to leafy shoots.
questions.ncertEvidence: In banana, pineapple and Chrysanthemum, the lateral branches originate from the basal and underground portion of the main stem, grow horizontally beneath the soil and then come out obliquely upwards giving rise to leafy shoots.

questions.question: Epiphyllous condition (stamens attached to perianth) is a characteristic feature of which family?
questions.explanation: In Liliaceae, the stamens are epiphyllous, meaning they are attached to the tepals (perianth).
questions.ncertEvidence: Androecium: stamen six, six in two whorls, epiphyllous.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of plants exhibit an underground stem that serves as a storage organ and propagates vegetatively?
questions.explanation: Potato (tuber), Ginger (rhizome), and Zaminkand (corm) are examples of underground stems modified for storage and perennation. Sweet potato is a root modification.
questions.ncertEvidence: Underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, colocasia are modified to store food in them. They also act as organs of perennation to tide over conditions unfavourable for growth.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, the aestivation of the corolla is described as vexillary. Which of the following correctly describes the arrangement of petals in this type?
options: One posterior standard, two lateral wings, two anterior keels
Two posterior standards, one lateral wing, two anterior keels
One anterior standard, two lateral wings, two posterior keels
Two anterior standards, two lateral wings, one posterior keel
questions.explanation: In vexillary aestivation, the large posterior petal (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Identify the correct pairing of the plant part to its specific modification in the given list: (i) Cactus - leaf, (ii) Pea - leaf, (iii) Onion - leaf, (iv) Australian Acacia - stem.
questions.explanation: In Cactus, leaves are modified into spines (protection); in Pea, leaves are modified into tendrils (climbing); in Onion, leaves are modified for food storage (fleshy leaves). Australian Acacia has phyllodes (modified petiole), not stem.
questions.ncertEvidence: Leaves are often converted into tendrils for climbing as in peas or into spines for defence as in cacti. The fleshy leaves of onion and garlic store food.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the root system is correct?
options: In monocots, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem
The fibrous root system develops from the radicle in dicots
Adventitious roots are found only in plants growing in marshy areas
Tap root systems are typical of plants that propagate vegetatively
questions.explanation: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots, called the fibrous root system.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding phyllotaxy in plants.
options: In alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner
In opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves arise at each node and lie on the same side
In whorled phyllotaxy, more than three leaves arise at a node and are arranged in a specific sequence
Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of flowers on the floral axis
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch. Alternate (e.g., China rose), opposite (e.g., Calotropis), and whorled (e.g., Alstonia) are the three types.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch. This is usually of three types - alternate, opposite, alternate and whorled.

questions.question: In a flower, the thalamus is cup-shaped and the ovary is half-inferior. This condition is known as:
questions.explanation: In perigynous flowers, the gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level. The ovary is half-inferior.
questions.ncertEvidence: If gynoecium is situated in the centre and other parts of the flower are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, it is called perigynous. The ovary here is said to be half inferior.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the family Solanaceae?
questions.explanation: Solanaceae is characterized by a persistent calyx (gamosepalous), valvate aestivation, and often superior ovaries. Vexillary aestivation and diadelphous stamens are features of Fabaceae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Solanaceae: Calyx: sepals five, united, persistent, valvate aestivation.

questions.question: Consider the following statements and identify the correct option: (A) The region of the stem where leaves are born are called nodes. (B) The portion between two nodes is called the internode.
options: Both A and B are correct
Both A and B are incorrect
questions.explanation: The stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers and fruits. It develops from the plumule of the embryo. The regions of the stem where leaves are born are called nodes while internodes are the portions between two nodes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stem is the ascending part of the axis bearing branches, leaves, flowers and fruits. It develops from the plumule of the embryo of a germinating seed. The regions of the stem where leaves are born are called nodes while internodes are the portions between two nodes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an epigynous flower?
questions.explanation: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it. Examples include guava, cucumber, and the ray florets of sunflower.
questions.ncertEvidence: In epigynous flower, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary. Hence the ovary is said to be inferior as in flowers of guava and cucumber, and the ray florets of sunflower.

questions.question: In which of the following plants are the roots adventitious and modified to support the main axis like 'stilt roots'?
questions.explanation: Stilt roots arise from the lower nodes of the stem in plants like maize and sugarcane to provide support.
questions.ncertEvidence: In maize and sugarcane, supporting roots called stilt roots come out of the lower nodes of the stem.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the phyllotaxy in China rose, Mustard, and Sunflower?
questions.explanation: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as seen in China rose, mustard, and sunflower plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sunflower plants.

questions.question: The type of aestivation where the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction is known as:
questions.explanation: If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and Gulmohur, the aestivation is called imbricate.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and Gulmohur, the aestivation is called imbricate.

questions.question: Which part of the flower is responsible for the formation of the fruit wall (pericarp) after fertilization?
questions.explanation: After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit and the ovary wall develops into the pericarp.
questions.ncertEvidence: After fertilisation, the ripened ovules develop into seeds and the ovary matures into a fruit. The wall of the ovary develops into the wall of fruit called pericarp.

questions.question: In which family of flowering plants is the gynoecium characterized by a superior ovary with a single ovule attached to the base?
questions.explanation: In the Asteraceae family (often discussed in the context of basal placentation), the ovary is inferior, but the description of a single ovule at the base refers to basal placentation, which is correctly represented by Asteraceae (Sunflower). Note: NCERT mentions basal placentation in sunflower and marigold.
questions.ncertEvidence: In basal placentation, the placenta develops at the base of ovary and a single ovule is attached to it, as in sunflower, marigold.

questions.question: Which of the following plants possess a succulent stem modified to perform photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: In some plants of arid regions, stems become flattened (Opuntia) or fleshy cylindrical (Euphorbia) and contain chlorophyll to carry out photosynthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: In some plants of arid regions, stems become flattened (Opuntia) or fleshy cylindrical (Euphorbia) and contain chlorophyll to carry out photosynthesis.

questions.question: What is the characteristic feature of the fruit in the family Fabaceae?
questions.explanation: The fruit of the Fabaceae family is typically a legume, which is a dry dehiscent fruit.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fruit: legume; seed: non-endospermic, one to many.

questions.question: Identify the type of placentation where the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary.
questions.explanation: In marginal placentation, the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows, as in pea.
questions.ncertEvidence: In marginal placentation, the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary and the ovules are borne on this ridge forming two rows, as in pea.

questions.question: Which of the following structures represents a modification of the leaf for climbing?
questions.explanation: Leaves are often modified into tendrils for climbing as seen in peas, or into spines for defense as in cacti.
questions.ncertEvidence: They (leaves) are converted into tendrils for climbing as in peas or into spines for defence as in cacti.

questions.question: The floral formula ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2) represents which of the following families?
questions.explanation: The floral formula ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2) corresponds to the family Solanaceae, characterized by gamosepalous and gamopetalous conditions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Floral formula of Solanaceae: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G(2).

questions.question: Which of the following modifications correctly explains the transfer of function from a photosynthetic stem to a storage organ in specific plant species?
options: Phylloclade of Opuntia to the tuber of Solanum tuberosum
Rhizome of Ginger to the corm of Colocasia
Tendrils of Cucurbita to the thorns of Citrus
Stolon of Jasmine to the offset of Eichhornia
questions.explanation: Both rhizomes and corms are underground stem modifications primarily used for perennation and storage of food, unlike aerial stems designed for photosynthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Stems may be modified to perform the function of storage of food, support, protection and of vegetative propagation.

questions.question: If a plant exhibits a superior ovary, how would you correctly describe its floral symmetry and floral parts arrangement?
options: Hypogynous flower with stamens attached to the thalamus below the ovary
Perigynous flower with parts arising from the rim of the thalamus
Epigynous flower with the thalamus enclosing the ovary
Hypogynous flower with the ovary situated below the other floral whorls
questions.explanation: In hypogynous flowers, the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it, making the ovary superior.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: In hypogynous flower the gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other parts are situated below it. The ovary in such flowers is said to be superior.

questions.question: Consider the venation pattern of a leaf. If a plant has reticulate venation, what is the most likely condition of its root system and floral symmetry?
options: Tap root system and pentamerous flowers
Fibrous root system and trimerous flowers
Adventitious root system and zygomorphic flowers
Tap root system and parallel venation in petals
questions.explanation: Reticulate venation is a characteristic feature of dicotyledons, which typically possess a tap root system and floral parts in multiples of 4 or 5 (pentamerous/tetramerous).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Reticulate venation is characteristic of dicotyledons, which have tap root systems.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, if the vexillum is removed, what effect will it have on the symmetry and protection of the inner floral parts?
options: The flower loses its characteristic zygomorphic symmetry and standard petal protection
The flower becomes actinomorphic and the stamens are exposed
The ovary becomes superior instead of half-inferior
The aestivation changes from valvate to imbricate
questions.explanation: Fabaceae flowers are zygomorphic with vexillary aestivation where the posterior standard petal (vexillum) overlaps the two lateral wings, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior keel petals.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Papilionaceous corolla has five petals; the largest (standard or vexillum) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a succulent stem modification with its physiological advantage in arid conditions?
options: Flattened stem of Opuntia; contains chlorophyll for photosynthesis
Fleshy cylindrical stem of Euphorbia; acts as a climbing organ
Underground stem of Potato; facilitates gas exchange
Runner of Grass; stores water in nodes
questions.explanation: In Opuntia, the stem becomes flattened and fleshy, containing chlorophyll to carry out photosynthesis, an adaptation to arid environments.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: In some plants of arid regions, stems become flattened (Opuntia) or fleshy cylindrical (Euphorbia) structures. They contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.

questions.question: If you observe a plant where the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly, which taxonomic group are you likely observing?
questions.explanation: Sheathing leaf bases are a characteristic feature of monocotyledonous plants, such as grasses and bananas.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.

questions.question: How does the placentation in Primrose (Free Central) differ from that in Mustard (Parietal) regarding the ovary structure?
options: Ovules develop on a central axis without septa in Primrose, whereas ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary in Mustard
Primrose has a multilocular ovary, while Mustard is unilocular
Mustard has a free central axis, while Primrose has parietal placentation
Both have basal placentation with different ovary positions
questions.explanation: In free central placentation (e.g., Primrose), ovules are on a central axis without septa. In parietal placentation (e.g., Mustard), ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: When the ovules are borne on central axis and septa are absent, as in Dianthus and Primrose the placentation is called free central.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the aestivation found in the petals of China Rose and the sepals of Calotropis?
questions.explanation: China Rose petals show twisted aestivation (one margin overlaps the next), while Calotropis sepals show valvate aestivation (margins just touch each other).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: When margins of sepals or petals overlap one another... it is called twisted (China rose). When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin... it is said to be valvate (Calotropis).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the transformation of a vegetative bud in a plant like Bougainvillea?
options: Modification into woody, pointed thorns for protection
Modification into fleshy scales for food storage
Modification into a succulent structure for water storage
questions.explanation: In Bougainvillea, axillary buds are modified into woody, straight, and pointed thorns, which protect the plant from browsing animals.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Axillary buds of stem may also get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns (Citrus, Bougainvillea). They protect plants from browsing animals.

questions.question: Why is the fruit of a strawberry or cashew considered a 'false fruit' compared to a mango?
options: Because the thalamus contributes to fruit formation instead of the ovary alone
Because they do not develop from flowers
Because they are seedless parthenocarpic fruits
Because they develop from a multi-carpellary ovary
questions.explanation: False fruits (pseudocarps) are those where parts other than the ovary (like the thalamus) contribute to fruit formation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: In some fruits, called false fruits, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation (e.g., apple, strawberry, cashew).

questions.question: Which of the following plants possesses a root system where the primary root is replaced by a large number of roots that originate from the base of the stem?
questions.explanation: In monocotyledonous plants like wheat, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots originating from the base of the stem, known as fibrous root systems.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocotyledonous plants, the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by a large number of roots. These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system, as seen in the wheat plant.

questions.question: In the region of the root, the cells of the meristematic activity are characterized by:
options: Small size, thin-walled, and dense protoplasm
questions.explanation: The region of meristematic activity consists of very small, thin-walled cells with dense protoplasm that divide repeatedly.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly.

questions.question: Identify the modification in which the stem becomes flattened and fleshy, containing chlorophyll to carry out photosynthesis in arid regions.
questions.explanation: Opuntia is an example of a phylloclade, where the stem is modified into a flattened, fleshy structure for photosynthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: In Opuntia, the stem is modified into a flattened, fleshy structure (phylloclade) and contains chlorophyll and carries out photosynthesis.

questions.question: In alternate phyllotaxy, how many leaves arise at each node?
questions.explanation: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner, as seen in China rose.
questions.ncertEvidence: In alternate type of phyllotaxy, a single leaf arises at each node in alternate manner, as in china rose, mustard and sun flower.

questions.question: A flower is referred to as 'zygomorphic' when:
options: It can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane
It can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane
It cannot be divided into two similar halves by any vertical plane
The floral parts are arranged in a spiral manner
questions.explanation: Zygomorphic flowers exhibit bilateral symmetry, meaning they can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane.
questions.ncertEvidence: When a flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia.

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, the aestivation of the petals is described as:
questions.explanation: Fabaceae (Papilionoideae) members show vexillary aestivation where the largest petal (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).
questions.ncertEvidence: In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

questions.question: Which part of the embryo develops into the shoot during seed germination?
questions.explanation: The plumule is the portion of the embryo axis that grows into the shoot, whereas the radicle develops into the root.
questions.ncertEvidence: The plumule and radicle are the two structures present in the embryo. The plumule develops into the shoot and the radicle into the root.

questions.question: Epigynous flowers are characterized by:
options: The margin of the thalamus growing upward enclosing the ovary completely
The ovary being situated above the other floral parts
The thalamus forming a cup-shaped structure
questions.explanation: In epigynous flowers, the margin of the thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, resulting in an inferior ovary.
questions.ncertEvidence: In epigynous flowers, the margin of thalamus grows upward enclosing the ovary completely and getting fused with it, the other parts of flower arise above the ovary.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the family Solanaceae regarding its androecium?
questions.explanation: Plants in the family Solanaceae, such as Solanum nigrum, possess stamens that are epipetalous, meaning they are attached to the petals.
