questions.explanation: Dicot roots typically exhibit 2 to 4 xylem and phloem patches (diarch to tetrarch), whereas monocot roots have more than six xylem bundles (polyarch) and a large, well-developed pith.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot root, there are usually two to four xylem and phloem patches. Later, a cambium ring develops. In monocot root, there are usually more than six xylem bundles (polyarch).

questions.question: What is the key functional distinction between the endodermis of a root and the endodermis of a stem?
options: Root endodermis contains Casparian strips for water regulation, whereas stem endodermis is often referred to as the 'starch sheath'.
Stem endodermis contains Casparian strips, whereas root endodermis does not.
Root endodermis is absent, while stem endodermis is highly prominent.
Both act as the same barrier, but stem endodermis is the only one that conducts photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex in roots is the endodermis, characterized by Casparian strips. In the stem, the endodermis is referred to as the 'starch sheath' because its cells are rich in starch grains.
questions.ncertEvidence: The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. In dicot stem, the cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is referred to as the starch sheath. In roots, the endodermis comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces, with Casparian strips.

questions.question: Differentiate between the cambium found in the vascular bundles and the cork cambium.
options: Vascular cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem, while cork cambium produces periderm.
Vascular cambium produces periderm, while cork cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem.
Vascular cambium is only found in monocots, while cork cambium is only found in dicots.
Vascular cambium forms the bark, while cork cambium forms the wood.
questions.explanation: Vascular cambium is involved in secondary growth of the vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), whereas cork cambium (phellogen) is involved in the formation of the periderm (cork, phellogen, and phelloderm).
questions.ncertEvidence: The meristematic layer that is responsible for cutting off vascular tissues—microspores and phloem—is called vascular cambium. The phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.

questions.question: How do bulliform cells differ from typical epidermal cells in monocot leaves?
options: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colorless cells that cause leaf curling under water stress, unlike typical epidermal cells.
Bulliform cells are photosynthetic cells located in the mesophyll, while epidermal cells are non-photosynthetic.
Bulliform cells provide structural support through lignified walls, whereas epidermal cells are thin-walled.
Bulliform cells produce stomata, whereas epidermal cells produce trichomes only.
questions.explanation: In grasses (monocots), certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells. When turgid, they make the leaf surface exposed, and when flaccid, they cause leaf curling to minimize water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: Compare the mesophyll of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf and an isobilateral (monocot) leaf.
options: Dicot leaf mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, while monocot leaf mesophyll is not.
Monocot leaf mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, while dicot leaf mesophyll is not.
Dicot leaf mesophyll consists only of spongy parenchyma, while monocot leaf mesophyll consists only of palisade parenchyma.
Both types of leaves possess identical mesophyll structures with no differentiation.
questions.explanation: In a dorsiventral leaf (dicot), the mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma. In an isobilateral leaf (monocot), the mesophyll is not differentiated into these two types.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dorsiventral leaf, the mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma - divided into palisade parenchyma and spongy parenchyma. In isobilateral leaf, the mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the location and function of the trichomes in shoots versus the root hairs in roots?
options: Trichomes are epidermal outgrowths on the shoot that prevent water loss, while root hairs are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells for absorption.
Trichomes are unicellular structures for absorption, while root hairs are multicellular outgrowths for protection.
Trichomes are internal vascular tissues, while root hairs are external dermal tissues.
Trichomes are involved in photosynthesis, while root hairs are involved in vegetative propagation.
questions.explanation: Trichomes are epidermal hairs on the shoot system that may be branched or unbranched and help in preventing water loss due to transpiration. Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells (epiblema) that help in the absorption of water and minerals.
questions.ncertEvidence: The epidermal hairs on the stem are called trichomes. They are usually multicellular... they help in preventing water loss due to transpiration. Root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals from the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the structure of the plant body is correct in the context of tissue systems?
options: The epidermal tissue system is the outermost covering of the whole plant body.
The ground tissue system forms the vascular bundles in the plant.
The vascular tissue system consists of only xylem and phloem in dicot stems.
The ground tissue system includes all tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundles.
questions.explanation: According to NCERT, the ground tissue system includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles. It consists of simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.
questions.ncertEvidence: The ground tissue system includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles.

questions.question: In a dorsiventral leaf, the mesophyll is differentiated into two types of cells. Select the correct description of these cells.
options: Palisade parenchyma is placed adaxially and is vertically arranged.
Spongy parenchyma is placed adaxially and is loosely arranged.
Palisade parenchyma is placed abaxially and contains intercellular spaces.
Spongy parenchyma is placed adaxially and is vertically arranged.
questions.explanation: In dicotyledonous leaves, the mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carries out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells - the palisade parenchyma placed adaxially and the spongy parenchyma situated below the palisade cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other.

questions.question: Which characteristic is specific to the vascular bundles of a monocot stem compared to a dicot stem?
options: Presence of water-containing cavities within the vascular bundles.
Vascular bundles are arranged in a ring.
Presence of cambium between xylem and phloem.
Vascular bundles are open and collateral.
questions.explanation: Monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath. A large number of scattered vascular bundles are present, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath. In the center, water-containing cavities are present.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the monocot stem, a large number of scattered vascular bundles are present, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath. Water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles.

questions.question: Regarding the secondary growth in dicot stems, which of the following is true concerning the vascular cambium?
options: It is formed by the intrafascicular cambium and interfascicular cambium.
It is entirely primary in origin.
It produces phellem towards the inside.
It remains confined to the phloem region only.
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium in dicot stems is formed by the fusion of the intrafascicular cambium (present within the bundle) and the interfascicular cambium (formed by medullary ray cells).
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of medullary rays, adjoining these intrafascicular cambium become meristematic and form the interfascicular cambium. Thus, a continuous ring of cambium is formed.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of layers in the periderm from the outside to the inside?
questions.explanation: The phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as the periderm. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides; the outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem, and the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement regarding the root hairs in a dicot root.
options: They are unicellular elongations of epidermal cells.
They are also called epiblema hairs.
They help in the absorption of water and minerals.
questions.explanation: In roots, the outermost layer is the epidermis, often called epiblema. Many of the cells of the epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Many of the cells of the epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs.

questions.question: The 'conjoint vascular bundles' typically found in stems are characterized by:
options: Xylem and phloem being situated at the same radius.
Xylem and phloem being situated at different radii.
Phloem being on the inner side of xylem.
Xylem being on the outer side of phloem.
questions.explanation: In conjoint type of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius of vascular bundles. Such bundles are common in stems and leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: In conjoint type of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius of vascular bundles.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of sclerenchyma cells?
options: They are dead and without protoplasts at maturity.
They are living and possess thick cellulosic cell walls.
They are thin-walled and have large intercellular spaces.
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells are long or narrow cells with thick and lignified cell walls having a few or numerous pits. They are usually dead and without protoplasts.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sclerenchyma are usually dead and without protoplasts.

questions.question: In the anatomy of a monocot root, the pith is described as:
questions.explanation: In monocot roots, the pith is large and well-developed, unlike in dicot roots where the pith is small or inconspicuous.
questions.ncertEvidence: The pith is large and well-developed in monocot roots.

questions.question: Identify the function of the 'Bulliform cells' found in certain monocot leaves.
options: They help in leaf rolling to minimize water loss during stress.
They are involved in the storage of starch.
They facilitate the transport of food.
They protect the leaf from herbivory.
questions.explanation: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells. When these cells absorb water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: If a researcher observes a plant stem section where the vascular bundles are scattered in the ground tissue and each bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, which of the following characteristics would they likely observe in the same plant?
options: Presence of cambium in vascular bundles
questions.explanation: The description (scattered vascular bundles with bundle sheath) is characteristic of monocot stems. Monocots typically exhibit parallel venation in their leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monocot stem has scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue and a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

questions.question: A student examines a root section and notes that the xylem is exarch and polyarch. Which of the following tissues would be directly external to the endodermis in this root?
questions.explanation: Exarch and polyarch xylem indicate a monocot root. In roots, the tissue external to the endodermis is the cortex (composed of thin-walled parenchyma cells).
questions.ncertEvidence: In roots, the endodermis is followed by a few layers of thin-walled parenchymatous cells referred to as cortex.

questions.question: During secondary growth in a dicot stem, the activity of the cambial ring is not uniform. Why does the 'spring wood' appear lighter in color compared to 'autumn wood'?
options: The vessels formed in spring have wider lumens
The vessels formed in spring have thicker cell walls
The xylem fibers are more numerous in spring wood
The tracheids are absent in spring wood
questions.explanation: In spring, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities, resulting in lighter-colored wood.
questions.ncertEvidence: The spring wood is also lighter in colour and has a lower density whereas the autumn wood is darker and has a higher density.

questions.question: In a dorsiventral leaf, if the palisade parenchyma is located towards the adaxial epidermis, what is the functional significance of the spongy parenchyma located towards the abaxial epidermis?
options: Facilitation of gaseous exchange via intercellular spaces
Primary site for intense light harvesting
questions.explanation: Spongy parenchyma cells are oval or round and loosely arranged with large intercellular spaces, which facilitate the diffusion of gases.
questions.ncertEvidence: The spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells.

questions.question: Why is the heartwood of a tree considered non-functional for conduction, despite its structural integrity?
options: Deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the lumen
Conversion of xylem parenchyma into sclerenchyma
Death of all tracheary elements due to lack of cytoplasm
Inability of tracheids to transport water under pressure
questions.explanation: Heartwood is hard and durable because of the deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances, and essential oils in the central layers of the stem.
questions.ncertEvidence: These substances make it hard, durable and resistant to the attacks of microorganisms and insects. This region comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls.

questions.question: When observing a section of a dicot root, a student identifies the passage cells. What is the specific physiological role of these cells?
options: Permitting radial movement of water from cortex to protoxylem
Acting as a storage site for starch
Protecting the vascular cylinder from pathogens
Regulating the rate of secondary growth
questions.explanation: Passage cells are thin-walled cells present in the endodermis opposite to the protoxylem, facilitating the movement of water from the cortex to the pericycle.
questions.ncertEvidence: The endodermis is composed of a single layer of barrel-shaped cells. Some of the endodermal cells facing the protoxylem do not have these suberin thickenings and are called passage cells.

questions.question: A plant specimen shows a distinct hypodermis made of collenchyma and vascular bundles arranged in a ring. What is the primary function of the collenchymatous hypodermis?
options: Providing mechanical support to the young stem
Storing food reserves for the plant
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant, such as young stems and petioles of leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of a leaf.

questions.question: During the formation of the cork cambium (phellogen) in a dicot stem, the cells of the cortex dedifferentiate. What are the layers produced by the phellogen towards the outside and inside, respectively?
questions.explanation: The phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork (phellem) and the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex (phelloderm).
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.question: In monocot leaves, the bulliform cells are responsible for which of the following responses under water stress?
options: Rolling of leaves to minimize surface area
Opening of stomata for CO2 intake
questions.explanation: When bulliform cells in the leaves of grasses absorb water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimize water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells. When these cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the arrangement of vascular bundles in a typical dicot stem?
questions.explanation: Dicot stems have vascular bundles arranged in a ring. Each bundle is conjoint (xylem and phloem together), collateral (phloem outside, xylem inside), and open (presence of cambium).
questions.ncertEvidence: The vascular bundles are arranged in a ring; the arrangement of vascular bundles in a ring is a characteristic of dicot stem. Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem.

questions.question: If an investigator observes a plant stem section where the vascular bundles are arranged in a ring and possess a cambium layer between xylem and phloem, what can be inferred about the plant's secondary growth potential?
options: The plant is capable of producing secondary vascular tissues.
The plant will only undergo primary growth throughout its life.
The vascular bundles are closed, preventing radial expansion.
The plant belongs to the monocotyledonous group.
questions.explanation: The presence of cambium between xylem and phloem in a ring-like arrangement is characteristic of open vascular bundles, which allow for secondary growth in dicot stems.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot stems, vascular bundles are arranged in a ring and possess cambium, allowing for secondary growth.

questions.question: A student examines a root section and finds that the endodermis has suberin-rich Casparian strips. What is the primary physiological inference regarding water transport in this region?
options: Water is forced to pass through the plasma membrane of endodermal cells.
Water moves freely through the intercellular spaces of the endodermis.
The endodermis acts as a passive filter for all dissolved solutes.
The Casparian strips prevent the symplastic movement of water.
questions.explanation: Casparian strips are water-impermeable due to suberin deposition, forcing water to switch from the apoplast pathway to the symplast pathway by entering the cytoplasm.
questions.ncertEvidence: The inner boundary of the cortex, the endodermis, has water-impermeable waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips.

questions.question: During the study of secondary growth, if the vascular cambium activity is significantly higher towards the inner side than the outer side, what will be the resulting structure?
options: A larger volume of secondary xylem is formed compared to secondary phloem.
The bark will be thicker than the wood.
The secondary phloem will crush the primary xylem.
The vascular cambium will eventually stop dividing.
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium cells divide more actively towards the inner side to produce secondary xylem (wood), which accumulates in greater quantity than secondary phloem.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells cut off towards pith mature into secondary xylem and the cells cut off towards periphery mature into secondary phloem; the amount of secondary xylem produced is more than secondary phloem.

questions.question: If a plant tissue section shows the presence of bulliform cells in the epidermis, what can be inferred about the plant's environmental adaptation?
options: The plant is adapted to minimize water loss during water stress.
The plant is adapted to high-light intensity in tropical rainforests.
The plant is a dicot with extensive root systems.
The plant relies on rapid transpiration for nutrient uptake.
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colorless cells in grass leaves that lose water during stress, causing the leaf to curl inward to reduce the surface area exposed to sunlight.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells. When they absorb water and become turgid, the leaf surface is exposed; when they lose water due to stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: In a transverse section of a dicot stem, if the pith is found to be very small or inconspicuous, what is the most likely inference regarding the developmental stage?
options: The plant has undergone significant secondary growth.
The plant is in its early seedling stage.
The vascular bundles are arranged in a scattered manner.
questions.explanation: In older dicot stems, the accumulation of secondary xylem (wood) often occupies the center of the stem, compressing or rendering the pith inconspicuous.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot stems, the primary xylem is in the center; as secondary growth proceeds, the secondary xylem occupies the bulk of the stem.

questions.question: If you observe a stem where the vascular bundles are scattered and surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, what must be true about the root system of this plant?
options: It is a fibrous root system.
It is a succulent root system.
questions.explanation: Scattered vascular bundles surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheaths are characteristic of monocot stems; monocots possess fibrous root systems.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

questions.question: Why does the cork cambium (phellogen) produce phelloderm on the inner side and phellem on the outer side?
options: To facilitate the replacement of the ruptured epidermis and provide protection.
To allow for the transport of water to the outer bark.
To store excess carbohydrates produced during photosynthesis.
To increase the rate of gas exchange through the cuticle.
questions.explanation: Phellogen replaces the damaged epidermis by forming phellem (cork) outside and phelloderm (secondary cortex) inside, collectively known as periderm.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides; the outer cells differentiate into cork (phellem) while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex (phelloderm).

questions.question: Which of the following inferences regarding the difference between spring wood and autumn wood is scientifically accurate based on cambial activity?
options: Spring wood has wider vessels, while autumn wood has narrower vessels.
Spring wood is darker in color due to higher density.
Autumn wood is formed when the cambium is highly active.
Spring wood contains more fibers and fewer tracheary elements.
questions.explanation: In spring, cambium is active and produces vessels with wide cavities; in autumn, cambium is less active and produces narrow vessels, resulting in darker, denser wood.
questions.ncertEvidence: In spring, the cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. In winter, the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements that have narrow vessels.

questions.question: If a tissue is identified as 'collenchyma' in a plant section, what mechanical inference can be drawn about the plant organ?
options: It provides both mechanical support and tensile strength to growing parts.
It provides rigid support to mature, woody stems.
It is responsible for the transport of minerals in mature roots.
It functions primarily as a photosynthetic tissue in the epidermis.
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant, such as young stems and petioles, due to the thickening of corners with cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of a leaf.

questions.question: If you observe a root section with more than six vascular bundles (polyarch), what is the most valid inference regarding the plant type?
options: The plant is likely a monocot.
The plant must be a dicot.
The root is undergoing secondary growth.
questions.explanation: Dicot roots typically have 2-4 xylem bundles (diarch to tetrarch), while monocot roots typically exhibit a polyarch arrangement (more than 6).
questions.ncertEvidence: Monocot roots usually have more than six xylem bundles (polyarch).

questions.question: Which specific anatomical feature is responsible for the distinct 'ring' appearance in the secondary xylem of a woody dicot stem, allowing for age determination?
options: Differential activity of the vascular cambium due to seasonal variations
The presence of medullary rays within the secondary phloem
The accumulation of tyloses in the non-functional heartwood
The varying thickness of the cork cambium layers
questions.explanation: Annual rings are formed due to the differential activity of the vascular cambium, which is more active in spring (early wood) and less active in winter (late wood), creating distinct concentric layers.
questions.ncertEvidence: The activity of cambium is under the control of many physiological and environmental factors. In temperate regions, the climatic conditions are not uniform through the year.

questions.question: If you observe a plant section where the vascular bundles are scattered and surrounded by a large parenchymatous ground tissue, which organ is this section likely taken from?
questions.explanation: Monocot stems are characterized by numerous scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, embedded in ground tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocot stem, the vascular bundles are scattered and each vascular bundle is surrounded by a large, conspicuous, parenchymatous ground tissue.

questions.question: Which cell type is characterized by the presence of a Casparian strip in its radial and tangential walls, effectively blocking the apoplastic pathway?
questions.explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex, the endodermis, possesses water-impermeable waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips.
questions.ncertEvidence: The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips.

questions.question: In a dicot root, which tissue layer is responsible for the initiation of lateral roots and the secondary growth process?
questions.explanation: The pericycle, located just inside the endodermis, contains cells that become meristematic to initiate lateral roots and participate in the formation of vascular cambium during secondary growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in these cells (pericycle).

questions.question: What is the primary difference between 'Heartwood' and 'Sapwood' regarding their physiological function in a mature tree?
options: Heartwood is non-functional for conduction, while sapwood conducts water and minerals
Heartwood is light-colored, while sapwood is dark-colored
Heartwood consists of living cells, while sapwood consists of dead cells
Heartwood is formed by cork cambium, while sapwood is formed by vascular cambium
questions.explanation: Heartwood is the central, non-functional, dark-colored wood filled with tannins and resins, while sapwood is the peripheral, functional wood involved in conduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: The peripheral region of the secondary xylem, which is lighter in colour, is known as the sapwood. It is involved in the conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf. The central, hard, dark-coloured, old wood is heartwood. It does not conduct water but gives mechanical support.

questions.question: Which anatomical structure in a dicot stem is often referred to as the 'conjunctive tissue' during secondary growth?
options: Parenchymatous cells between xylem and phloem
The cambial ring formed by intrafascicular and interfascicular cambium
The suberized cells of the phelloderm
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium ring is formed by the union of intrafascicular cambium and the interfascicular cambium (derived from medullary rays), which then functions as a complete ring.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of medullary rays, adjoining these intrafascicular cambium become meristematic and form the interfascicular cambium. Thus, a continuous ring of cambium is formed.

questions.question: In a leaf, the mesophyll tissue is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma. Which plant type displays this 'dorsiventral' leaf anatomy?
questions.explanation: Dicot leaves are dorsiventral, showing a clear differentiation of mesophyll into palisade and spongy parenchyma, whereas monocot leaves are isobilateral.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot leaves, the mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells - the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma.

questions.question: What is the specific role of 'Bulliform cells' found in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves?
options: To control leaf rolling and minimize water loss during stress
To facilitate rapid photosynthesis due to thin cell walls
To provide mechanical strength against wind
To store minerals and calcium oxalate crystals
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colorless cells in monocot leaves that lose water and shrink, causing the leaf to curl inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is associated with the periderm but is formed by the activity of the cork cambium (phellogen)?
questions.explanation: Phellogen (cork cambium) cuts off cells on both sides: phellem (cork) towards the outside and phelloderm (secondary cortex) towards the inside. Together, these three constitute the periderm.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm. Phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.

questions.question: In a monocot root, the vascular bundles are described as polyarch. What does this indicate about the number of xylem and phloem bundles?
questions.explanation: Monocot roots typically have more than six xylem bundles, a condition known as polyarch, compared to the limited number (usually 2-4) in dicot roots (diarch to tetrarch).
questions.ncertEvidence: The number of xylem bundles is usually more than six (polyarch) in monocot root.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the characteristics of meristematic tissues is INCORRECT?
options: Cells possess a large, conspicuous nucleus and dense cytoplasm.
Cells exhibit high metabolic activity with numerous plasmodesmata connections.
Cells possess thin primary cell walls made of cellulose.
Cells contain large vacuoles to provide turgor pressure for rapid cell expansion.
questions.explanation: Meristematic cells are characterized by small vacuoles or the absence of vacuoles, as they are actively dividing. Large vacuoles are typical of mature, differentiated cells, not meristematic ones.
questions.ncertEvidence: Meristematic cells have dense cytoplasm and a conspicuous nucleus; vacuoles are usually absent.

questions.question: Regarding the anatomy of dicot and monocot roots, identify the statement that DOES NOT apply to both.
options: Presence of a single-layered epidermis with root hairs.
Presence of a well-developed pith in the center of the stele.
Presence of a cortex composed of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces.
Presence of an endodermis characterized by Casparian strips.
questions.explanation: In dicot roots, the pith is either small or completely absent. In contrast, monocot roots have a large and well-developed pith.
questions.ncertEvidence: Pith is small or inconspicuous in dicot root, whereas it is large and well developed in monocot root.

questions.question: Which feature is NOT a characteristic of the vascular bundles in a typical dicot stem?
options: They are arranged in a ring.
They are surrounded by a bundle sheath of sclerenchyma.
They are open, possessing a cambium between xylem and phloem.
questions.explanation: Bundle sheaths are characteristic of monocot stems (where bundles are scattered and surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheath) and C4 plants (Kranz anatomy). Dicot stems have open vascular bundles arranged in a ring.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot stem, vascular bundles are arranged in a ring; in monocot stem, vascular bundles are scattered and each is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath.

questions.question: Select the option that does not correctly describe the components of the phloem in angiosperms.
options: Sieve tube elements are living, but lack a nucleus at maturity.
Companion cells are specialized parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements.
Phloem fibers are the only dead component of the phloem and are absent in primary phloem.
Phloem parenchyma is present in all monocots and dicots.
questions.explanation: Phloem parenchyma is absent in most monocots. It is generally present in dicotyledonous plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering cylindrical cells... it is absent in most of the monocotyledons.

questions.question: Identify the statement that is FALSE regarding the secondary growth in dicot stems.
options: The vascular cambium activity is more active towards the inner side than the outer side.
The intrafascicular cambium and interfascicular cambium form a complete cambial ring.
Secondary xylem produced by the cambium is called wood.
The phellogen cuts off cells only towards the inner side to form the phelloderm.
questions.explanation: Phellogen (cork cambium) cuts off cells on both sides: the outer side forms the phellem (cork) and the inner side forms the phelloderm (secondary cortex).
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the leaf anatomy in a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf?
options: Presence of bulliform cells in the upper epidermis.
Differentiation of mesophyll into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
Stomata are generally more abundant on the abaxial surface.
Vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells.
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells are specialized large, empty, colorless cells found in the upper epidermis of isobilateral (monocot) leaves, not dicot leaves.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells.

questions.question: In the context of the root apical meristem, which statement is INCORRECT?
options: The root cap is formed by the calyptrogen.
The quiescent center consists of cells with very high division rates.
The dermatogen gives rise to the epidermis (epiblema).
The plerome gives rise to the stele.
questions.explanation: The quiescent center is a region in the root apical meristem where cells have a very low or inactive rate of cell division, acting as a reservoir of cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quiescent center is a region of inactive meristematic cells.

questions.question: Identify the feature that is NOT associated with the anatomy of a monocot stem.
options: Vascular bundles are scattered in the ground tissue.
Vascular bundles are closed, lacking cambium.
Water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles.
Secondary growth occurs due to the activity of the interfascicular cambium.
questions.explanation: Monocot stems lack cambium in their vascular bundles (closed bundles) and therefore do not undergo secondary growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monocot stem has scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath... vascular bundles are closed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true regarding the endodermis of a dicot root?
options: It is the innermost layer of the cortex.
It contains Casparian strips made of suberin.
It is responsible for regulating the flow of water and solutes into the stele.
It is characterized by the presence of large intercellular spaces to facilitate gas exchange.
questions.explanation: The endodermis cells are compactly arranged without any intercellular spaces, which is essential for the function of the Casparian strip in controlling water movement.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of endodermis are closely packed without any intercellular spaces.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the cork cambium (phellogen) is INCORRECT?
options: It is a meristematic tissue that develops in the cortex region.
It is responsible for the formation of periderm.
It cuts off cells on the outer side to form the secondary cortex.
It is formed due to the dedifferentiation of cortical cells.
questions.explanation: The phellogen cuts off cells on the outer side to form phellem (cork), and cells on the inner side to form phelloderm (secondary cortex).
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is primarily responsible for the mechanical support of growing parts of young dicotyledonous stems?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous stems and provides mechanical support to the growing parts.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Collenchyma section.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement regarding the structural nature of sieve tube elements in mature angiosperms.
options: They lack a nucleus but possess peripheral cytoplasm
They contain a large central vacuole and nucleus
They are dead cells at maturity
They are devoid of both cytoplasm and nucleus
questions.explanation: Mature sieve tube elements possess peripheral cytoplasm and a large central vacuole but lack a nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Phloem section.

questions.question: In a dorsiventral leaf, what is the specific location of the palisade parenchyma?
questions.explanation: In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the mesophyll is differentiated into palisade parenchyma placed adaxially and spongy parenchyma placed abaxially.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Leaf.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes the vascular bundles of monocot stems from dicot stems?
questions.explanation: Monocot stem vascular bundles are closed (lack cambium), whereas dicot stems have open bundles with cambium.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Anatomy of Monocotyledonous Stem.

questions.question: What is the characteristic feature of the endodermis in the root of a plant?
questions.explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis, which is characterized by the presence of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Root.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the bulliform cells found in the leaves of grasses?
options: Rolling of leaves to minimize water loss
questions.explanation: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells, which help in the rolling of leaves to minimize water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Anatomy of Monocotyledonous Leaf.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the secondary xylem (wood) produced by the cambium?
options: It is produced towards the inner side
It is produced towards the outer side
It is formed by the activity of the cork cambium
It consists of sieve tubes and companion cells
questions.explanation: The vascular cambium cells divide to form cells towards the pith (inner side) that mature into secondary xylem.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Secondary Growth.

questions.question: What characterizes the 'phellem' layer in the periderm?
options: It is the cork, which is suberized and dead
It is the secondary cortex, which is thin-walled
It is the actively dividing cork cambium
It consists of living parenchyma cells
questions.explanation: The phellogen (cork cambium) cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into phellem (cork), which is suberized and dead.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Periderm.

questions.question: Identify the type of vascular bundle where xylem and phloem are arranged in an alternate manner on different radii.
questions.explanation: In roots, xylem and phloem are arranged in an alternate manner on different radii, which is known as a radial vascular bundle.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Vascular System.

questions.question: Why is heartwood dark in color compared to sapwood?
options: Deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, and oils
Increased presence of living parenchyma cells
questions.explanation: The heartwood is dark in color due to the deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances, and essential oils in the central/innermost layers of secondary xylem.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants - Heartwood and Sapwood.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of parenchyma cells in plants?
options: Their walls are thin and made of cellulose
They possess heavily lignified secondary cell walls
They are primarily responsible for mechanical support
questions.explanation: Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls made of cellulose. They may be oval, spherical, or polygonal in shape and are generally living.
questions.ncertEvidence: Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls made of cellulose.

questions.question: In dicot stems, the cells of the cambium present between primary xylem and primary phloem is called:
questions.explanation: The cambium present inside the vascular bundle between primary xylem and primary phloem is known as intrafascicular cambium.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of cambium present between primary xylem and primary phloem is the intrafascicular cambium.

questions.question: Which feature is absent in the root of a monocotyledonous plant?
questions.explanation: Monocot roots do not undergo secondary growth. Secondary growth is a characteristic feature of dicot roots and stems.
questions.ncertEvidence: Monocotyledonous root does not undergo any secondary growth.

questions.question: The Casparian strips are found in the:
questions.explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces, and its tangential and radial walls have deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips.
questions.ncertEvidence: The tangential and radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material-suberin-in the form of casparian strips.

questions.question: Stomata are absent in:
questions.explanation: Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves and sometimes young stems, but they are absent in the epidermis of roots.
questions.ncertEvidence: Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange.

questions.question: Bulliform cells are found in:
questions.explanation: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about collenchyma tissue?
options: It provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant
It is found only in monocots
It lacks cellulose in its cell walls
questions.explanation: Collenchyma is a living mechanical tissue that provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant such as young stem and petiole of a leaf.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant, such as young stem and petiole of a leaf.

questions.question: The heartwood is characterized by:
options: It is dark in colour and resistant to microorganisms
It is light in colour and conducts water
It consists of living xylem elements
It is formed by the activity of cork cambium
questions.explanation: Heartwood is dark brown due to the deposition of tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances, and essential oils. These substances make it hard, durable, and resistant to the attacks of microorganisms and insects.
questions.ncertEvidence: The heartwood is dark in colour due to the deposition of tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the innermost layers of the stem.

questions.question: Which layer is known as phellogen?
questions.explanation: The cork cambium is a meristematic tissue that develops in the cortex region. It is also known as phellogen.
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen, a couple of layers thick, is made of narrow, thin-walled and nearly rectangular cells. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.question: The vascular bundles in dicot stems are described as:
questions.explanation: In dicot stems, vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral, and possess cambium between xylem and phloem, making them open.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot stem, vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral and open.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the characteristics of parenchyma cells is correct?
options: The cell walls are thin and made up of cellulose.
They are always specialized for the storage of food.
They typically possess thickened corners due to pectin deposition.
They are dead cells at maturity providing mechanical support.
questions.explanation: Parenchyma cells have thin cell walls made of cellulose. They may perform various functions like photosynthesis, storage, or secretion, but their structural definition is thin-walled living cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Parenchyma is the major component of organs; cells are generally isodiametric, thin-walled, and made of cellulose.

questions.question: Collenchyma is characterized by the localized deposition of which materials at the corners of the cells?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are characterized by localized thickening of the cell wall, which is composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collenchyma cells are much thickened at the corners due to a deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about sclereids?
options: They are a type of sclerenchyma with highly thickened, lignified walls and very narrow cavities.
They are living cells found in the fruit walls of nuts and pulp of guava.
They provide flexibility to the plant organs.
They are elongated cells found in the xylem of gymnosperms only.
questions.explanation: Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened, dead sclerenchymatous cells with very narrow cavities (lumens).
questions.ncertEvidence: Sclereids are spherical, oval or cylindrical, highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities (lumens).

questions.question: In roots, the xylem is described as exarch. What does this mean?
options: The protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the center.
The protoxylem lies towards the center and metaxylem towards the periphery.
The protoxylem and metaxylem are arranged in a ring.
The protoxylem is absent in the primary root.
questions.explanation: Exarch condition refers to the arrangement where protoxylem is towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the center, which is characteristic of roots.
questions.ncertEvidence: In roots, the protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the companion cells associated with sieve tube elements?
options: They help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.
They provide mechanical strength to the phloem.
They undergo apoptosis to form the sieve plates.
questions.explanation: Companion cells are specialized parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements and help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells that are closely associated with sieve tube elements and help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.

questions.question: Which tissue system in plants provides the main site for photosynthesis and storage?
questions.explanation: The ground tissue system includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles. It is the main site for photosynthesis, storage, and mechanical support.
questions.ncertEvidence: The ground tissue system forms the main bulk of the plant; it includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles.

questions.question: What is the distinguishing feature of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf?
options: Stomata are generally present more on the abaxial surface.
Stomata are present equally on both surfaces.
The mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
The vascular bundles are of similar sizes throughout.
questions.explanation: In a dorsiventral leaf (dicot), the abaxial surface generally bears more stomata than the adaxial surface.
questions.ncertEvidence: In a dorsiventral leaf, the abaxial surface generally bears more stomata than the adaxial surface.

questions.question: What is responsible for the formation of annual rings in woody trees?
options: Seasonal activity of the vascular cambium.
The activity of the primary meristem.
questions.explanation: Annual rings are formed due to the differential activity of the vascular cambium during different seasons of the year.
questions.ncertEvidence: The activity of cambium is under the control of many physiological and environmental factors... the kinds of wood formed during these seasons are spring wood and autumn wood, forming annual rings.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is responsible for the gaseous exchange in the bark of woody stems?
questions.explanation: Lenticels are lens-shaped openings that permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem.
questions.ncertEvidence: At certain regions, the phellogen cuts off closely arranged parenchymatous cells on the outer side instead of cork cells. These parenchymatous cells soon rupture the epidermis, forming a lens-shaped openings called lenticels.

questions.question: In a dicot root, the initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in which tissue?
questions.explanation: The pericycle is the layer from which lateral roots and part of the vascular cambium in dicot roots originate.
questions.ncertEvidence: Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in these cells (pericycle).

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of collenchyma cells?
options: Deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin at corners
Presence of thin, cellulosic cell walls with no intercellular spaces
Lignified cell walls with narrow lumen
Cells are dead at maturity and provide only mechanical support
questions.explanation: Collenchyma is characterized by the deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin at the corners of the cells, providing mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collenchyma cells are much thickened at the corners due to a deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin.

questions.question: In roots, the protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. This arrangement is called:
questions.explanation: When the protoxylem is directed towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the center, the arrangement is known as exarch, which is typical of roots.
questions.ncertEvidence: In roots, the protoxylem lies towards periphery and metaxylem lies towards the centre. Such arrangement of primary xylem is called exarch.

questions.question: Which tissue system includes all tissues formed outside the vascular cambium?
questions.explanation: Bark is a non-technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium, including secondary phloem, periderm, and phellem.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bark is a non-technical term that refer to all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium, therefore including secondary phloem.

questions.question: The casparian strips are found in which layer of the dicot root?
questions.explanation: The endodermis of the root is characterized by the presence of Casparian strips, which are water-impermeable waxy material depositions of suberin.
questions.ncertEvidence: The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material-suberin-in the form of casparian strips.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bulliform cells is correct?
options: They are large, empty, colourless cells in the epidermis of grasses
They are responsible for the secondary growth in monocots
They are involved in the secretion of resins and oils
They are specialized phloem parenchyma cells
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells present in the adaxial epidermis of grass leaves. They help in the rolling of leaves to minimize water loss.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells.

questions.question: Which cells are responsible for the formation of the phellogen during secondary growth in dicot stems?
questions.explanation: The phellogen (cork cambium) develops from the cortical cells as the stem undergoes secondary growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen is a couple of layers thick. It is made of narrow, thin-walled and nearly rectangular cells. Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into phellem (cork) while the inner cells differentiate into phelloderm.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the companion cells?
options: They are specialized parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements
They are dead cells that provide mechanical support
They contain large vacuoles but no nucleus
They are found only in gymnosperms
questions.explanation: Companion cells are specialized parenchymatous cells that are closely associated with sieve tube elements and maintain the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: The companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells that are closely associated with sieve tube elements.

questions.question: The 'conjunctive tissue' in dicot roots refers to:
options: Parenchymatous cells lying between xylem and phloem
The layer of cells just below the epidermis
questions.explanation: In dicot roots, the parenchymatous tissue that lies between the xylem and the phloem bundles is called the conjunctive tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and phloem are called conjunctive tissue.

questions.question: Heartwood is characterized by:
options: Deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, and oils
Active conduction of water and minerals
Being the peripheral region of secondary xylem
Presence of living protoplast in all cells
questions.explanation: Heartwood is the dark-coloured, central region of the secondary xylem that is non-functional for conduction due to the deposition of organic substances like tannins, resins, oils, gums, and aromatic substances.
questions.ncertEvidence: In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem.

questions.question: In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells. Which of the following statements regarding these cells is correct?
options: They are responsible for the radial conduction of water
They are absent in the veins of the leaf
They contain chloroplasts in C3 plants
They are composed of collenchyma cells
questions.explanation: In dorsiventral leaves, vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells which facilitate the radial conduction of water.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Leaf section

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is primarily responsible for providing mechanical support to the growing parts of a plant, such as a young stem and petiole of a leaf?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to the growing parts of the plant, such as young stems and the petiole of a leaf.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, The Tissues section, Collenchyma

questions.question: A student observes a transverse section of a stem and identifies vascular bundles that are scattered, surrounded by a large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue, and lack a bundle sheath. This stem most likely belongs to:
questions.explanation: Monocot stems have scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, but the ground tissue is not differentiated into cortex and pericycle.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Monocotyledonous Stem section

questions.question: In dicot roots, the initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in the:
questions.explanation: The pericycle cells in dicot roots are responsible for the initiation of lateral roots and the vascular cambium during secondary growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Root section

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the endodermis in a dicot root?
options: Presence of Casparian strips on radial and tangential walls
Presence of starch grains in all cells
questions.explanation: The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis, which comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells characterized by water-impermeable waxy material suberin in the form of Casparian strips.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Root section

questions.question: The 'wood' in plants is technically referred to as:
questions.explanation: Secondary xylem is commonly known as wood.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Secondary Growth section

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the arrangement of vascular bundles in a dicot stem?
questions.explanation: In dicot stems, the vascular bundles are arranged in a ring, which is a characteristic feature of their primary structure.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Stem section

questions.question: Phellem, phellogen, and phelloderm are collectively known as:
questions.explanation: Phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Secondary Growth section

questions.question: Bulliform cells are specialized epidermal cells found in the leaves of many grasses. Their primary function is:
options: Rolling of leaves to minimize water loss
questions.explanation: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells called bulliform cells, which help in the rolling of leaves to minimize water loss during water stress.
questions.ncertEvidence: Anatomy of Flowering Plants, Anatomy of Monocotyledonous Leaf section

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is characterized by cells that are living, possess thin cellulosic cell walls, and are generally isodiametric in shape?
questions.explanation: Parenchyma cells are living, possess thin cellulosic walls, and are isodiametric. Collenchyma cells have thickened corners, while sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity.
questions.ncertEvidence: Parenchyma is the primary constituent within plants; cells are generally isodiametric, thin-walled, and living.

questions.question: In dicot stems, the cells of the endodermis are rich in which of the following substances?
questions.explanation: The endodermis of the dicot stem is also referred to as the starch sheath because its cells are rich in starch grains.
questions.ncertEvidence: The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. The cells of the endodermis are rich in starch grains and the layer is also referred to as the starch sheath.

questions.question: Which type of vascular bundles are found in monocot stems?
questions.explanation: Monocot stems possess conjoint, collateral, and closed vascular bundles, meaning cambium is absent.
questions.ncertEvidence: In monocot stem, vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.

questions.question: Bulliform cells are specialized cells found in the leaves of many grasses. What is their primary function?
options: Water storage and leaf rolling to minimize water loss
questions.explanation: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colorless cells present in the upper epidermis of grasses that help in rolling the leaf during water stress.
questions.ncertEvidence: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells. When the bulliform cells in the leaves have absorbed water and are turgid, the leaf surface is exposed. When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.

questions.question: The 'wood' in a plant refers to which of the following tissues?
questions.explanation: Secondary xylem produced by the vascular cambium constitutes the wood in dicot plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: The wood is technically secondary xylem.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the phloem in angiosperms?
options: Presence of sieve cells instead of sieve tubes
questions.explanation: Angiosperm phloem contains sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers. Gymnosperms lack sieve tubes and companion cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Angiosperms have sieve tube elements and companion cells and have phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

questions.question: Which layer of the root is known as the 'starch sheath' equivalent in stems, but specifically in roots, it contains Casparian strips?
questions.explanation: The endodermis of roots is characterized by the presence of Casparian strips made of suberin.
questions.ncertEvidence: The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips.

questions.question: What is the result of the activity of the cork cambium (phellogen) on its inner side?
questions.explanation: Phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork (phellem), and the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex (phelloderm).
questions.ncertEvidence: The phellogen cuts off cells on both sides. The outer cells differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the vascular bundles in a dicot root?
options: They are radial and xylem is exarch
They are conjoint and xylem is endarch
They are radial and xylem is endarch
They are conjoint and xylem is exarch
questions.explanation: Dicot roots have radial vascular bundles where xylem and phloem are arranged in an alternate manner on different radii, and the protoxylem is directed towards the periphery (exarch).
questions.ncertEvidence: In dicot root, there are usually two to four xylem and phloem patches. Later an cambium ring develops between the xylem and phloem. Such bundles are different types of vascular bundles. ... xylem is exarch.

questions.question: Which cells are responsible for the regulation of the opening and closing of stomata?
questions.explanation: Guard cells are specialized epidermal cells that regulate the opening and closing of stomata.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue is primarily found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, where a delicate lining is required?
questions.explanation: Squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. They are found in the walls of blood vessels and air-sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary.

questions.question: In which of the following locations are ciliated columnar epithelial cells typically found in the human body?
options: Ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons
Inner surface of hollow organs like bronchi
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is found in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes to move particles or mucus in a specific direction.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: Identify the feature that distinguishes compound epithelium from simple epithelium.
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption, providing protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.

questions.question: Which of the following cell junctions facilitates the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells?
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.question: Which type of connective tissue contains fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells, and is located beneath the skin?
questions.explanation: Areolar connective tissue is present beneath the skin and serves as a support framework for epithelium, containing fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.

questions.question: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many:
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, and the cells present are fibroblasts.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding smooth muscle fibers is correct?
options: They are fusiform and taper at both ends
They are attached to bones via tendons
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (spindle-shaped) and taper at both ends (fusiform). They do not show striations and are involuntary.
questions.ncertEvidence: The smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform) and do not show striations. Cell junctions hold them together and they are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath.

questions.question: Which component of the neuron provides protection and support to the nerve cells?
questions.explanation: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and protect and support neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and protect and support neurons.

questions.question: The cockroach, Periplaneta americana, has a body divisible into three distinct regions. These are:
questions.explanation: The body of the cockroach is segmented and divisible into three distinct regions: head, thorax, and abdomen.
questions.ncertEvidence: The entire body is covered by a hard chitinous exoskeleton (brown in colour). In each segment, exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites... The body of the cockroach is segmented and divisible into three distinct regions: head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.question: In male cockroaches, which of the following structures are present exclusively on the 9th sternum?
options: A pair of short, thread-like anal styles
A pair of jointed anal cerci
questions.explanation: Anal styles are present only in male cockroaches and are located on the 9th sternum, while anal cerci are present in both sexes.
questions.ncertEvidence: In males, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9th and 10th terga and ventrally by the 9th sternum. It contains dorsal anus, ventral male genital pore and gonapophysis. In males, genital pouch bears a pair of short, thread-like anal styles which are absent in females.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding epithelial tissues is correct according to NCERT?
options: Epithelial tissues have a free surface which faces either a body fluid or the outside environment.
The cells in epithelial tissue are loosely packed with a large amount of intercellular matrix.
Simple epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and functions in protection.
Compound epithelium is primarily involved in absorption and secretion.
questions.explanation: Simple epithelium is composed of a single layer of cells. Compound epithelium is multi-layered and provides protection. Epithelial cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: Epithelial tissue has a free surface, which faces either a body fluid or the outside environment and thus provides a covering or a lining for some part of the body.

questions.question: Where are ciliated columnar epithelial cells primarily found in the human body?
options: Blood vessel linings and air sacs of lungs
Ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons
Inner surface of the stomach and intestine
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is found in the bronchioles and the fallopian tubes to move particles or mucus in a specific direction.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: Which type of cell junction helps to stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions perform a cementing function to keep neighboring cells together and prevent leakage.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of areolar connective tissue?
options: It serves as a support framework for epithelium.
It is classified as a dense connective tissue.
It is found primarily in tendons and ligaments.
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is present beneath the skin and serves as a support framework for epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium.

questions.question: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibers are present in:
options: Rows between many parallel bundles of fibers
A matrix rich in hyaluronic acid
Loose networks dispersed throughout the tissue
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibers are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following cells are responsible for secreting fibers of structural proteins in connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are cells that produce and secrete fibers like collagen and elastin.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: Which muscle tissue is characterized by the presence of intercalated discs?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together, called intercalated discs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit.

questions.question: What is the primary function of neuroglial cells in the neural tissue?
options: Provide insulation to the blood vessels
questions.explanation: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and protect and support neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and protect and support neurons.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about smooth muscle fibers?
options: They are branched and have intercalated discs
They are attached to bones by tendons
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (taper at both ends) and do not show striations; they are involuntary.
questions.ncertEvidence: The smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform) and do not show striations. Cell junctions hold them together and they are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath.

questions.question: Which of the following connective tissues stores fat?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin, specialized to store fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding epithelial tissues: (I) The cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix. (II) They always rest on a basement membrane. (III) Blood vessels are abundant in epithelial tissue to provide nutrients. Which of the following is correct?
options: Only I and II are correct
Only II and III are correct
Only I and III are correct
