questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues are avascular; they lack blood vessels and receive nutrients via diffusion from the underlying connective tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Epithelial tissue is avascular and rests on a non-cellular basement membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the structural differences between endocrine and exocrine glands?
options: Exocrine glands secrete products into ducts, whereas endocrine glands are ductless
Exocrine glands are ductless, whereas endocrine glands secrete products into ducts
Both secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland
Both have ducts but differ in the type of secretion
questions.explanation: Exocrine glands secrete mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, digestive enzymes, and other cell products via ducts or tubes. Endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland.
questions.ncertEvidence: Exocrine glands secrete products through ducts or tubes. Endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

questions.question: Regarding the muscular tissue of the heart, identify the incorrect statement:
options: Intercalated discs function as boosters for contraction
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are uninucleated, branched, and involuntary. Multinucleated cells are characteristic of skeletal muscle.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the difference between tendons and ligaments?
options: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones; ligaments attach one bone to another
Tendons attach one bone to another; ligaments attach muscles to bones
Tendons are dense irregular; ligaments are dense regular
Both are types of loose connective tissue
questions.explanation: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones, and ligaments attach one bone to another. Both are dense regular connective tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tendons, which attach skeletal muscles to bones and ligaments which attach one bone to another are examples of dense regular connective tissue.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding the earthworm (Pheretima):
options: The clitellum is a prominent dark band of glandular tissue in segments 14-16
The pharynx is located in segments 1-3
The gizzard is responsible for digestion of proteins
Calciferous glands are found in the intestine
questions.explanation: In earthworms, the clitellum is a prominent dark band of glandular tissue occurring in segments 14-16. The gizzard (segments 8-9) grinds soil particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the earthworm, a prominent dark band of glandular and sticky skin called clitellum is present in the segments 14-16.

questions.question: In the cockroach (Periplaneta americana), which mouthpart acts like a tongue?
questions.explanation: The hypopharynx acts as a tongue within the cavity enclosed by the mouthparts of the cockroach.
questions.ncertEvidence: A median flexible lobe acting as tongue (hypopharynx) lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouthparts.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the cockroach: (I) Malpighian tubules are 100-150 in number. (II) They are lined by glandular and ciliated cells. (III) They absorb nitrogenous waste products. Which of these are correct?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are 100-150 in number, yellow, thread-like structures. They are lined by glandular and ciliated cells and absorb nitrogenous waste products to convert them into uric acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: Malpighian tubules are 100-150 in number, yellow, thread-like structures. They are lined by glandular and ciliated cells and absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut.

questions.question: The blood vascular system of the earthworm is:
questions.explanation: Earthworms have a closed type of blood vascular system, consisting of heart, blood vessels and capillaries.
questions.ncertEvidence: Earthworm exhibits closed type of blood vascular system, consisting of heart, blood vessels and capillaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the connective tissue matrix?
options: The matrix is always fibrous protein
The matrix is composed of collagen only
The matrix is composed of elastin only
questions.explanation: In connective tissues, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin, and the matrix is modified polysaccharides.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. The fibres provide strength, elasticity and flexibility to the tissue. These cells also secrete modified polysaccharides, which accumulate between cells and fibres and act as matrix.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Epithelial tissues are characterised by very little intercellular matrix. Reason (R): The cells in epithelial tissue are compactly packed with minimal intercellular spaces.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue consists of cells arranged in one or more layers, compactly packed with little intercellular matrix, forming a continuous sheet.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Epithelial Tissue Characteristics.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Columnar epithelium is found in the lining of the stomach and intestine. Reason (R): The primary function of columnar epithelium is protection against chemical and mechanical stress.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Columnar epithelium is indeed found in the stomach and intestine, but its primary function in these locations is secretion and absorption, not protection.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Columnar Epithelium location and function.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Connective tissues are the most abundant and widely distributed in the body of complex animals. Reason (R): They are named 'connective' because they exclusively link bones to muscles.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Connective tissues are the most abundant, but they are named 'connective' because they link and support other tissues/organs of the body, not just bones to muscles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Introduction to Connective Tissue.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones. Reason (R): Tendons are a type of dense irregular connective tissue.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Tendons attach skeletal muscle to bone, but they are composed of dense regular connective tissue, not dense irregular.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Dense Connective Tissue classification.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Smooth muscle fibres taper at both ends (fusiform). Reason (R): Smooth muscle fibres show striations and are under voluntary control.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Smooth muscles are non-striated and involuntary. They are fusiform (spindle-shaped).
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Smooth Muscle characteristics.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Intercalated discs are essential features of cardiac muscle fibres. Reason (R): These discs function as boosters for muscle contraction, allowing cells to contract as a unit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are communication junctions that allow cardiac muscle cells to contract as a unit by transmitting signals efficiently.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Cardiac Muscle properties.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cockroaches are dioecious. Reason (R): Both male and female reproductive organs are present in the same individual in cockroaches.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cockroaches are dioecious, meaning sexes are separate. They are not hermaphrodites.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Reproductive system of Cockroach.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Malpighian tubules are the primary excretory organs of the cockroach. Reason (R): They help in the removal of excretory products from the haemolymph.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are yellow coloured, thin filamentous tubules that absorb nitrogenous waste from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Excretory system of Cockroach.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Earthworms have a closed circulatory system. Reason (R): Blood is confined to the heart and blood vessels in earthworms.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Earthworms possess a closed circulatory system where blood remains confined within the heart and blood vessels.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Circulatory system of Earthworm.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The gizzard in an earthworm is used for the grinding of food particles. Reason (R): The gizzard is located in the 8th-9th segment of the earthworm.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The gizzard is indeed used for grinding food (soil particles), but it is located in the 8th-9th segment in the earthworm's digestive tract.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Digestive system of Earthworm.

questions.question:
Match the following epithelial tissues with their primary locations in the body:

A. Squamous epithelium   i. Ducts of glands
B. Cuboidal epithelium   ii. Blood vessel walls
C. Columnar epithelium   iii. Fallopian tubes
D. Ciliated epithelium  iv. Stomach lining
questions.explanation: Squamous forms the lining of blood vessels, cuboidal is found in gland ducts, columnar lines the stomach/intestine, and ciliated lines structures like Fallopian tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2 Epithelial Tissue

questions.question:
Match the connective tissue types with their specific examples:

A. Loose connective   i. Tendons
B. Dense regular      ii. Bone
C. Dense irregular    iii. Areolar tissue
D. Specialized       iv. Skin
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue. Tendons are dense regular, skin dermis is dense irregular, and bone is specialized connective tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3 Connective Tissue

questions.question:
Match the muscle tissue characteristics with their features:

A. Skeletal muscle    i. Involuntary, branched
B. Smooth muscle      ii. Voluntary, striated
C. Cardiac muscle     iii. Involuntary, spindle-shaped
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscles are voluntary and striated; Smooth muscles are spindle-shaped and involuntary; Cardiac muscles are branched and involuntary.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4 Muscle Tissue

questions.question:
Match the following cell junctions with their functions:

A. Tight junctions     i. Cementing neighboring cells
B. Adhering junctions  ii. Preventing substance leakage
C. Gap junctions      iii. Facilitating communication
questions.explanation: Tight junctions prevent leakage, adhering junctions cement cells together, and gap junctions allow ionic/small molecule communication.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1 Cell Junctions

questions.question:
Match the cockroach organ systems with their structures:

A. Excretory system    i. Malpighian tubules
B. Reproductive system  ii. Mushroom gland
C. Circulatory system   iii. Alary muscles
D. Respiratory system   iv. Tracheae
questions.explanation: Cockroach excretion is via Malpighian tubules, reproduction uses mushroom glands in males, circulation utilizes alary muscles, and respiration via tracheae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.5 Cockroach

questions.question:
Match the following components of the cockroach alimentary canal with their function/location:

A. Gizzard        i. Storage of food
B. Crop           ii. Grinding food
C. Hepatic caeca  iii. Digestive juice secretion
D. Ileum          iv. Anterior part of hindgut
questions.explanation: Gizzard grinds food, crop stores it, hepatic caeca secrete digestive juices, and ileum is the first segment of the hindgut.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.5.3 Alimentary canal

questions.question:
Match the types of glands with their secretory nature:

A. Exocrine gland    i. Hormones via blood
B. Endocrine gland   ii. Mucus/Saliva via ducts
C. Heterocrine gland iii. Both exocrine and endocrine functions
questions.explanation: Exocrine glands secrete products through ducts; endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones; heterocrine glands (like pancreas) perform both.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2 Epithelial Tissue

questions.question:
Match the connective tissue cells with their respective roles:

A. Fibroblasts     i. Secrete histamine/heparin
B. Macrophages    ii. Phagocytic action
C. Mast cells      iii. Produce fibers
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts produce fibers, macrophages are phagocytic cells, and mast cells secrete histamine and heparin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3 Connective Tissue

questions.question:
Match the cockroach head appendages with their corresponding functions:

A. Mandibles       i. Tasting
B. Maxillae        ii. Grinding
C. Labrum          iii. Holding food
D. Labium          iv. Upper lip
questions.explanation: Mandibles are for grinding, maxillae assist in holding food, labrum is the upper lip, and labium is the lower lip with sensory functions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.5.2 Mouthparts

questions.question:
Match the following epithelial tissue modifications with their structures:

A. Microvilli        i. Increase surface area
B. Cilia            ii. Move particles/mucus
C. Stereocilia       iii. Absorption in epididymis
questions.explanation: Microvilli increase surface area for absorption; cilia move particles/mucus; stereocilia are non-motile structures found in the epididymis.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2 Epithelial Tissue

questions.question: Arrange the following steps of cockroach blood circulation in the correct chronological sequence starting from the heart.
options: Heart -> Perivisceral sinus -> Pericardial sinus -> Ostia
Heart -> Pericardial sinus -> Perivisceral sinus -> Ostia
Heart -> Ostia -> Perivisceral sinus -> Pericardial sinus
Heart -> Perivisceral sinus -> Ostia -> Pericardial sinus
questions.explanation: Blood from the heart is pumped into sinuses (perivisceral and perineural). It then reaches the pericardial sinus and enters the heart through ostia.
questions.ncertEvidence: The blood from sinuses enter heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to sinuses again.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of layers in the wall of the alimentary canal of the cockroach from the lumen outwards.
options: Cuticle -> Epithelium -> Basement membrane -> Circular muscles -> Longitudinal muscles
Cuticle -> Epithelium -> Basement membrane -> Longitudinal muscles -> Circular muscles
Epithelium -> Cuticle -> Basement membrane -> Circular muscles -> Longitudinal muscles
Basement membrane -> Epithelium -> Cuticle -> Circular muscles -> Longitudinal muscles
questions.explanation: The wall of the alimentary canal of cockroach consists of an inner lining of cuticle, followed by epithelium, basement membrane, circular muscles, and outer longitudinal muscles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The wall of the alimentary canal of cockroach consists of an inner lining of cuticle, followed by epithelium, basement membrane, circular muscles and outer longitudinal muscles.

questions.question: Sequence the following parts of the cockroach digestive system in the order that food passes through during digestion.
options: Crop -> Gizzard -> Hepatic caeca -> Mesenteron -> Ileum
Gizzard -> Crop -> Hepatic caeca -> Mesenteron -> Ileum
Crop -> Hepatic caeca -> Gizzard -> Mesenteron -> Colon
questions.explanation: Food enters the crop for storage, moves to the gizzard for grinding, then to the mesenteron (midgut) where hepatic caeca secrete digestive juices.
questions.ncertEvidence: The food enters the crop for storage and then to gizzard. The midgut is lined by glandular epithelium.

questions.question: Arrange the following developmental stages of Periplaneta americana in correct chronological order.
questions.explanation: Cockroaches undergo paurometabolous development, meaning development is through the nymphal stage, not a pupal stage.
questions.ncertEvidence: The development of P. americana is paurometabolous, meaning that there is development through nymphal stage.

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence of structures encountered by air as it enters the cockroach tracheal system.
questions.explanation: Air enters through spiracles, travels into the tracheal tubes, subdivides into tracheoles, and finally reaches the tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: The oxygen enters the body through 10 pairs of spiracles... the tracheoles carry oxygen to the air spaces in the tissues.

questions.question: Arrange the following parts of the male reproductive system of a cockroach in the sequence of sperm transport.
options: Testes -> Seminal vesicles -> Ejaculatory duct -> Phallic gland
Testes -> Ejaculatory duct -> Seminal vesicles -> Phallic gland
Seminal vesicles -> Testes -> Ejaculatory duct -> Phallic gland
Testes -> Phallic gland -> Seminal vesicles -> Ejaculatory duct
questions.explanation: Sperms are produced in the testes, stored in seminal vesicles, and travel through the ejaculatory duct to the male gonopore.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores which are discharged during copulation.

questions.question: Sequence the layers of the skin from the outer surface to the inner layers in mammals.
questions.explanation: The skin consists of the outer epidermis, the underlying dermis, and the deeper subcutaneous tissue (hypodermis).
questions.ncertEvidence: Skin is the outer covering of the body. It consists of epidermis and dermis.

questions.question: Arrange the components of a reflex arc in the correct sequence of signal transmission.
options: Receptor -> Sensory neuron -> Integration center -> Motor neuron -> Effector
Receptor -> Motor neuron -> Integration center -> Sensory neuron -> Effector
Effector -> Sensory neuron -> Integration center -> Motor neuron -> Receptor
Sensory neuron -> Receptor -> Integration center -> Effector -> Motor neuron
questions.explanation: A reflex arc involves a receptor, a sensory afferent neuron, an integration center in the CNS, a motor efferent neuron, and an effector organ.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neural system provides an organised network of point-to-point connections for a quick coordination.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of stages in the formation of a cockroach spermatophore?
options: Testes -> Seminal vesicles -> Mushroom gland -> Ejaculatory duct
Testes -> Mushroom gland -> Seminal vesicles -> Ejaculatory duct
Mushroom gland -> Testes -> Seminal vesicles -> Ejaculatory duct
Testes -> Seminal vesicles -> Ejaculatory duct -> Mushroom gland
questions.explanation: Sperms are produced in testes, stored in seminal vesicles, and encapsulated by secretions from the mushroom gland before ejaculation.
questions.ncertEvidence: The seminal vesicles store sperms. The mushroom gland is an accessory reproductive gland.

questions.question: Sequence the passage of food in the earthworm's digestive tract.
options: Mouth -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Stomach -> Intestine
Mouth -> Oesophagus -> Pharynx -> Gizzard -> Stomach -> Intestine
Mouth -> Pharynx -> Gizzard -> Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Intestine
Mouth -> Gizzard -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Intestine
questions.explanation: In earthworms, food passes from the mouth to the pharynx, then the oesophagus, into the gizzard (grinding), then the stomach, and finally the intestine.
questions.ncertEvidence: The alimentary canal is a straight tube and runs between first to last segment of the body. A terminal mouth opens into the buccal cavity leads into pharynx, oesophagus, gizzard, stomach, and intestine.

questions.question: In the diagram of the alimentary canal of the cockroach, which label represents the 'Hepatic caecae' which secretes digestive juice?
options: A structure at the junction of foregut and midgut
A structure at the junction of midgut and hindgut
questions.explanation: Hepatic caecae are a ring of 6-8 blind tubules present at the junction of the foregut and midgut in a cockroach, which secrete digestive juice.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Alimentary canal of cockroach.

questions.question: In the diagram of the cockroach reproductive system, the structure labeled as 'Seminal vesicle' stores sperms in which form?
questions.explanation: In the male reproductive system of the cockroach, sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Reproductive system of cockroach.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the cross-section of a bone, the central space containing bone marrow is labeled. What is this space called?
questions.explanation: The marrow cavity is the space in the center of the bone that contains bone marrow.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.2: Skeletal connective tissue.

questions.question: In a diagram of simple squamous epithelium, which feature correctly describes the appearance of the cells?
options: Single layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.1.1: Epithelial tissue.

questions.question: In a diagram of a cockroach's head, which label points to the structure that acts as a sensory organ and helps in monitoring the environment?
questions.explanation: Antennae have sensory receptors that help in monitoring the environment of the cockroach.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Morphology of cockroach.

questions.question: In a diagrammatic representation of a neuron, the label pointing to the branched processes that receive information is:
questions.explanation: Dendrites are the branched processes of a neuron that receive impulses from other neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.1.4: Neural tissue.

questions.question: In the diagram of the Malpighian tubules of a cockroach, where are they located?
options: At the junction of midgut and hindgut
At the junction of foregut and midgut
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of midgut and hindgut.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Excretory system of cockroach.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the structure of an areolar connective tissue, which type of cells are responsible for secreting fibres of structural proteins?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are cells present in areolar connective tissue that produce and secrete fibres.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.1: Areolar connective tissue.

questions.question: In a diagram of cockroach mouthparts, which structure is referred to as the 'upper lip'?
questions.explanation: The labrum is the upper lip of the cockroach's mouthparts.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Mouthparts of cockroach.

questions.question: In a diagram of the cockroach thorax, which segment bears the first pair of wings?
questions.explanation: The forewings (tegmina) arise from the mesothorax, while the hindwings arise from the metathorax.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.4: Anatomy of cockroach (Wings).

questions.question: In a diagrammatic representation of a cockroach's alimentary canal, the structure labeled as 'proventriculus' is primarily responsible for:
questions.explanation: The proventriculus (or gizzard) in a cockroach has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate-like teeth, which grind the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.3: The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.

questions.question: Looking at the diagram of the cockroach reproductive system, which structure is specifically involved in the formation of the ootheca?
questions.explanation: In female cockroaches, the secretions of the collaterial glands form a hard capsule called the ootheca around the eggs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.4: The secretion of these glands form a hard capsule around the eggs called oothecae.

questions.question: In a histological diagram of epithelial tissues, which junction is specifically shown connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions?
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.

questions.question: Identify the structure in a diagram of earthworm reproductive anatomy that serves as a storage site for sperms obtained from another earthworm during copulation.
questions.explanation: In earthworms, there are four pairs of spermathecae located in the 6th-9th segments. They receive and store spermatozoa during copulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.3: Four pairs of spermathecae are located in 6th-9th segments. They receive and store spermatozoa during copulation.

questions.question: In a diagram of the earthworm's alimentary canal, the typhlosole is a feature of which region?
questions.explanation: The intestine of the earthworm has a characteristic fold called the typhlosole, which increases the effective area of absorption.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.2: The intestine of earthworm has a characteristic fold called typhlosole that increases the effective area of absorption.

questions.question: If a diagram depicts the cross-section of a bone, what are the small spaces containing osteocytes called?
questions.explanation: In bone tissue, osteocytes are present in spaces called lacunae.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.3: The bone cells (osteocytes) are present in the spaces called lacunae.

questions.question: In a diagram of cockroach mouthparts, which structure functions like a tongue?
questions.explanation: The hypopharynx acts as a tongue and lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouthparts in a cockroach.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.2: A median flexible lobe acting as tongue (hypopharynx) lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouthparts.

questions.question: In a diagram of the earthworm, the clitellum is a prominent glandular thickening found in which segments?
questions.explanation: In the earthworm, segments 14-16 are covered by a prominent dark band of glandular tissue called the clitellum.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.1: In the earthworm, segments 14-16 are covered by a prominent dark band of glandular tissue called clitellum.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue, if shown in a diagram, is primarily found in the inner surface of bronchioles?
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: In a diagram of a nerve cell, which part receives impulses and transmits them towards the cell body?
questions.explanation: Dendrites are the branched processes of a neuron that receive impulses and transmit them towards the cell body.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.4: The dendrites are the branched processes of a neuron that receive impulses and transmit them towards the cell body.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is characterized by the presence of a 'typhlosole' in its intestine to increase the effective area of absorption?
questions.explanation: In Pheretima, the intestine from the 26th to the 35th segment (except the last few segments) contains an internal median fold of the dorsal wall called the typhlosole, which increases the surface area for absorption.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Earthworm section, Digestive system.

questions.question: In Periplaneta americana, the gizzard is responsible for:
questions.explanation: The gizzard in cockroaches has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and an inner thick cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate-like teeth, which grind the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Cockroach section, Digestive system.

questions.question: Which of the following structures in the male cockroach is responsible for the storage of sperms?
questions.explanation: In male cockroaches, sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Cockroach section, Reproductive system.

questions.question: Identify the organism where the respiratory system consists of a network of tracheae that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles.
questions.explanation: The respiratory system of the cockroach consists of a network of tracheae that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles present on the lateral side of the body.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Cockroach section, Respiratory system.

questions.question: In Pheretima, the blood glands are located in the:
questions.explanation: Blood glands are present on the 4th, 5th and 6th segments in the earthworm, which produce blood cells and hemoglobin which is dissolved in blood plasma.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Earthworm section, Circulatory system.

questions.question: The 'clitellum' in Pheretima is a prominent glandular thickening of the skin found in segments:
questions.explanation: The body of the earthworm is marked by segments. A prominent dark band of glandular tissue called clitellum covers segments 14-16.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Earthworm section, Morphology.

questions.question: Which of the following cells in the cockroach are analogous to the vertebrate liver in their function of excretion and storage of fat and glycogen?
questions.explanation: The fat body in cockroaches is responsible for the storage of fat, glycogen, and protein, performing functions similar to the vertebrate liver.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Cockroach section, Excretory system.

questions.question: In the frog (Rana tigrina), the skin serves as an accessory respiratory organ. This type of respiration is called:
questions.explanation: When the frog is in water, skin acts as an aquatic respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration). Dissolved oxygen in the water is exchanged through the skin by diffusion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Frog section, Respiratory system.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct path of food in the alimentary canal of the cockroach?
options: Mouth -> Pharynx -> Oesophagus -> Crop -> Gizzard -> Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum
Mouth -> Oesophagus -> Gizzard -> Crop -> Ileum -> Colon -> Rectum
Mouth -> Pharynx -> Crop -> Gizzard -> Ileum -> Rectum -> Colon
Mouth -> Oesophagus -> Crop -> Ileum -> Gizzard -> Colon -> Rectum
questions.explanation: The food moves from the mouth to the pharynx, then to the oesophagus, into the crop for storage, then to the gizzard for grinding, followed by the midgut (ileum, colon, rectum).
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Cockroach section, Digestive system.

questions.question: In Pheretima, the calciferous glands are present in the stomach and their function is to:
questions.explanation: The stomach of the earthworm contains calciferous glands, which neutralize the humic acid present in the humus that the earthworm consumes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Earthworm section, Digestive system.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct location and primary function of squamous epithelium in the human body?
options: Walls of blood vessels; diffusion boundary
Ducts of glands; secretion and absorption
Inner surface of bronchi; movement of particles
questions.explanation: Squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, where it forms a diffusion boundary.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Simple Epithelium.

questions.question: Where are ciliated columnar epithelial cells typically located, and what is their specific functional adaptation?
options: Fallopian tubes; to move particles or mucus in a specific direction
Intestinal mucosa; to increase surface area for absorption
Nephrons; to facilitate active transport of solutes
Exocrine glands; to synthesize and secrete digestive enzymes
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is found in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Simple Epithelium.

questions.question: Identify the primary function and characteristic location of compound epithelium.
options: Dry surface of the skin; protection against chemical and mechanical stresses
Lining of the stomach; secretion of enzymes and mucus
Alveoli of lungs; gas exchange via simple diffusion
Lining of salivary ducts; movement of secreted products
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses, as seen on the dry surface of the skin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.2: Compound Epithelium.

questions.question: What is the specialized function of the tight junctions found between epithelial cells?
options: To stop substances from leaking across a tissue
To perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together
To facilitate rapid communication between cells via ions
To anchor the epithelium to the underlying connective tissue
questions.explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue, maintaining the integrity of the epithelial barrier.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.3: Cell Junctions.

questions.question: Which connective tissue type is characterized by fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells, and where is it located?
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue present beneath the skin. It contains fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.1: Loose Connective Tissue.

questions.question: Which statement accurately matches a connective tissue with its functional location?
options: Dense regular connective tissue; tendons and ligaments
Adipose tissue; lining the respiratory tract
Cartilage; forming the framework of the bone marrow
Blood; supporting the structure of the nervous system
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, which are the principal components of tendons and ligaments.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.2: Dense Connective Tissue.

questions.question: What is the primary location and function of the chondrocytes in the human skeletal system?
options: Within fluid-filled lacunae in cartilage; secretion of matrix
Within the Haversian canals of bone; transport of nutrients
On the surface of tendons; providing tensile strength
Inside the adipose tissue; storage of lipids
questions.explanation: The cells of cartilage (chondrocytes) are enclosed in small cavities within the matrix secreted by them.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.3: Specialized Connective Tissue.

questions.question: Which feature distinguishes the smooth muscle from cardiac muscle in terms of location and control?
options: Involuntary; found in the walls of internal visceral organs
Voluntary; found attached to bones for locomotion
Involuntary; found only in the heart with intercalated discs
Voluntary; found in the blood vessels for vasoconstriction
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are involuntary and are located in the walls of internal visceral organs like the blood vessels, stomach, and intestine.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4: Muscle Tissue.

questions.question: What is the functional significance of the intercalated discs found in cardiac muscle?
options: Communication junctions that allow cells to contract as a unit
Structural anchors that attach muscle to bone
Storage sites for calcium ions required for contraction
Points of attachment for collagen fibres in dense tissue
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4: Muscle Tissue.

questions.question: What is the function of neuroglial cells found in neural tissue?
options: They conduct nerve impulses across the synapse
They synthesize neurotransmitters for signal transmission
They form the myelin sheath in the peripheral nervous system only
questions.explanation: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and they protect and support neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.5: Neural Tissue.

questions.question: Which specific structural adaptation in the epithelium of the bronchioles facilitates the movement of particles or mucus in a specific direction?
options: Presence of cilia on the free surface
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is found in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes; the cilia move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ciliated epithelium is mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes. The function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.

questions.question: In connective tissues, which component is responsible for secreting structural proteins like collagen and elastin?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are the cells of connective tissue proper that produce and secrete fibers (collagen and elastin).
questions.ncertEvidence: In all connective tissues, except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: Which feature of cardiac muscle tissue ensures that a contraction signal spreads rapidly across the entire heart?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells communicate with each other through intercalated discs, which are fusion plasma membranes that allow the cells to contract as a unit.
questions.ncertEvidence: Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e., when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.

questions.question: The primary function of the transitional epithelium (urothelium) found in the urinary bladder is:
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium is specialized to allow the organ to stretch and accommodate varying volumes of fluid, such as in the urinary bladder.
questions.ncertEvidence: Transitional epithelium is found in the urinary bladder, allowing it to stretch.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the structural arrangement of dense regular connective tissue?
options: Collagen fibers present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers
Collagen fibers oriented in many directions randomly
A matrix rich in hyaluronic acid with scattered cells
Cells arranged in a single layer with no fiber matrix
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibers are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers, providing high tensile strength.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

questions.question: What is the functional significance of tight junctions in epithelial tissue?
options: They stop substances from leaking across a tissue
They provide cytoplasmic channels for rapid communication
They anchor cells to the basement membrane
They allow for the passage of ions and small molecules
questions.explanation: Tight junctions perform a cementing function to keep neighboring cells together and prevent substances from leaking across the tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

questions.question: Which type of connective tissue serves as a support framework for epithelium and acts as a reservoir for water and salts?
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is present beneath the skin and serves as a support framework for epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium.

questions.question: The structural difference between bone and cartilage is best defined by:
options: Hardness of matrix due to calcium salts in bone versus pliability in cartilage
Presence of blood vessels in cartilage versus their absence in bone
Bone containing fibroblasts while cartilage contains osteocytes
Cartilage being vascular while bone is avascular
questions.explanation: Bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts, whereas the ground substance of cartilage is solid and pliable.
questions.ncertEvidence: The intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression. The bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres.

questions.question: Which cell type in connective tissue is responsible for the production of histamine and inflammatory reactions?
questions.explanation: Mast cells are connective tissue cells that secrete histamine, heparin, and serotonin, playing a role in inflammatory responses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mast cells secrete histamine, heparin, serotonin and are involved in inflammatory reactions.

questions.question: What is the primary function of gap junctions in tissues?
options: Facilitating communication between cells by connecting the cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate communication between adjacent cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasms of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.question: Arrange the following steps in the process of cockroach digestion in the correct sequential order as food passes through the alimentary canal:
questions.explanation: Food enters the oesophagus, moves to the crop for storage, then to the gizzard (proventriculus) for grinding, and finally to the midgut for digestion.
questions.ncertEvidence: The alimentary canal of the cockroach is divided into three regions: foregut, midgut, and hindgut. The food enters the oesophagus, moves to the crop, then the gizzard.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of events during the formation of a cockroach ootheca?
options: Egg release → Secretion of glandular fluids → Hardening of the case → Attachment to substrate
Secretion of glandular fluids → Egg release → Hardening of the case → Attachment to substrate
Egg release → Attachment to substrate → Secretion of glandular fluids → Hardening of the case
Hardening of the case → Egg release → Secretion of glandular fluids → Attachment to substrate
questions.explanation: Fertilized eggs are encased in capsules called oothecae. The female drops/glues them to a suitable surface after formation.
questions.ncertEvidence: The fertilized eggs are encased in capsules called oothecae. Ootheca is a dark reddish to blackish brown capsule, about 3/8" (8 mm) long. They are dropped or glued to a suitable surface.

questions.question: Select the correct order of the layers of the cockroach body wall from outermost to innermost:
questions.explanation: The exoskeleton of the cockroach is composed of plates called sclerites, which are secreted by the underlying epidermis.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body of the cockroach is covered by a hard chitinous exoskeleton. The exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites. It is secreted by the epidermis.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of flow of haemolymph in the cockroach circulatory system?
options: Sinuses → Ostia → Heart chambers → Anterior aorta
Heart chambers → Ostia → Sinuses → Anterior aorta
Anterior aorta → Heart chambers → Ostia → Sinuses
Sinuses → Heart chambers → Ostia → Anterior aorta
questions.explanation: Haemolymph from sinuses enters the heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to the sinuses again via the anterior aorta.
questions.ncertEvidence: The blood from sinuses enters the heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to sinuses again.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of the male reproductive tract in a cockroach starting from the testes:
options: Testes → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Male gonopore
Testes → Ejaculatory duct → Vas deferens → Male gonopore
Vas deferens → Testes → Ejaculatory duct → Male gonopore
Testes → Seminal vesicle → Vas deferens → Male gonopore
questions.explanation: Testes are located between 4th and 6th abdominal segments; vas deferens lead to the ejaculatory duct which opens out via the male gonopore.
questions.ncertEvidence: Testes are present on each lateral side in the 4th-6th abdominal segments. From each testis arises a thin vas deferens, which opens into the ejaculatory duct through seminal vesicle.

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of cockroach development in the correct order:
questions.explanation: Cockroaches exhibit paurometabolous development, meaning development is through the nymphal stage, which resembles the adult.
questions.ncertEvidence: The development of P. americana is paurometabolous, meaning that there is development through the nymphal stage. The nymphs look very much like adults.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of flow of air through the respiratory system of a cockroach:
questions.explanation: Air enters through spiracles, travels through a network of tracheal tubes, and reaches the tracheoles where gaseous exchange occurs.
questions.ncertEvidence: The respiratory system consists of a network of trachea, that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles present on the lateral side of the body.

questions.question: Arrange the following segments of the cockroach abdomen in the correct order from anterior to posterior:
questions.explanation: The abdomen of both males and females consists of 10 segments, ordered sequentially from 1 to 10.
questions.ncertEvidence: In both sexes, the abdomen consists of 10 segments.

questions.question: Choose the correct sequence of structures encountered by urine/excretory products in the cockroach excretory system:
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules absorb waste from haemolymph and release it into the gut (hindgut), where it is excreted through the anus.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the female reproductive system components starting from the ovaries?
questions.explanation: Each ovary consists of eight ovarian tubules or ovarioles, joining to form a single oviduct, which opens into the genital chamber/vestibulum.
questions.ncertEvidence: Each ovary consists of eight ovarioles. The oviducts of each ovary unite into a single median oviduct (also called vagina) which opens into the genital chamber.

questions.question: Most epithelial tissues are characterized by a basement membrane, but which of the following is a known exception regarding the nature of the intercellular matrix in animal tissues?
options: Connective tissue has an abundant intercellular matrix, whereas epithelial tissue has very little.
Neural tissue contains an extensive intercellular matrix compared to connective tissue.
Muscular tissue possesses the highest amount of intercellular matrix among all primary tissues.
Epithelial tissue is the only tissue type that lacks any form of intercellular substance.
questions.explanation: In epithelial tissue, cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix. In contrast, connective tissue is characterized by cells widely spaced and embedded in an abundant intercellular matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: Epithelial tissues are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix, while connective tissues have cells widely spaced and embedded in an abundant intercellular matrix.

questions.question: Identify the exception among the following connective tissues regarding the secretion of fibers by fibroblasts.
questions.explanation: In most connective tissues, cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. Blood is the exception, where the plasma does not contain fibers except during the time of clotting.
questions.ncertEvidence: In all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: Which of the following muscle types is an exception to the general rule that muscle fibers are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath called epimysium?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle fibers are branched and connected by intercalated discs, and they do not form the typical parallel bundles wrapped in dense connective tissue sheaths seen in skeletal muscle.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together.

questions.question: While most epithelia are avascular, which of the following represents a structural exception found in the body?
options: There is no vascularized epithelium; all epithelia are avascular.
The germinal epithelium of the ovary is highly vascularized.
The transitional epithelium of the urinary bladder is highly vascularized.
All epithelial tissues receive nutrients directly from blood vessels within the epithelium.
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly states that epithelial tissues are avascular and rely on the underlying connective tissue for nutrients via diffusion; there are no exceptions to this rule in the provided scope.
questions.ncertEvidence: Epithelial tissues are avascular; they do not have their own blood supply and rely on underlying connective tissue for nourishment.

questions.question: Which type of junction is an exception to the rule that all cell junctions provide mechanical support?
questions.explanation: While tight and adhering junctions provide mechanical support, gap junctions are specialized for communication by facilitating the transfer of ions and small molecules between cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small and big molecules.

questions.question: Regarding the distribution of connective tissue, which of the following is an exception to the presence of collagen fibers?
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue where the plasma is devoid of fibers, unlike other connective tissues like tendons, ligaments, and cartilage which contain structural fibers.
questions.ncertEvidence: In all connective tissues except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: Which of the following cell types in connective tissue is an exception because it does not secrete fibers?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts, chondrocytes, and osteoblasts are responsible for secreting fibers and matrix. Macrophages are phagocytic cells involved in defense, not fiber production.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fibroblasts are cells that secrete and produce fibres.

questions.question: Most smooth muscles are involuntary, but which statement correctly identifies an exception or specific characteristic?
options: Smooth muscles are involuntary but are not under the direct control of the somatic nervous system.
Smooth muscles are voluntary in the iris of the eye.
Smooth muscles are multinucleated like skeletal muscles.
Smooth muscles possess striations like cardiac muscles.
questions.explanation: Smooth muscles are involuntary (fusiform). The option correctly identifies that their control is distinct from the voluntary somatic nervous system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform and involuntary. As they are not under the direct control of the somatic nervous system, they are known as involuntary muscles.

questions.question: Which type of tissue is unique because its cells are not separated by a large intercellular matrix, yet it is classified as a specialized connective tissue?
questions.explanation: Bone has a very hard and non-pliable ground substance (calcium salts), making it an exception to the 'soft' nature of connective tissue matrix, although it still fits the definition of connective tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bone has a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres which give bone its strength.

questions.question: In the context of epithelial shape, which is an exception to the rule that columnar cells are always taller than they are wide?
questions.explanation: Pseudostratified epithelium appears to be multilayered because the nuclei are at different levels, making the cells appear to vary in height and shape, unlike standard columnar epithelia.
questions.ncertEvidence: In pseudostratified epithelium, all cells rest on the basement membrane but are of different heights, giving a false impression of stratification.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the difference in the lining of the bronchioles versus the fallopian tubes?
options: Bronchioles are lined by ciliated columnar epithelium, while fallopian tubes are lined by ciliated cuboidal epithelium.
Bronchioles are lined by ciliated cuboidal epithelium, while fallopian tubes are lined by ciliated columnar epithelium.
Both are lined by ciliated squamous epithelium.
Both are lined by ciliated columnar epithelium.
questions.explanation: NCERT specifies that ciliated epithelium is found in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles (cuboidal) and fallopian tubes (columnar).
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Ciliated epithelium is present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: Choose the correct distinction between dense regular and dense irregular connective tissues regarding fiber arrangement.
options: In dense regular, collagen fibers are present in a regular pattern; in dense irregular, fibers are oriented in many directions.
In dense regular, collagen fibers are oriented randomly; in dense irregular, fibers are oriented in parallel rows.
Dense regular contains only elastic fibers; dense irregular contains only collagen fibers.
Dense regular is found in the skin; dense irregular is found in tendons.
questions.explanation: Dense regular connective tissue has collagen fibers in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers, whereas dense irregular has fibroblasts and many fibers oriented differently.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.2: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres. Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) that are oriented differently.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the secretion mode of exocrine and endocrine glands?
options: Exocrine glands secrete products via ducts; endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones directly into fluid bathing the gland.
Exocrine glands are ductless; endocrine glands secrete via ducts.
Exocrine glands secrete hormones; endocrine glands secrete mucus and enzymes.
Exocrine glands are unicellular; endocrine glands are exclusively multicellular.
questions.explanation: Exocrine glands have ducts for secretions like mucus, saliva, earwax, oil, milk, and digestive enzymes, while endocrine glands are ductless.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.2: These glands secrete products through ducts or tubes. In contrast, endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete their products, called hormones, directly into the fluid bathing the gland.

questions.question: Compare the intercellular material of cartilage and bone; identify the correct statement.
options: Cartilage matrix is slightly pliable and resists compression; bone matrix is hard and non-pliable.
Cartilage matrix is hard and non-pliable; bone matrix is pliable.
Both cartilage and bone possess a hard, non-pliable matrix.
Neither cartilage nor bone possess intercellular material.
questions.explanation: Cartilage has a solid and pliable matrix due to chondroitin salts, whereas bone is a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.2: The intercellular material of cartilage is solid and pliable and resists compression. Cells of bone (osteocytes) are present in spaces called lacunae. The ground substance is rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres which give bone its strength.

questions.question: Differentiate between the structural location of tight junctions and gap junctions.
options: Tight junctions stop substances from leaking across a tissue; gap junctions facilitate communication between cells.
Tight junctions facilitate communication; gap junctions stop substances from leaking.
Both junctions perform identical functions of cell-to-cell adhesion.
Tight junctions are found in blood; gap junctions are found in bone.
questions.explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasms of adjoining cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.3: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other.

questions.question: How do the locations of tendons and ligaments differ in terms of their connecting role?
options: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones; ligaments attach one bone to another.
Tendons attach one bone to another; ligaments attach skeletal muscles to bones.
Tendons are a type of loose connective tissue; ligaments are specialized connective tissue.
Tendons are cartilaginous; ligaments are osseous.
questions.explanation: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and ligaments attach one bone to another.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.2: Tendons, which attach skeletal muscles to bones and ligaments which attach one bone to another are examples of dense regular connective tissues.

questions.question: Distinguish between the function of smooth muscle and cardiac muscle fibers.
options: Smooth muscle fibers are involuntary and fusiform; cardiac muscle fibers are involuntary and branched.
Smooth muscle fibers are voluntary and branched; cardiac muscle fibers are involuntary and fusiform.
Smooth muscle fibers are multinucleated; cardiac muscle fibers are uninucleated.
Smooth muscle fibers are striated; cardiac muscle fibers are non-striated.
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (tapering at both ends) and involuntary, while cardiac muscle fibers are contractile tissues present only in the heart, characterized by branching and involuntary nature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.2: The smooth muscle fibres are fusiform (taper at both ends) and do not show striations. Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together.

questions.question: Compare the structure of simple epithelium versus compound epithelium.
options: Simple epithelium is composed of a single layer of cells; compound epithelium is made of two or more layers of cells.
Simple epithelium is multi-layered; compound epithelium is single-layered.
Simple epithelium is specialized for protection; compound epithelium is specialized for diffusion.
Simple epithelium is found in the skin; compound epithelium is found in the lining of the stomach.
questions.explanation: Simple epithelium is composed of a single layer of cells and functions as a lining for body cavities, ducts, and tubes. Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a protective function.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Simple epithelium is composed of a single layer of cells and functions as a lining for body cavities, ducts, and tubes. The compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a protective function as it does in our skin.

questions.question: What is the key difference between the matrix of areolar tissue and adipose tissue?
options: Areolar tissue has a loose arrangement of fibers and cells; adipose tissue is specialized to store fats.
Areolar tissue stores fat; adipose tissue stores fibers.
Areolar tissue is a dense connective tissue; adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue.
Areolar tissue is found in the heart; adipose tissue is found in the tendons.
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue present beneath the skin, while adipose tissue is also a loose connective tissue but is specialized to store fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.3.1: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin. Adipose tissue is another type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.

questions.question: Differentiate between the location of neurons and neuroglia in neural tissue.
options: Neurons are the units of neural system; neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body and protect and support neurons.
Neuroglia are the units of neural system; neurons make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue.
Neurons are supportive cells; neuroglia are the functional units.
Neurons are found only in the CNS; neuroglia are found only in the PNS.
questions.explanation: Neurons are the functional unit of the neural system, whereas neuroglia comprise more than half the volume of neural tissue and provide protection and support.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.5: Neurons are the unit of neural system. Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body. Neuroglia protect and support neurons.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the intercellular matrix of connective tissues is correct according to NCERT?
options: It is composed of modified polysaccharides only.
It is secreted by the cells of the connective tissue.
It is absent in all types of specialized connective tissues.
It is primarily composed of living cells rather than fibers.
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly states that in connective tissues, the cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin and also secrete modified polysaccharides which accumulate between cells and fibers, acting as the matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: Connective tissues are most abundant and widely distributed in the body of complex animals. The cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: In cockroach (Periplaneta americana), the development is paurometabolous. What does this term specifically imply?
options: Development through the nymphal stage which resembles the adult.
Development involving a complete larval stage and pupa.
Development where the organism undergoes drastic metamorphosis.
Development that occurs entirely within the ootheca.
questions.explanation: Paurometabolous development means the development is through the nymphal stage. The nymphs look very much like adults.
questions.ncertEvidence: The development of P. americana is paurometabolous, meaning that there is development through the nymphal stage.

questions.question: Which type of junction facilitates the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions and molecules?
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate communication by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.question: Regarding the anatomy of the cockroach, which of the following structures is responsible for grinding the food particles?
questions.explanation: The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth, which help in grinding the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the location of the transitional epithelium?
options: It lines the urinary bladder and ureters.
It lines the inner surface of the stomach.
It lines the ducts of salivary glands.
It lines the moist surface of the buccal cavity.
questions.explanation: Transitional epithelium is a specialized type of epithelium found in the urinary bladder and ureters to allow for stretching.
questions.ncertEvidence: Transitional epithelium is found in the urinary bladder and ureters.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of the segments in the cockroach leg starting from the body attachment.
questions.explanation: The legs of the cockroach are composed of five segments: coxa, trochanter, femur, tibia, and tarsus, in that order.
questions.ncertEvidence: The legs are composed of five segments: coxa, trochanter, femur, tibia and tarsus.

questions.question: Which cells in the areolar connective tissue are responsible for secreting fibers?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are the cells that produce and secrete fibers of structural proteins in connective tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: In the male cockroach, which segment bears the anal styles?
questions.explanation: In males, genital pouches or chamber lie at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9th and 10th terga and ventrally by the 9th sternum. It contains anal styles.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the male, genital pouch or chamber lies at the hind end of abdomen bounded dorsally by 9th and 10th terga and ventrally by the 9th sternum. It contains dorsal anus, genital pore and gonapophysis.

questions.question: Which of the following is the characteristic feature of compound epithelium?
options: It has a limited role in secretion and absorption.
It consists of a single layer of cells.
It is primarily found in the inner lining of the intestine.
It is composed of tall and slender cells with nuclei at the base.
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption; its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
questions.ncertEvidence: The compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption.

questions.question: What is the function of the Malpighian tubules in cockroaches?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are yellow colored thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of midgut and hindgut, which help in the removal of excretory products from hemolymph.
questions.ncertEvidence: At the junction of midgut and hindgut is present another ring of 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous Malpighian tubules. They help in removal of excretory products from haemolymph.

questions.question: A histologist observes a tissue sample where cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix, and the tissue rests on a basement membrane. If this tissue is found lining the moist surface of the buccal cavity, what is its primary function?
options: Protection against chemical and mechanical stress
questions.explanation: The buccal cavity is lined by compound epithelium (specifically non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium), which provides protection against mechanical and chemical abrasion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios describes the physiological significance of gap junctions in cardiac muscle tissue?
options: To prevent the leakage of extracellular fluid
To allow cells to communicate by sending ions and small molecules rapidly
To anchor the muscle fibers to the connective tissue
To provide structural rigidity to the heart wall
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate communication between cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasms of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.question: In a laboratory experiment, an animal tissue is treated with an enzyme that specifically degrades collagen fibers. Which tissue type would show the most significant loss of tensile strength?
questions.explanation: Dense connective tissues are characterized by the presence of fibers and fibroblasts packed compactly; dense irregular connective tissue contains collagen fibers oriented in different directions, providing high tensile strength.
questions.ncertEvidence: In dense connective tissues, the fibres and fibroblasts are compactly packed. Orientation of fibres show a regular or irregular pattern and are called dense regular and dense irregular tissues.

questions.question: If the ducts of exocrine glands are damaged, which specific type of epithelium would be most directly involved in the regenerative repair process?
questions.explanation: The ducts of glands are typically lined by simple cuboidal epithelium, which is involved in secretion and absorption.
questions.ncertEvidence: Simple cuboidal epithelium is composed of a single layer of cube-like cells. This is commonly found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys and its main functions are secretion and absorption.

questions.question: Consider a patient with a disorder affecting the formation of elastin fibers. Which of the following structures would be most severely compromised?
questions.explanation: Ligaments are dense regular connective tissues that attach bone to bone and contain a large amount of elastin fibers to allow for flexibility and recoil.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ligaments attach one bone to another. This tissue has considerable strength and contains elastin fibers.

questions.question: A student identifies a tissue sample under a microscope as 'loose connective tissue'. Which feature would confirm this classification?
options: Cells and fibers are loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance
The tissue is entirely composed of closely packed collagen fibers
The tissue consists of a single layer of flattened cells
The tissue contains only specialized cells without any matrix
questions.explanation: Loose connective tissue has cells and fibers loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, such as areolar tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: In loose connective tissue, the cells and fibres are loosely arranged in a semi-fluid ground substance, for example, areolar tissue.

questions.question: What is the functional consequence of the presence of 'disc-like' structures between cardiac muscle cells?
options: They act as fusion points that allow the heart to contract as a single unit
They serve as storage sites for calcium ions
They prevent the heart from over-stretching during contraction
They increase the surface area for oxygen absorption
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are communication junctions between cardiac muscle cells that allow the heart to contract as a unit (syncytium).
questions.ncertEvidence: Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e., when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the primary difference between tendons and ligaments regarding their fiber composition and function?
options: Tendons are dense regular connective tissue connecting muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone and contain more elastin
Tendons connect bone to bone; ligaments connect muscle to bone and are composed of only cartilage
Tendons are dense irregular connective tissue; ligaments are loose connective tissue
Tendons contain only elastic fibers; ligaments contain only collagen fibers
questions.explanation: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones (dense regular connective tissue). Ligaments attach one bone to another and contain a higher proportion of elastin fibers compared to tendons.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones and ligaments attach one bone to another. Ligaments contain elastin fibers.

questions.question: A histological slide shows goblet cells interspersed among columnar epithelial cells. What is the most likely location of this tissue?
options: Lining of the stomach and intestine
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are unicellular glands that secrete mucus. They are commonly found in the lining of the alimentary canal (stomach and intestine).
questions.ncertEvidence: Goblet cells of the alimentary canal are unicellular glands. The columnar epithelium is found in the lining of stomach and intestine and help in secretion and absorption.

questions.question: Why is the skin considered a dry surface compared to the lining of the esophagus?
options: The skin has a keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, whereas the esophagus has a non-keratinized one
The skin is composed of simple cuboidal cells
The esophagus is lined by ciliated epithelium
questions.explanation: The skin's epidermis consists of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which provides a waterproof barrier, while the esophagus is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Compound epithelium is dry on the surface of the skin and moist on the surface of the buccal cavity and pharynx.

questions.question: If an epithelial tissue is found in areas where protection against chemical and mechanical stresses is required, which of the following characteristics would be most prominent?
