options: Multi-layered cells with limited role in secretion and absorption
Single layer of flattened cells facilitating diffusion
Presence of cilia for movement of particles
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium consists of two or more cell layers and has a limited role in secretion and absorption; its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular junctions would be most critical in preventing the leakage of substances across a tissue layer in the urinary bladder?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions are specialized junctions that help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

questions.question: In a histological slide of connective tissue, you observe cells that are modified to store fats. Which type of connective tissue are you likely observing?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin, where the cells are specialized to store fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.

questions.question: An athlete suffers a ligament injury. Based on the structural organization of connective tissues, which fiber arrangement is disrupted?
options: Dense regular connective tissue with collagen fibers in regular rows
Dense irregular connective tissue with fibroblasts in random orientation
Loose areolar tissue with loosely arranged fibers
Specialized cartilage tissue with chondrocytes in lacunae
questions.explanation: Ligaments are dense regular connective tissues where collagen fibers are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibers.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres. Ligaments attach bone to bone.

questions.question: Which statement correctly infers the functional difference between smooth and cardiac muscle cells based on their structural features?
options: Cardiac muscles have intercalated discs for communication, while smooth muscles lack them
Smooth muscles are striated and voluntary, while cardiac muscles are non-striated
Cardiac muscles are spindle-shaped, while smooth muscles are branched
Smooth muscles contain multiple nuclei, while cardiac muscles are uninucleate
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are branched and possess intercalated discs that allow cells to contract as a unit; smooth muscle cells are fusiform (spindle-shaped) and lack such discs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together. Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit.

questions.question: Why does the cockroach continue to live for a week even after its head is removed?
options: The head holds only a small portion of the nervous system, while the rest is situated along the ventral part of the body
The head is not involved in respiratory functions
The cockroach can breathe through its skin
The head is purely for sensory perception and not for metabolic control
questions.explanation: In cockroaches, the head holds a small proportion of the nervous system, while the rest is situated along the ventral (belly-side) part of the body.
questions.ncertEvidence: The head holds a small proportion of the nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral (belly-side) part of the body. So, if the head of a cockroach is cut off, it will still live for as long as one week.

questions.question: Which structural feature of the cockroach's alimentary canal is responsible for grinding food particles?
questions.explanation: The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth, which help in grinding the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth. Gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Malpighian tubules in Periplaneta americana?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules which help in the removal of excretory products from haemolymph. Cockroaches are uricotelic.
questions.ncertEvidence: Malpighian tubules are yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules. They help in removal of excretory products from haemolymph. The insect excretes uric acid and is therefore uricotelic.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the location and function of the 'alary muscles' in a cockroach?
options: Fan-shaped muscles associated with the heart to maintain circulation
Muscles attached to the wings for flight
Muscles controlling the movement of the gizzard
Muscles associated with the respiratory spiracles
questions.explanation: The heart of the cockroach consists of elongated muscular tube with funnel-shaped chambers with ostia on either side. Blood from sinuses enter heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to sinuses by alary muscles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The heart of the cockroach consists of elongated muscular tube with funnel-shaped chambers with ostia on either side. Blood from sinuses enter heart through ostia and is pumped anteriorly to sinuses by alary muscles.

questions.question: In the male cockroach, what is the role of the mushroom-shaped gland?
questions.explanation: The mushroom-shaped gland is present in the 6th-7th abdominal segments of the male cockroach and functions as an accessory reproductive gland.
questions.ncertEvidence: A characteristic mushroom shaped gland is present in the 6th-7th abdominal segments which functions as an accessory reproductive gland.

questions.question: Which specific type of epithelial tissue is primarily found in the inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes, functioning to move particles or mucus in a specific direction?
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium consists of cells bearing cilia on their free surface, which move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Epithelial Tissue - Ciliated epithelium.

questions.question: In the context of connective tissue, which component is secreted by fibroblasts to provide strength and elasticity to the tissue?
questions.explanation: In most connective tissues, cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin, which provide strength, elasticity, and flexibility.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.2: Connective Tissue - Fibers.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the functional significance of gap junctions in cardiac muscle tissue?
options: They stop substance leakage across tissue
They facilitate rapid communication by connecting cytoplasms of adjacent cells
They anchor the cytoskeleton to the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules, and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Epithelial Tissue - Cell Junctions.

questions.question: Which cell type in the areolar connective tissue is responsible for secreting histamine and heparin?
questions.explanation: Mast cells are present in connective tissue and are responsible for the secretion of histamine, heparin, serotonin, etc., involved in inflammatory responses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.2: Connective Tissue - Areolar tissue.

questions.question: Which statement correctly identifies the characteristic of smooth muscle fibers?
options: They are fusiform, non-striated, and involuntary
They are cylindrical, striated, and voluntary
They are branched, striated, and involuntary
They are multinucleated and lack junctional complexes
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform (tapering at both ends) and do not show striations; they are involuntary in nature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.3: Muscle Tissue - Smooth muscle fibers.

questions.question: Where is the site of attachment for the tendon in the human musculoskeletal system?
questions.explanation: Tendons are dense regular connective tissues that attach skeletal muscles to bones.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.2: Connective Tissue - Dense regular connective tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following structures in the cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is responsible for grinding the food particles?
questions.explanation: The gizzard (proventriculus) in the cockroach has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and an inner thick cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate-like teeth, which grind food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.2: Alimentary canal of Cockroach.

questions.question: In the male reproductive system of a cockroach, where are the sperms stored?
questions.explanation: Sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.3: Reproductive System of Cockroach.

questions.question: What is the function of the Malpighian tubules in the cockroach?
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are yellow colored filamentous tubules present at the junction of midgut and hindgut, which help in the removal of excretory products from the haemolymph as uric acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.4.2: Excretory system of Cockroach.

questions.question: Which cell type forms the lining of the blood vessels and the air sacs of the lungs?
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. They are found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals, Section 7.2.1: Epithelial Tissue - Simple squamous epithelium.

questions.question: Which of the following epithelial tissues is NOT primarily associated with the function of secretion or absorption?
questions.explanation: Squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, where it is involved in diffusion, not secretion or absorption.
questions.ncertEvidence: Squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the structural components of connective tissue:
options: Fibroblasts are responsible for the secretion of all types of fibers
Collagen fibers provide strength to the tissue
Elastin fibers provide flexibility to the tissue
The ground substance is composed of modified polysaccharides
questions.explanation: While fibroblasts secrete structural proteins like collagen and elastin, they do not secrete all components (e.g., the ground substance is secreted by the cells but consists of modified polysaccharides).
questions.ncertEvidence: The cells of connective tissue secrete modified polysaccharides, which accumulate between cells and fibres and act as matrix.

questions.question: Select the option that is NOT a characteristic feature of smooth muscle fibers:
questions.explanation: Intercalated discs are communication junctions found exclusively in cardiac muscle, not in smooth muscle fibers.
questions.ncertEvidence: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform and do not show striations. Cardiac muscle tissue is a contractile tissue present only in the heart. Cell junctions fuse the plasma membranes of cardiac muscle cells and make them stick together.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the neural tissue?
questions.explanation: Osteocytes are mature bone cells found in connective tissue, whereas neurons and neuroglia are the primary components of neural tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neural tissue is made up of neurons and neuroglial cells.

questions.question: In the context of the cockroach digestive system, which of the following is NOT a part of the foregut?
questions.explanation: The ileum is a part of the hindgut, while the oesophagus, crop, and gizzard constitute the foregut.
questions.ncertEvidence: The alimentary canal of cockroach is divided into three regions: foregut, midgut and hindgut. The foregut includes oesophagus, crop and gizzard.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is NOT involved in the excretory system of a cockroach?
questions.explanation: Ommatidia are the individual visual units of the compound eye, whereas Malpighian tubules, fat bodies, and urecose glands are associated with excretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. In addition, the fat body, nephrocytes and urecose glands also subserve the function of excretion.

questions.question: Regarding Earthworm (Pheretima), which of the following is NOT a function of the typhlosole?
options: Increasing the effective area of absorption
questions.explanation: The typhlosole is an internal median fold of the dorsal wall of the intestine that increases the surface area for absorption; it has no role in blood volume regulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: The intestine of earthworm has an internal median fold of dorsal wall called typhlosole which effectively increases the area of absorption.

questions.question: Which of the following cell types is NOT found in the connective tissue proper?
questions.explanation: Chondrocytes are the specialized cells of cartilage (a specialized connective tissue), whereas fibroblasts, mast cells, and macrophages are found in loose connective tissue (areolar tissue).
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells. Cartilage is a specialized connective tissue containing chondrocytes.

questions.question: Which of the following structures in the cockroach is NOT associated with the reproductive system?
questions.explanation: Hepatic caecae are blind tubules present at the junction of the foregut and midgut, involved in digestion, not reproduction.
questions.ncertEvidence: A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caecae is present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a function associated with the specialized connective tissue known as bone?
options: Providing structural frame to the body
questions.explanation: Bone marrow produces blood cells, but the production of antibodies is the function of lymphocytes (white blood cells) within the immune system, not the bone tissue itself as a structural entity.
questions.ncertEvidence: Bones have a hard and non-pliable ground substance rich in calcium salts and collagen fibres which give bone its strength. It is the main tissue that provides structural frame to the body.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the intercellular matrix in epithelial tissue is correct?
options: It is abundant and contains collagen fibers.
It is minimal and acts as a binding substance.
It is completely absent in all epithelial types.
It is primarily composed of elastic fibers.
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues are characterized by cells that are compactly packed with very little intercellular matrix, which serves to bind the cells together.
questions.ncertEvidence: Epithelial tissue has a free surface, which faces either a body fluid or the outside environment and thus provides a covering or a lining for some part of the body. The cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix.

questions.question: In cockroach (Periplaneta americana), the 'gizzard' is specifically responsible for:
questions.explanation: The gizzard (proventriculus) in cockroaches has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and inner thick cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth, which grind the food.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.

questions.question: Which type of cell junction in the epithelium facilitates the communication between cells by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells?
questions.explanation: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells, for rapid transfer of ions, small molecules and sometimes big molecules.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement regarding the structural organization of Cockroach:
options: The head is formed by the fusion of six segments.
Each thoracic segment bears two pairs of wings.
The abdomen in both sexes consists of 12 segments.
The exoskeleton is made up of chitinous plates called sternites only.
questions.explanation: The head of the cockroach is formed by the fusion of six segments and shows great mobility in all directions due to a flexible neck.
questions.ncertEvidence: The head is triangular in shape and lies anteriorly at right angles to the longitudinal body axis. It is formed by the fusion of six segments and shows great mobility in all directions.

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is correctly described as 'specialized connective tissue'?
questions.explanation: Connective tissues are classified into three types: loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, and specialized connective tissue. Bone, blood, and cartilage are specialized connective tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: Specialized connective tissues include cartilage, bone and blood.

questions.question: In the alimentary canal of the cockroach, the hepatic caecae are located at the junction of:
questions.explanation: At the junction of foregut and midgut, a ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caecae are present, which secrete digestive juice.
questions.ncertEvidence: At the junction of foregut and midgut, a ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caecae are present, which secrete digestive juice.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'Dense Irregular Connective Tissue' is accurate?
options: Fibroblasts and fibers are oriented randomly.
It is present in tendons and ligaments.
It contains only parallel bundles of collagen fibers.
It is a type of loose connective tissue.
questions.explanation: In dense irregular connective tissue, fibroblasts and many fibers (mostly collagen) are oriented differently (randomly). This tissue is present in the skin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibers (mostly collagen) that are oriented differently.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of the segments from anterior to posterior in the cockroach thorax:
questions.explanation: The thorax of the cockroach consists of three parts: prothorax, mesothorax, and metathorax.
questions.ncertEvidence: The thorax consists of three parts - prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax.

questions.question: Which cell type is responsible for the secretion of fibers of structural proteins like collagen or elastin in connective tissues?
questions.explanation: In connective tissue, cells like fibroblasts secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.
questions.ncertEvidence: In all connective tissues, except blood, the cells secrete fibers of structural proteins called collagen or elastin.

questions.question: Regarding the Malpighian tubules in cockroaches, identify the correct statement:
options: They are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules.
They are attached to the junction of foregut and midgut.
They are responsible for the secretion of digestive enzymes.
They are present in the thorax region only.
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules attached at the junction of midgut and hindgut, which help in the removal of excretory products from haemolymph.
questions.ncertEvidence: At the junction of midgut and hindgut, there are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules called Malpighian tubules. They help in removal of excretory products from haemolymph.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the structure of the cockroach's alimentary canal?
options: The crop is followed by the gizzard, which helps in grinding the food particles.
The midgut is lined by the cuticle, forming the stomodaeum.
The hepatic caecae are present at the junction of the foregut and the midgut.
The gizzard is a part of the hindgut involved in the absorption of water.
questions.explanation: In Periplaneta americana, the crop is followed by the gizzard (proventriculus), which has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth, which grind the food.
questions.ncertEvidence: The crop is followed by gizzard or proventriculus. It has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth. Gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.

questions.question: In the epithelial tissue, which junction helps to stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions perform a cementing function to keep neighboring cells together and prevent substances from leaking across a tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

questions.question: Which of the following types of connective tissue is primarily composed of fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells embedded in a semi-fluid ground substance?
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue that contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages, and mast cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin... it contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.

questions.question: Identify the correct anatomical description of the cockroach's respiratory system.
options: Tracheal tubes open through 10 pairs of spiracles present on the lateral side of the body.
The opening of the spiracles is regulated by sphincters.
Exchange of gases takes place at the spiracles by simple diffusion.
The tracheal tubes are lined with non-chitinous rings to prevent collapse.
questions.explanation: The respiratory system of a cockroach consists of a network of trachea, that open through 10 pairs of small holes called spiracles present on the lateral side of the body. Opening of the spiracles is regulated by sphincters.
questions.ncertEvidence: The opening of the spiracles is regulated by sphincters.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Muscular tissue is incorrect?
options: Skeletal muscle fibers are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath.
Smooth muscle fibers are fusiform and are held together by cell junctions.
Cardiac muscle cells are multinucleated and branched.
Smooth muscle fibers do not show striations.
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are uninucleated, not multinucleated. Skeletal muscles are multinucleated.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cardiac muscle cells are multinucleated is incorrect; they are uninucleated.

questions.question: Where are the Malpighian tubules found in a cockroach, and what is their function?
options: At the junction of midgut and hindgut; excretion.
In the crop; storage of food.
At the junction of foregut and midgut; secretion of digestive enzymes.
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules are yellow colored thin filamentous structures present at the junction of midgut and hindgut of a cockroach, which help in the removal of excretory products from haemolymph.
questions.ncertEvidence: At the junction of midgut and hindgut are present 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous Malpighian tubules. They help in removal of excretory products from haemolymph.

questions.question: Which type of epithelium is found in the inner surface of bronchioles and fallopian tubes?
questions.explanation: Ciliated epithelium is mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: In dense connective tissue, if the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, it is called:
questions.explanation: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the cockroach's nervous system?
options: The brain is represented by the supra-oesophageal ganglion.
The ventral nerve cord consists of 5 thoracic and 5 abdominal ganglia.
The head holds a small part of the nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of the body.
The nervous system is entirely absent in the head region.
questions.explanation: The nervous system of cockroach consists of a series of fused, segmentally arranged ganglia joined by paired longitudinal connectives on the ventral side. Three ganglia lie in the thorax, and six in the abdomen. The brain is represented by supra-oesophageal ganglion.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nervous system of cockroach consists of a series of fused, segmentally arranged ganglia joined by paired longitudinal connectives on the ventral side. Three ganglia lie in the thorax, and six in the abdomen. The nervous system of cockroach is spread throughout the body. The head holds a bit of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral (belly-side) part of its body. So, now you understand that if the head of a cockroach is cut off, it will still live for as long as one week. In the head region, the brain is represented by supra-oesophageal ganglion.

questions.question: Which cells in the areolar tissue are responsible for secreting fibers of structural proteins?
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are the cells that produce and secrete fibers in the connective tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres)

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding epithelial tissue is correct?
options: The cells of the epithelium are held together with little intercellular material.
Epithelial tissue has a rich supply of blood vessels for direct nourishment.
Simple epithelium is composed of two or more layers of cells.
The free surface of epithelial cells is always attached to a basement membrane.
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues have a free surface, which faces either a body fluid or the outside environment and thus provides a covering or a lining for some part of the body. The cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.1: 'The cells are compactly packed with little intercellular matrix.'

questions.question: Where are the goblet cells of the alimentary canal primarily found and what is their function?
options: In the columnar epithelium; to secrete mucus.
In the squamous epithelium; to facilitate diffusion.
In the cuboidal epithelium; to aid in absorption.
In the ciliated epithelium; to move particles.
questions.explanation: Columnar epithelium is composed of a single layer of tall and slender cells. Their nuclei are located at the base. Some of the columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium. Goblet cells are unicellular glands present in the alimentary canal that secrete mucus.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.1: 'Some of the columnar or cuboidal cells get specialised for secretion and are called glandular epithelium. They are mainly of two types: unicellular... e.g., goblet cells of the alimentary canal.'

questions.question: Which of the following junctions helps to stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue. Adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together. Gap junctions facilitate the cells to communicate with each other by connecting the cytoplasm of adjoining cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.1: 'Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.'

questions.question: Which type of connective tissue contains fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells embedded in a matrix containing fibres?
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts (cells that produce and secrete fibres), macrophages and mast cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.2: 'Areolar tissue present beneath the skin... It contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.'

questions.question: Identify the characteristic feature of dense irregular connective tissue.
options: Fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) are oriented differently.
Collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.
It provides structural frame to the body and contains large amount of fat.
The matrix is solid and pliable and resists compression.
questions.explanation: In dense irregular connective tissue, fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) are oriented differently, unlike dense regular connective tissue where fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.2: 'Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) that are oriented differently.'

questions.question: Which muscle fibre type is described as having striations and is bundled together in a parallel fashion with connective tissue sheaths?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle tissue is closely attached to skeletal bones. In a typical muscle such as the biceps, striated (striped) skeletal muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.3: 'In a typical muscle such as the biceps, striated (striped) skeletal muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion.'

questions.question: What is the primary function of neuroglial cells in neural tissue?
questions.explanation: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body. They protect and support neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.2.4: 'Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body. They protect and support neurons.'

questions.question: In the cockroach (Periplaneta americana), which part of the alimentary canal is responsible for grinding food particles?
questions.explanation: The gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate called teeth. Gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.2: 'The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.'

questions.question: What is the role of Malpighian tubules in the cockroach?
questions.explanation: Excretion in cockroach is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.2: 'Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells.'

questions.question: Which structure in the male cockroach is responsible for the storage of sperms?
questions.explanation: In male cockroaches, sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores which are discharged during copulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XI, Chapter 7, Section 7.4.3: 'Sperms are stored in the seminal vesicles and are glued together in the form of bundles called spermatophores.'

questions.question: Which of the following cell junctions is primarily responsible for preventing substances from leaking across a tissue?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue, whereas adhering junctions perform cementing to keep neighbouring cells together, and gap junctions facilitate communication.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tight, adhering and gap junctions are cell junctions present in the epithelium (Page 101, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, and is involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary?
questions.explanation: The simple squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air-sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary. (Page 102, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding compound epithelium is correct?
options: It is composed of a single layer of cells
It plays a major role in secretion and absorption
It has a limited role in secretion and absorption
It is found in the lining of the stomach
questions.explanation: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Its main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses.
questions.ncertEvidence: Compound epithelium is made of more than one layer (multi-layered) of cells and thus has a limited role in secretion and absorption. Their main function is to provide protection against chemical and mechanical stresses. (Page 102, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Which type of connective tissue contains fibroblasts that produce and secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin?
questions.explanation: In all connective tissues (except blood), the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. Fibroblasts are the cells responsible for this in areolar, dense regular, and dense irregular tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: In all connective tissues, except blood, the cells secrete fibres of structural proteins called collagen or elastin. (Page 104, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of dense regular connective tissue?
options: Collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres
The tissue is composed of loose cells with a jelly-like matrix
It is primarily found in the skin
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres, such as in tendons and ligaments.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres. (Page 105, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of skeletal muscle fibres?
options: They are tapered at both ends
They are held together by cell junctions
They are closely attached in bundles and are striated
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle tissue is closely attached to skeletal bones. In a typical muscle, such as the biceps, striated skeletal muscle fibres are bundled together in a parallel fashion.
questions.ncertEvidence: A sheath of tough connective tissue encloses several bundles of muscle fibres. (Page 107, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Which of the following cells are found in the neural tissue and are described as 'excitable cells'?
questions.explanation: Neural tissue exerts the greatest control over the body's responsiveness to changing conditions. Neurons, the unit of neural system, are excitable cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neurons, the unit of neural system are excitable cells. (Page 107, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: Identify the characteristic feature of the cockroach (Periplaneta americana) regarding its body segmentation.
options: The body is divided into head, thorax, and abdomen
The body is divided into head and trunk
The body is divided into cephalothorax and abdomen
questions.explanation: The entire body of the cockroach is covered by a hard chitinous exoskeleton. In each segment, the exoskeleton has hardened plates called sclerites. The body is divisible into three regions: head, thorax, and abdomen.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body of the cockroach is divisible into three regions – head, thorax and abdomen. (Page 110, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: In the cockroach, which structure is responsible for the removal of excretory products from the haemolymph?
questions.explanation: Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. (Page 113, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: What is the function of the 'gizzard' in the digestive system of a cockroach?
questions.explanation: The gizzard has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plate-like teeth. Gizzard helps in grinding the food particles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The gizzard helps in grinding the food particles. (Page 112, Structural Organisation in Animals)

questions.question: If a patient presents with a condition requiring the replacement of damaged cells in the alveolar walls and the walls of blood vessels, which tissue type would be the primary focus for physiological regeneration?
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is composed of a single layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries and is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Simple squamous epithelium is found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs.

questions.question: In a biological model, if a substance needs to be secreted and absorbed across a surface lining the proximal convoluted tubules of the nephron, which epithelial specialization is most critical?
questions.explanation: Cuboidal epithelium is found in ducts of glands and tubular parts of nephrons in kidneys, where its main functions are secretion and absorption. Microvilli increase the surface area for these processes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: The epithelium of proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) of nephron in the kidney has microvilli.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular junctions would be most critical in preventing the leakage of digestive enzymes into the underlying connective tissue in the intestinal lining?
questions.explanation: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Tight junctions help to stop substances from leaking across a tissue.

questions.question: If a tissue is characterized by cells loosely arranged in a matrix of protein fibers called collagen and elastin, and it serves to attach skin to underlying muscles, this tissue is classified as:
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is a type of loose connective tissue present beneath the skin and often serves as a support framework for epithelium.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin serves as a support framework for epithelium.

questions.question: During a study of skeletal muscle, a researcher observes the banding pattern. Which protein is primarily responsible for the dark 'A' band in the sarcomere?
questions.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibers have dark bands containing myosin and light bands containing actin.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Skeletal muscle tissue is closely attached to skeletal bones. In a typical muscle such as the biceps, striated (striped) skeletal muscle fibers are bundled together in a parallel fashion.

questions.question: A student examines a tissue slide showing cells with a large central fat globule and a peripherally displaced nucleus. Identify the tissue and its primary function.
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: The cells of this tissue (adipose) are specialised to store fats.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between dense regular and dense irregular connective tissue?
options: Dense regular has collagen fibers in rows; dense irregular has fibers oriented differently.
Dense regular is found in skin; dense irregular is found in tendons.
Dense regular contains only elastin; dense irregular contains only collagen.
Dense regular is loose; dense irregular is compact.
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres. In dense irregular connective tissue, fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) are oriented differently.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Dense regular connective tissues... collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres. Dense irregular connective tissue has fibroblasts and many fibres (mostly collagen) oriented differently.

questions.question: If an injury damages the structure responsible for holding bones together at a joint, which specific tissue type was likely affected?
questions.explanation: Ligaments, which attach one bone to another, are dense regular connective tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Ligaments attach one bone to another.

questions.question: Which feature of cardiac muscle ensures that a contraction signal spreads rapidly from one cell to the next, allowing the heart to beat as a single unit?
questions.explanation: Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit, i.e., when one cell receives a signal to contract, its neighbours are also stimulated to contract.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: Communication junctions (intercalated discs) at some fusion points allow the cells to contract as a unit.

questions.question: In the context of the cockroach (Periplaneta americana), where would one find the hepatic caeca, and what is their primary function?
options: At the junction of foregut and midgut; secretion of digestive juice
In the hindgut; absorption of water
In the crop; storage of food
At the junction of midgut and hindgut; excretion
questions.explanation: A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca are present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice.
questions.ncertEvidence: Structural Organisation in Animals: A ring of 6-8 blind tubules called hepatic or gastric caeca are present at the junction of foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue is primarily found in the walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, where it functions as a diffusion boundary?
questions.explanation: Simple squamous epithelium is composed of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries, found in walls of blood vessels and air sacs of lungs, involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary.
questions.ncertEvidence: Simple squamous epithelium is made of a single thin layer of flattened cells with irregular boundaries. They are found in the walls of blood vessels and air-sacs of lungs and are involved in functions like forming a diffusion boundary.

questions.question: Where are the ciliated columnar epithelial cells typically located in the human body?
questions.explanation: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface, they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: If the columnar or cuboidal cells bear cilia on their free surface they are called ciliated epithelium. Their function is to move particles or mucus in a specific direction over the epithelium. They are mainly present in the inner surface of hollow organs like bronchioles and fallopian tubes.

questions.question: Which connective tissue is characterized by the presence of fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells embedded in a semi-fluid ground substance?
questions.explanation: Areolar tissue is present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts, macrophages, and mast cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Areolar tissue present beneath the skin. It serves as a support framework for epithelium. It contains fibroblasts, macrophages and mast cells.

questions.question: What is the primary function of adipose tissue?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Adipose tissue is another type of loose connective tissue located mainly beneath the skin. The cells of this tissue are specialised to store fats.

questions.question: In dense regular connective tissue, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many:
questions.explanation: In dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the dense regular connective tissues, the collagen fibres are present in rows between many parallel bundles of fibres.

questions.question: Which muscle tissue is involuntary, fusiform in shape, and does not show striations?
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle fibres are fusiform (tapering at both ends) and do not show striations. Cell junctions hold them together and they are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath.
questions.ncertEvidence: The smooth muscle fibres are fusiform (tapering at both ends) and do not show striations. Cell junctions hold them together and they are bundled together in a connective tissue sheath.

questions.question: Which component of neural tissue provides protection and support to neurons and makes up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body?
questions.explanation: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body. They protect and support neurons.
questions.ncertEvidence: Neuroglia make up more than one-half the volume of neural tissue in our body. They protect and support neurons.

questions.question: What is the specific name of the cockroach's forewings, which are opaque, dark, and leathery?
questions.explanation: The forewings of a cockroach are called tegmina or mesothoracic wings. They are opaque, dark, and leathery and cover the hind wings when at rest.
questions.ncertEvidence: The fore wings arise from mesothorax and the hind wings from metathorax. The fore wings, called tegmina or mesothoracic wings, are opaque, dark and leathery and cover the hind wings when at rest.

questions.question: How many malpighian tubules are typically present in a cockroach?
questions.explanation: Excretion in cockroach is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut. There are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Excretion is performed by Malpighian tubules. Each tubule is lined by glandular and ciliated cells. They absorb nitrogenous waste products and convert them into uric acid which is excreted out through the hindgut. There are 100-150 yellow coloured thin filamentous tubules.

questions.question: Which of the following organelles is considered the 'powerhouse of the cell' and typically contains circular DNA?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are sites of aerobic respiration and produce cellular energy in the form of ATP. They contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mitochondria are sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.question: Which component of the cell envelope determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing?
questions.explanation: The bacterial cell wall is responsible for providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of the endomembrane system?
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Peroxisomes are not included because their functions are not coordinated with these organelles.
questions.ncertEvidence: The endomembrane system includes endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles.

questions.question: The 'fluid mosaic model' of the plasma membrane was proposed by:
questions.explanation: S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane in 1972.
questions.ncertEvidence: The improved model was later proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972) widely accepted as fluid mosaic model.

questions.question: Which organelle is rich in acid hydrolases (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) and is active at acidic pH?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) which are optimally active at acidic pH.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lysosomal vesicles contain hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at acidic pH.

questions.question: Which type of chromosome has a centromere situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm?
questions.explanation: In acrocentric chromosomes, the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
questions.ncertEvidence: In the acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular structures is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are the sites of protein synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are the sites of protein synthesis.

questions.question: The cytoskeleton in a cell is involved in many functions such as:
options: Mechanical support, motility, and maintenance of the shape of the cell
questions.explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. It provides mechanical support, motility, and maintenance of the shape of the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. It is involved in many functions such as mechanical support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
questions.ncertEvidence: The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct statement regarding the nuclear envelope?
options: It consists of two parallel membranes with a space between them (perinuclear space)
It is a single membrane structure
It is continuous with the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, which forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, which forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the cell membrane is consistent with the fluid mosaic model?
options: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
The peripheral proteins are embedded partially or totally in the lipid bilayer.
The cell membrane is composed only of lipids and proteins with no carbohydrates.
The lipid bilayer is perfectly static and prevents the movement of all integral proteins.
questions.explanation: According to the fluid mosaic model, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: In the context of the endomembrane system, which organelle is primarily responsible for the synthesis of proteins?
questions.explanation: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) bears ribosomes on its surface and is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Rough endoplasmic reticulum is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

questions.question: Which specific component of the chloroplast contains the enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins?
questions.explanation: The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stroma contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding the structure of the Golgi apparatus.
options: The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis and concave trans faces.
The Golgi cisternae are scattered randomly throughout the cytoplasm without any polarity.
The Golgi apparatus consists of a single large sac that is continuous with the nuclear envelope.
The Golgi apparatus is composed of flattened sacs that do not show any differentiation into faces.
questions.explanation: Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis (forming) and concave trans (maturing) faces.
questions.ncertEvidence: They are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane-bound organelles found in all cells—both within the cytoplasm and in organelles like chloroplasts and mitochondria.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are the non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells – both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.

questions.question: Regarding the cytoskeleton, which of the following is correct?
options: It is an elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures present in the cytoplasm.
It is composed primarily of lipids and carbohydrates.
It is exclusive to plant cells for structural support.
It is a membrane-bound organelle involved in protein modification.
questions.explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton.
questions.ncertEvidence: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton.

questions.question: What is the primary function of lysosomes?
options: Digestion of macromolecules using hydrolytic enzymes.
Synthesis of ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.
Detoxification of drugs in liver cells.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at the acidic pH.
questions.ncertEvidence: The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the arrangement of microtubules in the axoneme of a cilium or flagellum?
options: It is a 9+2 array of microtubules.
It is a 9+0 array of microtubules.
It is a 2+9 array of microtubules.
It consists of a central core of microfilaments surrounded by 9 peripheral microtubules.
questions.explanation: The core called the axoneme, possesses microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine pairs of doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules (9+2 array).
questions.ncertEvidence: The core called the axoneme, possesses microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine pairs of doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules.

questions.question: Chromosomes with the centromere situated close to its end, forming one extremely short and one very long arm, are called:
questions.explanation: Acrocentric chromosome has centromere situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.
questions.ncertEvidence: Acrocentric chromosome has centromere situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell theory:
I. All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
II. All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
III. Viruses are considered an exception to the cell theory as they are acellular.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Cell theory, proposed by Schleiden and Schwann and later modified by Virchow, states that all organisms are made of cells and arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). Viruses lack cellular machinery and are considered exceptions.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.2: Cell Theory.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the structural differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes lack a nuclear envelope but possess 80S ribosomes.
Eukaryotes contain circular extrachromosomal DNA in the form of plasmids.
Prokaryotes exhibit a fluid mosaic model of cell membrane similar to eukaryotes.
Eukaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles in the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes share a similar phospholipid bilayer structure for their plasma membrane, described by the fluid mosaic model. Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes and lack membrane-bound organelles.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.3: Prokaryotic Cells.

questions.question: Regarding the endomembrane system, identify the correct sequence of protein flow for secretion.
options: ER → Golgi complex → Lysosomes → Plasma membrane
ER → Golgi complex → Secretory vesicles → Plasma membrane
Nuclear envelope → ER → Golgi complex → Vacuoles
Golgi complex → ER → Lysosomes → Plasma membrane
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Proteins synthesized in the ER move to the Golgi complex for modification and packaging, then are transported via vesicles to the plasma membrane.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.3: The Endomembrane System.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the function of the Golgi apparatus?
options: It is the site of glycoprotein and glycolipid synthesis.
It is the primary site of ATP production in plant cells.
It is involved in the synthesis of steroid hormones.
It contains hydrolytic enzymes that digest macromolecules.
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids through modification of materials synthesized in the ER.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.3: The Golgi Apparatus.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding mitochondria and chloroplasts.
options: Both are part of the endomembrane system.
Both contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Both are found in all eukaryotic cells.
Both are involved in the synthesis of proteins on 80S ribosomes.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles because they contain their own DNA and 70S ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.4 (Mitochondria) and 8.5.5 (Plastids).

questions.question: Which of the following features is unique to the plant cell wall?
options: Presence of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectins.
questions.explanation: The cell wall of plants is primarily composed of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins. It provides structural support and protection.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.1: Cell Wall.

questions.question: What is the role of the nucleolus within the nucleus?
options: Storage of genetic material in the form of chromatin.
Synthesis of mRNA for protein translation.
Regulation of cell division via spindle formation.
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a non-membrane-bound spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm and is the site for active ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.9: Nucleus.

questions.question: Identify the function of the 'Fluid Mosaic Model' regarding the plasma membrane.
options: It explains the lateral movement of proteins within the lipid bilayer.
It describes the rigid structure of the cell wall.
It explains the process of active transport across the nuclear membrane.
It accounts for the synthesis of phospholipids in the smooth ER.
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson describes the membrane as a fluid structure where proteins can move laterally within the lipid bilayer.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.2: Cell Membrane.

questions.question: Lysosomes are known as 'suicide bags' because they:
options: Contain hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting all types of organic materials.
Are responsible for the synthesis of lipids.
Direct the formation of the spindle apparatus.
Are involved in the detoxification of drugs.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain various hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at acidic pH, capable of digesting cellular components.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.3: Lysosomes.

questions.question: Which cytoskeletal structure is composed of tubulin protein and is involved in cell division?
questions.explanation: Microtubules are composed of tubulin protein and form the structural basis of the cytoskeleton, cilia, flagella, and spindle fibers during cell division.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life, Section 8.5.8: Cytoskeleton.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. Reason (R): Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells and can survive without oxygen.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are indeed the smallest living cells and lack a cell wall. However, the ability to survive without oxygen is a physiological trait that does not explain why they lack a cell wall.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mycoplasma are the smallest cells and they lack a cell wall.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The fluid mosaic model describes the structure of the plasma membrane. Reason (R): The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The fluid nature of the membrane allows for the lateral movement of proteins, which is central to the fluid mosaic model.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Mitochondria are referred to as the powerhouses of the cell. Reason (R): Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce cellular energy in the form of ATP.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through aerobic respiration, which is why they are called the powerhouses of the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Lysosomes are known as 'suicidal bags' of the cell. Reason (R): Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that are optimally active at a neutral pH.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at acidic pH, not neutral pH.
questions.ncertEvidence: The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) optimally active at the acidic pH.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found only in eukaryotic cells. Reason (R): Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells – both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The Golgi apparatus is primarily involved in the synthesis of proteins. Reason (R): The Golgi apparatus consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is the principal director of macromolecule packaging and modification, not protein synthesis (which occurs on ribosomes).
questions.ncertEvidence: Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Chromatin contains DNA and some basic proteins called histones. Reason (R): During different stages of cell division, cells show structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Chromatin composition and the condensation into chromosomes during division are distinct, well-established facts.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chromatin contains DNA and some basic proteins called histones, some non-histone proteins and RNA. During different stages of cell division, cells show structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The nucleolus is a membrane-bound structure found inside the nucleus. Reason (R): The nucleolus is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm and is not membrane-bound.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Centrosomes contain two cylindrical structures called centrioles. Reason (R): Centrioles lie perpendicular to each other and are made up of nine unevenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Centrioles are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, not unevenly spaced.
questions.ncertEvidence: Centrosome contains two cylindrical structures called centrioles. They lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel. They are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Plant cells have a large central vacuole that occupies up to 90 percent of the volume of the cell. Reason (R): The membrane of the vacuole is called the tonoplast, which facilitates the transport of ions against concentration gradients into the vacuole.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The tonoplast facilitates the transport of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, maintaining the concentration higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
questions.ncertEvidence: In plant cells the vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell. The membrane is called the tonoplast. In plant cells the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole.

questions.question: Match the following cell organelles with their characteristic functions/features:
questions.explanation: A: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes (i); B: Mitochondria are sites of aerobic respiration (ii); C: Ribosomes are sites of protein synthesis (iii); D: Golgi apparatus involves packaging of materials (iv).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Descriptions of Lysosomes, Mitochondria, Ribosomes, and Golgi apparatus functions.

questions.question: Match the cytoskeletal structures with their correct descriptions:
questions.explanation: Microtubules are composed of tubulin (ii), Microfilaments are involved in cell motility (i), and Intermediate filaments provide mechanical support (iii).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Cytoskeleton section discussing Microtubules, Microfilaments, and Intermediate filaments.

questions.question: Match the following scientists with their contribution to Cell Theory/Biology:
questions.explanation: Schleiden studied plants (ii), Schwann studied animals (i), Virchow proposed omnis cellula-e cellula (iv), and Leeuwenhoek first observed a live cell (iii).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Cell Theory and historical discovery section.

questions.question: Match the plastid types with their storage function:
questions.explanation: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), Elaioplasts store oils and fats, and Aleuroplasts store proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Plastids classification into Chloroplasts, Chromoplasts, and Leucoplasts (Amyloplasts, Elaioplasts, Aleuroplasts).

questions.question: Match the phase of Meiosis I with the corresponding event:
questions.explanation: Leptotene involves compaction (iii), Zygotene involves synapsis (iv), Pachytene involves crossing over (i), and Diplotene involves chiasmata formation (ii).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 10: Cell Cycle and Cell Division - Meiosis I prophase I sub-stages.

questions.question: Match the following components of the endomembrane system with their role:
questions.explanation: ER is for protein/lipid synthesis, Golgi for packaging, Lysosomes for digestion, and Vacuoles for storage.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Endomembrane system section.

questions.question: Match the chromosome types based on centromere position:
questions.explanation: Metacentric (middle), Sub-metacentric (slightly away from middle), Acrocentric (close to end), Telocentric (terminal).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Structure of Chromosomes section.

questions.question: Match the following cell inclusions/structures with their nature:
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are infoldings of plasma membrane (ii), Inclusion bodies are non-membrane bound storage (i), and Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins (iii).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Prokaryotic cell section.

questions.question: Match the specific mitotic stages with their characteristic morphological observation:
questions.explanation: Prophase (chromatin condensation), Metaphase (chromosomes at equator), Anaphase (splitting of centromere), Telophase (nucleolus reappears).
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 10: Cell Cycle and Cell Division - Mitosis phases.

questions.question: Match the following biomolecule-related organelles with their specific enzyme content:
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolases (lipases, proteases), Glyoxysomes contain enzymes for glyoxylate cycle, and Mitochondria contain enzymes for oxidative phosphorylation.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life - Functions and enzyme localization in organelles.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of events during the formation of a secretory protein in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Rough ER -> Golgi apparatus -> Secretory vesicles -> Plasma membrane
Nucleus -> Smooth ER -> Golgi apparatus -> Lysosomes
Rough ER -> Smooth ER -> Golgi apparatus -> Plasma membrane
Golgi apparatus -> Rough ER -> Secretory vesicles -> Plasma membrane
questions.explanation: Secretory proteins are synthesized in the Rough ER, processed in the Golgi apparatus, packaged into secretory vesicles, and then released via the plasma membrane.
questions.ncertEvidence: The endomembrane system includes ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles, coordinating functions in protein synthesis and transport.

questions.question: Identify the correct order of components in the cell envelope of a typical bacterium from outermost to innermost layer.
questions.explanation: The bacterial cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three-layered structure: the outermost glycocalyx, followed by the cell wall and the plasma membrane.
questions.ncertEvidence: Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically complex cell envelope consisting of a tightly bound three layered structure i.e., the outermost glycocalyx followed by the cell wall and then the plasma membrane.

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of prophase I of meiosis in the correct chronological order.
questions.explanation: Prophase I of meiosis is subdivided into these five phases based on chromosomal behavior.
questions.ncertEvidence: Prophase of the first meiotic division is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of mitosis. It has been further subdivided into the following five phases based on chromosomal behaviour, i.e., Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of steps involved in the process of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is divided into four stages of nuclear division: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mitosis is divided into the four stages of nuclear division: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the flow of information during the movement of materials from the cytoplasm into the nucleus through the nuclear pore complex?
