questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972.
questions.ncertEvidence: The improved model of the structure of cell membrane was proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972) widely accepted as fluid mosaic model.

questions.question: Which organelle is referred to as the 'powerhouse of the cell' and why?
options: Mitochondria, because they produce cellular energy in the form of ATP.
Lysosome, because they digest waste products.
Endoplasmic Reticulum, because they synthesize proteins.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called the powerhouse of the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is considered the non-membrane bound organelle that helps in the division of animal cells?
questions.explanation: Centrioles are non-membrane bound organelles found in animal cells which help in cell division.
questions.ncertEvidence: Centrosome is an organelle usually containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles. They are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. Both the centrioles in a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel.

questions.question: Identify the characteristic feature of the middle lamella in plant cells.
options: It is mainly composed of calcium pectate
It is a thin layer of cellulose
It is present only in secondary cell wall
It is synthesized by the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together.
questions.ncertEvidence: The middle lamella is a layer mainly of calcium pectate which holds or glues the different neighbouring cells together.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the fluid mosaic model is correct?
options: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer
Proteins are always embedded in the center of the lipid bilayer
Lipids are arranged in a single layer with polar tails inside
The cell membrane is composed only of lipids and proteins
questions.explanation: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its fluidity.
questions.ncertEvidence: The improved model of the structure of cell membrane was proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972) widely accepted as fluid mosaic model. According to this, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Golgi apparatus in a cell?
options: Packaging materials to be delivered to the intracellular targets or secreted outside the cell
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.

questions.question: In prokaryotes, the genetic material is essentially:
options: A single circular DNA molecule, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane
Multiple linear DNA molecules with histones
A single linear DNA molecule associated with histones
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack a well-defined nucleus and the genetic material is basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane. It is a single circular DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: The prokaryotic cells lack a well-defined nucleus and the genetic material is basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane. In addition to the genomic DNA, many bacteria have small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is involved in the synthesis of steroidal hormones in animal cells?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.
questions.ncertEvidence: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding ribosomes.
options: They are composed of RNA and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane
They are found only in eukaryotic cells
They are surrounded by a single lipid membrane
They are the site of lipid synthesis
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the mitochondrial matrix?
options: It contains single circular DNA molecule and 70S ribosomes
It contains multiple linear DNA molecules and 80S ribosomes
It is devoid of any genetic material
It contains only enzymes for the Krebs cycle
questions.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: The inner compartment is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. The matrix also possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins.

questions.question: What is the function of the nucleolus within the nucleus?
options: Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about lysosomes is correct?
options: They are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes
They are involved in the synthesis of structural proteins
They are absent in animal cells
They are formed by the fusion of ribosomes
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. These are rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes.
questions.ncertEvidence: These are membrane bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus. The isolated lysosomal vesicles have been found to be very rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the cell membrane structure as proposed by the fluid mosaic model is incorrect?
options: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
The peripheral proteins lie on the surface of the membrane while the integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.
The fluid nature of the membrane is also important from the point of view of functions like cell growth and secretion.
Lipids are arranged in a bilayer with the hydrophobic tails facing the aqueous environment and heads towards the interior.
questions.explanation: In the lipid bilayer, the nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment, meaning the hydrophobic tails face inward, while the hydrophilic polar heads face outward toward the aqueous environment.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.1: The lipid component mainly consists of phosphoglycerides... the nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is characterized by the presence of hydrolytic enzymes that are optimally active at acidic pH?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at the acidic pH.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.9: These lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures... rich in almost all types of hydrolytic enzymes... optimally active at the acidic pH.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Mesosome in prokaryotes:
options: It is formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae.
It is the site of protein synthesis in prokaryotic cells.
It is structurally analogous to the lysosomes of eukaryotic cells.
It is composed primarily of cellulose and hemicellulose.
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are characteristic of prokaryotes, formed by infoldings of the plasma membrane. They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.3.2: In prokaryotes, a special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell.

questions.question: Which of the following components of the endomembrane system is primarily responsible for the synthesis of proteins?
questions.explanation: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) bears ribosomes on its surface and is actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.6: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

questions.question: The 'storage sacs' of solid or liquid contents in plant cells, bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast, are known as:
questions.explanation: The vacuole is a membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm containing water, sap, and excretory products. It is bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.10: The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm... It is bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast.

questions.question: Which of the following cytoskeletal structures is responsible for the formation of the spindle apparatus during cell division?
questions.explanation: Microtubules are components of the cytoskeleton that form the structural basis of spindle fibers, centrioles, cilia, and flagella.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.13: Microtubules... are involved in the formation of the spindle apparatus during cell division.

questions.question: Regarding the ribosomes in eukaryotic cells, which statement is accurate?
options: They are 80S type, consisting of 60S and 40S subunits.
They are 70S type, consisting of 50S and 20S subunits.
They are found only in the cytoplasm attached to the RER.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S, while prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. The 'S' stands for Svedberg's unit, which is an indirect measure of density and size.
questions.ncertEvidence: Class XI Biology, Chapter 8, Section 8.5.11: Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S while the prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. Each ribosome has two subunits, larger and smaller.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular components is described as the 'non-membrane bound organelle' present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells. Lysosomes and vacuoles are membrane-bound, and mesosomes are specific to prokaryotes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are the non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells - both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.

questions.question: In the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane, what is the primary factor that allows for the 'fluid' nature of the membrane?
questions.explanation: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer, which is the basis of the fluid mosaic model.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for the synthesis of steroids and lipids in animal cells?
questions.explanation: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is the major site for lipid synthesis. In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are also synthesized in the SER.
questions.ncertEvidence: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.

questions.question: The 'axoneme' of cilia and flagella is characterized by an arrangement of microtubules denoted as:
questions.explanation: The core of cilia and flagella, called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis, usually arranged in a 9+2 configuration.
questions.ncertEvidence: The core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules.

questions.question: Which of the following plastids stores oils and fats?
questions.explanation: Elaioplasts are leucoplasts that store oils and fats. Amyloplasts store carbohydrates, and aleuroplasts store proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: Elaioplasts store oils and fats; aleuroplasts store proteins.

questions.question: The nucleolus is a site for the active synthesis of which molecule?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm and is a site for active ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Golgi apparatus in a secretory cell?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The Golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell.

questions.question: Which structure in a prokaryotic cell is a specialized differentiated form of the cell membrane?
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae.
questions.ncertEvidence: In prokaryotes, essentially all the prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane. An unique structure formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell is the mesosome.

questions.question: In the context of the cell cycle, chromosomes are most condensed and visible during which phase?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are most condensed at metaphase, making it the best stage to study chromosome morphology.
questions.ncertEvidence: Metaphase is the best stage to study morphology of chromosomes.

questions.question: Which of the following organelles is considered part of the endomembrane system?
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Mitochondria and chloroplasts are not part of it because their functions are not coordinated with these components.
questions.ncertEvidence: The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular components is correctly matched with its structural characteristic described in NCERT?
options: Centrosome: Non-membrane bound organelle containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles.
Lysosome: Double-membrane bound vesicular structure rich in hydrolytic enzymes.
Ribosome: Membrane-bound organelle found only in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells.
Vacuole: Membrane-bound space containing sap, water, and excretory products found only in animal cells.
questions.explanation: Centrosomes are non-membrane bound organelles containing two centrioles. Lysosomes are single-membrane bound; ribosomes are non-membrane bound; vacuoles are prominent in plant cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Centrosome and centrioles are non-membrane bound organelles.

questions.question: If a cell is treated with a chemical that inhibits the assembly of microtubules, which of the following structures will be most directly affected in its function?
questions.explanation: Cilia and flagella have an axoneme, which is composed of a core of microtubules arranged in a 9+2 array. Inhibiting microtubule assembly disrupts their structure and movement.
questions.ncertEvidence: The core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis.

questions.question: Regarding the endomembrane system, which of the following functional pathways is correct?
questions.explanation: The endomembrane system includes the ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles because their functions are coordinated.
questions.ncertEvidence: Many of the organelles are considered together as an endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated.

questions.question: A cell biologist observes a cell under an electron microscope and notes the presence of 'cristae'. What can be inferred about this specific organelle?
options: It is the site of aerobic respiration.
It is involved in the synthesis of lipids.
It is responsible for protein glycosylation.
It contains hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion.
questions.explanation: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane, which are the sites of aerobic respiration.
questions.ncertEvidence: The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cristae towards the matrix.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic ribosomes?
options: Prokaryotes possess 70S ribosomes, while eukaryotes possess 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
Prokaryotes possess 80S ribosomes, while eukaryotes possess 70S ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
Both prokaryotes and eukaryotes possess 70S ribosomes exclusively.
Prokaryotic ribosomes are membrane-bound, while eukaryotic ribosomes are free.
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are of the 70S type, while eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes are of the 80S type.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are the granular structures... In prokaryotes, ribosomes are 70S and in eukaryotes they are 80S.

questions.question: Which component of the nucleus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm and is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

questions.question: Which plastid is responsible for storing proteins in plants?
questions.explanation: Aleuroplasts store proteins, amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), and elaioplasts store oils and fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Amyloplasts store carbohydrate (starch) e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement regarding the plasma membrane based on the Fluid Mosaic Model.
options: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
The membrane is composed exclusively of proteins.
The fluid nature of the membrane is strictly due to the presence of carbohydrates.
Proteins are arranged only on the outer surface of the bilayer.
questions.explanation: According to the fluid mosaic model, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-membrane bound organelle found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells - both within eukaryotes and prokaryotes.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is considered the 'powerhouse' of the cell, and is typically absent in prokaryotes?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce cellular energy in the form of ATP. They are membrane-bound organelles absent in prokaryotic cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called 'powerhouse of the cell'.

questions.question: Identify the non-membrane bound organelle that is found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of all living cells, including both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells – both within the cell as well as in chloroplasts and mitochondria and on rough ER.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'Elaioplasts' within a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Elaioplasts are a type of leucoplast specifically adapted for the storage of oils and fats.
questions.ncertEvidence: Elaioplasts store oils and fats.

questions.question: In the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane, which component is primarily responsible for the 'fluid' nature that enables lateral movement of proteins?
questions.explanation: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.
questions.ncertEvidence: The quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer.

questions.question: Which stage of meiosis is characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules?
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, appear during the pachytene stage of prophase I.
questions.ncertEvidence: The stage is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.

questions.question: Which organelle is often referred to as the 'suicide bag' of the cell due to its high content of hydrolytic enzymes?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicular structures rich in hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that can digest various macromolecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lysosomal vesicles contain hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at the acidic pH.

questions.question: The 'axoneme' of a cilium or flagellum typically exhibits which arrangement of microtubules?
questions.explanation: The core of the cilium or flagellum, called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis, typically arranged in a 9+2 array.
questions.ncertEvidence: The core is called the axoneme, which possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules.

questions.question: Which structure in prokaryotes is an infolding of the plasma membrane into the cell, which may be in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae?
questions.explanation: Mesosomes are characteristic infoldings of the plasma membrane in prokaryotes, functioning similarly to mitochondria in eukaryotes.
questions.ncertEvidence: A special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

questions.question: The nucleolus is the site for the active synthesis of which cellular component?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm and is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
questions.ncertEvidence: The nucleolus is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary metabolite that acts as a toxin?
questions.explanation: Abrin and Ricin are toxic secondary metabolites, while Vinblastin is a drug, Curcumin is a pigment, and Codeine is a drug.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3: Some secondary metabolites (Toxins: Abrin, Ricin).

questions.question: In the context of the acid-insoluble fraction of a living tissue, which of the following is considered a macromolecule but not a polymer?
questions.explanation: Lipids have a molecular weight less than 800 Da but are found in the acid-insoluble fraction because they form vesicles during homogenization, thus they are not strict polymers.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.12: Lipids are not strictly macromolecules because their molecular weight does not exceed 800 Da.

questions.question: Which functional group is present in the amino acid Serine that distinguishes it from Glycine and Alanine?
questions.explanation: The R-group of Serine contains a hydroxymethyl group (-CH2OH), whereas Glycine has a hydrogen and Alanine has a methyl group.
questions.ncertEvidence: Figure 9.1: Amino acids (R groups: H for Glycine, CH3 for Alanine, CH2OH for Serine).

questions.question: Which of the following polysaccharides is a complex polymer of fructose?
questions.explanation: Inulin is a polymer of fructose, whereas starch, cellulose, and glycogen are polymers of glucose.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.10: Inulin is a polymer of fructose.

questions.question: The bond formed between two amino acids in a polypeptide chain is a:
questions.explanation: A peptide bond is formed by the reaction between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, with the elimination of water.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.9: In a polypeptide or a protein, amino acids are linked by a peptide bond.

questions.question: Which enzyme category catalyzes the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds?
questions.explanation: Lyases catalyze the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis leaving double bonds.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.15: Classification of Enzymes (Lyases).

questions.question: What is the primary structure of a protein?
options: The positional information of amino acids in a polypeptide chain
The folding of the polypeptide chain into an alpha-helix
The arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits
The three-dimensional shape of a single polypeptide chain
questions.explanation: The primary structure describes the sequence of amino acids, which is positional information.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.11: The sequence of amino acids i.e., the positional information in a protein - which is the first amino acid, which is second, and so on - is called the primary structure.

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains Uracil, while DNA contains Thymine.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.10: Nucleic acids: DNA and RNA (RNA contains ribose and uracil).

questions.question: What is the effect of a competitive inhibitor on the enzyme kinetics?
options: It resembles the substrate and competes for the active site
It binds to a site other than the active site
It increases the Vmax of the reaction
questions.explanation: In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme by competing for the active site.
questions.ncertEvidence: Section 9.16: Factors affecting enzyme activity (Competitive inhibition).

questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated fatty acid?
questions.explanation: Palmitic acid is a 16-carbon saturated fatty acid. Linoleic, linolenic, and arachidonic acids are unsaturated.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.1: Fatty acids (Palmitic acid is saturated).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary metabolite that is classified as a drug?
questions.explanation: Codeine is classified as a drug among secondary metabolites, whereas Vinblastin is a toxin/drug used in cancer therapy, and Ricin/Abrin are toxins.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3: Some secondary metabolites lists drugs like Vinblastin and Curcumin, but Codeine is specifically categorized under the drug function in the text.

questions.question: In the context of the primary structure of proteins, which bond is responsible for the linking of amino acids?
questions.explanation: Proteins are heteropolymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.
questions.ncertEvidence: Proteins are heteropolymers string of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following polysaccharides is a polymer of fructose?
questions.explanation: Inulin is a polymer of fructose, whereas starch, cellulose, and glycogen are polymers of glucose.
questions.ncertEvidence: Inulin is a polymer of fructose.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding enzymes is correct?
options: Enzymes increase the activation energy of the reaction
Enzymes are generally proteinaceous in nature
Enzymes function only at high temperatures
Enzymes are consumed in the reaction
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biocatalysts that are almost always proteins, they lower activation energy, and are not consumed in the reaction.
questions.ncertEvidence: Almost all enzymes are proteins.

questions.question: What is the nature of the glycosidic bond in a disaccharide like sucrose?
options: Between carbon 1 of glucose and carbon 2 of fructose
Between carbon 1 of glucose and carbon 4 of fructose
Between carbon 1 of glucose and carbon 1 of fructose
Between carbon 4 of glucose and carbon 1 of fructose
questions.explanation: In sucrose, the glycosidic bond is formed between the anomeric carbon (C1) of glucose and the anomeric carbon (C2) of fructose.
questions.ncertEvidence: In a polysaccharide like sucrose, one is a monosaccharide the other is a monosaccharide... joined by a glycosidic bond.

questions.question: The 'Km' value of an enzyme is the substrate concentration at which:
options: The reaction rate is half of Vmax
The reaction rate is equal to Vmax
questions.explanation: Km (Michaelis-Menten constant) is the substrate concentration at which the velocity of the reaction is half of the maximum velocity (Vmax).
questions.ncertEvidence: The substrate concentration at which the velocity of reaction is half of the maximum velocity is called Michaelis-Menten constant (Km).

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-reducing sugar?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because its anomeric carbons are involved in the glycosidic bond, preventing it from reacting with Benedict's or Fehling's reagent.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sucrose is a disaccharide and is a non-reducing sugar.

questions.question: The double-helical structure of DNA was proposed by Watson and Crick. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of B-DNA?
options: The pitch of the helix is 3.4 Å
The distance between two base pairs is 0.34 nm
The diameter of the helix is 34 Å
There are 12 base pairs per turn
questions.explanation: In B-DNA, the distance between two adjacent base pairs is 0.34 nm (or 3.4 Å), and there are 10 base pairs per turn.
questions.ncertEvidence: One full turn of the helical strand involves ten steps or ten base-pairs... the distance between two base pairs is 0.34 nm.

questions.question: Which class of enzymes is responsible for catalyzing the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds?
questions.explanation: Lyases are enzymes that catalyze the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lyases: Enzymes that cause removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis leaving double bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about lipid solubility is accurate according to NCERT?
options: Lipids are polymers of amino acids
questions.explanation: Lipids are not strictly macromolecules (their molecular weight does not exceed 800 Da) and are water-insoluble.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lipids are not strictly macromolecules... but they are water insoluble.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the structure of proteins: (I) The primary structure of a protein is positional information of amino acids. (II) In the secondary structure, the polypeptide chain is folded into a right-handed helix. (III) Tertiary structure is absolutely necessary for the many biological activities of proteins. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: According to NCERT, the primary structure provides positional information, secondary structures like the alpha-helix are common, and the tertiary structure is essential for biological activity.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Proteins are polypeptides; structures of proteins.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about enzyme inhibition is correct?
options: Competitive inhibitors structurally resemble the substrate.
Non-competitive inhibitors bind to the active site.
Allosteric inhibition is a form of competitive inhibition.
Inhibitors permanently bind to the enzyme by covalent bonds in all cases.
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors closely resemble the substrate in molecular structure and inhibit the activity of the enzyme by competing with the substrate for the active site.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Factors affecting enzyme activity.

questions.question: Select the incorrect statement regarding nucleic acids:
options: DNA and RNA consist of nucleotides only.
A nucleotide is composed of a nitrogenous base, a sugar, and a phosphate group.
The sugar in RNA is deoxyribose.
Nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides.
questions.explanation: The sugar in RNA is ribose, whereas the sugar in DNA is deoxyribose.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Nucleic acids.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of lipids?
options: Lipids are strictly polymers of fatty acids.
Lipids are generally water-insoluble but soluble in organic solvents.
All lipids possess a glycerol backbone.
Lipids are always strictly defined as macromolecules.
questions.explanation: Lipids are water-insoluble, but they are not strictly polymers. Not all lipids contain glycerol, and they are not considered macromolecules because their molecular weight does not exceed 10,000 Daltons.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Lipids section.

questions.question: Regarding the 'lock and key' hypothesis of enzyme action, which statement is true?
options: The active site is rigid and unchanging.
The substrate induces a change in the shape of the enzyme.
The enzyme is consumed during the reaction.
The activation energy of the reaction is increased.
questions.explanation: The 'lock and key' model suggests the enzyme's active site is a rigid structure that perfectly fits the substrate, unlike the 'induced fit' model.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Nature of enzyme action.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about polysaccharides is incorrect?
options: Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose.
Starch forms helical secondary structures and can hold I2 molecules.
Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide in plants.
Inulin is a polymer of fructose.
questions.explanation: Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide in animals, not plants; starch is the storage polysaccharide in plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Polysaccharides.

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about the primary metabolite vs secondary metabolite:
options: Secondary metabolites have an identifiable function in normal physiological processes.
Primary metabolites like pigments, alkaloids, and essential oils are absent in plants.
Secondary metabolites are products of secondary metabolism.
Primary metabolites have no ecological importance.
questions.explanation: Secondary metabolites are products of secondary metabolism and do not have an identifiable function in normal physiological processes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Primary and Secondary Metabolites.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the peptide bond is correct?
options: It is formed by the dehydration of an amino group and a carboxyl group.
It is formed by the hydrolysis of two amino acids.
It is a weak hydrogen bond.
It is formed between the R-groups of adjacent amino acids.
questions.explanation: A peptide bond is a covalent bond formed by the dehydration synthesis reaction between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Proteins.

questions.question: Select the correct statement concerning co-factors:
options: Co-enzymes are organic compounds but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient.
Prosthetic groups are loosely attached to the apoenzyme.
Metal ions are always considered co-enzymes.
The apoenzyme is the fully functional form of the enzyme.
questions.explanation: Co-enzymes are organic compounds that associate with the apoenzyme transiently, usually during the course of catalysis. Prosthetic groups are tightly bound.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Co-factors.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding the effect of temperature on enzyme activity?
options: Enzymes show highest activity at a particular temperature called optimum temperature.
Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a permanently inactive state.
High temperature increases enzyme activity indefinitely.
Enzymes are equally active at all temperatures.
questions.explanation: Enzymes show high activity in a narrow range of temperature called optimum temperature. Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Factors affecting enzyme activity.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cellulose does not contain complex helices and cannot hold iodine. Reason (R): Cellulose is a polymeric polysaccharide that forms a straight chain structure.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose units joined by beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds, resulting in a straight-chain structure that does not form complex helices like starch, thus it cannot hold iodine molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cellulose does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold iodine.

questions.question: Assertion (A): All amino acids are optically active. Reason (R): Glycine contains an asymmetric carbon atom.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Glycine is the simplest amino acid and is optically inactive because the alpha-carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms. Therefore, not all amino acids are optically active.
questions.ncertEvidence: Glycine is the simplest amino acid and it is optically inactive as it does not have an asymmetric carbon.

questions.question: Assertion (A): The primary structure of a protein is positional information. Reason (R): The left end of the protein chain is represented by the C-terminal amino acid.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The primary structure of a protein is indeed positional information. However, the left end is the N-terminal amino acid, and the right end is the C-terminal amino acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: The left end represented by the first amino acid and the right end represented by the last amino acid. The first amino acid is also called as N-terminal amino acid.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world. Reason (R): RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct NCERT data points, but the abundance of RuBisCO does not explain why Collagen is the most abundant in the animal world.
questions.ncertEvidence: Collagen is the most abundant protein in animal world and Ribulose bisphosphate Carboxylase-Oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Enzymes increase the rate of reaction by lowering the activation energy. Reason (R): The substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: While both statements are true, the formation of the enzyme-substrate complex is the mechanism by which the enzyme facilitates the reaction, but the direct reason for the rate increase is the lowering of activation energy.
questions.ncertEvidence: The activation energy of reaction is lowered by the enzyme to make the transition state more stable.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Competitive inhibitors are structurally similar to the substrate. Reason (R): Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site, thereby preventing the substrate from binding.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibition occurs because the inhibitor mimics the substrate, allowing it to occupy the active site and compete with the actual substrate.
questions.ncertEvidence: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor.

questions.question: Assertion (A): DNA and RNA are nucleic acids. Reason (R): They consist of a pentose sugar, a nitrogenous base, and a phosphate group.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are polynucleotides. The monomeric unit, a nucleotide, is composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group.
questions.ncertEvidence: A nucleic acid containing deoxyribose is called deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) while that which contains ribose is called ribonucleic acid (RNA). Each nucleotide has three chemically distinct components: heterocyclic compound, monosaccharide, and phosphoric acid.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Saturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds. Reason (R): Unsaturated fatty acids are solid at room temperature.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids lack double bonds and are typically solid at room temperature. Unsaturated fatty acids possess one or more double bonds and are typically liquid at room temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fatty acids could be saturated (without double bond) or unsaturated (with one or more C=C double bonds).

questions.question: Assertion (A): The acid-insoluble fraction represents the macromolecular fraction. Reason (R): Macromolecules are polymers with a molecular weight of 800 Daltons or more.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The acid-insoluble fraction contains macromolecules (proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides, lipids) which have molecular weights greater than 800 Daltons, except for lipids which are small but appear in this fraction.
questions.ncertEvidence: The acid insoluble fraction has only four types of organic compounds i.e., proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids. These classes of compounds, with the exception of lipids, have molecular weights in the range of ten thousand Daltons and above.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Non-competitive inhibitors bind to the enzyme at a site other than the active site. Reason (R): This binding causes a conformational change in the enzyme, rendering the active site non-functional.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Non-competitive inhibitors do not compete for the active site; they bind to an allosteric site, altering the enzyme's structure so that the active site can no longer bind the substrate effectively.
questions.ncertEvidence: Inhibitors which do not resemble the substrate in structure but inhibit the enzyme activity are known as non-competitive inhibitors.

questions.question:
Match the following biomolecules with their representative chemical class:
(A) Lecithin (i) Amino acid
(B) Palmitic acid (ii) Phospholipid
(C) Alanine (iii) Heterocyclic ring
(D) Adenine (iv) Fatty acid
questions.explanation: Lecithin is a phospholipid, Palmitic acid is a saturated fatty acid, Alanine is a simple amino acid, and Adenine is a nitrogenous base containing a heterocyclic ring.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Classification of lipids and amino acids.

questions.question:
Match the following enzymes with their specific catalytic action:
(A) Dehydrogenases (i) Linking two compounds
(B) Isomerases (ii) Transfer of groups
(C) Ligases (iii) Interconversion of isomers
(D) Transferases (iv) Oxidoreduction
questions.explanation: Dehydrogenases catalyze oxidoreduction, Isomerases handle interconversion, Ligases join two compounds, and Transferases transfer functional groups.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Classification and nomenclature of enzymes.

questions.question:
Match the following polysaccharides with their biological function or occurrence:
(A) Cellulose (i) Storage in plants
(B) Starch (ii) Storage in animals
(C) Glycogen (iii) Structural component of plants
(D) Chitin (iv) Exoskeleton of arthropods
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a structural polymer in plants, Starch is the storage form in plants, Glycogen is the storage form in animals, and Chitin forms the exoskeleton of arthropods.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Polysaccharides section.

questions.question:
Match the following protein structures with their descriptive characteristics:
(A) Primary structure (i) Three-dimensional folding
(B) Secondary structure (ii) Sequence of amino acids
(C) Tertiary structure (iii) Multiple polypeptide chains
(D) Quaternary structure (iv) Alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheets
questions.explanation: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids; secondary involves helices/sheets; tertiary involves global folding; quaternary involves arrangement of multiple subunits.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Structure of proteins.

questions.question:
Match the following co-factors with their chemical nature:
(A) Prosthetic group (i) Loosely bound organic co-factor
(B) Co-enzyme (ii) Inorganic ions
(C) Metal ions (iii) Tightly bound organic molecule
questions.explanation: Prosthetic groups are tightly bound, co-enzymes are loosely bound organic co-factors, and metal ions are inorganic.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Co-factors.

questions.question:
Match the following RNA/DNA components with their chemical nature:
(A) Adenine (i) Pyrimidine
(B) Uracil (ii) Purine
(C) Ribose (iii) Pentose sugar
(D) Phosphoric acid (iv) Inorganic acid
questions.explanation: Adenine is a purine, Uracil is a pyrimidine, Ribose is a pentose sugar, and phosphoric acid is an inorganic acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Nucleic acids.

questions.question:
Match the following amino acids with their chemical properties:
(A) Glycine (i) Sulfur-containing
(B) Cysteine (ii) Hydroxy group-containing
(C) Serine (iii) Acidic
(D) Glutamic acid (iv) Simplest amino acid
questions.explanation: Glycine has a hydrogen as the R-group (simplest), Cysteine contains sulfur, Serine contains a hydroxyl group, and Glutamic acid is an acidic amino acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Amino acids classification.

questions.question:
Match the following biomolecule categories with their average composition in a cell:
(A) Water (i) 10-15%
(B) Proteins (ii) 70-90%
(C) Nucleic acids (iii) 5-7%
(D) Carbohydrates (iv) 3%
questions.explanation: Water constitutes 70-90%, Proteins 10-15%, Nucleic acids 5-7%, and Carbohydrates 3% of the total cellular mass.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Table 9.1 Average composition of cells.

questions.question:
Match the following lipid types with their characteristic feature:
(A) Triglyceride (i) Glycerol + 3 Fatty acids
(B) Phospholipid (ii) Glycerol + 2 Fatty acids + Phosphate
(C) Steroid (iii) Ring structure (e.g., Cholesterol)
(D) Fatty Acid (iv) Carboxyl group attached to R-group
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are esters of glycerol and three fatty acids, phospholipids are derivatives containing phosphate, steroids are cyclic, and fatty acids contain a carboxylic group.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Lipids.

questions.question:
Match the following enzyme inhibition concepts with their definitions:
(A) Competitive inhibition (i) Inhibitor resembles substrate structure
(B) Non-competitive inhibition (ii) Inhibitor binds to site other than active site
(C) Feedback inhibition (iii) End product inhibits first enzyme
(D) Allosteric regulation (iv) Modulation by binding at non-catalytic site
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibition involves structural similarity; non-competitive involves binding elsewhere; feedback is a metabolic control; allosteric involves regulation via non-catalytic sites.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules - Factors affecting enzyme activity.

questions.question: Arrange the following steps in the correct sequence of the analytical technique used to determine the chemical composition of a living tissue:
options: Grinding in trichloroacetic acid -> Filtration/Centrifugation -> Separation of acid-soluble and acid-insoluble pools -> Elemental analysis
Elemental analysis -> Grinding in trichloroacetic acid -> Filtration -> Separation of acid-soluble and acid-insoluble pools
Grinding in trichloroacetic acid -> Separation of pools -> Filtration -> Elemental analysis
Filtration -> Grinding in trichloroacetic acid -> Separation of acid-insoluble pool -> Elemental analysis
questions.explanation: The standard protocol for analyzing chemical composition involves grinding tissue in trichloroacetic acid (Cl3CCOOH) using a mortar and pestle, followed by filtration to separate the filtrate (acid-soluble pool) and the retentate (acid-insoluble pool).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.3 (How to Analyse Chemical Composition?)

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of structural levels in the formation of a functional protein?
options: Primary structure -> Secondary structure -> Tertiary structure -> Quaternary structure
Primary structure -> Tertiary structure -> Secondary structure -> Quaternary structure
Secondary structure -> Primary structure -> Tertiary structure -> Quaternary structure
Primary structure -> Quaternary structure -> Secondary structure -> Tertiary structure
questions.explanation: The primary structure (amino acid sequence) folds into secondary structures (alpha-helix/beta-pleated sheets), which further fold into tertiary structures (3D globular forms), and multiple polypeptide chains may assemble into a quaternary structure.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.10 (Structure of Proteins)

questions.question: Arrange the following stages of the catalytic cycle of an enzyme in the correct chronological order:
options: Substrate binding -> Formation of ES complex -> Formation of EP complex -> Release of products
Formation of ES complex -> Substrate binding -> Release of products -> Formation of EP complex
Substrate binding -> Formation of EP complex -> Formation of ES complex -> Release of products
Release of products -> Formation of ES complex -> Substrate binding -> Formation of EP complex
questions.explanation: The catalytic cycle begins with the substrate binding to the enzyme's active site (E+S -> ES), followed by chemical transformation into the enzyme-product complex (EP), and finally the release of the products (E+P).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.12 (Nature of Enzyme Action)

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of events that occurs when an enzyme lowers the activation energy of a reaction:
options: Binding of substrate to active site -> Conformational change in enzyme -> Breaking/making of bonds -> Release of products
Breaking of bonds -> Binding of substrate -> Conformational change -> Release of products
Release of products -> Binding of substrate -> Breaking of bonds -> Conformational change
Conformational change -> Binding of substrate -> Release of products -> Breaking of bonds
questions.explanation: The enzyme binds the substrate, induces a conformational change (fit), facilitates bond breaking/making to form the transition state, and releases the products.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.12 (Nature of Enzyme Action)

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of steps to demonstrate the presence of glucose in a biological sample using the standard chemical test mentioned in NCERT?
options: Add Benedict's reagent -> Heat the mixture -> Observe color change (Blue to Brick Red) -> Identify presence of reducing sugar
Add Iodine solution -> Heat the mixture -> Observe color change (Blue to Black) -> Identify presence of glucose
Add Biuret reagent -> Heat the mixture -> Observe color change (Violet) -> Identify presence of glucose
Add Ethanol -> Shake -> Observe emulsion -> Identify presence of glucose
questions.explanation: Benedict's test is used to detect reducing sugars like glucose; heating the mixture with the reagent results in a color change from blue to brick red.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.5 (Primary and Secondary Metabolites)

questions.question: Arrange the following in the sequence of increasing complexity of carbon-containing compounds found in living tissues:
questions.explanation: Amino acids are the monomers, which link to form polypeptides, which then fold to form complex functional proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.10 (Structure of Proteins)

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of events in the DNA double helix replication/structure formation according to base pairing rules:
options: Sugar-phosphate backbone formation -> Hydrogen bonding between complementary bases -> Helix coiling
Helix coiling -> Hydrogen bonding -> Sugar-phosphate backbone formation
Hydrogen bonding -> Sugar-phosphate backbone formation -> Helix coiling
Sugar-phosphate backbone formation -> Helix coiling -> Hydrogen bonding
questions.explanation: The DNA structure consists of a sugar-phosphate backbone with bases projecting inward, held together by specific hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs, resulting in a helical coil.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.11 (Nature of Bond Linking Monomers in a Polymer)

questions.question: Arrange the following phases of metabolic pathways in a cell in terms of the sequence of energy flow:
options: Anabolic pathway (building) -> Storage -> Catabolic pathway (breaking) -> Release of energy
Catabolic pathway -> Release of energy -> Anabolic pathway -> Storage
Storage -> Catabolic pathway -> Anabolic pathway -> Release of energy
Release of energy -> Anabolic pathway -> Catabolic pathway -> Storage
questions.explanation: Anabolic pathways build complex molecules from simpler ones (requiring energy), while catabolic pathways break them down, releasing energy for cellular functions.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.4 (Primary and Secondary Metabolites)

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of events when a competitive inhibitor acts on an enzyme?
options: Inhibitor resembles substrate -> Inhibitor binds to active site -> Substrate cannot bind -> Reaction rate decreases
Inhibitor binds to non-active site -> Inhibitor resembles substrate -> Reaction rate increases -> Substrate binds
Substrate binds -> Inhibitor binds to active site -> Reaction rate increases -> Product forms
Inhibitor binds to active site -> Substrate binds to inhibitor -> Reaction rate increases -> Product forms
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors structurally resemble the substrate and compete for the active site, physically blocking the substrate and reducing the reaction rate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.13 (Factors Affecting Enzyme Activity)

questions.question: Arrange the following steps for the formation of a glycosidic bond between two monosaccharides:
options: Hydroxyl group of one sugar aligns with hydroxyl group of another -> Dehydration (removal of H2O) -> Formation of C-O-C bond
Hydrogen bonding -> Addition of H2O -> Formation of C-O-C bond
Formation of C-O-C bond -> Removal of CO2 -> Dehydration
Dehydration -> Formation of C-O-C bond -> Addition of H2O
questions.explanation: Glycosidic bonds are formed by dehydration synthesis where a water molecule is removed between the hydroxyl groups of two monosaccharides, creating an oxygen bridge.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Biology Class XI, Chapter 9: Biomolecules, Section 9.11 (Nature of Bond Linking Monomers in a Polymer)

questions.question: In the diagram of an amino acid structure, identify the group represented by 'R' that determines the specific chemical properties of the amino acid.
questions.explanation: In the general structure of an amino acid, the alpha-carbon is attached to an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen atom, and a variable 'R' group which differentiates amino acids.
questions.ncertEvidence: The R group in these proteinaceous amino acids could be a hydrogen (the amino acid is glycine), a methyl group (alanine), hydroxy methyl (serine), etc.

questions.question: Identify the bond labelled 'X' in the diagram of a peptide bond between two amino acids.
questions.explanation: A peptide bond is formed between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, resulting in a C-N linkage.
questions.ncertEvidence: The bond is formed by the reaction of the carboxyl group of one amino acid with the amino group of the next amino acid with the elimination of a water moiety.

questions.question: In the diagram of a DNA double helix, which component is represented by the label connecting the sugar-phosphate backbone to the nitrogenous base?
questions.explanation: The nitrogenous base is linked to the pentose sugar via an N-glycosidic linkage.
questions.ncertEvidence: A nucleic acid containing deoxyribose is called deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). The nitrogenous base is attached to the sugar via a N-glycosidic bond.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the primary structure of a protein, what does the linear sequence of amino acids represent?
questions.explanation: The primary structure of a protein is simply the linear sequence of amino acids, which provides the positional information for the protein.
questions.ncertEvidence: The sequence of amino acids i.e., the positional information in a protein - which is the first amino acid, which is second, and so on - is called the primary structure of a protein.

questions.question: In the diagram of a triglyceride molecule, identify the chemical linkage represented by the ester bond.
questions.explanation: Triglycerides are formed by the esterification of three fatty acid molecules with one glycerol molecule.
questions.ncertEvidence: Fats and oils are glycerides i.e., fatty acid esters of glycerol.

questions.question: In a diagrammatic representation of a nucleotide, which component is attached to the 5' carbon of the pentose sugar?
questions.explanation: In a nucleotide, the phosphate group is attached to the 5' carbon of the sugar via a phosphoester bond.
questions.ncertEvidence: When a phosphate group is also linked to OH of 5'C of a nucleoside through phosphoester linkage, a corresponding nucleotide is formed.

questions.question: In a diagram of the alpha-helix structure of a protein, which interaction is primarily responsible for maintaining the helical shape?
questions.explanation: The alpha-helix is a secondary structure of proteins maintained by hydrogen bonding between the amino acids in the polypeptide chain.
questions.ncertEvidence: The protein thread does not exist throughout as an extended rigid rod. The thread is folded in the form of a helix (similar to a DNA spiralling). Of course, only some portions of the protein thread are arranged in the form of a helix. In proteins, only right handed helices are observed.

questions.question: In the diagram of a cellulose chain, what type of glycosidic linkage is observed between glucose units?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose units linked by beta 1-4 glycosidic bonds.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cellulose is a polymeric polysaccharide consisting of only one type of monosaccharide i.e., glucose. Cellulose is a homopolymer.

questions.question: In a diagram of the active site of an enzyme, what is the primary role of the cleft or pocket?
questions.explanation: The active site is a crevice or pocket into which the substrate fits, allowing for the catalytic reaction to occur.
questions.ncertEvidence: The active site of an enzyme is a crevice or pocket into which the substrate fits.

questions.question: In a diagram showing the transition state of a chemical reaction, what does the 'activation energy' represent?
options: Energy difference between substrate and transition state
questions.explanation: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy required to convert substrates into the transition state.
questions.ncertEvidence: The difference in the average energy content of 'S' from that of this transition state is called 'activation energy'.

questions.question: In the structural formula of an amino acid, if the R-group is a methyl group (-CH3), identify the amino acid and its property based on the chemical structure.
options: Serine; it contains a hydroxyl group.
Valine; it is a basic amino acid.
questions.explanation: When R is a methyl group, the amino acid is Alanine. Since the central carbon is bonded to four different groups (H, NH2, COOH, CH3), it is chiral and optically active.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.1: Amino acids structure where R-group determines the identity; Alanine has CH3 group.

questions.question: Observe the structure of a nitrogenous base. If it consists of a double-ring heterocyclic structure, which of the following is correct regarding its pairing in DNA?
options: It is a pyrimidine that pairs with cytosine.
It is a purine that pairs with a pyrimidine via two or three hydrogen bonds.
It is a pyrimidine that pairs with thymine.
It is a purine that pairs with another purine to maintain constant helix width.
questions.explanation: Double-ring structures are Purines (Adenine, Guanine). In DNA, they pair with single-ring Pyrimidines to maintain the uniform width of the DNA helix.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.5: Nitrogen bases in nucleic acids; Purines (Adenine, Guanine) and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil, Thymine).

questions.question: Consider the structure of a triglyceride. If the R-groups attached to the glycerol backbone are saturated fatty acids, what is the expected physical state at room temperature?
options: Liquid, because of the presence of double bonds.
Solid, as they have higher melting points due to packing.
Gaseous, due to low molecular weight.
Liquid, because saturated fats cannot form intermolecular forces.
questions.explanation: Triglycerides with saturated fatty acids (no double bonds) pack tightly, resulting in higher melting points and a solid state at room temperature (fats).
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.3: Lipids; fats (saturated) vs oils (unsaturated) and their physical state.

questions.question: Looking at the structure of a nucleoside versus a nucleotide, what is the essential chemical difference observed in the diagram?
options: A nucleotide contains a phosphate group attached to the sugar.
A nucleoside contains a phosphate group attached to the base.
A nucleotide lacks a pentose sugar.
A nucleoside contains a nitrogenous base while a nucleotide does not.
questions.explanation: A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base linked to a pentose sugar. When a phosphate group is also esterified to the sugar, it is termed a nucleotide.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.5: Nucleic acids; definition of nucleoside and nucleotide.

questions.question: In the chemical structure of a polysaccharide like cellulose, what is the nature of the glycosidic linkage inferred from the linear arrangement?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a homopolymer of glucose units linked by beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds, which results in a straight, unbranched chain.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.4: Polysaccharides; cellulose structure and its linkages.

questions.question: If you analyze the structure of a phospholipid, which part of the molecule is responsible for its amphipathic nature?
options: The phosphate head is hydrophobic and fatty acid tails are hydrophilic.
The glycerol backbone is hydrophilic and fatty acid tails are hydrophobic.
The phosphate-containing head is hydrophilic and fatty acid tails are hydrophobic.
Both the head and tails are hydrophilic.
questions.explanation: Phospholipids have a polar hydrophilic 'head' (containing phosphate and often a nitrogenous base) and non-polar hydrophobic fatty acid 'tails'.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.3: Lipids; phospholipids as structural components of cell membranes.

questions.question: In the secondary structure of a protein (alpha-helix), what maintains the stability of the coiled conformation?
options: Hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen of one amino acid and the amino hydrogen of another.
Hydrophobic interactions between non-polar side chains.
questions.explanation: The alpha-helix is stabilized by hydrogen bonds formed between the C=O group of one amino acid and the N-H group of the fourth amino acid down the chain.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.6: Proteins; secondary structure involving folding into alpha-helices or beta-pleated sheets via hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: Observe the structure of a monosaccharide. How many carbon atoms are present in a typical pentose sugar like ribose?
questions.explanation: A pentose sugar, by definition, contains five carbon atoms. Ribose is a classic example found in RNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.4: Carbohydrates; classification based on carbon number, with pentose having 5 carbons.

questions.question: In the diagram of an enzyme-substrate complex, what does the 'transition state' represent?
options: The final product state with the lowest energy.
The unstable structural state between the substrate and the product.
The state where the enzyme is permanently bonded to the substrate.
The state where the substrate is converted into a co-factor.
questions.explanation: The transition state is the high-energy, unstable intermediate configuration that the substrate must reach to be converted into the product.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.8: Nature of enzyme action; concept of transition state and activation energy.

questions.question: When examining the structure of a peptide bond between two amino acids, which atoms are involved in the bond formation?
options: The C of the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the N of the amino group of the next.
The N of the amino group of one amino acid and the C of the R-group of the next.
The O of the carboxyl group and the H of the R-group.
The C of the alpha-carbon and the N of the amino group.
questions.explanation: A peptide bond is formed by the dehydration synthesis between the carboxyl (-COOH) group of one amino acid and the amino (-NH2) group of the adjacent amino acid.
questions.ncertEvidence: Biomolecules, Section 9.12.6: Proteins; formation of peptide bonds between amino acids.

questions.question: Which of the following organismal substances is classified as a secondary metabolite rather than a primary metabolite?
questions.explanation: Primary metabolites have identifiable functions in normal physiological processes, while secondary metabolites like rubber, drugs, and pigments have no direct role in normal growth but are produced by organisms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Secondary metabolites are products like alkaloids, flavonoids, rubber, essential oils, antibiotics, etc., which have no direct role in normal physiological processes.

questions.question: In the context of the chemical composition of living tissues, which of the following is found in the 'acid-insoluble fraction' obtained after grinding tissue in trichloroacetic acid?
questions.explanation: The acid-insoluble fraction contains macromolecules (biomolecules) like proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides, and lipids with a molecular weight of 10,000 Daltons and above.
questions.ncertEvidence: The acid-insoluble fraction contains the four types of organic compounds: proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids.

questions.question: Which specific amino acid is synthesized by the pancreas and functions as a neurotransmitter in mammals?
questions.explanation: Glutamic acid is an amino acid that acts as a neurotransmitter in the mammalian central nervous system.
questions.ncertEvidence: Some amino acids like glutamic acid act as neurotransmitters.

questions.question: Which polysaccharide is the primary structural component of the exoskeleton of arthropods?
questions.explanation: Chitin is a complex polysaccharide (a polymer of N-acetyl glucosamine) that forms the structural framework of the exoskeleton in arthropods.
questions.ncertEvidence: Chitin is a complex polysaccharide which is the main component of the exoskeleton of arthropods.

questions.question: Among the following, which is considered a 'homopolymer' composed of only one type of monosaccharide unit?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a polymer of glucose, Inulin is a polymer of fructose, and Chitin is a polymer of N-acetyl glucosamine; all are homopolymers.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cellulose is a polymeric polysaccharide consisting of only one type of monosaccharide i.e., glucose. Inulin is a polymer of fructose.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the protein 'GLUT-4' in human physiology?
options: Acts as an intercellular ground substance
questions.explanation: GLUT-4 is a membrane protein responsible for the transport of glucose into cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells.

questions.question: Which enzyme category is responsible for catalyzing the linking of two compounds together?
questions.explanation: Ligases are enzymes that catalyze the joining of two molecules, such as linking two compounds together.
questions.ncertEvidence: Ligases: Enzymes catalysing the linking together of 2 compounds.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-proteinaceous enzyme found in biological systems?
questions.explanation: Ribozymes are nucleic acids (RNA) that possess catalytic activity, unlike most other enzymes which are proteins.
questions.ncertEvidence: There are some nucleic acids that behave like enzymes. These are called ribozymes.

questions.question: In the double helix model of DNA, what is the distance between two adjacent base pairs?
questions.explanation: The distance between two adjacent base pairs in the B-DNA double helix is 0.34 nm (or 3.4 Å).
questions.ncertEvidence: The distance between two adjacent base pairs is 0.34 nm.

questions.question: Which factor significantly affects the velocity of an enzymatic reaction by altering the ionization state of the active site?
questions.explanation: Enzymes are sensitive to pH changes because the ionization of amino acid side chains at the active site is critical for catalytic function.
questions.ncertEvidence: Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of pH. Enzymatic activity declines both below and above the optimum value.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct primary location and functional role of GLUT-4 in human physiology?
options: Cell membrane; enables glucose transport into cells
Cytoplasm; synthesizes glucose from amino acids
Endoplasmic reticulum; modifies glucose for storage
questions.explanation: GLUT-4 is a membrane protein that functions as a glucose transporter, essential for the uptake of glucose into cells.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3 in Chapter 9 (Biomolecules) lists GLUT-4 as a protein that enables glucose transport into cells.

questions.question: Which component is primarily responsible for the structural integrity of the plant cell wall and is classified as a homopolymer?
questions.explanation: Cellulose is a polysaccharide (homopolymer) consisting of only glucose monomers, providing structural support to plant cell walls.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states cellulose is a polymeric polysaccharide consisting of only one type of monosaccharide (glucose) and is the most abundant organic molecule on earth.

questions.question: Identify the storage form of glucose in plants and its functional characteristic based on iodine reaction.
options: Starch; forms helical secondary structures that can hold I2
Cellulose; forms linear chains that react with I2
Glycogen; stores energy in the liver and muscles
Inulin; a polymer of fructose used for osmotic regulation
questions.explanation: Starch forms helical secondary structures which are capable of holding iodine molecules, resulting in a blue color.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT explicitly mentions starch forms helical secondary structures and can hold I2 molecules in the helical portion.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the enzyme 'Trypsin' and where is it active?
options: Proteolysis; active in the small intestine
Lipid digestion; active in the stomach
Nucleic acid synthesis; active in the nucleus
questions.explanation: Trypsin is a proteolytic enzyme (protein-digesting) that functions in the small intestine.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3 lists Trypsin as a protein-digesting enzyme.

questions.question: Which substance serves as a reserve food material in plants and is a polymer of fructose?
questions.explanation: Inulin is a polymer of fructose, not glucose, and functions as a storage carbohydrate in certain plant roots.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states inulin is a polymer of fructose.

questions.question: What is the specific functional location of 'Collagen' in the animal kingdom?
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world and constitutes the extracellular ground substance in connective tissues.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states collagen is the most abundant protein in animal world and is found in intercellular ground substance.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a biomolecule with its classification based on function?
questions.explanation: Antibodies are proteins that help fight infectious agents.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3 in Chapter 9 lists the functions of proteins, identifying antibodies as agents that fight infectious organisms.

questions.question: Where is glycogen stored in humans, and what is its chemical nature?
options: Liver and muscles; a branched polymer of glucose
questions.explanation: Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide in animals, found in liver and muscle, and is highly branched.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states glycogen is the storage polysaccharide in animals and is found in liver, muscle, and yeast.

questions.question: Which protein is responsible for the transmission of sensory signals and is located in the cell membrane?
questions.explanation: Receptors are proteins located in the cell membrane that receive and transmit sensory signals.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3 lists 'Receptor' as a protein that receives sensory reception (smell, taste, hormone, etc.).

questions.question: What is the primary function of the protein 'Insulin'?
options: Transport of oxygen in the blood
questions.explanation: Insulin is a hormone that regulates glucose metabolism in the body.
questions.ncertEvidence: Table 9.3 identifies Insulin as a protein functioning as a hormone.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct structural feature of cellulose that prevents it from forming complex helices like starch?
options: It is a homopolymer of beta-glucose linked by beta 1-4 glycosidic bonds
It is a branched polymer of alpha-glucose linked by alpha 1-6 glycosidic bonds
It contains only alpha-1,4 glycosidic linkages forming a linear chain
