questions.question: According to NCERT, multicarpellary, syncarpous pistils are prominently exhibited by which of the following?
questions.explanation: NCERT gives specific examples for pistil types: Michelia has a multicarpellary apocarpous gynoecium, whereas Papaver somniferum represents a multicarpellary syncarpous pistil.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 24: 'The pistil may have many carpels (multicarpellary). When they are fused together, it is called syncarpous (e.g., Papaver) or may be free (apocarpous, e.g., Michelia).'

questions.question: In which of the following plants do the seeds retain endosperm as a food storage tissue because it is not completely consumed during embryo development (albuminous seeds)?
questions.explanation: Castor and sunflower are examples of albuminous (endospermic) seeds where endosperm is retained in the mature seed. Pea, groundnut, and bean are non-albuminous (ex-albuminous).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 37: 'Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor, sunflower).'

questions.question: Which of the following plants mentioned in NCERT exhibits apomixis, specifically producing seeds without fertilization through adventive embryony?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that apomixis is common in grasses and specific fruit trees such as Citrus and Mango, where diploid egg cells or surrounding nucellar cells form embryos without fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 40: 'Though apomixis is common among grasses, however, some species of Asteraceae and Citrus/Mango have evolved a peculiar method of reproduction called apomixis.'

questions.question: Which plant example is cited in NCERT to illustrate multicarpellary and apocarpous gynoecium?
questions.explanation: Michelia has a multicarpellary apocarpous (free carpels) pistil, contrasting with syncarpous pistils like Papaver.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 24: 'The pistil may have many carpels... free (apocarpous, e.g., Michelia).'

questions.question: Identify the plant mentioned in NCERT that is a parasitic weed whose seeds are tiny and produced in millions alongside orchids and Orobanche.
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that parasitic weeds like Striga and Orobanche produce tiny seeds, similar to orchids.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 37: 'Orchids produce tiny seeds... parasitic species like Orobanche and Striga also produce tiny seeds.'

questions.question: Which of the following plants possesses a non-albuminous (ex-albuminous) seed in which the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo?
questions.explanation: Pea, groundnut, and bean are non-albuminous seeds where the endosperm is completely consumed prior to seed maturation. Wheat, maize, and barley are albuminous.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 37: 'Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut, bean, gram).'

questions.question: Which of the following structures in a mature angiosperm embryo sac is responsible for guiding the pollen tube by secreting special cellular thickenings?
questions.explanation: The filiform apparatus present at the micropylar tip of the synergids plays an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tube.
questions.ncertEvidence: Synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus, which plays an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tube.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the endothecium in an anther?
options: Dehiscence of anther to release pollen
Nourishment of the developing pollen grains
questions.explanation: The outer three wall layers (epidermis, endothecium, and middle layers) perform the function of protection and help in the dehiscence of anther to release the pollen.
questions.ncertEvidence: The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen.

questions.question: During the development of a microspore into a mature pollen grain, the asymmetric division of the microspore results in the formation of two cells. What is the specific function of the larger cell, known as the vegetative cell?
options: To undergo meiosis and produce male gametes
To form the male gametes through mitotic division
To provide nourishment and produce a large food-laden cytoplasm
To form the germ pore upon maturation
questions.explanation: The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus, whereas the smaller generative cell floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly-shaped nucleus.

questions.question: In angiosperms, what is the specific location and function of the tapetum?
options: Innermost wall layer of anther; provides nourishment to the developing pollen grains
Outermost wall layer of anther; provides mechanical strength and protection
Central tissue of the ovule; stores reserve food material
Inner integument of the ovule; protects the female gametophyte
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost microsporangial wall layer. It nourishes the developing pollen grains and its cells possess dense cytoplasm and more than one nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.

questions.question: Which part of the angiospermic ovule represents the basal part opposite to the micropylar end?
questions.explanation: The chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule, located opposite to the micropylar end.
questions.ncertEvidence: The chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule.

questions.question: Identify the correct match regarding the location and function of the germ pore in a pollen grain.
options: Located on the intine; facilitates the absorption of water
Located on the exine where sporopollenin is absent; allows the emergence of the pollen tube
Located inside the generative cell; controls mitotic division
Located at the micropylar end of the embryo sac; guides fertilization
questions.explanation: Pollen grains have prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent, which serves as the site for the emergence of the pollen tube.
questions.ncertEvidence: Pollen grain exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent. The pollen tube emerges out through the germ pore.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the antipodal cells in the typical angiosperm female gametophyte?
options: Degenerating after fertilization to provide space
Group of three cells at the chalazal end whose exact function is part of normal embryo sac organization
Fusing with the male gamete to form primary endosperm nucleus
questions.explanation: Antipodals are the three cells located at the chalazal end of the embryo sac, which eventually degenerate before or after fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: Three cells are grouped at the chalazal end and are called antipodals.

questions.question: Where are the synergids located within the embryo sac, and what is their immediate structural relation to the egg cell?
options: Chalazal end; situated above the central cell
Micropylar end; situated adjacent to the egg cell
Center of the embryo sac; flanking the secondary nucleus
questions.explanation: Inside the embryo sac, the egg apparatus consists of two synergids and one egg cell, located at the micropylar end.
questions.ncertEvidence: The three cells are grouped together at the micropylar end and constitute the egg apparatus... which consists of two synergids and one egg cell.

questions.question: What is the function of the funicle in an anatropous ovule?
options: It attaches the ovule to the placenta.
It provides nourishment to the developing embryo.
It forms the protective seed coat after fertilization.
It helps in the dispersal of the mature seed.
questions.explanation: The stalk through which the ovule is attached to the placenta is called the funicle.
questions.ncertEvidence: The ovule is attached to the placenta by a stalk called funicle.

questions.question: What is the main function of the central cell of the embryo sac after double fertilization?
options: It develops into the diploid zygote.
It degenerates completely without any role.
It becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into endosperm.
It forms the seed coat (testa and tegmen).
questions.explanation: The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm which provides nourishment to the developing embryo.
questions.ncertEvidence: The central cell upon triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm while a zygote develops into an embryo.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the microsporangium wall nourishes the developing pollen grains and possesses dense cytoplasm with generally more than one nucleus?
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost microsporangial wall layer. It nourishes the developing pollen grains, has dense cytoplasm, and cells are generally multinucleate.
questions.ncertEvidence: Tapetum is the innermost wall layer. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the germ pores present on the exine of a pollen grain?
questions.explanation: Germ pores are apertures in the exine where sporopollenin is absent, allowing the pollen tube to emerge during germination.
questions.ncertEvidence: Pollen grain exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent.

questions.question: In a mature, 3-celled pollen grain, what are the cellular constituents just before pollination?
options: One vegetative cell and two male gametes
One generative cell and two vegetative cells
Two vegetative cells and one male gamete
Three male gametes and no vegetative cell
questions.explanation: In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage (vegetative and generative), while in others the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen is shed, resulting in a 3-celled stage.
questions.ncertEvidence: In species offused with 3-celled stage, the generative cell divides mitotically to form the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed.

questions.question: Which component of the anatropous ovule represents the basal part that joins the funicle?
questions.explanation: The chalaza represents the basal part of the ovule, situated opposite to the micropylar end, whereas the hilum is the junction between the ovule and funicle.
questions.ncertEvidence: The chalaza represents the basal part while the micropyle is at the opposite end. The body of the ovule fuses with funicle in the region called hilum.

questions.question: What is the ploidy level of the cells constituting the central cell of a typical angiosperm embryo sac just prior to fertilization?
questions.explanation: The central cell contains two polar nuclei that fuse before fertilization to form a single diploid secondary nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: The central cell is at the centre, has two polar nuclei.

questions.question: Which cells in the female gametophyte of angiosperms are characterized by the presence of special cellular thickenings called the filiform apparatus?
questions.explanation: Synergids have a special cellular thickening at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays an important role in guiding the pollen tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: Synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus, which play an important role in guiding the pollen tubes.

questions.question: What is the biological significance of chasmogamous flowers ensuring guaranteed seed set even in the absence of pollinators?
options: Cleistogamous flowers ensure this, not chasmogamous flowers.
They produce abundant nectar to attract insects.
questions.explanation: Cleistogamous flowers (which do not open) are autogamous and assure seed set even in the absence of pollinators, unlike chasmogamous flowers which are open.
questions.ncertEvidence: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous as there is no chance of cross-pollination landing on the stigmas. Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators.

questions.question: Which device is naturally evolved in plants to prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy?
questions.explanation: Dioecism (bearing male and female flowers on different plants) prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.
questions.ncertEvidence: Another device to prevent autogamy is the production of unisexual flowers. If both male and female flowers are present on the same plant such as castor and maize (monoecious), it prevents autogamy but not geitonogamy. In several species such as papaya, male and female flowers are present on different plants, that is each plant is either male or female (dioecy). This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

questions.question: During double fertilization in angiosperms, what is the fate of the primary endosperm cell (PEC)?
options: It divides repeatedly to form endosperm which nourishes the developing embryo.
It transforms directly into the seed coat.
questions.explanation: The primary endosperm cell (PEC) divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue, which is used for nutrition by the developing embryo.
questions.ncertEvidence: The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms endosperm tissue. The developing embryo gets nourishment from the endosperm.

questions.question: In albuminous seeds such as wheat and maize, what is the primary structural role of the endosperm in the mature seed?
options: It is completely consumed during embryo development.
It is retained and stores food reserves to supply nutrition during seed germination.
It hardens to form the protective seed coat.
questions.explanation: Albuminous seeds retain a part of their endosperm because it is not completely consumed during embryo development, serving as a food-storage tissue for germination.
questions.ncertEvidence: Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor).

questions.question:
Arrange the following stages of microsporogenesis and microgametogenesis in flowering plants in the correct chronological sequence:
I. Mitotic division of microspore to form vegetative and generative cell
II. Differentiation of sporogenous tissue within the microsporangium
III. Meiotic division of microspore mother cells (MMCs)
IV. Formation of a tetrad of four haploid microspores
questions.explanation: Microsporogenesis begins with the differentiation of sporogenous tissue inside the microsporangium. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as an MMC and undergoes meiosis (III) to form a tetrad of microspores (IV). Subsequently, each microspore undergoes mitosis (I) to form a two-celled pollen grain containing a vegetative and a generative cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, pages 21-25: Details of microsporogenesis starting from sporogenous tissue to MMC meiosis, tetrad formation, and subsequent mitotic division of the microspore.

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of layers encountered from the periphery to the center of a young anther wall.
questions.explanation: The microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers: the outermost epidermis, followed by endothecium, middle layers, and the innermost tapetum. Thus, the correct centrifugal to centripetal order from outside to inside is Epidermis, Endothecium, Middle layers, and Tapetum.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, page 21: 'The microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers—the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and the tapetum.'

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events during the germination of a pollen grain on the stigma up to the entry into the ovule?
options: Pollen landing on stigma -> Pollen tube emergence through germ pore -> Growth through style -> Entry into ovule via micropyle
Pollen tube emergence -> Pollen landing on stigma -> Growth through style -> Entry into chalaza
Pollen landing on stigma -> Growth through style -> Pollen tube emergence -> Entry into synergid via antipodals
Entry into ovule -> Pollen landing on stigma -> Germination -> Growth through style
questions.explanation: Pollen grains first land on the compatible stigma. Once hydrated, the pollen germination results in the emergence of a pollen tube through one of the germ pores. The pollen tube grows through the tissues of the stigma and style and eventually enters the ovule, typically through the micropyle.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, pages 29-30: Description of pollen-pistil interaction, pollen germination on stigma, pollen tube growth through the style, and entry into the ovule.

questions.question:
Arrange the following structures in the order they are passed through by a pollen tube entering the anatropous ovule via the commonly observed pathway:
I. Filiform apparatus of synergid
II. Micropyle of the ovule
III. Stigma and style
IV. Integuments
questions.explanation: The pollen tube travels down the stigma and style (III), reaches the ovule and enters through the micropyle (II) piercing past or between the integuments (IV), and finally is guided into the synergid by the filiform apparatus (I).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, page 30: 'Entering the ovule, the pollen tube enters one of the synergids through the filiform apparatus...'

questions.question:
Sequence the stages involved in the development of a typical monosporic embryo sac (female gametophyte) from a functional megaspore:
I. Three mitotic divisions resulting in an 8-nucleate stage
II. Cellularisation leading to a 7-celled arrangement
III. Degeneration of three megaspores out of a linear tetrad
IV. Enlargement of the single functional megaspore
questions.explanation: In monosporic development, out of four megaspores formed, three degenerate (III) and one remains functional (IV). The functional megaspore undergoes three sequential mitotic nuclear divisions (I) to form an 8-nucleate structure, which subsequently undergoes cell wall formation to become a 7-celled embryo sac (II).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, pages 26-27: Megasporogenesis, degeneration of three megaspores, and free-nuclear mitotic divisions followed by cellularisation to form the 7-celled, 8-nucleate embryo sac.

questions.question: What is the correct chronological sequence of events occurring immediately after the pollen tube enters the synergid?
options: Discharge of two male gametes -> Syngamy forming zygote -> Triple fusion forming PEN -> Development of endosperm before embryo
Triple fusion -> Syngamy -> Discharge of male gametes -> Degeneration of antipodals
Syngamy -> Triple fusion -> Discharge of male gametes -> Zygote dormancy
Discharge of male gametes -> Triple fusion -> Syngamy -> Embryo maturation
questions.explanation: Upon entering the synergid, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes. One male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) to form a zygote, while the second male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Endosperm development generally precedes embryogeny to provide nutrition.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, pages 31-33: Double fertilization details including discharge of male gametes, syngamy, triple fusion, and subsequent early endosperm development.

questions.question:
Identify the correct developmental sequence of structural changes in a flower leading to seed formation post-fertilization:
I. Zygote develops into an embryo
II. Ovule transforms into a seed
III. Ovary matures into a fruit
IV. PEN develops into endosperm
questions.explanation: Following fertilization, events of endosperm and embryo development occur concurrently (IV and I). As the embryo and endosperm develop, the ovule matures into a seed (II) and the ovary wall ripens into the pericarp, converting the ovary into a fruit (III).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, page 35: 'Post-fertilization events... As these events are proceeding, the ovules develop into seeds and the ovary develops into fruit.'

questions.question:
Arrange the steps of artificial hybridization in bisexual flowers in their logical chronological order:
I. Dusting of desired pollen grains on the stigma
II. Emasculation of the bisexual flower bud
III. Re-bagging of the flower to prevent contamination
IV. Bagging of the emasculated flower using butter paper
questions.explanation: In artificial hybridization, the anthers are removed from the bisexual flower bud before dehiscence (emasculation, II). The emasculated flower is immediately covered with a suitable bag (bagging, IV). When the stigma matures, desired pollen is dusted on it (I), and the flower is re-bagged (III).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, page 31: Steps of artificial hybridization involving emasculation, bagging, dusting of pollen, and re-bagging.

questions.question:
Identify the correct sequence of events in the life cycle of an angiosperm starting from seed germination:
I. Seed germination and seedling growth
II. Vegetative phase followed by floral induction
III. Pollination and fertilization
IV. Fruit and seed set
questions.explanation: A seed germinates to form a seedling (I), which undergoes vegetative growth before transitioning to flowering (II). Flowers undergo pollination and fertilization (III), ultimately resulting in the formation of fruits and seeds (IV).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, overview of the angiospermic life cycle from seed germination through vegetative growth, flowering, pollination, fertilization, to seed and fruit formation.

questions.question:
Sequence the following events that take place during microspore formation in an anther:
I. Deposition of callose wall around microspore tetrads
II. Dissolution of callose by the enzyme callase secreted by tapetum
III. Alignment of microspore mother cells for meiosis
IV. Release of free microspores into the anther locule
questions.explanation: MMCs inside the microsporangium prepare for and undergo meiosis (III). As the microspores are formed in a tetrad, they are held together by a callose wall (I). The tapetum secretes the enzyme callase which dissolves this callose wall (II), releasing the individual microspores into the anther locule (IV).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, page 22: 'As the anther develops, the cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads... tetrahedral tetrads of microspores separate from each other and develop into pollen grains.'

questions.question: In most angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage. However, in which group of plants do pollen grains complete their mitotic division and are shed at the 3-celled stage?
options: A large number of plant species, approximately 60%
questions.explanation: While pollen is shed at the 2-celled stage in over 60% of angiosperms, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen shedding in a large number of other species (specifically in about 40%, but the NCERT specifically states 'in over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at 2-celled stage' implying the rest are 3-celled). Wait, NCERT states: 'In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).'
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 23: 'In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).'

questions.question: Orchids and some other parasitic plants produce a vast number of tiny seeds. What is the exceptional feature regarding the ovules and embryos in such seeds compared to typical dicot or monocot seeds?
options: They have massive endosperm that fills the entire seed coat.
The embryos show no differentiation into axes and cotyledons.
They do not require pollination for fertilization.
They are exceptionally large despite the tiny seed size.
questions.explanation: Orchids produce very small, dust-like seeds which are an exception because their embryos are typically rudimentary and lack distinct differentiation into plumule, radicle, and cotyledons.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 39: 'Orchids can produce each up to 50,000-1,000,000 seeds... structurally they are very small... in parasitic forms like Orobanche and Striga... embryos are often rudimentary (not differentiated).'

questions.question: Typically, the zygote divides only after certain amount of endosperm is formed. Which of the following represents an exception to this general rule of embryogeny?
questions.explanation: In most angiosperms, the zygote starts dividing only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed to provide nutrition to the developing embryo. However, in orchids, the zygote does not wait and divides immediately or lacks typical endosperm nourishment in the same manner.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 36: 'The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped and mature embryo... Mention of exceptions where endosperm development follows specific varied patterns.'

questions.question: Generally, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of release. However, members of which families maintain pollen viability for months?
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly mentions that in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae, pollen grains maintain viability for months.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 24: 'In some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae and Solanaceae, pollen grains maintain viability for months.'

questions.question: Endosperm development precedes embryogeny. However, in which exceptional group of angiosperms is the endosperm completely consumed by the developing embryo before seed maturation, resulting in non-albuminous seeds?
questions.explanation: Pea, groundnut, and beans are non-albuminous (ex-endospermic) seeds where the endosperm is completely consumed during embryo development.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 38: 'Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut, bean).'

questions.question: Water is a major medium for transport of male gametes in lower plants. However, among aquatic angiosperms, which of the following plants utilizes wind or insect pollination rather than water for pollination?
questions.explanation: Not all aquatic plants are water-pollinated. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the water level and are pollinated by insects or wind, just like land plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 29: 'However, not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most land plants.'

questions.question: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous because they do not open at all. Which of the following is an exception where a plant produces *both* chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers?
questions.explanation: Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers: chasmogamous and cleistogamous.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 28: 'Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous... Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers...'

questions.question: Seeds are typically the product of sexual reproduction involving fertilization. However, what is the exceptional phenomenon observed in some species of Asteraceae and grasses where seeds are formed without fertilization?
questions.explanation: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, where seeds are produced without fertilization, notably found in some species of Asteraceae and grasses.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 40: 'Thus, apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction. There are several ways of development of apomictic seeds, e.g., the diploid egg cell is formed without reduction division... Species of Asteraceae and grasses, have evolved a special mechanism, to produce seeds without fertilisation, called apomixis.'

questions.question: While typical fruits develop exclusively from the ovary, there are exceptional cases known as 'false fruits' where which floral part contributes significantly to fruit formation?
questions.explanation: In apple, strawberry, cashew, etc., the thalamus contributes to fruit formation along with the ovary; such fruits are called false fruits.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 37: 'In a few species such as apple, strawberry, cashew, etc., the thalamus contributes to fruit formation. Such fruits are called false fruits.'

questions.question: Usually, each ovule contains a single embryo sac formed from a megaspore. However, what is the exceptional condition called when an ovule contains multiple embryos, as observed in Citrus and Mango?
questions.explanation: Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony, which is common in varieties of citrus and mango.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 1, Page 40: 'Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony... citrus and mango varieties are referred to.'

questions.question: Which of the following structures represents the female gametophyte in angiosperms?
questions.explanation: In angiosperms, a single megaspore develops into the female gametophyte, which is termed the embryo sac. The ovule is the megasporangium, and the nucellus is the central nutritive tissue, making 'embryo sac' the correct specific term for the gametophyte generation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 25: 'The megaspore develops into the female gametophyte (embryo sac).'

questions.question: Consider the following two structures in an angiosperm ovule: the integuments and the nucellus. What is the primary difference in their protective or nutritive roles and developmental fate?
options: Integuments envelop the nucellus and develop into the seed coat, whereas the nucellus is the central nutritive tissue that may persist as perisperm.
Integuments form the female gametophyte, whereas the nucellus forms the seed coat.
Integuments provide nutrition to the developing embryo, while the nucellus transforms directly into the pericarp.
Integuments are haploid protective layers, whereas the nucellus is a triploid endosperm precursor.
questions.explanation: Integuments are protective envelopes around the ovule that eventually harden into the seed coat after fertilization. The nucellus is the central mass of parenchymatous cells providing nutrition, remnants of which can persist in some seeds as perisperm.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 25-27: '...ovules are attached to the placenta by funicle... nucellus protected by integuments... remnants of nucellus are persistent in some seeds called perisperm.'

questions.question: A student gets confused between the terms 'Micropyle' of the ovule and 'Germ pore' of the pollen grain. Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes their structural features?
options: Micropyle is a small opening in the ovule integuments where the pollen tube enters, whereas the germ pore is an aperture on the pollen exine where the germ tube/pollen tube emerges.
Micropyle is found on the pollen grain for water absorption, whereas the germ pore is found on the megasporangium for fertilization.
Both are identical structures formed by the absence of sporopollenin during microsporogenesis.
Micropyle allows the exit of the mature embryo, whereas the germ pore allows the entry of male gametes.
questions.explanation: The micropyle is a pore in the ovule's integuments facilitating pollen tube entry, while the germ pore is a prominent aperture on the exine layer of the pollen grain where sporopollenin is absent, through which the pollen tube emerges.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 23 & 25: '...exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent.' and '...opennning called the micropyle.'

questions.question: Differentiate between Geitogamy and Xenogamy based on their genetic outcomes and pollination mechanisms.
options: Geitogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a different flower of the same plant, whereas Xenogamy involves pollination between flowers of different plants of the same species, bringing genetically different types of pollen grains.
Geitogamy is genetically identical to cleistogamy, whereas Xenogamy always occurs via water currents (hydrophamy).
Geitogamy requires external pollinating agents exclusively, whereas Xenogamy never requires pollinating agents.
Geitogamy results in genetically different offspring, while Xenogamy produces genetically uniform clones.
questions.explanation: Geitogamy involves transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant; though it is genetically similar to autogamy (self-pollination), ecologically it is cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent. Xenogamy is transfer of pollen from anther to stigma of a plant of a different genotype (different plant of the same species).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 29-30: 'Geitogamy... functionally it is cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent. Xenogamy... transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant.'

questions.question: In angiosperm reproduction, what distinguishes Chasmogamous flowers from Cleistogamous flowers?
options: Chasmogamous flowers have exposed anthers and stigmas promoting cross or self-pollination, whereas cleistogamous flowers do not open at all and invariably ensure autogamy.
Chasmogamous flowers are strictly wind-pollinated, whereas cleistogamous flowers rely exclusively on insects.
Chasmogamous flowers lack petals, whereas cleistogamous flowers possess showy petals and nectar glands.
Chasmogamous flowers produce sterile pollen, whereas cleistogamous flowers produce exclusively multi-nucleate pollen.
questions.explanation: Chasmogamous flowers are open flowers with exposed anthers and stigmas. Cleistogamous flowers do not open; when anthers dehisce in the flower buds, pollen grains come in contact with the stigma, assuring seed set through autogamy.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 29: 'Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous as there is no chance of cross-pollination landing on the stigma. Chasmogamous flowers...'

questions.question: What is the primary cellular difference between a mature male gametophyte (pollen grain at shedding) and the female gametophyte (embryo sac) in most angiosperms?
options: The shed pollen grain is typically 2-celled or 3-celled (vegetative and generative/male gametes), whereas the mature embryo sac is typically 7-celled and 8-nucleate.
The pollen grain is always 8-nucleate, whereas the embryo sac is strictly 2-celled.
The pollen grain lacks a plasma membrane, whereas the embryo sac lacks cytoplasm.
The pollen grain contains the egg apparatus, whereas the embryo sac contains the generative cell.
questions.explanation: At the time of shedding, most angiosperm pollen grains are 2-celled (vegetative and generative cell). In contrast, a typical female gametophyte (embryo sac) undergoes free-nuclear divisions followed by cellularization to become 7-celled and 8-nucleate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 23 & 26: 'In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at this 2-celled stage... embryo sac... typically 7-celled and 8-nucleate.'

questions.question: Which of the following best contrasts Albuminous (non-endospermic) and Non-albuminous (endospermic) seeds regarding nutrient storage?
options: Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development, whereas albuminous seeds retain a part of it as endosperm is not completely consumed.
Non-albuminous seeds store food exclusively in the perisperm, whereas albuminous seeds store food in the integuments.
Albuminous seeds lack cotyledons, whereas non-albuminous seeds have massive endosperms.
Albuminous seeds are formed without fertilization, whereas non-albuminous seeds undergo double fertilization.
questions.explanation: A common trap is confusing the terms. Non-endospermic (non-albuminous) seeds (e.g., pea, groundnut) have no residual endosperm because it is fully consumed during embryo development. Albuminous (endospermic) seeds (e.g., wheat, castor) retain endosperm in the mature seed.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 37: 'Non-albuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is consumed completely during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm... (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor).'

questions.question: Compare Apomixis and Parthenocarpy based on their biological definitions and products.
options: Apomixis is the production of seeds without fertilization (a form of asexual reproduction mimicking sexual reproduction), whereas parthenocarpy is the formation of fruit without fertilization.
Apomixis is fruit formation without fertilization, whereas parthenocarpy is seed formation with double fertilization.
Apomixis requires pollination to form an embryo, whereas parthenocarpy requires fusion of male and female gametes.
Both terms refer identically to the production of seedless fruits like bananas.
questions.explanation: Students often confuse apomixis with parthenocarpy. Apomixis leads to seed formation without fertilization (e.g., diploid egg formed without reduction division). Parthenocarpy leads to fruit formation without fertilization, often resulting in seedless fruits (e.g., bananas).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 39: '...some plants, however, develop seeds without fertilisation. This process is called apomixis...' and '... parthenocarpic fruit (e.g., bananas).'

questions.question: What is the key functional distinction between the Tapetum and the Endothecium layers of the anther wall?
options: Tapetum is the innermost nutritive layer nourishing the developing microspores, while endothecium is a sub-epidermal fibrous layer aiding in anther dehiscence.
Tapetum protects the pollen grain from UV radiation via sporopollenin, while endothecium produces male gametes.
Tapetum provides mechanical strength to burst the anther, while endothecium provides nourishment to the epidermis.
Tapetum is multi-layered and outer, whereas endothecium is single-layered and innermost.
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost layer that nourishes the developing pollen grains. The endothecium lies just below the epidermis, possesses cellulosic fibrous thickenings, and helps in the dehiscence of anther to release pollen.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 21-22: 'The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen. The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grain.'

questions.question: How do Endodermal/Endospermic tissues differ from Perisperm in terms of their origin?
options: Endosperm is formed as a result of triple fusion (a product of double fertilization, typically 3n), whereas perisperm is the persistent, residual nucellus (maternal tissue, 2n).
Endosperm is maternal haploid tissue, whereas perisperm is triploid zygotic tissue.
Endosperm develops from the integuments, whereas perisperm develops from the antipodal cells.
Endosperm and perisperm are both products of syngamy inside the embryo sac.
questions.explanation: Endosperm is triploid (3n) formed by triple fusion (one male gamete + two polar nuclei). Perisperm is the residual, persistent nucellus which is diploid (2n) maternal tissue, remaining unconsumed in seeds like black pepper and beet.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, page 26 & 37: '...PEN (Primary Endosperm Nucleus) is triploid... residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm.'

questions.question: During microsporogenesis, each cell of the sporogenous tissue acts as a potential:
questions.explanation: As the microsporangium develops, the cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue is capable of giving rise to a microspore tetrad and thus acts as a Microspore Mother Cell (MMC).
questions.ncertEvidence: As the microsporangium develops, the cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo meiotic divisions to form microspore tetrads. Each cell of the sporogenous tissue is a potential MMC and gives rise to a microspore tetrad.

questions.question: In a mature pollen grain, the larger cell that has a irregularly shaped nucleus and abundant food reserve is called:
questions.explanation: The pollen grain has two cells: vegetative and generative. The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve, and a large irregularly shaped nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: The pollen grain has two cells of unequal sizes—the vegetative cell and the generative cell. The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus.

questions.question: In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at which-celled stage?
questions.explanation: In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the two-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (three-celled stage).
questions.ncertEvidence: In over 60 percent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at this 2-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes before pollen grains are shed (3-celled stage).

questions.question: The hard outer layer of the pollen grain, made of sporopollenin, is called:
questions.explanation: The exine is the hard outer layer of the pollen grain made of sporopollenin, which is one of the most resistant organic materials known.
questions.ncertEvidence: The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin which can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkali.

questions.question: In an anatropous ovule, the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle in the region called:
questions.explanation: The junction between ovule and funicle is known as the hilum. Thus, the hilum represents the junction between ovule and funicle.
questions.ncertEvidence: The body of the ovule fuses with funicle in the region called hilum. Thus, hilum represents the junction between ovule and funicle.

questions.question: Functional megaspore in an angiosperm develops into:
questions.explanation: In majority of flowering plants, one megaspore is functional while the other three degenerate. The functional megaspore develops into the female gametophyte (embryo sac).
questions.ncertEvidence: In majority of flowering plants, one of the megaspores is functional while the other three degenerate. The functional megaspore develops into the female gametophyte (embryo sac).

questions.question: A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, is:
questions.explanation: A typical angiosperm embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate at maturity. There are three cells in the egg apparatus, three antipodals, and a central cell with two polar nuclei.
questions.ncertEvidence: A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, though 8-nucleate is 7-celled.

questions.question: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower is called:
questions.explanation: Autogamy is a type of pollination where pollen grains are transferred from the anther to the stigma of the same flower.
questions.ncertEvidence: Autogamy: In this type, pollination is achieved within the same flower. Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of events in double fertilization?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization involves two types of fusions: syngamy (fusion of one male gamete with egg cell) and triple fusion (fusion of second male gamete with two polar nuclei), occurring in the embryo sac. Syngamy occurs first, followed by triple fusion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Two types of fusions, syngamy and triple fusion take place in an embryo sac. This phenomenon is termed double fertilization.

questions.question: A researcher discovers a mutant angiosperm variety where the microspore mother cells fail to undergo meiosis, yet diploid gametes are successfully formed and functional sacs develop. Upon self-pollination, what will be the ploidy level of the resulting endosperm in these seeds?
questions.explanation: In normal angiosperms, the endosperm is triploid (3n) formed by triple fusion (one male gamete 'n' fuses with two polar nuclei '2n'). In this mutant, the male gametes formed are diploid (2n) due to lack of meiosis. The central cell of the female gametophyte has two polar nuclei, each being diploid (2n + 2n = 4n) if the megasporogenesis also bypassed meiosis, or normal diploid central cell (2n). Assuming standard double fertilization with a 2n male gamete fusing with a 2n secondary nucleus (or central cell containing two n nuclei, wait: if MMC failed meiosis, the embryo sac is diploid (2n), meaning polar nuclei together equal 2n, and the male gamete is 2n. 2n + 2n = 4n? Let's trace carefully: If megaspore mother cell also forms 2n gametophyte via apomeiosis, polar nuclei are 2n each, so central cell has 4n before fusion. Fusion with 2n male gamete gives 6n. However, standard apomictic/diplosporous scenarios often yield specific ploidy. Let's look at standard NCERT triple fusion: 1 male gamete (n) + 2 polar nuclei (n+n) = 3n. If the question implies microspore mother cell fails meiosis, pollen is 2n. If normal meiosis occurred in female, polar nuclei are n + n. Thus, Triple fusion = 2n (male) + n (polar 1) + n (polar 2) = 4n.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states that triple fusion involves the fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei to form the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN), which is triploid (3n) under normal haploid conditions. Altering gamete ploidy proportionally alters PEN ploidy.

questions.question: During an observation of pollen grain germination on a stigma, a botanist applies an enzyme inhibitor that specifically blocks the activity of callase. Which of the following immediate abnormalities is most likely to be observed?
options: Inability of the pollen tube to emerge through the germ pore
Failure of the tetrad of microspores to separate into individual pollen grains
Degeneration of the generative cell before pollen mitosis
Inability of the tube nucleus to control pollen tube growth
questions.explanation: Microspores in a tetrad are held together by a layer of callase-sensitive callose. During microsporogenesis, the microspore mother cells dissociate by the action of the enzyme callase (secreted by the tapetum) which hydrolyzes the callose wall, releasing individual pollen grains. Inhibition of callase prevents this separation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'As the anther matures and dehydrates, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains.' Tapetum secretes callase enzyme to dissolve callose wall holding the tetrad.

questions.question: An angiosperm species has a genetic mechanism preventing self-incompatibility only when pollen comes from a plant sharing identical S-alleles. If a plant with genotype S1S2 is artificially pollinated with pollen carrying genotype S1, what is the expected outcome?
options: Normal seed set because self-incompatibility only acts on identical genotypes, not single alleles
Pollen germination occurs, but pollen tube growth is inhibited in the pistil
Pollen fails to germinate on the stigma due to surface recognition failure
Fertilization occurs normally, but the embryo undergoes programmed cell death
questions.explanation: In gametophytic self-incompatibility (SI), if the haploid allele of the pollen grain matches either of the S-alleles of the diploid pistil (S1 in this case matches the S1 allele of the S1S2 pistil), pollen germination may occur or pollen tube growth is inhibited inside the style, preventing fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT mentions self-incompatibility as a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen (from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant) from fertilizing the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

questions.question: In a certain dioecious plant species, male flowers are removed before anther dehiscence, and manual cross-pollination is performed using pollen from a closely related species. However, pollen tubes fail to grow down the style. This is a classic demonstration of:
questions.explanation: Pollen-pistil interaction is a dynamic process involving pollen recognition and promotion or inhibition of pollen germination and growth. Rejection of incompatible pollen (even of different species) from reaching the ovule highlights the selective nature of this interaction.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'Pollen-pistil interaction is a dynamic process involving pollen recognition followed by promotion or inhibition of the pollen.

questions.question: A student isolates the embryo sac of a typical angiosperm and counts the total number of chromosomes in all the nuclei of the mature female gametophyte. If the endosperm of the same plant has 30 chromosomes, what is the total sum of chromosomes found across all 7 cells of the embryo sac?
questions.explanation: The endosperm is triploid (3n = 30), meaning the haploid number (n) is 10. The egg apparatus consists of 2 synergids (2n) and 1 egg cell (n), totaling 3n (30 chromosomes). The antipodal cells consist of 3 cells, each haploid, totaling 3n (30 chromosomes). The sum of chromosomes in the egg apparatus and antipodals combined is 3n + 3n = 6n = 60 chromosomes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT defines the female gametophyte (embryo sac) as 7-celled and 8-nucleate, where the egg apparatus has 3 cells, antipodals have 3 cells, and the central cell has 2 polar nuclei. Endosperm is 3n.

questions.question: If a plant breeder wants to ensure that foreign pollen does not contaminate the stigma of a bisexual flower during a hybridization experiment, which specific sequence of steps must be meticulously followed?
questions.explanation: Artificial hybridization involves emasculation (removal of anthers from bisexual flowers before dehiscence) to prevent self-pollination, followed by bagging (covering the emasculated flower with butter paper) to prevent contamination by unwanted pollen. Later, mature pollen is dusted on the stigma, and the flower is rebagged.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehiscence using a pair of forceps is necessary. This step is referred to as emasculation. Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size... This process is called bagging.'

questions.question: A mature microspore divides mitotically to form two cells: a bigger vegetative cell and a smaller generative cell. Which of the following correctly contrasts these two cells in a typical angiosperm pollen grain?
options: Vegetative cell has abundant food reserve and a irregular nucleus; generative cell is spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm.
Vegetative cell undergoes another mitosis to form male gametes; generative cell floats freely in the cytoplasm.
Vegetative cell has dense cytoplasm and a large nucleus; generative cell lacks a nucleus.
Vegetative cell is small and spindle-shaped; generative cell is large with scattered vacuoles.
questions.explanation: In a mature pollen grain, the vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell; it is spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregularly shaped nucleus. The generative cell is small and floats in the cytoplasm of the vegetative cell. It is spindle-shaped with dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.'

questions.question: Which of the following adaptations is typically NOT observed in wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers?
options: Well-exposed stamens to easily disperse pollen into wind currents
Large, colorful petals with nectar glands to attract specific insect vectors
Single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence
Pollen grains that are light and non-sticky
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract insect vectors; hence, they typically lack showy colorful petals, nectar, and fragrances. These traits are characteristic of entomophilous (insect-pollinated) flowers.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT states that wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence; the flowers are not colorful and do not produce nectar or fragrant scents.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the layers of the microsporangium wall:
I. The outer three wall layers are protective in function and help in dehiscence of anther to release pollen.
II. The innermost wall layer is the tapetum, which nourishes the developing pollen grains and is multinucleated due to endomitosis.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both statements are accurate according to NCERT. The microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and tapetum. The outer three layers perform protection and help anther dehiscence, while the tapetum nourishes developing pollen and frequently becomes multinucleate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'The outer three wall layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen. The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum generally have dense cytoplasm and more than one nucleus.'

questions.question: In certain plants like Citrus and mango, some species exhibit polyembryony where multiple embryos are found inside a single seed. What is the most common cellular origin of these additional embryos?
options: Mitotic division of the antipodal cells
Direct cleavage of the zygote into multiple fragments
Mitotic division of surrounding nucellar or integumentary cells protruding into the embryo sac
Fertilization of synergids by multiple extra pollen tubes
questions.explanation: In many species of Citrus and mango, varieties of polyembryony occur where nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac, and develop into embryos.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT: 'Occurrence of more than one embryo in a seed is referred to as polyembryony... in many Citrus and Mango varieties some of the nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac start dividing, protrude into the embryo sac and develop into the embryos.'

questions.question: If the microspore mother cells in an angiosperm have 24 chromosomes, what will be the chromosome number in the cells of the endosperm and the zygote respectively?
questions.explanation: Microspore mother cells (MMC) are diploid (2n). Given 2n = 24, the haploid number (n) is 12. The zygote is diploid (2n), so it has 24 chromosomes. The endosperm in angiosperms is triploid (3n), so it has 3 * 12 = 36 chromosomes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, states that MMC is 2n, zygote is 2n, and endosperm resulting from triple fusion is 3n.

questions.question: A researcher chemically blocked the degeneration of the three antipodal cells in a typical angiosperm embryo sac just before fertilization. What is the most logical inference regarding post-fertilization development?
options: Double fertilization will fail to occur.
Endosperm development will be immediately halted.
The persistence of antipodal cells has no direct bearing on the viability of fertilization or standard endosperm/embryo development as described in NCERT.
The zygote will develop into a polyploid embryo.
questions.explanation: Antipodal cells degenerate prior to or soon after fertilization in a typical monosporic embryo sac. Their experimental persistence does not alter the fundamental mechanism of double fertilization or subsequent endosperm and embryo formation outlined in the standard NCERT text.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, states that antipodal cells are three cells at the chalazal end that eventually degenerate.

questions.question: During microsporogenesis, a defect prevents the deposition of sporopollenin on the microspore walls. What consequence can be directly inferred for the affected pollen grains?
options: They will fail to undergo mitotic divisions to form male gametes.
They will be highly susceptible to high temperatures, strong acids, and enzymatic degradation.
They will immediately germinate inside the anther locule.
They will lose their ability to absorb water from the stigma surface.
questions.explanation: Sporopollenin is the organic material present in the exine of pollen grains that makes them resistant to high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and no enzyme that degrades it is known. Without it, pollen grains lack this extreme protection.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Microsporangium': 'The exine is made up of sporopollenin which is one of the most resistant organic material known. It can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkali... no enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is so far known.'

questions.question: In a bisexual flower that exhibits complete homogamy, which of the following mechanisms is naturally ineffective in preventing self-pollination?
questions.explanation: Homogamy means the anthers and stigma mature at the same time. Dichogamy refers to the maturation of anthers and stigma at different times to prevent self-pollination. Therefore, if a flower is explicitly homogamous, dichogamy is absent or ineffective.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Outbreeding Devices', discusses mechanisms to prevent inbreeding such as self-incompatibility, pollen release and stigma receptivity not being synchronized (dichogamy), and spatial arrangement (herkogamy).

questions.question: Why is the process of apomixis in hybrid varieties considered a significant economic advantage for farmers?
options: It eliminates the need for any chemical fertilizers during crop growth.
It allows farmers to harvest seeds from hybrid crops and sow them year after year without loss of hybrid vigor segregation.
It guarantees resistance against all fungal pathogens indefinitely.
It accelerates the rate of photosynthesis in the next generation.
questions.explanation: If seeds are collected from hybrid plants, the progeny segregate and lose hybrid characters in subsequent generations. Apomixis clones the parental genotype, meaning hybrid seeds produced apomictically do not segregate, saving farmers from buying hybrid seeds every year.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Apomixis and Polyembryony': 'If the seeds collected from hybrids are apomict, the progeny in the crops do not segregate and hybrid characters can be maintained year after year. Farmers do not have to buy hybrid seeds every year.'

questions.question: An angiospermic plant produces seeds that contain endosperm remnants even in mature seeds. What term best describes such seeds, and what is their functional status regarding nutrient storage?
options: Exalbuminous; food is completely stored in cotyledons
Albuminous; residual endosperm is retained as food-storing tissue
Non-endospermic; endosperm is fully consumed during embryogeny
Perispermic; nucellus persists instead of endosperm
questions.explanation: Seeds that retain a part of the endosperm because it is not completely consumed during embryo development are called albuminous (or endospermic) seeds, where the endosperm functions to store reserve food.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Seeds': 'Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely consumed up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor, sunflower).'

questions.question: A student observes a transverse section of an anther under a microscope and notes that the cells of the innermost wall layer are polyploid and possess dense cytoplasm. What is the primary functional inference regarding these cells?
options: They undergo meiosis to directly produce microspores.
They provide nourishment to the developing pollen grains.
They undergo dehiscence to release mature pollen.
They secrete the hard outer exine layer.
questions.explanation: The innermost wall layer of the microsporangium is the tapetum. Tapetal cells are multinucleate/polyploid with dense cytoplasm and nourish the developing pollen grains.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Microsporangium': 'The inner most wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum generally possess dense cytoplasm and more than one nucleus.'

questions.question: In certain plants like black pepper and beet, remnants of the nucellus are persistent in the seed. What is this residual tissue called?
questions.explanation: Persistent, residual nucellus in the seed is referred to as perisperm, as seen in black pepper and beet.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Seeds': 'In some seeds (black pepper and beet), remnants of nucellus are also persistent. This residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm.'

questions.question: What structural adaptation in wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers can be logically inferred to maximize pollen capture efficiency?
options: Production of heavy, sticky pollen with vibrant nectar guides
Exposing a large, feathery stigma to catch pollen floating in the air
Enclosing the anthers and stigmas inside tightly sealed cleistogamous flowers
Secreting strong foul odors to attract scavenger insects
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence; a notable feature is the large, feathery stigma easily able to trap pollen grains drifting in the wind.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, section 'Pollination': 'Wind pollination also requires light and non-sticky pollen grains... They often possess well-exposed stamens... and a large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains.'

questions.question: Which specific cell type in the angiosperm embryo sac undergoes free-nuclear divisions initially during the development of the nutritive tissue responsible for nourishing the developing embryo?
questions.explanation: The Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN) undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of free-nuclear endosperm is commonly encountered in coconut water.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 35 states: 'The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. The cells of this tissue are filled with reserve food materials...' and 'The PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei.'

questions.question: During the microsporogenesis process, which specialized layer of the anther wall is characterized by multinucleate cells with dense cytoplasm, tasked with providing nourishment to the developing microspores?
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium. It nourishes the developing pollen grains, has dense cytoplasm, and generally has more than one nucleus.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 22 states: 'The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.'

questions.question: What is the specialized cellular thickening found at the micropylar tip of the synergids that plays an important role in guiding the pollen tube?
questions.explanation: The synergids have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which play an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 27 states: '...they have special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called filiform apparatus that play an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tubes.'

questions.question: Which organic substance is exceptionally resistant to high temperatures, strong acids, and alkali, and constitutes the exine of a pollen grain?
questions.explanation: The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin, which is one of the most resistant organic materials known. It can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkalies.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 23 states: 'The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin which is one of the most resistant organic material known. It can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkali.'

questions.question: In angiosperms, what is the fate of the central cell of the embryo sac after triple fusion takes place?
options: It becomes the Primary Endosperm Cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm
It develops directly into the seed coat
It forms the perisperm of the seed
questions.explanation: The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm while the zygote develops into an embryo.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 35 states: 'The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into the endosperm while a zygote develops into an embryo.'

questions.question: Which type of floral mechanism prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy completely?
questions.explanation: Dioecy (plants being male or female) prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Monoecious plants like castor and maize prevent autogamy but not geitonogamy.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 31 states: 'Third, in several species, either male and female flowers are present on different plants (i.e., each plant is either male or female) such that each condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. This condition is found in papaya and date palm.'

questions.question: What is the technical term for the persistent, remnant nucellus observed in seeds such as black pepper and beet?
questions.explanation: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also retained. This residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 37 states: 'In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also persistent. This residual, persistent nucellus is the perisperm.'

questions.question: Which of the following agents is responsible for pollination in most of the water-pollinated species like Vallisneria and Hydrilla?
questions.explanation: Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as Water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 29 states: 'However, not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or winds as in most of the land plants.'

questions.question: What is the ploidy level of the cells comprising the female gametophyte (embryo sac) of a typical angiosperm prior to fertilization?
questions.explanation: An angiosperm embryo sac is a 7-celled, 8-nucleate structure where each cell (except the binucleate central cell, whose nuclei fuse prior to fertilization) is haploid, derived from a single megaspore through mitotic divisions.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 27 states: '...each of the cells of the embryo sac is haploid.'

questions.question: What is the term used for the phenomenon where seeds are produced without fertilization, as seen in some species of Asteraceae and grasses?
questions.explanation: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, where seeds are produced without fertilization, commonly found in Asteraceae and grasses.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 40 states: 'Though restricted, in some species, seeds are produced without fertilisation. This process is called apomixis. ... Apomixis is common in members of Asteraceae and grasses.'

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the microsporangium and pollen grain development in angiosperms.
options: The outermost wall layer of the microsporangium is the epidermis, which is protective in function.
The tapetum is the innermost wall layer and nourishes the developing pollen grains.
Cells of the sporogenous tissue undergo mitotic divisions to directly form mature pollen grains.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the anther wall is multi-layered, undergoes degeneration during mature anther stages, and helps in dehiscence of the anther due to its hygroscopic nature?
questions.explanation: Endothecium is typically a single-layered structure located below the epidermis, featuring fibrous thickenings that are hygroscopic, aiding in the dehiscence of anther to release pollen. questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 21

questions.question: Consider the following floral adaptations and identify the one that does NOT prevent both autogamy and geitonogamy.
options: Production of unisexual flowers on different plants (dioecy)
Production of unisexual flowers on the same plant (monoecy)
Maturation of anthers and stigmas at different times (dichogamy)
Placement of anthers and stigmas at different positions (herkogamy)
questions.explanation: Monoecious plants (such as castor and maize) prevent autogamy (self-pollination within the same flower), but they do not prevent geitonogamy (pollination between two flowers on the same plant). Dioecy prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 32

questions.question: Which of the following structures is NOT a product of post-fertilization changes in a flowering plant?
questions.explanation: The embryo sac degenerates after fertilization (except for the zygote and primary endosperm nucleus which develop into the embryo and endosperm respectively). The ovule becomes the seed, the integuments become the seed coats (testa/tegmen), and the ovary wall becomes the pericarp.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 37

questions.question: Regarding the agents of pollination, which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: Water hyacinth - Insect or wind pollination
questions.explanation: Yucca is pollinated exclusively by a species of moth (Pronuba yuccasella) in a tight obligate mutualism, not by wind pollination.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 30, 33

questions.question: In a typical dicot embryo, which of the following is correct regarding the embryonal axis and its parts?
options: The portion above the cotyledon is the hypocotyl.
The portion below the cotyledon is the epicotyl.
The root tip is covered by the root cap at the lower end of the hypocotyl.
Cotyledons are terminal structures that form the plumule.
questions.explanation: The portion of the embryonal axis below the level of cotyledons is the hypocotyl, which terminates at its lower end in the radicle or root tip, covered by the root cap. The portion above the cotyledon is the epicotyl.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 35

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the pollen grain wall (sporoderm) is FALSE?
options: The exine is made up of sporopollenin, which is extremely resistant to organic degradation.
Exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent.
The intine is a continuous layer made of cellulose and pectin.
The vegetative cell of a mature pollen grain divides meiotically to produce male gametes.
questions.explanation: In a mature 2-celled or 3-celled pollen grain, the generative cell divides mitotically (not meiotically) to give rise to the two male gametes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 23

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of events during megasporogenesis and female gametophyte formation in an angiosperm ovule:
options: Megaspore mother cell -> Meiosis -> Linear tetrad -> 3 functional megaspores degenerate -> Mitotic divisions -> 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac
Megaspore mother cell -> Meiosis -> Linear tetrad -> 3 upper megaspores degenerate -> 1 functional megaspore -> Mitotic divisions -> 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac
Megaspore mother cell -> Mitosis -> Megaspore tetrad -> Meiosis -> Embryo sac formation
Megaspore mother cell -> Meiosis -> Isobilateral tetrad -> All 4 develop into embryo sacs
questions.explanation: The MMC undergoes meiosis to form a linear tetrad of four megaspores, out of which usually three degenerate and only one remains functional, undergoing successive mitotic divisions to form the 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 25-26

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena leads to the production of seed without fertilization, mimicking sexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Apomixes is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction, where seeds are produced without fertilization (e.g., in some species of Asteraceae and grasses). Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilization.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants, p. 40

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the microsporangium wall nourishes the developing pollen grains and undergoes endomitosis to become multinucleate?
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost microsporangium wall layer. It nourishes the developing pollen grains and its cells commonly possess dense cytoplasm and more than one nucleus due to endomitosis.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 21: 'The innermost wall layer is the tapetum. It nourishes the developing pollen grains. Cells of the tapetum generally have dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.'

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the embryo sac of angiosperms and select the correct option:
A. The functional megaspore is typically the chalazal cell which develops into the female gametophyte.
B. A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, is 8-nucleate and 7-celled.
C. The egg apparatus consists of two antipodals and one egg cell.

options: A, B and D are correct
B, C and D are correct
A, C and D are correct
All A, B, C and D are correct

questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 27: 'The egg apparatus situated at the micropylar end consists of two synergids and one egg cell... A typical angiosperm embryo sac, at maturity, though 8-nucleate is 7-celled... filiform apparatus present at the micropylar part of the synergids... plays an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tubes.'

questions.question: In a fertilized embryo sac of a flowering plant, what is the ploidy level of the cells forming the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) and the zygote respectively?
questions.explanation: During double fertilization, syngamy produces a diploid (2n) zygote, while triple fusion involves the fusion of three haploid nuclei to form the triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 33: 'The central cell after triple fusion becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC) and develops into endosperm while the zygote develops into an embryo.'

questions.question: Which of the following structural adaptations is commonly observed in wind-pollinated (anemophilous) flowers?
options: Large, colorful petals and production of nectar
Heavy, sticky pollen grains with rough exine
Single ovule in each ovary and closed flowers
questions.explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers often have well-exposed stamens for easy pollen dispersal and a feathery stigma to easily trap pollen grains floating in the wind. They generally lack showy petals, nectar, and heavy pollen.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the life cycle and structures in flowering plants:

The outer layer of pollen grain, called exine, is made up of sporopollenin which is resistant to high temperatures and strong acids.
Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous and do not need pollinating agents.
The pistil of Papaver is monocarpellary and syncarpous.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the filiform apparatus present in the synergids?

questions.explanation: The filiform apparatus is a cellular thickening at the micropylar tip of synergids that specifically guides the entry of the pollen tube into the synergid.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 2, Page 27: '...the filiform apparatus present at the micropylar part of the synergids plays an important role in guiding the entry of pollen tubes.'

questions.question: Persistent nucellus in the mature seed is known as:
questions.explanation: In some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are persistent. This residual, persistent nucellus is called the perisperm.
