GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, involving transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one (C-1). ICSI stands for Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection, a laboratory procedure to form an embryo by direct injection of sperm into the ovum (D-3).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.3 and 4.4 (MTP and Amniocentesis / Assisted Reproductive Technologies)

questions.question:
Match the types of IUDs in List I with their respective examples in List II:

List I:
A. Non-medicated IUD
B. Copper releasing IUD
C. Hormone releasing IUD

List II:
1. Lippes loop
2. Copper T
3. Progestasert
4. Multiload 375
5. LNG-20

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD (A-1). Copper T and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing IUDs (B-2 and 4). Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs (C-3 and 5).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception)

questions.question:
Match the contraceptive methods in List I with their characteristic feature in List II:

List I:
A. Periodic abstinence
B. Coitus interruptus
C. Lactational amenorrhea
D. Vasectomy

List II:
1. Couples avoid coitus from day 10 to 17 of menstrual cycle
2. Male partner withdraws penis from the vagina just before ejaculation
3. Relies on the absence of ovulation during intense lactation
4. Irreversible surgical method in males

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Periodic abstinence involves avoiding coitus during the fertile period (days 10-17 of the menstrual cycle) (A-1). Coitus interruptus (withdrawal) involves the male partner withdrawing his penis just before ejaculation (B-2). Lactational amenorrhea utilizes the absence of ovulation during intense lactation postpartum (C-3). Vasectomy is a surgical termination of fertility (sterilization) in males (D-4).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception - Natural methods and Surgical methods)

questions.question:
Match the terms related to amniocentesis and assisted reproductive technologies in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I:
A. Amniocentesis
B. In vitro fertilization
C. Artificial insemination
D. IUT

List II:
1. Fetal sex determination and genetic disorder test based on chromosomal pattern in amniotic fluid
2. Fertilization outside the body in almost similar conditions as in the body
3. Transfer of semen collected from husband or donor into the uterus
4. Transfer of embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is a fetal sex determination and genetic disorder test using chromosomal analysis of amniotic fluid cells (A-1). In vitro fertilization (IVF) is fertilization outside the body under simulated body conditions (B-2). Artificial insemination (AI) involves transferring semen into the female vagina or uterus (C-3). Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT) refers to transferring embryos with more than 8 blastomeres directly into the uterus (D-4).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.3 and 4.4 (Amniocentesis and Assisted Reproductive Technologies)

questions.question:
Match the barrier methods of contraception in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I:
A. Condoms
B. Diaphragms
C. Cervical caps
D. Vaults

List II:
1. Barrier made of thin rubber/latex sheath used to cover penis in males or vagina/cervix in females
2. Barrier made of rubber inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus
3. Reusable rubber barrier covering the uterine cervix specifically
4. Dome-shaped rubber barriers covering the vault of the vagina

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath used to cover the penis in males or vagina/cervix in females (A-1). Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barriers made to cover the cervix during coitus in females, with specific anatomical coverages corresponding to diaphragms (B-2), cervical caps (C-3), and vaults (D-4) as described in NCERT.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception - Barrier methods)

questions.question:
Match the contraceptive terms in List I with their clinical attributes in List II:

List I:
A. Saheli
B. Progestasert
C. Tubectomy
D. Vasectomy

List II:
1. Once-a-week oral pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value
2. Hormone releasing intrauterine device
3. Surgical sterilization in females involving blockage of fallopian tubes
4. Surgical sterilization in males involving blockage of vas deferens

Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Saheli is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill developed by CDRI Lucknow, taken once a week (A-1). Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD (B-2). Tubectomy is surgical sterilization in females involving cutting and tying fallopian tubes (C-3). Vasectomy is surgical sterilization in males involving cutting and tying vas deferens (D-4).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception)

questions.question:
Match the following categories related to sexually transmitted infections (STIs) based on their curability and causative pathogen type:

List I:

questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.3 (Contraception) - Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs).

questions.question: What is the location and purpose of the procedure known as Amniocentesis?
options: Sampling of amniotic fluid surrounding the developing fetus to determine genetic disorders and sex
Sampling of chorionic villi directly from the placenta for hormone assays
Sampling of maternal blood to detect fetal heart rate abnormalities
Sampling of uterine tissue to check for endometrial thickness
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is a fetal sex determination test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo, also used to detect genetic disorders.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Amniocentesis).

questions.question: Which of the following barrier methods of contraception is specifically designed to be inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix just before coitus?
questions.explanation: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus to block the entry of sperm. Vasectomy and tubectomy are surgical methods, and CuT is an intrauterine device.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception) - Barrier methods.

questions.question:
Match the contraceptive methods in List I with their corresponding mode of action in List II:

List I (Methods)
A. Multiload 375
B. Withdrawal / Coitus interruptus
C. Lactational amenorrhea
D. Saheli

List II (Mechanism)
1. Prevents ovulation and implantation by altering uterine environment
2. Avoidance of coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle
3. Suppression of ovulation and conception due to absence of menstruation during intense lactation
4. Phallic withdrawal just before ejaculation to insemination prevention
5. Hormone-releasing IUD
questions.explanation: Multiload 375 is a hormone-releasing/copper-releasing IUD (specifically copper-releasing IUD); Withdrawal is coitus interruptus where male withdraws penis before ejaculation; Lactational amenorrhea relies on absence of menstruation during intense lactation; Saheli is a non-steroidal oral pill that prevents implantation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 (Contraception).

questions.question: The primary mechanism by which copper-releasing Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) like CuT prevent pregnancy is by:
options: Increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
Preventing the release of the secondary oocyte from the ovary
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 - Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs).

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) such as 'Saheli':
options: It contains a non-steroidal preparation called centchroman.
It is taken once a week.
It inhibits ovulation and thereby prevents fertilization.
It has very high contraceptive value with few side effects.
questions.explanation: Saheli is a non-steroidal oral pill that acts primarily by preventing implantation, not by inhibiting ovulation, which distinguishes it from conventional steroidal oral pills.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 - Oral Pills.

questions.question: Which permanent surgical method of contraception in females involves cutting and tying a small part of the fallopian tube?
questions.explanation: Tubectomy is a surgical sterilization method in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through vagina. Vasectomy is done in males.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2 - Surgical Methods (Sterilization).

questions.question: MTP (Medical Termination of Pregnancy) is considered relatively safe up to how many weeks of pregnancy?
questions.explanation: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second-trimester abortions are much more risky.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.4 - Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP).

questions.question: Which Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) involves the transfer of an embryo formed by in vitro fertilization with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus?
questions.explanation: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus, a procedure known as Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT). ZIFT involves transfer of embryos up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.6 - Amniocentesis and ART.

questions.question: Amniocentesis is a prenatal diagnostic technique based on the chromosomal pattern of cells found in which of the following?
options: Amniotic fluid surrounding the developing fetus
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis involves taking a small sample of the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing fetus to test for chromosomal abnormalities and genetic disorders.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.6 - Amniocentesis.

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections (STIs) is completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
questions.explanation: Syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydiasis are bacterial STIs that are completely curable if detected early and treated. Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV are currently not completely curable.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.5 - Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).

questions.question: Which Assisted Reproductive Technology is specifically recommended when a male partner has a very low sperm count or inability to ejaculate normally?
questions.explanation: In Artificial Insemination (AI), the semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI) of the female, useful in cases of male infertility due to very low sperm count.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.6 - Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART).

questions.question:
Arrange the following steps involved in IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilization and Embryo Transfer) in the correct chronological order:
I. Fusion of gametes outside the body in simulated conditions
II. Transfer of embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus
III. Stimulation of ovaries for superovulation using FSH
IV. Recovery of mature oocytes (ovum pick-up)
questions.explanation: In IVF-ET, the correct sequence starts with ovarian stimulation (III) to produce multiple eggs, followed by the retrieval of mature oocytes (IV), then fertilization in vitro (I), and finally the transfer of the embryo into the uterus or fallopian tube (II).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 64: 'In this method, popularly known as test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IET).'

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events when using oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) to prevent conception?
options: Inhibition of ovulation and implantation -> Alteration of cervical mucus quality -> Prevention of sperm entry
Alteration of cervical mucus quality -> Inhibition of ovulation and implantation -> Prevention of sperm entry
Prevention of sperm entry -> Inhibition of ovulation and implantation -> Alteration of cervical mucus quality
Suppression of gonadotropins -> Inhibition of ovulation and implantation -> Alteration of cervical mucus quality
questions.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills primarily act by suppressing the release of gonadotropins (FSH and LH) which prevents ovulation, and they also alter the quality of cervical mucus to retard/prevent the entry of sperms and make the endometrium unfavorable for implantation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 60: 'They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as retard the entry of sperms.'

questions.question: Identify the correct chronological sequence of steps in the surgical method of male sterilization (Vasectomy):
options: Ligation of fallopian tube -> Incision in scrotum -> Blocking of gamete transport
Incision in scrotum -> Small part of vas deferens removed/tied up -> Blocking of sperm transport
Blocking of sperm transport -> Incision in abdomen -> Ligation of vas deferens
Puncture of uterus -> Cauterization of vas deferens -> Sterilization
questions.explanation: In vasectomy, a small incision is made in the scrotum, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up (ligated) on both sides, which blocks the transport of sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 61: 'Vasectomy: a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.'

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct order of events during the medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) in the first trimester?
options: Surgical evacuation -> Vacuum aspiration -> Confirmation of pregnancy
Confirmation of pregnancy -> Evaluation of gestational age -> Administration of abortifacient drugs / surgical vacuum aspiration
Cervical dilation -> Hysterectomy -> Fetal heart rate monitoring
Laparoscopy -> Division of zygote -> Uterine curettage
questions.explanation: For MTP, a clinician first confirms the pregnancy and evaluates gestational age (safest in the first trimester, up to 12 weeks), followed by appropriate medical (using drugs) or surgical (vacuum aspiration) procedures.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 62: 'MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy.'

questions.question:
Arrange the steps of ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) in the correct operational sequence:
I. Collection of ova and sperms
II. In vitro fertilization to form zygote
III. Transfer of zygote into the fallopian tube
IV. Ovarian stimulation
questions.explanation: The process begins with ovarian stimulation (IV), followed by the collection of ova and sperms (I), fertilizing them in vitro to form a zygote (II), and finally transferring the zygote into the fallopian tube (III).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 64: 'The zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT)...'

questions.question: What is the correct pathway of events when using barrier methods like condoms?
options: Placement on penis/vagina -> Prevention of ovum release -> Blockage of fertilization
Prevention of sperm meeting ovum -> Physical blocking of gametes -> Reduction of conception risk
Physical blocking of gamete meeting -> Prevention of sperm from entering the female reproductive tract -> Avoidance of fertilization
Inhibition of spermatogenesis -> Barrier placement -> Prevention of implantation
questions.explanation: Barrier methods physically block gametes from meeting. Specifically, condoms prevent the deposition of ejaculated semen into the female reproductive tract, thus preventing sperm from reaching the ovum.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 59: 'Barriers prevent sperms from reaching ovum. These are made of thin rubber/latex sheath...'

questions.question: Identify the correct sequence of events leading to the action of Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) like Copper-T:
options: Insertion into uterus -> Phagocytosis of sperms by macrophages -> Suppression of sperm motility -> Reduction of fertilizing capacity of sperms
Suppression of ovulation -> Thickening of cervical mucus -> Prevention of implantation
Inhibition of implantation -> Release of hormones -> Prevention of zygote formation
Blockage of fallopian tube -> Prevention of ovulation -> Expulsion of zygote
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs (CuT) increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the copper ions released suppress sperm motility and their fertilizing capacity.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 60: 'Cu releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.'

questions.question: Arrange the chronological steps for the diagnosis and management of infertility using GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer):
options: Transfer of zygote to uterus -> Collection of ovum -> Fertilization in vivo
Stimulation of ovaries -> Collection of an ovum from a donor -> Transfer of the ovum into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one
Collection of sperms -> Artificial insemination -> Implantation in cervix
In vitro fertilization -> Embryo culture -> Transfer to fallopian tube
questions.explanation: GIFT involves the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce her own eggs but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further development.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 64: 'Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and further development.'

questions.question: What is the correct sequential progression of diagnostic checks and treatments for a couple undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) due to severe male infertility (very low sperm count)?
options: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) -> Direct injection of sperm into ovum in lab -> Zygote/embryo transfer
Artificial Insemination (AI) -> Natural fertilization -> Tubal transfer
In vitro fertilization -> Ovary stimulation -> Gamete transfer
Vasectomy reversal -> Hormonal therapy -> Natural conception
questions.explanation: In cases of male infertility due to very low sperm count, ICSI is used where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum in the laboratory to form an embryo, which is subsequently transferred.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 64: 'Intra cyto-plasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.'

questions.question: Identify the correct step-by-step sequence in the mechanism of Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM):
options: Intense lactation after parturition -> High prolactin levels -> Suppression of gonadotropins -> Absence of ovulation and menstruation
Suppression of ovulation -> Absence of lactation -> Menstruation resumption
High estrogen and progesterone -> Stimulation of menstruation -> Ovulation prevention
Intense lactation -> Increased LH surge -> Implantation prevention
questions.explanation: LAM is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. High levels of prolactin suppress gonadotropins, thus preventing ovulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Page 59: 'Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.'

questions.question: Which of the following birth control methods is an exception because it permanently blocks gamete transport rather than being a temporary barrier or hormonal method?
questions.explanation: Surgical methods (sterilization) like vasectomy and tubectomy are permanent methods that block gamete transport, whereas lactational amenorrhea, diaphragms, and oral pills are temporary methods.
questions.ncertEvidence: Surgical methods, also known as sterilization, are advised for male/female partners as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. Vasectomy is sterilization in males.

questions.question: All of the following are statutory reasons for Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) in India except:
options: To get rid of an unwanted pregnancy resulting from unprotected casual sex after the first trimester
Continuation of pregnancy posing a grave threat to the life of the pregnant woman
Risk that if the child is born, it would suffer from physical or mental abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped
questions.explanation: MTPs are legally allowed to avoid unwanted pregnancies due to unprotected sex or contraceptive failure only up to 12 weeks (first trimester) under the opinion of one registered medical practitioner. After the first trimester (up to 22 weeks), two registered medical practitioners are required, and simple unprotected casual sex without risk to the mother or fetus is not a legal ground for late-term termination.
questions.ncertEvidence: MTPs are considered safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second trimester abortions are much more riskier. Grounds include failure of contraceptives, rape, or risk to mother/child.

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections (STIs) is an exception to the rule of being completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, and chlamydiasis are bacterial STIs and are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. However, infections like Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV infections are not completely curable.
questions.ncertEvidence: Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: Among the following contraceptive options, which one does NOT function by inhibiting ovulation or fertilization, acting instead as an exception by primarily preventing implantation?
questions.explanation: Copper releasing IUDs (like CuT) increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity of sperms, while hormonal methods inhibit ovulation and implantation. CuT specifically acts primarily by preventing implantation and affecting sperm function, unlike pills or LAM which suppress ovulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

questions.question: Which of the following methods of contraception relies entirely on the natural physiological absence of menstruation during intense lactation, making it an exception that is effective only up to a maximum limited period?
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. However, this is effective only up to a maximum period of 6 months following parturition.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lactational amenorrhea method (absence of menstruation) is based on the fact that ovulation do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. However, this method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of six months following parturition.

questions.question: Identify the exception among Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) where fertilization is strictly in vivo (inside the female body) rather than in vitro:
questions.explanation: GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube where fertilization happens in vivo. ICSI, IUT, and ZIFT involve in vitro (laboratory) fertilization or handling of embryos.
questions.ncertEvidence: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilisation and further development.

questions.question: In the context of amniocentesis, which statement represents an exception to its original legitimate medical utility and is legally penalized in India?
options: Determining the sex of the foetus to lead to female foeticide
Detecting chromosomal abnormalities like Down's syndrome
Identifying genetic metabolic disorders like phenylketonuria
Diagnosing fetal infections or developmental anomalies
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is legally permitted for detecting genetic disorders or chromosomal abnormalities. Using it for sex determination leading to female foeticide is legally banned in India to check statutory female infanticides.
questions.ncertEvidence: Amniocentesis is legally banned for sex-determination to legally check increasing menace of female foeticide.

questions.question: Which of the following contraceptive barriers for females is an exception because it is reusable, unlike male condoms which are single-use items?
questions.explanation: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barriers fitted into the female reproductive tract. Male and female condoms are strictly single-use disposable items.
questions.ncertEvidence: Condoms are disposable items. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are made of rubber and are reusable.

questions.question: All of the following barrier methods are designed for use by the female partner except:
questions.explanation: Nirodh is a popular brand of male condom. Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are barrier methods designed for females.
questions.ncertEvidence: Barriers are available for both males and females. Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in male or vagina and cervix in female.

questions.question: Which of the following hormones is the primary active agent found in emergency contraceptive pills when taken within 72 hours of coitus?
questions.explanation: Emergency contraceptives contain progestogens alone or progestogen-estrogen combination administered within 72 hours of coitus to avoid pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.
questions.ncertEvidence: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives.

questions.question: Choose the correct pair of barrier methods for birth control where one is specifically designed for males and the other exclusively for females, noting that both are single-use disposables.
options: Condoms for males and diaphragms for females
Condoms for males and cervical caps for females
Condoms for males and condoms for females
Vaults for females and diaphragms for females
questions.explanation: Both male and female condoms are barrier methods that are disposable (single-use), whereas diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are reusable rubber barriers.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 59: 'Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus... These are disposable.'

questions.question: A couple is confused between the mechanisms of Copper-releasing IUDs and Hormone-releasing IUDs. Which of the following correctly contrasts their primary modes of action within the uterus?
options: Cu ions suppress sperm motility, while hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms
Cu ions prevent ovulation, while hormone-releasing IUDs phagocytose sperms inside the fallopian tube
Cu ions cause phagocytosis of sperms in the cervix, while hormones inhibit gametogenesis
Cu ions make the cervix hostile to sperms, while hormone-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs (like CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) release Cu ions which suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity of sperms. Hormone-releasing IUDs (LNG-20, progestasert) make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 60: 'IUDs ... increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. The hormone-releasing IUDs, in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.'

questions.question: Identify the primary conceptual difference in the contraceptive action between periodic abstinence and coitus interruptus (withdrawal).
options: Periodic abstinence relies on avoiding coitus during the entire luteal phase, whereas coitus interruptus relies on avoiding ejaculation inside the vagina during coitus.
Periodic abstinence avoids coitus during the fertile period (Day 10-17 of menstrual cycle), whereas coitus interruptus involves withdrawal of the penis just before ejaculation.
Periodic abstinence prevents ovulation hormonally, whereas coitus interruptus acts as a permanent surgical method.
Periodic abstinence is a barrier method, whereas coitus interruptus is a natural method based on calendar calculation of safe periods.
questions.explanation: Periodic abstinence is based on abstaining from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation is expected (fertile period). Coitus interruptus is a natural method where the male partner withdraws his penis just before ejaculation to insemination avoidance.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 59: 'Periodic abstinence... couples abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle... Coitus interruptus... male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation.'

questions.question: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is often confused in its safety profile based on the trimester. Which statement accurately represents the legal and physiological safety of MTP according to NCERT?
options: MTPs are safely completed during the second trimester, while first-trimester abortions are invariably fatal.
First-trimester abortions are generally safe, whereas second-trimester abortions are much more risky.
Second-trimester MTPs are legally permitted without any medical practitioner's approval up to 24 weeks.
MTP is a contraceptive method meant to replace barrier methods for routine birth control.
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly states that MTPs during the first trimester are generally safe, whereas second-trimester abortions are much more risky and dangerous.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 62: 'MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second-trimester abortions are much more riskier.'

questions.question: Vasectomy and tubectomy are both permanent contraceptive methods (sterilization). What is the fundamental difference in what they block?
options: Vasectomy blocks the vas deferens preventing sperm transport, while tubectomy blocks the fallopian tube preventing ovum transport.
Vasectomy blocks the urethra, while tubectomy blocks the uterus directly.
Vasectomy stops testosterone production in testes, while tubectomy stops estrogen production in ovaries.
Vasectomy blocks the epididymis, while tubectomy blocks the vagina.
questions.explanation: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, blocking sperm transport. In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up, blocking ovum transport.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 61: 'Surgical methods, also called sterilisation... In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up... In tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up...'

questions.question: A student often gets confused between Lactational Amenorrhea and natural periodic abstinence. Select the correct physiological basis that distinguishes Lactational Amenorrhea.
options: It relies on the calendar method to predict ovulation failure during lactation.
It is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition, preventing conception due to high prolactin levels.
It involves the surgical blockage of milk ducts which indirectly stops menstruation.
It is a chemical method utilizing hormonal pills secreted in milk.
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are practically nil up to six months.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 59-60: 'Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.'

questions.question: Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) and emergency contraceptives both contain hormones. How do their composition and timing of usage typically differ?
options: OCPs are taken daily for 21 days starting within the first five days of the menstrual cycle, whereas emergency contraceptives are taken within 72 hours of coitus.
Emergency contraceptives are taken daily, whereas OCPs are taken only after unprotected intercourse.
OCPs contain only progesterone, whereas emergency pills contain only estrogen.
Emergency contraceptives prevent implantation by surgical removal, whereas OCPs prevent fertilization.
questions.explanation: Oral pills are taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle. Emergency contraceptives (progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations) are used within 72 hours of coitus as emergency contraception.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 60: 'Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combination is used by females as contraceptives... taken daily for a period of 21 days... Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can also be used as emergency contraceptives within 72 hours of coitus...'

questions.question: Distinguish between Amniocentesis and Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) regarding their primary statutory and clinical objectives in India.
options: Amniocentesis is used exclusively for sex determination, whereas ART is used for treating infertility.
Amniocentesis is a fetal sex determination test legally banned for misuse to detect female foeticide, whereas ART helps infertile couples have children.
Amniocentesis is a surgical sterilization method, whereas ART is a barrier method.
Amniocentesis determines chromosomal abnormalities and is legally banned for all purposes, whereas ART is mandatory for all couples after 5 years of marriage.
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is a prenatal diagnostic technique legally checked/banned for sex determination to prevent female foeticide, though its statutory use is to detect genetic disorders. ART refers to special techniques helping infertile couples.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, pages 62 & 63: 'Amniocentesis... legally banned for sex-determination to legally check increasing menace of female foeticide... Assisted reproductive technologies (ART)... special techniques that assist infertile couples to have children.'

questions.question: In the context of Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART), what is the key procedural difference between ZIFT and GIFT?
options: ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube, whereas GIFT transfers an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube.
ZIFT transfers embryos into the uterus, whereas GIFT transfers sperms into the vagina.
ZIFT stands for Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer of sperms, while GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer of embryos.
ZIFT is in-vivo fertilization method, while GIFT is in-vitro fertilization method.
questions.explanation: ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transfer of zygote or early embryos (upto 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube. GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 64: 'ZIFT: transfer of a zygote or early embryos (upto 8 blastomeres) into fallopian tube... GIFT: transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube who cannot produce one...'

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections (STIs) is considered completely curable if detected early and treated properly, contrasting with viral STIs like HIV and Herpes?
questions.explanation: Syphilis, gonorrhoea, and chlamydiasis are bacterial STIs that are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. In contrast, infections like Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV are incurable.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, page 65: 'Except for Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.'

questions.question: Read the following statement regarding methods of contraception: 'Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of fertilization by preventing ovulation.' Identify the term that makes this statement incorrect and select its correct replacement according to NCERT.
options: Replacing 'preventing ovulation' with 'preventing sperm and ovum from meeting'
questions.explanation: Natural methods of contraception work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting, whereas barrier methods or oral pills may prevent ovulation or sperm entry. Specifically, natural methods like periodic abstinence, withdrawal, and lactation amenorrhea prevent coitus during the fertile period to prevent sperm and ovum from meeting.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.1: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting.

questions.question: Consider the statement about oral contraceptive pills: 'Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen are used by females as tablets that are taken orally, which inhibit implantation and also alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard entry of sperms.' Which word in this statement must be changed to make it factually accurate according to NCERT regarding the primary action of combined pills?
options: Change 'inhibit implantation' to 'inhibit ovulation and implantation'
questions.explanation: Oral pills inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Mentioning only inhibition of implantation is incomplete; pills primarily inhibit ovulation as well.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.4: They [pills] inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms.

questions.question: In the context of Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs), read the statement: 'Copper releasing IUDs like CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375 suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.' If the word 'suppress' is replaced incorrectly, which of the following alternative words maintains the exact biological mechanism described in NCERT?
questions.explanation: Copper ions released by copper-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility and their fertilizing capacity, while hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. Non-medicated IUDs (like Lippes loop) phagocytose sperms within the uterus.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.3: Cu releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity of sperms.

questions.question: Read the statement about Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs): 'Some STIs like Hepatitis-B and HIV are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.' Identify the incorrect word in this statement and choose the correct replacement.
questions.explanation: Except for Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Hepatitis-B and HIV are not completely curable.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.4: Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: Identify the term that needs replacement in the following sentence to make it an accurate NCERT definition of amniocentesis: 'Amniocentesis is a fetal sex determination test based on the chromosomal pattern in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo, legally permitted in India to prevent female foeticide.'
options: Replace 'legally permitted in India to prevent female foeticide' with 'statutory ban for sex-determination to legally check female foeticide'
Replace 'fetal sex determination' with 'gestational diabetes screening'
questions.explanation: Amniocentesis is legally banned for sex determination in India to check female foeticide. It is meant for detecting genetic disorders, not for determining sex for selective abortion.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.1: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check female foeticide.

questions.question: Consider the statement on medical termination of pregnancy (MTP): 'MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., up to 20 weeks of pregnancy.' Which word is factually incorrect according to NCERT guidelines?
questions.explanation: According to NCERT, MTPs are considered safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy). Second-trimester abortions are much more risky.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.3: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, upto 12 weeks of pregnancy.

questions.question: Read the statement regarding surgical methods of contraception: 'Tubectomy is a sterilization procedure in males where a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.' Identify the incorrect word/phrase and its proper substitution.
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is the surgical sterilization procedure in males, where a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up. Tubectomy is performed in females by cutting/tying the fallopian tubes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.5: Surgical methods, also called sterilization, are advised for male/female partner as a terminal method... Vasectomy: a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.

questions.question: Examine the statement: 'Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition, hence the chances of conception are practically negligible up to maximum period of 2 years.' Which word/number makes this statement incorrect according to NCERT?
questions.explanation: The maximum period up to which lactational amenorrhea is effective is reported to be only up to 6 months following parturition, not 2 years.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.1: This method has been reported to be effective only upto a maximum period of 6 months following parturition.

questions.question: Read the statement: 'In IVF (In Vitro Fertilization), zygote or early embryos up to 8 blastomeres could be transferred into the fallopian tube, a process known as Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT).' Which term in the statement is incorrect and needs replacement?
options: Replace 'Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT)' with 'Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer (ZIFT)'
questions.explanation: Transfer of zygote or early embryos up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube is called ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer). Transfer of embryos with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus is called IUT.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.5.1: Transfer of zygote or early embryos (upto 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube (ZIFT) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT).

questions.question: Consider the statement on reproductive health: 'A rapid increase in population growth rate is mainly due to a rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in the number of people of reproductive age.' Which factor among these is typically associated with population growth increase rather than decline?
options: Number of people of reproductive age
questions.explanation: While death rate, MMR, and IMR decline, the number of people in the reproducible age increases, along with an increase in health facilities, which collectively drive population growth.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.1: Rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in number of people in reproducible age are probable reasons for this [population growth].

questions.question: A 28-year-old female visits a clinic seeking a permanent method of contraception after completing her desired family size of two children. Which of the following surgical procedures is most appropriate to discuss with her?
questions.explanation: Tubectomy is a surgical sterilization method in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or vagina, preventing gamete transport. Vasectomy is performed in males.
questions.ncertEvidence: Surgical methods, also known as sterilization, are advised for male/female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. Surgical intervention blocks gamete transport and thereby prevent conception. Sterilization procedure in the female is called 'tubectomy'.

questions.question: A couple approaches a reproductive clinic inquiring about a contraceptive method that not only prevents pregnancy but also offers protection against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs). Which of the following options should the physician recommend?
questions.explanation: Condoms are barrier methods of contraception that are disposable and also protect the user from acquiring STIs like AIDS, unlike oral pills, IUDS, or diaphragms which do not protect against STIs.
questions.ncertEvidence: An added advantage of barriers is that they are disposable, can be self-inserted and therefore give privacy to the user. Condoms are barriers that protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.

questions.question: During a medical counseling session regarding emergency contraception, a doctor needs to advise a patient on the timeframe within which a specific hormonal formulation must be taken following unprotected intercourse to prevent conception effectively.
questions.explanation: Emergency contraceptives containing progestogens or progestogen-oestrogen combinations must be administered within 72 hours of coitus to be effective as emergency contraception.
questions.ncertEvidence: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-oestrogen combinations within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives as they could be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

questions.question: An infertile couple is undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART). The technique involves the transfer of an embryo formed by in vitro fertilization, having more than 8 blastomeres, directly into the uterus. What is this specific procedure called?
questions.explanation: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus, a procedure known as Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT). Zygote or early embryos up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT).
questions.ncertEvidence: Embryos upto 8 blastomeres could be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT—zygote intrafallopian transfer) and those with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IUT—intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development.

questions.question: A lactating mother, whose infant is 3 months old and who is exclusively breast-feeding her child, asks about the likelihood of conception during this period. Based on natural contraceptive principles, what explains the low risk of conception?
options: High levels of circulating estrogen prevent ovulation
Absence of ovulation due to high prolactin and suppressed gonadotropins
Complete thickening of the cervical mucus blocking sperm entry
Permanent atrophy of the corpus luteum during lactation
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition, largely due to high prolactin levels which suppress gonadotropin release.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil up to six months.

questions.question: A 30-year-old male is advised a surgical contraceptive procedure that involves making a small incision on the scrotum to excise or tie off a small part of the deferent ducts. What is the immediate physiological consequence of this procedure?
options: Cessation of testosterone production by Leydig cells
Prevention of sperm from entering the seminal fluid / ejaculation
Inhibition of spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules
Permanent impotence and loss of libido
questions.explanation: Vasectomy involves cutting or tying the vas deferens, which blocks gamete transport (sperm cannot reach the urethra), thereby preventing sperm from being ejaculated. It does not affect hormone production or sexual urge.
questions.ncertEvidence: Sterilization procedure in the male is called 'vasectomy' where a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum to block gamete transport.

questions.question: A clinician is evaluating an intra-uterine device (IUD) that releases copper ions. Which of the following is the primary mechanism by which copper-releasing IUDs (like CuT) prevent pregnancy?
options: Increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and suppressing sperm motility
Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation by destroying the endometrium permanently
Inhibiting the secretion of progesterone from the ovary
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Copper releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.

questions.question: A couple is unable to produce children and wishes to opt for an ART technique where an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and further development. What is this technique?
questions.explanation: Gamete intrafallopian transfer (GIFT) involves the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ova but can provide the suitable environment for fertilization and further development.
questions.ncertEvidence: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and further development is known as GIFT.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is medically accurate according to Indian legislative and biological guidelines?
options: MTP is completely illegal under all circumstances in India.
MTP is safe during the first trimester, but second-trimester abortions are much more rislier and often illegal unless specific conditions are met.
MTP requires the consent of the male partner and the local village council.
MTP is a primary method of contraception.
questions.explanation: MTPs during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks) are generally much safer, whereas second-trimester abortions are much more risky. MTP is legally legalized in India under strict conditions to avoid misuse.
questions.ncertEvidence: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second trimester abortions are much more riskier. Another disturbing trend is the misuse of MTPs to illegally abort female foetuses.

questions.question: In a rural health camp, a nurse explains various birth control methods to newly married couples. She mentions barrier methods that are reusable, custom-fitted, and placed into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix. Which devices are being described?
questions.explanation: Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are barrier methods made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Unlike male/female condoms, these specific rubber barriers are reusable.
questions.ncertEvidence: In case of females, barriers are made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They are reusable. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber.

questions.question: A 28-year-old urban couple approaches a clinic for permanent contraception as they have completed their family size of two children. The male partner wishes to undergo a procedure that is surgical and highly effective. Which physiological consequence must the counselor inform him about regarding the procedure?
options: It inhibits the process of spermatogenesis in the testes permanently.
It prevents the transport of sperms by blocking the vas deferens.
It suppresses the secretion of testosterone from the Leydig cells.
It stops the seminal vesicles and prostate gland from producing seminal plasma.
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is a surgical method of contraception in males where a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, thereby blocking sperm transport. It does not affect spermatogenesis or hormone production.
questions.ncertEvidence: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum to block sperm transport.

questions.question: A sexually active individual is diagnosed with a bacterial sexually transmitted infection characterized by the appearance of a painless ulcer on the genitals, which later resolves spontaneously, followed weeks later by skin rashes and lymphadenopathy. Based on NCERT guidelines, what can be inferred about the curability of this infection if detected early?
options: It is completely curable if detected early.
It is incurable because viral agents mutate rapidly.
It can only be managed with palliative therapy to reduce symptoms.
It requires lifelong antiretroviral therapy for suppression.
questions.explanation: The symptoms described are characteristic of Syphilis, which is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum. According to NCERT, infections like syphilis, gonorrhoea, and chlamydiosis are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.
questions.ncertEvidence: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, and chlamydiosis are curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: A young female patient visits a gynecologist requesting an emergency contraceptive pill within 24 hours of unprotected coitus. To effectively prevent pregnancy, what is the primary mechanism by which standard emergency contraceptive pills (containing progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations) act when administered within 72 hours?
options: They lyse the fully formed corpus luteum and cause immediate sloughing of the functional endometrium.
They destroy the genetic material of the fertilized ovum before cleavage begins.
They delay or inhibit ovulation and alter the endometrial environment to prevent implantation.
They cause immediate constriction of the fallopian tubes to trap the blastocyst.
questions.explanation: Emergency contraceptives containing progestogens alone or combined with estrogen are effective if used within 72 hours of coitus because they primarily delay or prevent ovulation and modify the endometrium, making it unsuitable for implantation.
questions.ncertEvidence: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations within 72 hours of coitus is used as emergency contraceptives as they could avoid possible pregnancy by delaying or inhibiting ovulation and altering the endometrium.

questions.question: An infertile couple is undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART). The wife has blocked fallopian tubes, but her ovaries function normally and produce healthy secondary oocytes. The husband has a low sperm count. Which specific technique is most appropriate to achieve fertilization outside the body, followed by the transfer of the embryo into the uterus?
options: In Vitro Fertilization followed by Embryo Transfer (IVF-ET)
questions.explanation: In IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilization and Embryo Transfer), ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor are induced to form fertilization outside the body in laboratory conditions, and the early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) or zygote is transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT) or uterus (ET). Since her fallopian tubes are blocked, transfer directly into the uterus (ET) is chosen.
questions.ncertEvidence: In vitro fertilization (IVF-fertilization outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET) is one of such methods. Ova from the wife/donor and sperms from the husband/donor are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the lab.

questions.question: A public health campaign aims to reduce the incidence of Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) in a population. Epidemiologists analyze various contraceptive options to determine which ones simultaneously provide protection against STIs alongside preventing unwanted pregnancies. Which group of contraceptives should be promoted?
options: Oral contraceptive pills and hormonal implants
Diaphragms and cervical caps without spermicidal creams
questions.explanation: Condoms are barriers that prevent the deposition of ejaculate in the female reproductive tract. An added advantage of condoms is that they also protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.
questions.ncertEvidence: An added advantage of barrier methods like condoms is that they also protect the user from contracting STIs and AIDS.

questions.question: A 32-year-old lactating mother who delivered an infant 3 months ago exclusively feeds her child breast milk. She has not experienced her menstrual cycle since childbirth and inquires about her current susceptibility to pregnancy. Based on biological principles, what can be inferred?
options: She has complete permanent immunity against ovulation due to elevated estrogen levels.
Her risk of conception is high because lactation promotes rapid follicular maturation.
She experiences temporary absence of ovulation due to high prolactin and suppression of gonadotropins, providing natural contraception up to six months.
She must use emergency contraceptives immediately because lactation offers no contraceptive protection whatsoever.
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, chances of conception are virtually nil up to six months following parturition.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lactational amenorrhea method (absence of menstruation) is based on the fact that ovulation do not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. As long as the mother breast-feeds the child fully, chances of conception are virtually nil up to six months following parturition.

questions.question: A couple facing primary infertility consults a fertility clinic. Semen analysis of the male partner reveals severe oligospermia (extremely low sperm count in the ejaculate). Even though standard IVF yields poor fertilization rates due to insufficient viable sperms, the couple wants to use the husband's gametes. Which advanced laboratory procedure can directly overcome this male infertility factor?
questions.explanation: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a specialized procedure in ART where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum in the laboratory to form an embryo, bypassing low sperm count or motility issues.
questions.ncertEvidence: Intra cyto-plasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

questions.question: An evaluation of a national family planning program highlights the use of Copper-releasing Intra Uterine Devices (Cu-IUDs). How do copper ions released by these devices primarily exert their contraceptive action within the female reproductive tract?
options: They cause immediate degeneration of the anterior pituitary gland to halt LH surge.
They suppress sperm motility and their fertilizing capacity.
They stimulate excessive estrogen secretion to induce premature menstruation.
They physically obstruct the cervical os to prevent sperm entry.
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs (like CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) release Cu ions which suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: The Cu releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.

questions.question: A sexually transmitted infection is diagnosed in a patient, caused by a pathogen that primarily targets the human immune system, specifically destroying CD4+ T-lymphocytes, leading to severe immunodeficiency. According to NCERT, which mode of transmission is NOT responsible for spreading this pathogen?
options: Transfusion of contaminated blood and blood products
Sharing infected needles as in the case of intravenous drug abusers
Casual physical contact such as shaking hands and sharing eating utensils with an infected person
questions.explanation: AIDS (caused by HIV) is transmitted through sexual contact, blood transfusion, sharing infected needles, and from infected mother to child. It is not spread by mere touch or physical contact; HIV spreads only through body fluids.
questions.ncertEvidence: AIDS is not transmitted by mere touch or physical contact; it spreads only through body fluid contact.

questions.question: A 24-year-old female visits a family planning clinic seeking a long-term reversible contraceptive method. The physician recommends an Intra Uterine Device (IUD) that releases hormones. Which mechanism is characteristic of hormone-releasing IUDs like LNG-20?
options: Making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms
Completely preventing the development of ovaries during embryonic life
Inducing hypersecretion of progesterone to permanently block the fallopian tubes
Neutralizing vaginal acidity to destroy all bacterial flora
questions.explanation: Hormone-releasing IUDs (like Progestasert, LNG-20) make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms, in addition to phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
questions.ncertEvidence: Hormone-releasing IUDs, (Progestasert, LNG-20) in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.

questions.question: Which of the following birth control methods is categorized under surgical methods and is also known as sterilization in females?
questions.explanation: Tubectomy is a surgical sterilization method in females where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up. Vasectomy is the male sterilization procedure.
questions.ncertEvidence: Surgical methods, also called sterilization, are advised for male/female partners as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. Surgical intervention in males is vasectomy and in females it is tubectomy.

questions.question: Identify the technique where semen collected either from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI) of the female.
questions.explanation: In Artificial Insemination (AI), the semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus of the female.
questions.ncertEvidence: In such cases, infertility is corrected by special techniques known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART). One such technique is Artificial Insemination (AI).

questions.question: Which statutory amendment raised the legal age of marriage for females to 18 years and for males to 21 years in India?
questions.explanation: Statutory ban on age of marriage is set at 18 years for females and 21 years for males to prevent early marriages and associated health complications.
questions.ncertEvidence: Statutory ban on age of marriage (18 years for female and 21 years for male) and incestuous marriages are some of the legal steps taken.

questions.question: What is the primary mechanism of action of copper-releasing Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) such as CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375?
options: Increasing phagocytosis of sperms and suppressing sperm motility
Preventing the entry of sperms through the cervix
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs release Cu ions which suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms, while also increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.
questions.ncertEvidence: Copper releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the copper ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.

questions.question: Which sexually transmitted infection is considered completely curable if detected early and treated properly, unlike Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is a bacterial STI that is completely curable if detected early and treated. Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV are not completely curable.
questions.ncertEvidence: Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: What does the acronym MTP stand for in the context of reproductive health?
questions.explanation: MTP stands for Medical Termination of Pregnancy, which is also known as induced abortion.
questions.ncertEvidence: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion.

questions.question: Which natural method of contraception relies on the absence of menstruation following parturition due to intense lactation?
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition, thus acting as a natural contraceptive up to six months.
questions.ncertEvidence: Lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.

questions.question: Which assisted reproductive technology involves the transfer of an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus?
questions.explanation: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus, a procedure known as Intra Uterine Transfer (IUT). ZIFT is used for zygotes or early embryos up to 8 blastomeres transferred into the fallopian tube.
questions.ncertEvidence: Embryos upto 8 blastomeres could be transferred into the fallopian tubes (ZIFT—zygote intrafallopian transfer) and those with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IUT—intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development.

questions.question: Which government statutory act was introduced in India to legally check female foeticide and misuse of amniocentesis?
options: Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act
questions.explanation: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination was legally enacted through the Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act to check female foeticide.
questions.ncertEvidence: Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check increasing menace of female foeticide.

questions.question: What is the common hormone-releasing Intra Uterine Device (IUD) mentioned in NCERT?
questions.explanation: Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs that make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
questions.ncertEvidence: Hormone releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

questions.question: Identify the correct combination of birth control methods from the following, keeping in mind that all listed methods must function primarily by preventing ovulation or fertilization.
questions.explanation: Oral pills prevent ovulation, while condoms and diaphragms act as physical barriers preventing the meeting of sperm and ovum (fertilization). Vasectomy and tubectomy are sterilisation techniques (preventing gamete transport), while withdrawal and periodic abstinence are behavioral methods. Option 1 contains a sterilisation method and an intrauterine device alongside LAM. Option 4 contains CuT/Multiload which are IUDs. Option 3 contains withdrawal. Thus, evaluating the options for purely preventing ovulation/fertilization through pills and barriers, Option 2 is the cohesive set of barrier and hormonal/chemical methods.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2: Methods of Birth Control (Natural/Traditional, Barrier, IUDs, Oral pills, Injectables, Implants, Surgical methods).

questions.question: Which of the following sets includes only barrier methods of contraception used by human females?
questions.explanation: Condoms are used by males (though female condoms exist, the standard category is male use, and the question asks for a set exclusively for females). CuT and Multiload are IUDs. Oral pills and Saheli are hormonal/oral contraceptives. Diaphragms, cervical caps, and vaults are barrier methods made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.2: Barrier methods.

questions.question: Eliminate the incorrect statement regarding Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs) from the given choices.
options: They are inserted by expert doctors or nurses into the uterus through the vagina.
Copper releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility and the fertilizing capacity of sperms.
Hormone releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
They act as an ideal contraceptive for females who want to delay pregnancy and are completely free of any side effects.
questions.explanation: IUDs are widely accepted contraceptives and are inserted by doctors or nurses. Cu-releasing IUDs (like CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) suppress sperm motility, and hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperm. However, stating they are 'completely free of any side effects' is incorrect because bleeding, pelvic inflammatory diseases, and spontaneous expulsion are known side effects.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.3: Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs).

questions.question: Which among the following contraceptive approaches does NOT belong to the category of chemical or hormonal methods?
questions.explanation: Saheli is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill. Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD releasing progestogens. Combined oral pills contain synthetic estrogen and progestogen. Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing Intra Uterine Device (IUD), which relies on copper ions rather than hormones or chemical oral ingestion.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.4 & 4.2.3: Oral Pills and IUDs.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) and select the correct elimination of false facts:
options: MTPs are considered safe during the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy).
Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid misuse.
Second-trimester abortions are much safer and associated with fewer complications than first-trimester abortions.
MTP involves intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 4 are factual as per NCERT. Statement 3 is false because second-trimester abortions are much more riskier and complicated compared to first-trimester abortions.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.4: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP).

questions.question: Identify the method of assisted reproductive technology (ART) where fertilization is strictly in vivo (inside the female body) rather than in vitro:
questions.explanation: GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce one, where fertilization takes place in vivo. ZIFT (zygote into fallopian tube), ICSI (intra cytoplasmic sperm injection), and IVF (in vitro fertilization) all involve fertilisation outside the body in laboratory conditions (in vitro).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.6.1: Test Tube Baby Programmes and ART.

questions.question: Eliminate the incorrect match between the sexually transmitted infection (STI) and its causative pathogen:
questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, Gonorrhoea by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Genital warts by Human Papillomavirus. Chlamydiasis is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis, whereas Trichomonas vaginalis causes trichomoniasis. Thus, pairing chlamydiasis with Trichomonas vaginalis is incorrect.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.5: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).

questions.question: Which of the following set of Sexually Transmitted Infections are completely curable if detected early and treated properly, excluding viral infections?
questions.explanation: NCERT explicitly lists Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes, and HIV infections as infections that are NOT curable. Genital herpes and Hepatitis-B are viral. Among the options, Option 1 includes Genital herpes (incurable viral). Option 3 includes HIV, Hepatitis-B, and Genital warts (all incurable/viral). Option 4 includes Hepatitis-B (incurable). Option 2 lists Chlamydiasis, Gonorrhoea, and Syphilis, which are bacterial and completely curable if detected early.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.5: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs).

questions.question: Eliminate the wrong statement regarding Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) of birth control:
options: It is based on the principle that ovulation does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.
It has a high failure rate and is effective for a maximum period of up to two years.
High levels of prolactin during intense breastfeeding suppress gonadotropins.
It is a natural method of contraception without any side effects.
questions.explanation: LAM is effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition, not two years. Statements regarding absence of ovulation due to intense lactation, high prolactin suppressing gonadotropins, and it being a natural method with zero side effects are all correct per NCERT.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.2.1: Natural Methods (Lactational Amenorrhea).

questions.question: Which of the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) involves the direct injection of a sperm into an ovum in a laboratory?
questions.explanation: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is a specialized procedure in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum in the laboratory to form an embryo. IUI stands for Intra-uterine insemination, GIFT for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, and AI for Artificial Insemination.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.6.1: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART).

questions.question: Which of the following contraceptive methods is described by NCERT as highly effective, yet its reversal is very poor?
questions.explanation: Surgical methods (sterilization like vasectomy and tubectomy) are highly effective, but their reversibility is very poor. Students often confuse high effectiveness with high reversibility.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 4, Reproductive Health, Section 4.3.5 Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) and Surgical methods: 'While surgical methods are safe, their reversibility is very poor.'
