options: It functions in the culture medium where it is acted upon by an active enzyme produced by non-recombinant plasmids to yield blue colonies.
It functions inside the bacterial nucleus to replicate plasmid DNA during cell division.
It functions inside the restriction endonuclease to cleave foreign foreign DNA sequences.
It functions in the lysis buffer to degrade the bacterial cell wall.
questions.explanation: In insertional inactivation, recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of an enzyme $\beta$-galactosidase. This results in inactivation of the enzyme, which cannot convert the chromogenic substrate into a blue colored product, thus resulting in white colonies. Non-recombinants give blue colonies.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, page 200: 'Presence of a insert results into insertional inactivation of the beta-galactosidase and the colonies do not produce any colour, these are identified as recombinant colonies.'

questions.question: What is the function of a bioreactor in downstream processing and large-scale industrial biotechnology?
options: To isolate and purify proteins from transformed cells before cloning.
To provide the optimal growth conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, oxygen) to achieve the desired product on a large scale.
To amplify specific DNA sequences through thermal cycling reactions.
To separate DNA fragments based on size using an electric field.
questions.explanation: Bioreactors are vessels in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc., using microbial plant, animal or human cells. A bioreactor provides the optimal growth conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen) to achieve the desired product.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, page 204: 'Bioreactors can be thought of as vessels in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products... provided the optimal growth conditions (temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen).'

questions.question: Which specific structural region of the plasmid pBR322 is primarily responsible for conferring resistance to the antibiotic ampicillin?
questions.explanation: In plasmid pBR322, the genes ampR and tetR are specific structural regions that confer resistance to ampicillin and tetracycline, respectively.
questions.ncertEvidence: Plasmids like pBR322 have antibiotic resistance genes such as ampR and tetR that make it possible to select for transformants.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the 'ori' (origin of replication) sequence present in a cloning vector used in recombinant DNA technology?
options: It acts as a recognition site for restriction endonucleases.
It codes for proteins involved in plasmid translation.
It is the sequence from where replication starts and controls copy number.
It facilitates insertional inactivation of recombinant colonies.
questions.explanation: The origin of replication (ori) is a specific sequence from which replication starts, and any piece of DNA linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cells. It is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: ori is a sequence from where replication starts and any piece of DNA when linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cells. This sequence is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.

questions.question: In the naming of the restriction endonuclease EcoRI, what does the letter 'R' specifically designate?
options: The genus name of the source bacterium
The species name of the source bacterium
The strain of the source bacterium
The order in which the enzyme was isolated
questions.explanation: In EcoRI, 'E' comes from Escherichia (genus), 'co' from coli (species), and 'R' is derived from the name of the strain (RY13).
questions.ncertEvidence: The convention for naming restriction enzymes is the first letter of the name comes from the genus and the second two letters from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which they are isolated, e.g., EcoRI comes from Escherichia coli RY13. In EcoRI, the letter 'R' is derived from the name of strain.

questions.question: How do restriction endonucleases function structurally to interact with DNA?
options: They cut the DNA strand at random positions without sequence specificity.
They inspect the length of a DNA sequence and bind to specific palindrome recognition sequences to cut each strand.
They synthesize new DNA strands by adding nucleotides to the 3'-OH end.
They unwind the DNA double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs.
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases function by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points.
questions.ncertEvidence: Restriction enzymes 'inspect' the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it will bind to the DNA and cut each of the two double strands at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones.

questions.question: What structural feature characterizes the recognition sequences (palindromes) recognized by restriction enzymes?
options: Base pair sequences that read the same on the two strands when orientation of reading is kept the same (e.g., 5' to 3')
Sequences composed exclusively of alternating purines and pyrimidines
Long stretches of identical nucleotide repeats on a single strand
Sequences containing only adenine and thymine residues
questions.explanation: A palindromic sequence in DNA is a sequence of base pairs that reads same on the two strands when orientation of reading is kept the same, such as 5' to 3' on both strands.
questions.ncertEvidence: The restriction enzymes cut the DNA between the same two bases on the opposite strands; these sites are called restriction sites and they form palindromic nucleotide sequences in DNA.

questions.question: What is the structural role of the 'rop' region in the pBR322 plasmid vector?
options: It codes for proteins that facilitate the replication of the plasmid.
It acts as a selectable marker for ampicillin resistance.
It serves as a unique cleavage site for BamHI.
It provides recognition for RNA polymerase during transcription.
questions.explanation: The 'rop' gene in pBR322 codes for proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid, influencing copy number regulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: pBR322 also has rop, which codes for the proteins involved in the replication of the plasmid.

questions.question: Which structural property of agarose gel makes it effective for separating DNA fragments in gel electrophoresis?
options: It forms a molecular sieve whose pore size depends on the agarose concentration.
It carries a strong positive charge that attracts negatively charged DNA molecules.
It acts as a chemical catalyst that denatures double-stranded DNA into single strands.
It forms covalent bonds with the DNA fragments, anchoring them to the gel matrix.
questions.explanation: Agarose is a natural polymer that acts as a sieve. The DNA fragments separate according to size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: The DNA fragments resolve according to their size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel. Hence, the smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves.

questions.question: In the context of selectable markers, what structural change occurs in the plasmid when a foreign DNA fragment is inserted within the tetR gene of pBR322?
options: Loss of ampicillin resistance due to insertional inactivation
Loss of tetracycline resistance due to insertional inactivation
Gain of a new antibiotic resistance gene
Destruction of the origin of replication site
questions.explanation: Ligation of foreign DNA at a restriction site within an antibiotic resistance gene (like tetR) results in insertional inactivation of that gene, causing the recombinant plasmid to lose tetracycline resistance.
questions.ncertEvidence: A recombinant plasmid will lose tetracycline resistance due to insertion of foreign DNA inside the tetR gene (insertional inactivation).

questions.question: What structural and functional difference distinguishes an exonuclease from an endonuclease?
options: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases cut at specific positions within the DNA.
Exonucleases cut only single-stranded RNA, whereas endonucleases cut double-stranded DNA.
Exonucleases hydrolyze peptide bonds, whereas endonucleases hydrolyze phosphodiester bonds.
Exonucleases require ATP to function, whereas endonucleases operate independently of energy sources.
questions.explanation: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA molecule, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: Restriction enzymes belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases. These are of two kinds; exonucleases and endonucleases. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.

questions.question: Which structural feature of DNA molecules enables them to move toward the anode during agarose gel electrophoresis?
options: Overall negative charge due to phosphate groups
questions.explanation: DNA is a negatively charged molecule because of the phosphate backbone, which drives its movement toward the positive electrode (anode) when an electric field is applied.
questions.ncertEvidence: Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules they can be forced to move towards the anode under an electric field through a matrix.

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of steps involved in recombinant DNA technology?
options: Isolation of DNA -> Fragmentation of DNA -> Ligation of DNA into vector -> Insertion of recombinant DNA into host -> Culturing host cells -> Extraction of product
Fragmentation of DNA -> Isolation of DNA -> Insertion of recombinant DNA into host -> Ligation of DNA into vector -> Extraction of product -> Culturing host cells
Isolation of DNA -> Ligation of DNA into vector -> Fragmentation of DNA -> Extraction of product -> Insertion of recombinant DNA into host -> Culturing host cells
Extraction of product -> Isolation of DNA -> Fragmentation of DNA -> Ligation of DNA into vector -> Insertion of recombinant DNA into host -> Culturing host cells
questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA technology involves several steps in a specific sequence: isolation of genetic material (DNA), fragmentation of DNA by restriction endonucleases, isolation of a desired DNA fragment, ligation of the DNA fragment into a vector, transfer of the recombinant DNA into the host, culturing the host cells on a medium at a large scale, and extraction of the desired product.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 195, 'Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology' outlines the sequential steps.

questions.question: During the isolation of genetic material (DNA) from plant cells, what is the correct chronological order of treatments to precipitate purified DNA?
questions.explanation: To isolate DNA, cell walls are broken down (using cellulase for plants, lysozyme for bacteria). RNA is removed by ribonuclease, proteins by protease, and purified DNA is finally precipitated out by the addition of chilled ethanol.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 198, 'Isolation of the Genetic Material (DNA)'.

questions.question:
Arrange the following steps in the action of restriction endonuclease EcoRI in the correct chronological order:
I. Recognition of specific palindromic nucleotide sequence
II. Binding to DNA
III. Cleavage of sugar-phosphate backbones
IV. Generation of sticky ends with overhanging stretches
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes first bind to the DNA, then inspect and recognize the specific palindromic sequence, after which they cut the two strands of DNA a little away from the center of the palindrome sites between the same two bases, generating single-stranded overhanging stretches called sticky ends.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 196, 'Restriction Enzymes'.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of events when using the pBR322 vector for cloning with insertional inactivation?
options: Ligation of alien DNA at restriction site -> Disruption of antibiotic resistance gene -> Loss of resistance -> Screening of recombinants
Disruption of antibiotic resistance gene -> Ligation of alien DNA -> Screening of recombinants -> Loss of resistance
Screening of recombinants -> Ligation of alien DNA -> Disruption of antibiotic resistance gene -> Loss of resistance
Loss of resistance -> Screening of recombinants -> Ligation of alien DNA -> Disruption of antibiotic resistance gene
questions.explanation: When an alien DNA is ligated into a restriction site located within a marker gene (e.g., BamHI in tetR of pBR322), it leads to insertional inactivation of the antibiotic resistance gene. Consequently, the recombinant plasmid loses resistance to that antibiotic, allowing recombinants to be screened based on differential antibiotic sensitivity.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 201, 'Cloning Vectors - Selection of recombinants'.

questions.question: Arrange the steps involved in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) in their correct repeating cycle order:
questions.explanation: Each cycle of PCR has three steps: (1) Denaturation of target DNA at high temperature, (2) Annealing of two sets of primers at lower temperature, and (3) Extension of primers using thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) at optimum temperature.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 203, 'Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)'.

questions.question: In the process of recombinant protein production using a stirred-tank bioreactor, what is the correct operational sequence after inoculation?
options: Sparging sterile air -> Monitoring pH and temperature -> Foam control -> Periodic sampling -> Downstream processing
Downstream processing -> Sparging sterile air -> Monitoring pH and temperature -> Foam control -> Periodic sampling
Periodic sampling -> Foam control -> Downstream processing -> Sparging sterile air -> Monitoring pH and temperature
Foam control -> Downstream processing -> Sparging sterile air -> Monitoring pH and temperature -> Periodic sampling
questions.explanation: In a bioreactor, sterilized nutrient medium is inoculated, oxygen is made available via sparging sterile air, conditions such as temperature and pH are monitored and controlled, foam control and periodic sampling are carried out, and finally, the product is harvested and subjected to downstream processing.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 204-205, 'Bioreactors' and 'Downstream Processing'.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of procedures during the preparation of competent host cells for taking up recombinant DNA?
options: Treatment with divalent cation (Ca2+) -> Incubation of cells with recombinant DNA on ice -> Heat shock at 42°C -> Placing back on ice
Heat shock at 42°C -> Treatment with divalent cation (Ca2+) -> Incubation of cells on ice -> Placing back on ice
Incubation of cells on ice -> Heat shock at 42°C -> Treatment with divalent cation (Ca2+) -> Placing back on ice
Placing back on ice -> Heat shock at 42°C -> Treatment with divalent cation (Ca2+) -> Incubation on ice
questions.explanation: To make host cells competent, bacteria are first treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium, which increases efficiency. Cells are incubated with recombinant DNA on ice, followed by a heat shock (placing at 42°C) for a brief period, and then putting them back on ice, enabling the bacteria to take up the recombinant DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 202, 'Insertion of Recombinant DNA into the Host Cell/Organism'.

questions.question:
Arrange the following milestones of gel electrophoresis in correct chronological progression for separating DNA fragments:
I. Application of electric field
II. Loading of DNA samples into wells
III. Staining with ethidium bromide and visualization under UV light
IV. Migration through agarose matrix based on size
questions.explanation: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments are first loaded into wells in the gel matrix (II), an electric field is applied (I) causing the negatively charged DNA to move through the agarose matrix towards the anode based on size (IV), and finally, the separated DNA fragments are visualized by staining with ethidium bromide and exposure to UV radiation (III).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 197, 'Separation and isolation of DNA fragments'.

questions.question: What is the proper sequence of processes encompassed under 'Downstream Processing' before a therapeutic drug is marketed?
options: Separation of product -> Purification of product -> Addition of preservatives -> Clinical trials
Addition of preservatives -> Clinical trials -> Separation of product -> Purification of product
Clinical trials -> Addition of preservatives -> Separation of product -> Purification of product
Purification of product -> Separation of product -> Clinical trials -> Addition of preservatives
questions.explanation: After completion of the biosynthetic stage, the product has to be subjected through a series of processes collectively called downstream processing, which includes separation and purification of the product. The product is then formulated with suitable preservatives and undergoes strict clinical trials for quality control.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 205, 'Downstream Processing'.

questions.question: Identify the correct order of events when recombinant DNA is introduced into plant cells using the gene gun (biolistics) method:
options: Coating microparticles of gold/tungsten with DNA -> Bombarding cells with high velocity particles -> Integration of DNA into host genome -> Expression of foreign gene
Bombarding cells with high velocity particles -> Coating microparticles with DNA -> Integration of DNA into host genome -> Expression of foreign gene
Integration of DNA into host genome -> Coating microparticles with DNA -> Bombarding cells -> Expression of foreign gene
Expression of foreign gene -> Coating microparticles with DNA -> Bombarding cells -> Integration of DNA into host genome
questions.explanation: In the biolistics or gene gun method, cells are bombarded with high-velocity microparticles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA. Once inside the cell, the recombinant DNA integrates into the host genome and subsequently expresses the foreign gene.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 203, 'Methods of Introduction of Recombinant DNA into Host Cells'.

questions.question: Which of the following restriction endonucleases does NOT cut DNA by producing sticky ends, unlike the vast majority of commonly used restriction enzymes?
questions.explanation: Most restriction enzymes cut the strand a little away from the centre of the recognition sites, but between the same two bases on the opposite strands. This leaves single-stranded portions at the ends, called sticky ends. However, restriction enzymes like SmaI cut right at the centre of the recognition sequence, producing blunt or flush ends instead of sticky ends.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 196: 'Restriction enzymes cut the strand of DNA a little away from the centre of the recognition sites... This leaves single-stranded portions at the ends... Restriction enzymes cut at specific positions within the DNA...'

questions.question: In the context of selectable markers used in plasmid vectors like pBR322, which of the following statements is an exception to the standard insertional inactivation method?
options: Inactivation of the tetracycline resistance gene by inserting DNA at the BamHI site.
Inactivation of the ampicillin resistance gene by inserting DNA at the PstI site.
Selection of recombinants using alpha-complementation where insertional inactivation occurs in the lacZ gene coding for beta-galactosidase.
Using antibiotic resistance genes where insertional inactivation simultaneously inactivates both ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes with a single restriction site.
questions.explanation: Standard insertional inactivation using dual antibiotic markers (like pBR322) involves inactivating only *one* of the antibiotic resistance genes at a time depending on where the foreign DNA is ligated (e.g., BamHI inactivates tetR while ampR remains intact). A single restriction site cannot simultaneously inactivate both distinct antibiotic resistance genes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 199: 'You can insert a foreign DNA at the BamHI site of tetR gene in pBR322 vector... the recombinant plasmids will lose tetracycline resistance due to insertion of foreign DNA but can still be selected out from non-recombinants...'

questions.question: Identify the exception among the following methods used for introducing foreign DNA into host cells, specifically regarding plant host systems.
options: Heat shock method using divalent cations
questions.explanation: The heat shock method using divalent cations (like CaCl2) is specifically used to make bacterial host cells (like E. coli) competent to take up plasmids. For plant cells, methods like biolistics (gene gun) or disarmed Agrobacterium vectors are used, whereas micro-injection is typically used for animal cells.
questions.ncertEvidence:
NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 200-201: 'In this method (heat shock), BACTERIA are treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation...'
'Plant cells are bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA in a method known as biolistics...'

questions.question: Which of the following properties is NOT exhibited by the thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) isolated from Thermus aquaticus?
options: It remains active during the high-temperature denaturation step of PCR.
It synthesizes DNA by extending primers using nucleotides provided in the reaction mixture.
It has a high optimum temperature matching the denaturation temperature of around 94°C to 98°C.
It remains stable and functional at high temperatures required for double-stranded DNA melting.
questions.explanation: While Taq polymerase remains stable and does not denature at the high temperatures (94-95°C) used during the denaturation step of PCR, its optimum temperature for polymerization (catalytic activity) is actually around 72°C, not 94-98°C.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 203: 'The extension step... is where Taq polymerase is used because it remains active during the high temperature induced denaturation of double stranded DNA.'

questions.question: When isolating genetic material (DNA) from plant cells, which of the following enzymes is an exception and NOT required for the initial breakdown of cell boundaries compared to bacterial or fungal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made of cellulose, requiring cellulase for breakdown. Bacterial cell walls are broken down by lysozyme, and fungal walls by chitinase. Therefore, lysozyme is not required specifically for plant cell DNA isolation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 201: 'Since the DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA... Bacterial cell - lysozyme, Plant cells - cellulase, Fungus - chitinase.'

questions.question: Which of the following features is NOT a requirement for a cloning vector to facilitate successful gene cloning?
options: A high molecular weight to ensure stability inside the host
questions.explanation: Cloning vectors should ideally be small in molecular weight (size) so that they can easily enter host cells and are easy to manipulate in the laboratory. Large vectors are generally unstable and difficult to handle.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 198-199: 'Vectors used to transfer the piece of DNA into host... Origin of replication (ori), Selectable marker, Cloning sites.'

questions.question: In recombinant DNA technology, human proteins can be produced using heterologous hosts. Which of the following is an exception regarding the necessity of a bioreactor?
options: Small-scale laboratory experiments for initial academic testing do not strictly require large-scale bioreactors.
Large-scale production of recombinant proteins for therapeutic use requires processing volumes ranging from 100 to 1000 litres, necessitating bioreactors.
Bioreactors are exclusively used for culturing animal cell lines and cannot support microbial fermentation.
A bioreactor provides all growth conditions like temperature, pH, substrate, and oxygen required for optimal product formation.
questions.explanation: Bioreactors are used for large-scale production using microbial, plant, or animal cell systems, not exclusively animal cell lines. Stirred-tank bioreactors are commonly used for general fermentation involving bacteria and other microbes as well.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 204: 'To produce large quantities of these products, bioreactors are required. In bioreactors, large volumes (100-1000 liters) of culture can be processed.'

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding restriction enzymes is an exception to their general naming and functioning nomenclature?
options: The first letter of the name comes from the genus and the next two letters from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which they were isolated.
Roman numbers following the name indicate the order in which the enzymes were isolated from that strain.
Restriction enzymes can cleave DNA randomly without recognizing any specific nucleotide sequence.
They inspect the length of a DNA sequence and bind to specific recognition sequences.
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes do NOT cut DNA randomly; they are highly specific endonucleases that inspect DNA sequences and bind/cut only at specific recognition nucleotide sequences (palindrome sequences).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 195: 'Restriction enzymes belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases... Each restriction endonuclease functions by 'inspecting' the length of a DNA sequence.'

questions.question: Regarding the downstream processing step in recombinant DNA technology, which of the following is an exception to its primary objectives?
options: Separation of the biosynthesized product from the bioreactor culture
Purification of the organic product to ensure it meets clinical or industrial standards
Addition of preservatives and rigorous formulation testing
Amplification of the target gene sequence using thermal cycling
questions.explanation: Gene amplification is performed using Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) prior to or during cloning steps, whereas downstream processing refers to the stages after biosynthesis: separation and purification of the product.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 204: 'The processes include separation and purification, which are collectively referred to as downstream processing. The product has to be formulated with suitable preservatives.'

questions.question: Which of the following is an exception to the characteristics of the 'ori' (origin of replication) site in a vector?
options: It is a specific sequence from where replication starts.
Any piece of DNA when linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cell.
It is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.
It requires a selectable marker gene to initiate the unwinding of DNA strands.
questions.explanation: The origin of replication (ori) does not require a selectable marker gene to initiate unwinding or replication; ori functions independently to initiate replication and regulate copy number, while selectable markers are used to identify and eliminate non-transformants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 198: 'Origin of replication (ori): This is a sequence from where replication starts and any piece of DNA when linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within host cells. This sequence is also responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA.'

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is specifically required for isolating genetic material from plant cells compared to animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which requires cellulase for breakdown during the isolation of DNA. Animal cells lack a cell wall and lysozyme is used for bacterial cells, while chitinase is used for fungi.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 200: 'Since the DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA... Plant cells are walled, plant cell is broken with cellulase.'

questions.question: During the isolation of DNA, chilled ethanol is added to:
options: Break down the bacterial cell wall
questions.explanation: Chilled ethanol is added during DNA isolation to precipitate out the suspended DNA, which can then be removed by spooling. Proteases are used to digest proteins, and restriction enzymes are used later during cloning, not isolation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 201: 'Addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out the purified DNA.'

questions.question: Exonucleases differ from endonucleases in which of the following characteristics?
options: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA strand, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
Exonucleases cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences, whereas endonucleases cut randomly.
Exonucleases require ATP for their action, whereas endonucleases do not.
Exonucleases degrade single-stranded RNA, whereas endonucleases degrade double-stranded DNA.
questions.explanation: Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, while endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA sequence.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 195: 'Each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence... Endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA... Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA.'

questions.question: In the naming of the restriction enzyme EcoRI, the letter 'R' is derived from:
options: The genus of the source organism
The species of the source organism
questions.explanation: In EcoRI, 'E' stands for Escherichia (genus), 'co' for coli (species), 'R' for the strain (RY 13), and 'I' indicates the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 195: 'The convention for naming restriction enzymes is the first letter of the name comes from the genus and the two letters from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which they were isolated... In EcoRI, the letter 'R' is derived from the name of strain.'

questions.question: A recombinant DNA molecule is constructed by inserting a foreign DNA into the plasmid pBR322 using the restriction site BamHI. Which of the following selectables will be inactivated?
options: Both ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes
Neither ampicillin nor tetracycline resistance gene
questions.explanation: In pBR322, the restriction site BamHI is located within the tetracycline resistance gene ($tet^R$). Insertion of foreign DNA at this site causes insertional inactivation of the tetracycline resistance gene.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 198: 'The ligation of foreign DNA is carried out at a restriction site present in one of the two antibiotic resistance genes. For example, you can insert a foreign DNA at the BamHI site of tet^R gene in plasmid pBR322.'

questions.question: Which of the following is a true statement regarding the agro-bacterium mediated gene transfer in plants?
options: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants that delivers a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor.
Agrobacterium tumefaciens infects monocot plants exclusively to form crown galls.
The tumor-inducing (Ti) plasmid is pathogenic to the plant even after the tumor-causing genes are removed.
Agrobacterium transfers genes via micro-projectiles coated with recombinant DNA.
questions.explanation: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants that delivers T-DNA to transform cells into a tumor (crown gall). The tumor-causing genes can be eliminated to make it a useful cloning vector.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 200: 'Pathogens of several dicot plants are able to deliver a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor and direct these tumor cells to produce the chemicals required by the pathogen... The tumor inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens has now been modified... into a cloning vector.'

questions.question: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments migrate toward the:
options: Anode, because DNA is negatively charged
Cathode, because DNA is positively charged
Anode, because DNA is positively charged
Cathode, because DNA is negatively charged
questions.explanation: DNA fragments are negatively charged due to phosphate groups, and therefore, under an electric field, they move towards the positive electrode (anode).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 197: 'Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be moved under an electric field towards the anode (positive electrode).'

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using a stirred-tank bioreactor over a shake flask for large-scale production?
options: It facilitates better mixing and oxygen availability throughout the process for large volumes.
It requires no sterilization of growth media before inoculation.
It is exclusively used for analytical separation of proteins via electrophoresis.
It eliminates the need for any downstream processing steps.
questions.explanation: A stirred-tank bioreactor is designed for large-scale production where a stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 203: 'A stirred-tank bioreactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.'

questions.question: In the context of selectable markers, insertional inactivation is preferred over antibiotic resistance selection because:
options: It allows simultaneous selection of recombinants and non-recombinants based on color production using chromogenic substrates.
It completely destroys the plasmid vector after transformation.
It makes the host bacterium immune to all known antibiotics.
It prevents the replication of plasmids inside the host cell entirely.
questions.explanation: Insertional inactivation using systems like $\alpha$-galactosidase ($\beta$-galactosidase principle in pUC/blue-white selection) allows recombinants to be differentiated from non-recombinants based on the color of the colonies produced in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 199: 'Selection of recombinants due to inactivation of antibiotics is a cumbersome process because it requires simultaneous plating on two plates having different antibiotics. Therefore, alternative selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinants from non-recombinants on the basis of their ability to produce color in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.'

questions.question: Which of the following describes the correct sequence of steps involved in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
questions.explanation: PCR consists of three steps: Denaturation of target DNA at high temperature, Annealing of primers at lower temperature, and Extension of primers using thermostable DNA polymerase.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 201: 'Each cycle has three steps: (i) Denaturation (ii) Annealing (iii) Extension.'

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is typically used to cut DNA at specific recognition sequences during recombinant DNA technology?
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases are the molecular scissors used to cut DNA at specific base sequence recognition sites.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology (Restriction Enzymes).

questions.question: The process of introducing foreign DNA into host cells by using micro-injections involves injecting the recombinant DNA directly into the:
questions.explanation: In micro-injection, recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Methods of Introduction of Recombinant DNA into Host Cells.

questions.question: The tumbling movement or stirring of medium in a stirred-tank bioreactor helps primarily to:
options: Facilitate oxygen availability throughout the process
Remove the plasmid from the host
questions.explanation: A stirred-tank bioreactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Bioreactors).

questions.question: During the isolation of genetic material (DNA), purified DNA precipitates out after the addition of:
questions.explanation: To isolate DNA, chilled ethanol is added which precipitates out the purified DNA, visible as a collection of fine threads in suspension.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Isolation of the Genetic Material).

questions.question: The enzyme used to join the ends of a DNA fragment to a plasmid vector is:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase acts on cut DNA fragments and joins their ends, sealing the phosphodiester backbone between vector and insert.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology (Ligases).

questions.question: In naming restriction endonucleases, the first letter of the name comes from the:
questions.explanation: The convention for naming restriction enzymes is that the first letter comes from the genus and the next two letters from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which they are isolated.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology (Nomenclature).

questions.question: What is the role of selectable markers in a cloning vector?
options: To help in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of the transformants
To cut the foreign DNA at specific sites
To replicate the host genome at a faster rate
To stain the DNA fragments during gel electrophoresis
questions.explanation: Selectable markers help in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of the transformants, i.e., those hosting the vector.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Vectors (Selectable markers).

questions.question: The technique used to amplify a specific gene of interest in vitro is called:
questions.explanation: Polymerase Chain Reaction or PCR is used to make multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest in vitro.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes - Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology (Amplification of Gene of Interest using PCR).

questions.question: A recombinant DNA molecule is constructed by inserting a foreign gene at the BamHI site of plasmid pBR322. Which of the following plating outcomes will be observed when host E. coli cells are transformed with this ligation mixture?
options: Transformants will grow on tetracycline but fail to grow on ampicillin.
Transformants will grow on ampicillin but fail to grow on tetracycline.
Transformants will grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline.
Transformants will fail to grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline.
questions.explanation: The BamHI restriction site is located within the tetR gene (tetracycline resistance) of plasmid pBR322. Insertion of foreign DNA at this site inactivates the tetR gene due to insertional inactivation, while the ampR gene remains intact. Therefore, the recombinant colonies will retain resistance to ampicillin but lose resistance to tetracycline.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 201: 'When a foreign DNA is inserted at the BamHI site of tetR gene in pBR322, the recombinant plasmids lose tetracycline resistance due to insertional inactivation.'

questions.question: During the isolation of genetic material, chilled ethanol is added to the aqueous solution. What is the precise function of this step?
options: To precipitate purified DNA out of the solution
To degrade contaminating RNA molecules enzymatically
To lyse the bacterial cell wall and release cellular components
To dissolve membrane lipids and denature chromosomal proteins
questions.explanation: Chilled ethanol is added during nucleic acid extraction to precipitate purified DNA, making it visible as a collection of fine threads in suspension.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 204: 'The RNA can be removed by treatment with ribonuclease whereas proteins can be removed by treatment with proteases. Eventually, purified DNA precipitates out after the addition of chilled ethanol.'

questions.question: A researcher wishes to amplify a specific DNA segment using PCR. If the reaction mixture lacks DNA ligase, what will be the immediate consequence on the amplification cycles?
options: PCR amplification will proceed normally without any hindrance.
Primers will fail to anneal to the single-stranded template DNA.
Heat denaturation of double-stranded DNA will not occur at 94°C.
Taq polymerase will be unable to extend the annealed primers.
questions.explanation: PCR does not utilize DNA ligase. The thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) extends the primers by adding nucleotides complementary to the template strand without requiring ligation of fragments during standard amplification cycles.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 203: 'This repeating process is done many times... Tag polymerase extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template.'

questions.question: In a genetic engineering experiment, a student accidentally uses an exonuclease instead of an endonuclease to cut a linear double-stranded DNA molecule. What will be the outcome?
options: Specific internal sticky ends will be generated for vector ligation.
Nucleotides will be removed exclusively from the ends of the DNA strand.
Specific palindromic recognition sequences will be cleaved centrally.
The DNA molecule will be cut into numerous predictable fragments.
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases inspect and cut DNA at specific internal recognition sequences, generating sticky or blunt ends. In contrast, exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 197: 'Restriction enzymes belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases. These are of two kinds; exonucleases and endonucleases. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.'

questions.question: A bioreactor is being operated to produce a therapeutic protein using a recombinant bacterial strain. To maximize the volumetric yield and maintain optimal physiological conditions for the microbes, which type of bioreactor design is preferred for large-scale production?
options: Stirred-tank bioreactor with a curved mixing base and foam breaker
Static culture flask incubated in a temperature-controlled dark room
Plain glass beaker placed on a magnetic stirrer at room temperature
Unsealed conical flask shaken manually at periodic intervals
questions.explanation: For large-scale production of recombinant products, stirred-tank bioreactors are commonly used. They facilitate mixing, oxygen availability, foam control, pH monitoring, and temperature regulation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 204: 'A stirred-tank bioreactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.'

questions.question: If a foreign gene is ligated at the PvuI site situated within the ampR gene of plasmid pBR322, how will the recombinant transformants behave on selective media?
options: They will grow on tetracycline but will not grow on ampicillin.
They will grow on both ampicillin and tetracycline.
They will grow on ampicillin but will not grow on tetracycline.
They will not grow on either ampicillin or tetracycline.
questions.explanation: The PvuI restriction site is located within the ampR gene. Inserting foreign DNA here inactivates ampicillin resistance (insertional inactivation), while the tetR gene remains intact, allowing growth on tetracycline.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 201: 'The ligation of foreign DNA is carried out at a restriction site present in one of the two antibiotic resistance genes. For example, you can insert a foreign DNA at the BamHI site of tetR gene of pBR322 vector... (similarly PvuI/PstI inactivates ampR).'

questions.question: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments migrate toward the anode because:
options: DNA molecules are negatively charged due to phosphate groups.
The agarose gel matrix carries an overall positive electrical charge.
Ethidium bromide imparts a strong positive charge to the DNA fragments.
Alkaline buffer conditions neutralize the basic amino acids of DNA.
questions.explanation: DNA is a negatively charged molecule due to the phosphate backbone, which drives its migration toward the positive electrode (anode) when an electric field is applied.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 198: 'Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be moved under an electric field towards the anode (positive electrode).'

questions.question: Why is Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally well-suited for genetic engineering of plants?
options: It naturally transfers a specific segment of plasmid DNA (T-DNA) into plant host genomes.
It can infect all animal cell lines without requiring helper plasmids or microinjection.
Its genomic DNA contains active restriction endonucleases that splice foreign genes efficiently.
It replicates exclusively inside viral capsids, facilitating safe horizontal gene transfer.
questions.explanation: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several dicot plants that is able to deliver a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor and direct the cells to produce chemicals required by the pathogen. This natural genetic engineer has been modified for delivering genes of interest into plants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 202: 'Pathogens of plants and animals can also be used to deliver genes of hosts. For example, Agrobacterium tumefaciens... is a pathogen of several dicot plants able to deliver a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor...'

questions.question: In recombinant protein production, what does the downstream processing stage encompass?
options: Separation and purification of the synthesized product ready for marketing
Initial insertion of the target foreign gene into a suitable cloning vector
Culturing transformed host cells in a large-scale stirred-tank bioreactor
Amplification of target DNA sequences using thermal cycling and Taq polymerase
questions.explanation: Downstream processing is the stage of biotechnology that involves the separation and purification of the product before it is ready for commercial marketing as a finished product.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 204: 'The processes include separation and purification, which are collectively referred to as downstream processing. The product has to be formulated with suitable preservatives.'

questions.question: What is the role of ethidium bromide when visualized under UV light in agarose gel electrophoresis?
options: It stains DNA fragments, causing them to glow orange under UV light.
It acts as a restriction enzyme to cleave high molecular weight genomic DNA.
It functions as an alkaline denaturing agent to separate DNA double strands.
It serves as a tracking dye to monitor the progress of electrophoretic migration.
questions.explanation: Ethidium bromide is used to stain DNA fragments separated on agarose gels, allowing them to be visualized as bright orange bands when exposed to UV radiation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, p. 198: 'The separated DNA fragments can be visualized only after staining the DNA with a compound known as ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation.'

questions.question: A restriction endonuclease cuts DNA between G and A in the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' and 3'-CTTAAG-5'. What kind of ends are formed as a result of this cleavage?
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes like EcoRI cut the strand a little away from the center of the palindrome sites, between the same two bases on the opposite strands. This leaves single-stranded portions at the ends, known as overhanging stretches or sticky ends, which form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 196: 'EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases G and A only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA. This leaves overhanging stretches called sticky ends on each strand.'

questions.question: During the separation of DNA fragments using agarose gel electrophoresis, if a researcher accidentally loads the DNA sample near the positive electrode instead of the negative electrode, what will be the observed result?
options: DNA fragments will migrate towards the negative electrode normally.
DNA fragments will migrate faster towards the positive electrode.
DNA fragments will move off the gel into the buffer solution towards the positive electrode.
DNA fragments will fail to migrate through the gel and remain near the positive electrode.
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged. Therefore, during gel electrophoresis, DNA moves towards the positive electrode ( anode ). If loaded near the positive electrode, the negatively charged DNA will be immediately attracted to it and run off the gel into the surrounding buffer rather than migrating through the matrix.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 197: 'Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be forced to move towards the anode under an electric field through a matrix.'

questions.question: A recombinant vector carrying a foreign gene is inserted within the PstI site of the ampicillin-resistance gene ($amp^R$) in pBR322. When this plasmid is transformed into E. coli, the host cells will exhibit which of the following phenotype combinations?
options: Resistant to ampicillin, resistant to tetracycline
Susceptible to ampicillin, resistant to tetracycline
Resistant to ampicillin, susceptible to tetracycline
Susceptible to ampicillin, susceptible to tetracycline
questions.explanation: Insertion of a foreign DNA piece at the PstI site located within the $amp^R$ gene results in insertional inactivation of the ampicillin resistance gene. Thus, the transformants lose resistance to ampicillin (become susceptible/sensitive), while the tetracycline resistance gene ($tet^R$) remains intact, conferring resistance to tetracycline.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 200: 'The recombinant plasmids lose ampicillin resistance due to insertion of foreign DNA but can still be selected out from non-recombinants by plating on tetracycline containing medium.'

questions.question: Why is the enzyme cellulase specifically required for the isolation of genetic material (DNA) from plant cells, but not typically from animal cells?
options: Plant cells lack a plasma membrane.
Plant cells possess a rigid cell wall made of cellulose.
Animal cells have thick peptidoglycan walls.
Cellulose protects the nuclear membrane inside animal cells.
questions.explanation: Plant cells are encased in a rigid cell wall composed of cellulose. To release DNA, this barrier must be broken down enzymatically using cellulase, whereas animal cells lack a cell wall and only require lysis of the cell and nuclear membranes.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 203: 'Since the DNA is enclosed within the membranes, we have to break the cell open to release DNA... Plant cells: cellulase, fungus: chitinase, bacteria: lysozyme.'

questions.question: In the context of polymerase chain reaction (PCR), what would happen if the temperature of the denaturation step was reduced from 94°C to 50°C?
options: Primers would anneal to the single-stranded template efficiently.
Double-stranded DNA would fail to separate into single strands.
New complementary DNA strands would be synthesized rapidly.
questions.explanation: Denaturation requires high heat (approx 94°C) to break the hydrogen bonds holding the two strands of DNA together. Reducing this temperature to 50°C (the typical annealing temperature) is insufficient to melt the double helix, preventing primer binding and subsequent amplification.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 204: 'Denaturation: The double-stranded DNA is heated to a high temperature (94°C) for separation of the strands.'

questions.question: An experiment is designed to clone a gene using a plasmid vector. The restriction site for BamHI is situated inside the tetracycline resistance gene of pBR322. If a foreign DNA fragment is successfully ligated at this BamHI site, which selection strategy is used to identify recombinants?
options: Growth on ampicillin followed by testing growth on tetracycline
Growth on medium containing X-gal only
Direct plating on tetracycline medium to check for growth
questions.explanation: Ligation into the BamHI site inactivates tetracycline resistance ($tet^R$). Transformants are first selected on ampicillin (which selects for cells that took up the plasmid, whether recombinant or not), and then replica plated on tetracycline to identify those that cannot grow, indicating successful insertion (recombinants).
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 200: 'Selection of recombinants due to inactivation of antibiotics is a cumbersome procedure because it requires simultaneous plating on two plates having different antibiotics.'

questions.question: During the downstream processing of a recombinant protein, what is the primary objective of this phase before a product is marketed?
options: To ligate the gene of interest into an expression vector
To separate plasmid DNA from host chromosomal DNA
To ensure purification, quality control testing, and formulation with suitable preservatives
To increase the copy number of the recombinant DNA inside the host
questions.explanation: Downstream processing refers to the stages after the biosynthetic phase (fermentation), which include separation and purification of the product, formulation with preservatives, and rigorous quality control testing before it is ready for commercial use.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 206: 'Downstream processing: After completion of the biosynthetic stage, the product has to be subjected through a series of processes including separation and purification, which are collectively referred to as downstream processing.'

questions.question: If a stirred-tank bioreactor shows signs of excessive foam formation that interferes with the aeration system, which component of the bioreactor is primarily responsible for addressing or preventing this issue?
questions.explanation: Stirred-tank bioreactors are usually cylindrical with a curved base to facilitate mixing. They feature systems like an agitator, an oxygen delivery system, a foam control system (foam breaker), and temperature/pH control systems.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 205: 'A stirred-tank bioreactor is usually cylindrical... It has a foam control system, temperature control system, pH control system...'

questions.question: Why is Taq polymerase exclusively used in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) instead of standard DNA polymerases extracted from non-thermophilic organisms?
options: Taq polymerase works best at freezing temperatures.
Taq polymerase remains active during the high temperature denaturation steps required in PCR cycles.
Taq polymerase does not require primers to initiate DNA synthesis.
Taq polymerase synthesizes DNA without using dNTPs.
questions.explanation: PCR involves repeated heating cycles up to 94°C for DNA denaturation. Standard polymerases would denature and lose enzymatic activity at these high temperatures. Taq polymerase, isolated from Thermus aquaticus, is thermostable and withstands these temperatures without denaturation.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 204: 'The extension step is repeated with the help of a thermostable DNA polymerase (isolated from a bacterium, Thermus aquaticus), which remains active during the high temperature induced denaturation of double stranded DNA.'

questions.question: A foreign DNA fragment is inserted into the coding sequence of the beta-galactosidase enzyme in a plasmid vector for blue-white selection. What color will the colonies of recombinant bacteria appear on a medium containing X-gal?
questions.explanation: In insertional inactivation using the alpha-peptide of beta-galactosidase, presence of an insert disrupts the enzyme gene, rendering it inactive. Non-recombinants produce active enzyme that converts colorless X-gal into a blue-colored product (blue colonies). Recombinants cannot metabolize X-gal, resulting in white colonies.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Page 201: 'The presence of a insert results into insertional inactivation of the beta-galactosidase and the colonies do not produce any color, these are identified as recombinant colonies.'

questions.question: Which specific enzyme is responsible for cutting DNA at specific sites in the genetic engineering process?
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases are the 'molecular scissors' used to cut DNA at specific recognition sequences.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.1.1 (Restriction Enzymes): 'The first restriction endonuclease...'

questions.question: During the separation of DNA fragments using agarose gel electrophoresis, which direction do the negatively charged DNA fragments migrate?
options: They do not move in an electric field
questions.explanation: Due to the negative charge of phosphate backbone, DNA fragments move towards the anode (positive electrode) during electrophoresis.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2 (Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology): 'Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be forced to move towards the anode under an electric field...'

questions.question: What is the role of 'Ori' (origin of replication) sequence present in a cloning vector?
options: It codes for proteins required for selection of transformants
It is the sequence from where replication starts and controls copy number
It provides recognition sites for restriction enzymes
It helps in the ligation of foreign DNA
questions.explanation: Ori is a specific sequence from where replication starts, and any piece of DNA when linked to this sequence can be made to replicate within the host cells. It also controls the copy number of the linked DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2 (Vectors): 'Origin of replication (ori) — this is a sequence from where replication starts...'

questions.question: In recombinant DNA technology, antibiotics such as ampicillin, tetracycline, or kanamycin are used for what purpose?
options: To prevent bacterial contamination in the culture medium
As selectable markers to help in identifying and eliminating non-transformants
To facilitate the uptake of foreign DNA by host cells
To act as primers for PCR amplification
questions.explanation: Antibiotic resistance genes act as selectable markers that help in selecting transformants over non-transformants.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2 (Vectors): 'Selectable marker... pBR322 has selectable markers considering ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes.'

questions.question: What is the function of thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase) isolated from Thermus aquaticus in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
options: It unwinds the double-stranded DNA at high temperatures
It remains active during the high temperature denaturation and synthesizes DNA strands
It cuts the DNA at specific palindromic sequences
It joins the newly synthesized DNA fragments together
questions.explanation: Taq polymerase is thermostable and withstands high temperatures used in denaturation without denaturation, extending the primers efficiently.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.3 (Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology): '...thermostable DNA polymerase (isolated from a bacterium, Thermus aquaticus), which remain active during the high temperature induced denaturation of double stranded DNA.'

questions.question: Which method is directly used to introduce recombinant DNA into plant host cells by shooting high-velocity gold or tungsten micro-particles coated with DNA?
questions.explanation: Biolistics or gene gun method involves bombarding plant cells with high-velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.3 (Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology): 'In this method, appropriate cells are bombarded with high velocity micro-particles of gold or tungsten coated with DNA in a method known as biolistics or gene gun.'

questions.question: What does 'staining' with ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation accomplish in gel electrophoresis?
options: It cuts the DNA fragments into smaller pieces
It makes the separated DNA fragments visible as orange-colored bands
It denatures the double-stranded DNA into single strands
It neutralizes the negative charge of the DNA fragments
questions.explanation: Ethidium bromide stains DNA, and when exposed to UV radiation, the DNA fragments can be seen as bright orange bands.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2 (Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology): 'The separated DNA fragments can be visualized only after staining the DNA with ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation (orange bands).'

questions.question: What is the mechanism behind insertional inactivation using $\beta$-galactosidase in plasmid vectors like pUC series?
options: Insertion of foreign DNA inactivates the antibiotic resistance gene, causing cell death
Insertion of foreign DNA within the coding sequence of an enzyme results in blue colonies
Insertion of foreign DNA inactivates the enzyme $\beta$-galactosidase, resulting in non-blue (white) colonies
Insertion of foreign DNA promotes higher copy number and increased expression
questions.explanation: Recombinant colonies do not produce any color (white colonies) because the enzyme $\beta$-galactosidase is inactivated due to insertion of foreign DNA within its coding sequence.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2 (Vectors): '...presence of a chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured colonies if the plasmid in the bacteria does not have an insert. Presence of insert results in insertional inactivation of the beta-galactosidase and the colonies do not produce any colour, these are identified as recombinant colonies.'

questions.question: What is the primary role of a bioreactor in industrial-scale biotechnology?
options: To cut DNA sequences with high precision
To process large volumes of culture for the production of desired biological products
To amplify DNA segments through temperature cycling
To separate proteins based on molecular weight
questions.explanation: A bioreactor is a vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products using microbial, plant, animal, or human cells on a large scale.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.4 (Processes of Recombinant DNA Technology): 'Bioreactors can be thought of as vessels in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc., using microbial plant, animal or human cells.'

questions.question: Why are restriction enzymes named with a specific convention, such as EcoRI?
options: The first letter comes from the genus, the next two from species, and fourth from strain, followed by the order of discovery.
The first letter indicates the restriction type, followed by the molecular weight and code number.
The letters are derived from the scientist who discovered the enzyme and the year of isolation.
The name represents the specific number of base pairs it can cleave per second.
questions.explanation: The convention for naming restriction endonucleases is: first letter from the genus name, next two letters from the species name of the prokaryotic cell from which they are isolated, followed by the strain name, and Roman numbers indicating the order of discovery.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.1.1 (Restriction Enzymes): 'The first letter of the name comes from the genus and the next two letters come from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which the enzyme is isolated...'

questions.question:
Identify the correct combination of features required for a cloning vector used in recombinant DNA technology:
I. Presence of multiple restriction sites for the same enzyme within a marker gene
II. Presence of an origin of replication (ori)
III. Presence of selectable marker genes
iv. Small size to facilitate introduction into host cells
questions.explanation: Vectors must possess an origin of replication (ori), selectable markers to help identify transformants, and should be small in size. Multiple restriction sites for the same enzyme *within* a marker gene would disrupt the marker non-specifically or make insertion inactivation impossible to interpret cleanly if there are too many, but standard vectors avoid multiple sites for the same enzyme to prevent fragmenting the vector.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2: Features needed to facilitate cloning into a vector (origin of replication, selectable markers, cloning sites).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the isolation of genetic material (DNA) is NOT correct?
options: Plant cell walls are degraded using the enzyme cellulase.
RNA can be removed by treating the solution with ribonuclease.
Purified DNA precipitates out after the addition of chilled ethanol.
Proteins are removed by the addition of the enzyme deoxyribonuclease.
questions.explanation: Proteins are removed by treatment with proteases, not deoxyribonuclease (DNase). DNase would degrade the extracted DNA itself. Cellulase breaks down plant cell walls, RNase removes RNA, and chilled ethanol precipitates purified DNA.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.1: Isolation of the Genetic Material (DNA).

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding restriction endonucleases and eliminate the incorrect one:
options: They cut DNA at specific position indicated by palindromic recognition sequences.
They belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases.
Restriction endonucleases function by removing nucleotides from the ends of DNA molecules.
The convention for naming restriction enzymes starts with the genus name followed by species and strain.
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific internal sites, whereas exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA molecules.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.1.1: Restriction Enzymes.

questions.question: In the context of agarose gel electrophoresis, identify the incorrect statement among the following:
options: DNA fragments migrate towards the positive electrode (anode) during electrophoresis.
Smaller DNA fragments move faster and travel further through the agarose gel matrix.
Unstained DNA fragments can be directly visualized under normal visible light.
Ethidium bromide is used to stain DNA, which then glows orange under UV light.
questions.explanation: DNA fragments cannot be visualized directly under normal visible light because they are colorless. They must be stained with ethidium bromide and exposed to UV radiation to be visible as orange bands.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.1: Separation and isolation of DNA fragments.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is NOT involved in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) technique?
options: Denaturation of double-stranded DNA using high temperature
Annealing of primers using thermostable DNA polymerase at high temperatures
Extension of primers along the template DNA using Taq polymerase
Use of deoxynucleotides for synthesizing new DNA strands
questions.explanation: Annealing is carried out at a lower/cooler temperature (than denaturation and extension) to allow primers to bind to the template DNA. Primers do not anneal at high temperatures.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).

questions.question: A recombinant DNA molecule was created by inserting a gene of interest into the BamHI site of plasmid pBR322. Which of the following phenotypic combinations will be observed in the transformants?
options: Resistant to both Ampicillin and Tetracycline
Susceptible to Ampicillin and Resistant to Tetracycline
Resistant to Ampicillin and Susceptible to Tetracycline
Susceptible to both Ampicillin and Tetracycline
questions.explanation: The BamHI restriction site is located within the tetR gene (tetracycline resistance) in pBR322. Insertion of foreign DNA at this site causes insertional inactivation of the tetracycline resistance gene, making the recombinant susceptible to tetracycline while leaving the ampicillin resistance gene (ampR) intact.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2: Insertion of alien DNA is linked to restriction site inside one of the two antibiotic resistance genes (e.g., BamHI in tetR of pBR322).

questions.question: Which of the following methods is NOT a direct or vectorless method of introducing foreign DNA into host cells?
options: Competent host cell treatment with divalent cations
questions.explanation: Disarmed retroviral vectors utilize a vector (pathogen modified to be harmless) to deliver DNA into host cells, making it a vector-based method rather than a direct/vectorless method. Microinjection, biolistics, and divalent cation treatment (heat shock) are direct/vectorless methods.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.4: Methods of Introducing Recombinant DNA into Host Cell.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement regarding stirred-tank bioreactors:
options: The sparged stirred-tank bioreactor has a sterile air bubble system infused through the bottom.
It facilitates the mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.
It is exclusively used for analytical scale production of DNA in laboratories.
It contains a foam breaker, temperature control system, and pH control system.
questions.explanation: Stirred-tank bioreactors are used for large-scale production (bioprocessing) to grow microbes/cells to obtain large quantities of products, not just exclusively for small analytical scale lab work.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.4: Processes of Recombinant Technology (Bioreactors).

questions.question: During the process of insertional inactivation using $\beta$-galactosidase, recombinant colonies can be distinguished from non-recombinant colonies because:
options: Recombinants produce blue colored colonies in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Non-recombinants produce blue colored colonies, whereas recombinants are colorless.
Recombinants fail to grow on media containing ampicillin.
Non-recombinants undergo lysis due to insertional activation.
questions.explanation: In insertional inactivation, the gene coding for $\beta$-galactosidase is inactivated by the insertion of alien DNA. Thus, recombinant colonies do not produce any color and appear white/colorless, while non-recombinant colonies produce a blue color with the chromogenic substrate.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.2.2: Selection of recombinants through insertional inactivation (alpha-complementation / beta-galactosidase test).

questions.question: Which feature of Thermus aquaticus makes its DNA polymerase extremely useful in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
options: It can replicate RNA templates in addition to DNA templates.
It remains active during the high temperature denaturation steps of PCR.
It requires no primers to initiate DNA synthesis.
It operates at a very low optimum pH.
questions.explanation: Correction check: Wait, option 1 says RNA (false), option 2 says remains active at high denaturation temperatures (true), option 3 says requires no primers (false), option 4 says low pH (false). Let's check options mapping. The correct option is the one stating it remains active during high temperatures (thermostable). Let's review the options indices: index 1 corresponds to option 2.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 9, Section 9.3.2: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) - thermostable DNA polymerase isolated from bacterium Thermus aquaticus.

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is correctly matched with its specific function in recombinant DNA technology as described in NCERT?
options: EcoRI - Cuts DNA at random sites to produce blunt ends
DNA ligase - Joins the sticky ends of DNA strands by forming hydrogen bonds between bases
Taq polymerase - Remains active during the high temperature denaturation induced during PCR
Alkaline phosphatase - Removes phosphate groups from the 5' end of DNA
questions.explanation: Alkaline phosphatase removes the 5'-phosphate group to prevent self-ligation of plasmid vectors. EcoRI produces specific sticky ends, not random cuts or blunt ends. DNA ligase forms phosphodiester bonds, not just hydrogen bonds. Taq polymerase remains active during high temperature extension/synthesis, but denaturation happens at 94-98°C where DNA melts, not where Taq acts.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, page 197-201 mentions the tools of recombinant DNA technology including restriction enzymes, ligases, and host organisms.

questions.question: During the separation of DNA fragments using agarose gel electrophoresis, what is the exact basis for their movement toward the anode?
options: Their overall net positive charge due to basic amino acids in bound proteins
Their size-to-charge ratio being uniform, allowing smaller fragments to sieve through the gel matrix faster
The application of an electric field that forces negatively charged protein-DNA complexes to move
The intrinsic catalytic property of the agarose matrix to repel larger nucleotide polymers
questions.explanation: DNA fragments are negatively charged due to phosphate backbone. Because charge-to-mass ratio is constant for all DNA molecules, they move towards the anode solely based on size through the sieving effect of the agarose gel.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 198: 'Since DNA fragments are negatively charged molecules, they can be forced to move towards the anode under an electric field through a medium/matrix... smaller the fragment size, the farther it moves.'

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding plasmid vectors used in genetic engineering and select the option that correctly identifies them as True (T) or False (F):
I. Plasmids are extrachromosomal, self-replicating circular DNA molecules found in many bacteria.
II. pBR322 has two unique resistance genes for ampicillin and tetracycline which act as selectable markers.
III. Restriction sites within the antibiotic resistance genes in pBR322 allow for insertional inactivation.
IV. Ori is the sequence responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA in the host cell.
questions.explanation: All four statements are factual descriptions directly from NCERT regarding cloning vectors (pBR322) and their characteristic features like Ori, selectable markers, and cloning sites.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 199-201: Details of cloning vectors, features required to facilitate cloning (ori, selectable markers, cloning sites).

questions.question: A recombinant DNA molecule is constructed by inserting a foreign gene at the BamHI site of tetracycline resistance gene in pBR322. If this plasmid is transformed into E. coli cells, what will be the antibiotic resistance profile of the transformants?
options: Resistant to both ampicillin and tetracycline
Sensitive to both ampicillin and tetracycline
Resistant to ampicillin and sensitive to tetracycline
Sensitive to ampicillin and resistant to tetracycline
questions.explanation: The BamHI site is located inside the tetracycline resistance gene (tet^R). Insertion of foreign DNA at this site inactivates the tet^R gene (insertional inactivation), making the recombinant cells sensitive to tetracycline while remaining resistant to ampicillin via the intact amp^R gene.
questions.ncertEvidence: NCERT Class XII, Chapter 11, Page 200-201: Selection of recombinants due to inactivation of antibiotics (insertional inactivation).

questions.question: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) technique as outlined in NCERT?
options: Denaturation of double-stranded DNA using heat (around 94°C)
Annealing of two sets of synthetic oligonucleotide primers at 50-60°C
Extension of primers in the presence of thermostable DNA polymerase and deoxynucleotides
Ligation of the amplified PCR product into a plasmid vector using DNA ligase inside the thermal cycler
